        "contents": "# Orchestrator Example - Build and Flash Guide\n\n## Overview\n\nThis example provides two firmware variants:\n- **TX Variant (Node A)**: Transmits UWB packets periodically\n- **RX Variant (Node B)**: Receives UWB packets and collects statistics\n\nBoth variants communicate with the Orchestrator via RS-485 using UART.\n\n## Pin Configuration\n\n### UART Pins (RS-485 Communication)\n- **RX Pin**: GPIO 15 (UART_0_RX_PIN)\n- **TX Pin**: GPIO 19 (UART_0_TX_PIN)\n- **Baud Rate**: 115200\n\n**Note**: Pins 8 and 10 are used for:\n- **Pin 8**: DW3000_IRQ_Pin (interrupt pin for UWB chip)\n- **Pin 10**: DW3000_CS_Pin (SPI chip select for UWB chip)\n\nThe UART for RS-485 communication uses **pins 15 (RX) and 19 (TX)**, not pins 8 and 10.\n\n## Building and Flashing\n\n### Step 1: Build TX Variant (Node A)\n\n1. Edit &#96;Src/example_selection.h&#96;:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;c\n   // Comment out other examples:\n   //#define TEST_READING_DEV_ID\n   \n   // Uncomment TX variant:\n   #define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_TX\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n2. Edit &#96;Src/main.c&#96;:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;c\n   // Comment out other examples:\n   // extern int read_dev_id(void); read_dev_id();\n   \n   // Uncomment TX variant:\n   extern int orchestrator_tx(void); orchestrator_tx();\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n3. Build:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   make build\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n4. Flash to Node A board:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   make flash\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 2: Build RX Variant (Node B)\n\n1. Edit &#96;Src/example_selection.h&#96;:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;c\n   // Comment out TX variant:\n   //#define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_TX\n   \n   // Uncomment RX variant:\n   #define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_RX\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n2. Edit &#96;Src/main.c&#96;:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;c\n   // Comment out TX variant:\n   // extern int orchestrator_tx(void); orchestrator_tx();\n   \n   // Uncomment RX variant:\n   extern int orchestrator_rx(void); orchestrator_rx();\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n3. Build:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   make build\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n4. Flash to Node B board:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   make flash\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Important**: You need to build and flash **separately** for each board. The firmware is compiled with either TX or RX code, not both.\n\n## LED Behavior\n\nThe firmware uses &#96;dwt_setleds()&#96; which controls the **DW3000 UWB chip's internal LEDs**, not the board LEDs.\n\n- **On startup**: LEDs will blink once during initialization",

        },
        "contents": "## LED Behavior\n\nThe firmware uses &#96;dwt_setleds()&#96; which controls the **DW3000 UWB chip's internal LEDs**, not the board LEDs.\n\n- **On startup**: LEDs will blink once during initialization\n- **During operation**: LEDs may flash during UWB activity (TX/RX events)\n- **Board LEDs**: The DWM3001CDK board LEDs (LED_1, LED_2, LED_3, LED_4) are not directly controlled by this firmware\n\n## RS-485 Connection\n\nConnect the RS-485 transceiver to:\n- **A+**: Connect to RS-485 A+ line\n- **B-**: Connect to RS-485 B- line  \n- **GND**: Connect to ground\n- **UART RX**: Connect to GPIO 15\n- **UART TX**: Connect to GPIO 19\n- **DE/RE**: Connect to control RS-485 direction (if needed)\n\nThe firmware communicates at **115200 baud** with the Orchestrator.\n\n## Testing\n\nAfter flashing:\n\n1. **Connect RS-485** from each board to the Orchestrator (RPi 5)\n2. **Power on** both boards\n3. **Run the Orchestrator**:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   cd Orchestrator\n   npm start\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe Orchestrator will:\n- Send &#96;PNG&#96; (PING) commands to verify connectivity\n- Configure both nodes with &#96;CFG&#96; commands\n- Start tests with &#96;STRT&#96; commands\n- Collect statistics with &#96;STAT&#96; commands\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n### UART Not Working\n- Verify pins 15 (RX) and 19 (TX) are connected correctly\n- Check RS-485 transceiver wiring (A+, B-, GND)\n- Verify baud rate is 115200\n- Check that RS-485 termination resistors are present (120Ω at each end)\n\n### Wrong Variant Flashed\n- Make sure you build and flash separately for each board\n- Check &#96;example_selection.h&#96; has the correct &#96;#define&#96; uncommented\n- Check &#96;main.c&#96; has the correct function call uncommented\n\n### LEDs Not Flashing\n- The firmware controls DW3000 internal LEDs, not board LEDs\n- Board LEDs may not flash unless you add code to control them\n- Check UWB activity with the Orchestrator's statistics",
        "signatures": {},

        "contents": "int orchestrator_rx(void)\n{\n    uint32_t dev_id;\n\n    /* Display application name */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Initialize UART for RS-485 */\n    uart_init();\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC();\n    Sleep(2);\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n    dev_id = dwt_readdevid();\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED\");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enable LEDs */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure with default settings */\n    configure_uwb();\n\n    /* Main loop - process UART commands and RX packets */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        if (g_test_running)\n        {\n            process_rx_packet();\n        }\n        else\n        {\n            Sleep(100);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#endif",

        "contents": "/**\n * Application entry point\n */\nint orchestrator_tx(void)\n{\n    uint32_t dev_id;\n\n    /* Display application name */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Initialize UART for RS-485 */\n    uart_init();\n\n    /* Initialize app timer module */\n    uint32_t err_code = app_timer_init();\n    if (err_code != NRF_SUCCESS)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"TIMER INIT FAILED\");\n    }\n    else\n    {\n        /* Create timer instance */\n        err_code = app_timer_create(&amp;m_tx_timer_id, APP_TIMER_MODE_REPEATED, tx_timer_handler);\n        if (err_code == NRF_SUCCESS)\n        {\n            g_timer_initialized = 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC();\n    Sleep(2);\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n    dev_id = dwt_readdevid();\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED\");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enable LEDs */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure with default settings */\n    configure_uwb();\n\n    /* Main loop - process UART commands */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        // Command processing happens in UART interrupt handler\n        Sleep(100);\n    }\n}\n\n#endif",

        "contents": "int simple_rx(void)\n{\n    /* Hold copy of status register state here for reference so that it can be examined at a debug breakpoint. */\n    uint32_t status_reg;\n    /* Hold copy of frame length of frame received (if good) so that it can be examined at a debug breakpoint. */\n    uint16_t frame_len;\n\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW IC supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC, or could wait for SPIRDY event)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED\");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enabling LEDs here for debug so that for each RX-enable the D2 LED will flash on DW3000 red eval-shield boards. */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Loop forever receiving frames. */\n    while (TRUE)\n    {\n        /* TESTING BREAKPOINT LOCATION #1 */",

Used in TX only. */\n    DWT_PAC8,         /* Preamble acquisition chunk size. Used in RX only. */\n    9,                /* TX preamble code. Used in TX only. */\n    9,                /* RX preamble code.     {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": ".\\Src\\examples\\ex_02h_simple_rx_pdoa\\simple_rx_pdoa.c",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {
            "line": 50,
            "column": 79
          },
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 109,
            "column": 38
          }
        },
        "contents": "/**\n * Application entry point.\n */\nint simple_rx_pdoa(void)\n{\n    uint32_t dev_id;\n    int16_t last_pdoa_val = 0;\n\n    /* Sends application name to test_run_info function. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    dev_id = dwt_readdevid();\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_IDLE) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED\");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure DW3000. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Register RX call-back. */\n    dwt_setcallbacks(NULL, rx_ok_cb, rx_err_cb, rx_err_cb, NULL, NULL, NULL);\n\n    /* Enable wanted interrupts (RX good frames and RX errors). */\n    dwt_setinterrupt(DWT_INT_RXFCG_BIT_MASK | SYS_STATUS_ALL_RX_ERR, 0, DWT_ENABLE_INT);\n\n    /*Clearing the SPI ready interrupt*/\n    dwt_writesysstatuslo(DWT_INT_RCINIT_BIT_MASK | DWT_INT_SPIRDY_BIT_MASK);\n\n    /* Install DW IC IRQ handler. */\n    port_set_dwic_isr(dwt_isr);\n\n    /* Activate reception immediately. See NOTE 1 below. */\n    dwt_rxenable(DWT_START_RX_IMMEDIATE);\n\n    /*loop forever receiving frames*/\n    while (1)\n    {\n        if (last_pdoa_val != pdoa_val)",

        "contents": "/* Values for the PG_DELAY and TX_POWER registers reflect the bandwidth and power of the spectrum at the current\n * temperature. These values can be calibrated prior to taking reference measurements. See NOTE 2 below. */\nextern dwt_txconfig_t txconfig_options;\n\n/**\n * Application entry point.\n */\nint simple_tx_sts_sdc(void)\n{\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enabling LEDs here for debug so that for each TX the D1 LED will flash on DW3000 red eval-shield boards. */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. See NOTE 9 below. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure the TX spectrum parameters (power, PG delay and PG count) */\n    dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options);\n\n    /* can enable TX/RX states output on GPIOs 5 and 6 to help debug */\n    dwt_setlnapamode(DWT_LNA_ENABLE | DWT_PA_ENABLE);\n\n    /* Loop forever sending frames periodically. */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        /* Write frame data to DW IC and prepare transmission. See NOTE 3 below.*/",

        "contents": "/* Index to access to sequence number of the blink frame in the tx_msg array. */\n#define BLINK_FRAME_SN_IDX 1\n\n#define FRAME_LENGTH (sizeof(tx_msg) + FCS_LEN) // The real length that is going to be transmitted\n\n/* Inter-frame delay period, in milliseconds. */\n#define TX_DELAY_MS 500\n\n/* Values for the PG_DELAY and TX_POWER registers reflect the bandwidth and power of the spectrum at the current\n * temperature. These values can be calibrated prior to taking reference measurements. See NOTE 2 below. */\nextern dwt_txconfig_t txconfig_options;\n\n/**\n * Application entry point.\n */\nint simple_tx(void)\n{\n    uint32_t dev_id;\n\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC, or could wait for SPIRDY event)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    dev_id = dwt_readdevid();\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enabling LEDs here for debug so that for each TX the D1 LED will flash on DW3000 red eval-shield boards. */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure DW IC.         "contents": "int ack_data_tx(void)\n{\n    /* Hold copy of frame length of frame received (if good) so that it can be examined at a debug breakpoint. */\n    uint16_t frame_len = 0, tx_frame_len;\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    tx_frame_len = sizeof(tx_msg) + FCS_LEN;\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_IDLE) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED\");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. See NOTE 6 below. */\n    dwt_setrxaftertxdelay(50);\n\n    /* Set RX frame timeout for the response. */\n    dwt_setrxtimeout(RX_RESP_TO_UUS);\n    /* can enable TX/RX states output on GPIOs 5 and 6 to help debug */\n    dwt_setlnapamode(DWT_LNA_ENABLE | DWT_PA_ENABLE);\n\n    /* Loop forever transmitting data. */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        /* Write frame data to DW IC and prepare transmission.         "contents": "/* Hold copy of status register state here for reference so that it can be examined at a debug breakpoint. */\nstatic uint32_t status_reg;\n\n/* Hold copy of frame length of frame received (if good) so that it can be examined at a debug breakpoint. */\nstatic uint16_t frame_len;\n\n/**\n * Application entry point.\n */\nint simple_rx_sts_sdc(void)\n{\n    int goodSts = 0;    /* Used for checking STS quality in received signal */\n    int16_t stsQual;    /* This will contain STS quality index */\n    uint16_t stsStatus; /* Used to check for good STS status (no errors). */\n\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enabling LEDs here for debug so that for each RX-enable the D2 LED will flash on DW3000 red eval-shield boards. */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Loop forever receiving frames. */\n    while (TRUE)\n    {\n        /* TESTING BREAKPOINT LOCATION #1 */",

See NOTE 3 below. */\n    dwt_setrxaftertxdelay(TX_TO_RX_DELAY_UUS);\n\n    /* Set response frame timeout. */\n    dwt_setrxtimeout(RX_RESP_TO_UUS);\n\n    /* Loop forever sending and receiving frames periodically. */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        /* Write frame data to DW3000 and prepare transmission.         },
        "contents": "/*! ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n *  @file    read_dev_id.c\n *  @brief   This example just read DW IC's device ID. It can be used to verify\n *           the SPI comms are working correctly.\n *\n * @attention\n *\n * Copyright 2018 - 2021 (c) Decawave Ltd, Dublin, Ireland.\n *\n * All rights reserved.\n *\n * @author Decawave\n */\n\n#include \"deca_probe_interface.h\"\n#include &lt;deca_device_api.h&gt;\n#include &lt;example_selection.h&gt;\n#include &lt;port.h&gt;\n#include &lt;stdio.h&gt;\n\n#if defined(TEST_READING_DEV_ID)\n\nextern void test_run_info(unsigned char *data);\n\n/* Example application name and version to display on LCD screen/VCOM port. */\n#define APP_NAME \"READ DEV ID      \"\n\n/**\n * Application entry point.\n */\nint read_dev_id(void)\n{\n    int err;\n    uint32_t dev_id;\n\n    bsp_board_led_on(0);\n\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    bsp_board_led_on(1);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    bsp_board_led_on(2);\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    bsp_board_led_on(3);\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC, or could wait for SPIRDY event)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n\n    dev_id = dwt_readdevid();\n\n\n    /* Reads and validate device ID returns DWT_ERROR if it does not match expected else DWT_SUCCESS */\n    if ((err = dwt_check_dev_id()) == DWT_SUCCESS)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"DEV ID OK\");\n    }\n    else\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"DEV ID FAILED\");\n    }\n\n    return err;\n}\n\n#endif\n/*****************************************************************************************************************************************************\n * NOTES:\n ****************************************************************************************************************************************************/",

        "contents": "extern dwt_txconfig_t txconfig_options;\n\n/**\n * Application entry point.\n */\nint ack_data_rx(void)\n{\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_IDLE) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED\");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. See NOTE 9 below. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure the TX spectrum parameters (power, PG delay and PG count) */\n    dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options);\n\n    /* Set PAN ID and short address. See NOTE 2 below. */\n    dwt_setpanid(PAN_ID);\n    dwt_setaddress16(SHORT_ADDR);\n\n    /* Configure frame filtering. Only data frames are enabled in this example. Frame filtering must be enabled for Auto ACK to work. */\n    dwt_configureframefilter(DWT_FF_ENABLE_802_15_4, DWT_FF_DATA_EN);\n    /* Activate auto-acknowledgement. Time is set to 0 so that the ACK is sent as soon as possible after reception of a frame. */\n    dwt_enableautoack(0, 1);\n\n    /* can enable TX/RX states output on GPIOs 5 and 6 to help debug */\n    dwt_setlnapamode(DWT_LNA_ENABLE | DWT_PA_ENABLE);\n    /* Loop forever receiving frames. */\n    /* Clear previous received data flag */\n    dwt_writesysstatuslo(DWT_INT_RXFCG_BIT_MASK);\n\n    while (1)\n    {\n        /* Activate reception immediately. See NOTE 5 below. */",

        },
        "contents": "/* Statistics structure */\ntypedef struct {\n    uint32_t total_rx;        // Total packets received\n    uint32_t lost_pkts;       // Lost packets (sequence gaps)\n    uint32_t crc_err;         // CRC errors\n    uint32_t last_seq;        // Last received sequence number\n    uint8_t seq_init;         // Sequence initialized flag\n    \n    int64_t rssi_sum;         // Sum of RSSI values\n    int64_t snr_sum;          // Sum of SNR values\n    int64_t pre_q_sum;        // Sum of preamble quality values\n    uint32_t metric_count;    // Number of metrics collected\n} rx_stats_t;\n\n/* Global state */\nstatic uwb_config_t g_config = {\n    .channel = 5,\n    .data_rate = 1,           // 6.8Mbps\n    .preamble_len = 128,\n    .preamble_code = 9,\n    .tx_power_idx = 5,\n    .pkt_rate_hz = 100,\n    .payload_len = 64,\n    .configured = 0\n};\n\nstatic dwt_config_t dwt_config = {\n    5,                /* Channel number. */\n    DWT_PLEN_128,     /* Preamble length. */\n    DWT_PAC8,         /* Preamble acquisition chunk size. */\n    9,                /* TX preamble code. */\n    9,                /* RX preamble code. */\n    1,                /* SFD type */\n    DWT_BR_6M8,       /* Data rate. */\n    DWT_PHRMODE_STD,  /* PHY header mode. */\n    DWT_PHRRATE_STD,  /* PHY header rate. */\n    (129 + 8 - 8),    /* SFD timeout. */\n    DWT_STS_MODE_OFF, /* STS mode off. */\n    DWT_STS_LEN_64,   /* STS length. */\n    DWT_PDOA_M0       /* PDOA mode off. */\n};\n\nstatic rx_stats_t g_stats = {0};\nstatic volatile uint8_t g_test_running = 0;\nstatic uint8_t g_rx_buffer[FRAME_LEN_MAX];\n\n\n/* Forward declarations */\nstatic void uart_event_handler(app_uart_evt_t *p_event);\nstatic void parse_command(char *cmd);\nstatic void send_response(const char *response);\nstatic void configure_uwb(void);\nstatic void process_rx_packet(void);\n\n/**\n * UART event handler\n */\nstatic void uart_event_handler(app_uart_evt_t *p_event)\n{\n    static uint8_t rx_buffer[UART_BUFFER_SIZE];\n    static uint16_t rx_index = 0;",

            "line": 142,
            "column": 150
          }
        },
        "contents": "    while (TRUE)\n    {\n        /* TESTING BREAKPOINT LOCATION #1 */\n\n        /* Clear local RX buffer to avoid having leftovers from previous receptions  This is not necessary but is included here to aid reading\n         * the RX buffer.\n         * This is a good place to put a breakpoint. Here (after first time through the loop) the local status register will be set for last event\n         * and if a good receive has happened the data buffer will have the data in it, and frame_len will be set to the length of the RX frame. */\n        memset(rx_buffer, 0, sizeof(rx_buffer));\n\n        /* Activate reception immediately. See NOTE 2 below. */\n        dwt_rxenable(DWT_START_RX_IMMEDIATE);\n\n        /* Poll until a frame is properly received or an error/timeout occurs. See NOTE 3 below.\n         * STATUS register is 5 bytes long but, as the event we are looking at is in the first byte of the register, we can use this simplest API\n         * function to access it. */\n        waitforsysstatus(&amp;status_reg, NULL, (DWT_INT_RXFCG_BIT_MASK | SYS_STATUS_ALL_RX_ERR), 0);\n\n        if (status_reg &amp; DWT_INT_RXFCG_BIT_MASK)\n        {\n            /* A frame has been received, copy it to our local buffer. */\n            frame_len = dwt_getframelength();\n            if (frame_len &lt;= FRAME_LEN_MAX)\n            {\n                dwt_readrxdata(rx_buffer, frame_len - FCS_LEN, 0); /* No need to read the FCS/CRC. */\n            }\n\n            /* Clear good RX frame event in the DW IC status register. */\n            dwt_writesysstatuslo(DWT_INT_RXFCG_BIT_MASK);\n\n            test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"Frame Received\");\n        }\n        else\n        {\n            /* Clear RX error events in the DW IC status register. */\n            dwt_writesysstatuslo(SYS_STATUS_ALL_RX_ERR);\n        }\n    }\n}\n#endif\n/*****************************************************************************************************************************************************\n * NOTES:\n *\n * 1. In this example, maximum frame length is set to 127 bytes which is 802.15.4 UWB standard maximum frame length. DW IC supports an extended\n *    frame length (up to 1023 bytes long) mode which is not used in this example.\n * 2. Manual reception activation is performed here but DW IC offers several features that can be used to handle more complex scenarios or to\n *    optimise system's overall performance (e.g. timeout after a given time, automatic re-enabling of reception in case of errors, etc.).\n * 3. We use polled mode of operation here to keep the example as simple as possible, but RXFCG and error/timeout status events can be used to generate\n *    interrupts. Please refer to DW IC User Manual for more details on \"interrupts\".\n ****************************************************************************************************************************************************/",

        "contents": "int tx_with_cca(void)\n{\n\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC, or could wait for SPIRDY event)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enabling LEDs here for debug so that for each TX the D1 LED will flash on DW3000 red eval-shield boards. */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. See NOTE 7 below. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure the TX spectrum parameters (power, PG delay and PG count) */\n    dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options);\n\n    /* Configure preamble timeout to 3 PACs; if no preamble detected in this time we assume channel is clear. See NOTE 4*/\n    dwt_setpreambledetecttimeout(3);\n\n    /* Loop forever sending frames periodically. */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        /* Write frame data to DW3000 and prepare transmission. See NOTE 5 below.*/",

**No, there are no UART examples in `Src/examples` excluding `ex_21_orchestrator`.**

All UART references are in `ex_21_orchestrator` (RS-485 over UART).

The other examples focus on:
- UWB (Ultra-Wideband) TX/RX
- Two-Way Ranging (TWR)
- GPIO (`ex_13a_gpio`)
- Timer (`ex_18_timer`)
- SPI CRC (`ex_11a_spi_crc`)
- AES encryption
- Other UWB features

If you need a UART example, you can:
1. Use `ex_21_orchestrator` as a reference (it includes UART initialization and event handling)
2. Check the platform files (`Src/platform/`) for UART-related code
3. Create a new example based on the UART code in `ex_21_orchestrator`

CTS_PIN_NUMBER,<br/>           UART_HWFC,<br/>           false,<br/>           NRF_UART_BAUDRATE_115200<br/>       \};<br/><br/>       APP_UART_FIFO_INIT(&comm_params,<br/>                          UART_RX_BUF_SIZE,<br/>                          UART_TX_BUF_SIZE,<br/>                          uart_event_handle,<br/>                          APP_IRQ_PRIORITY_LOWEST,<br/>                          err_code);<br/><br/>       APP_ERROR_CHECK(err_code);<br/>   \}<br/>   ```<br/><br/><br/>4. **Implement the UART Event Handler**: Define a function to handle UART events:<br/><br/>   ```c<br/>   void uart_event_handle(app_uart_evt_t * p_event)<br/>   \{<br/>       uint8_t data;<br/>       switch (p_event->evt_type)<br/>       \{<br/>           case APP_UART_DATA_READY:<br/>               while (app_uart_get(&data) == NRF_SUCCESS)<br/>               \{<br/>                   // Process received data<br/>               \}<br/>               break;<br/><br/>           case APP_UART_COMMUNICATION_ERROR:<br/>               APP_ERROR_HANDLER(p_event->data.error_communication);<br/>               break;<br/><br/>           case APP_UART_FIFO_ERROR:<br/>               APP_ERROR_HANDLER(p_event->data.error_code);<br/>               break;<br/><br/>           default:<br/>               break;<br/>       \}<br/>   \}<br/>   ```<br/><br/><br/>5. **Enable UART in `sdk_config.h`**: Ensure that the UART module and its dependencies are enabled in your `sdk_config.h` file:<br/><br/>   ```c<br/>   #define APP_UART_ENABLED 1<br/>   #define APP_FIFO_ENABLED 1<br/>   #define NRFX_UART_ENABLED 1<br/>   #define NRFX_UARTE_ENABLED 1<br/>   ```<br/><br/><br/>This setup initializes the UART peripheral on the nRF52833, configures it with the specified parameters, and sets up an event handler to manage incoming data and handle errors. For more detailed information and additional configurations, you can refer to the Nordic DevZone discussions and examples:<br/><br/>- [UART1 and UART0 on nRF52833](https://devzone.nordicsemi.com/f/nordic-q-a/117206/uart1-and-uart0-on-nrf52833)<br/>- [NRF52833 Adding UART to Thread MQTTSN client publisher](https://devzone.nordicsemi.com/f/nordic-q-a/92434/nrf52833-adding-uart-to-thead-mqttsn-client-publisher)<br/>- [NRF52833 UART Application Compilation Error](https://devzone.nordicsemi.com/f/nordic-q-a/77270/nrf52833-uart-application-compilation-error)<br/><br/>These resources provide insights into configuring and troubleshooting UART on the nRF52833. |

## UART Pin Configuration on DWM3001CDK

**Default UART pins:**
- **TX (Transmit):** P0.19 (GPIO 19)
- **RX (Receive):** P0.15 (GPIO 15)

These pins are accessible via the Raspberry Pi compatible header:
- **TXD:** Pin 32 (P0.15)
- **RXD:** Pin 34 (P0.19)

## Important Notes

1. **Default behavior:** The DWM3001CDK uses USB CDC (Virtual COM port) by default. To use GPIO UART, enable it in firmware.

2. **RTS/CTS:** Not connected on DWM3001CDK; disable hardware flow control.

3. **Pin conflicts:** Avoid using P0.27 for UART RX; it's connected to the DW3110 IRQ line.

## Implementation Details

The board uses the **nRF52833 SoC** with the `app_uart.h` library. Your `ex_21_orchestrator` example already follows this pattern:

- Uses `APP_UART_FIFO_INIT()` for initialization
- Configures pins 15 (RX) and 19 (TX)
- Disables flow control (`APP_UART_FLOW_CONTROL_DISABLED`)
- Uses event handler for receiving data

## SDK Configuration

Ensure these are enabled in `sdk_config.h`:
```c
#define APP_UART_ENABLED 1
#define APP_FIFO_ENABLED 1
#define NRFX_UART_ENABLED 1
```

Your `ex_21_orchestrator` example aligns with these references. Should I check your `sdk_config.h` to confirm UART is enabled, or help create a standalone UART example?

        "contents": "/**\n * UART event handler\n */\nstatic void uart_event_handler(app_uart_evt_t *p_event)\n{\n    static uint8_t rx_buffer[UART_BUFFER_SIZE];\n    static uint16_t rx_index = 0;\n\n    switch (p_event-&gt;evt_type)\n    {\n        case APP_UART_DATA_READY:\n        {\n            uint32_t err_code;\n            uint8_t byte;\n            err_code = app_uart_get(&amp;byte);\n            if (err_code == NRF_SUCCESS)\n            {\n                if (byte == '\\r' || byte == '\\n')\n                {\n                    if (rx_index &gt; 0)\n                    {\n                        rx_buffer[rx_index] = '\\0';\n                        parse_command((char *)rx_buffer);\n                        rx_index = 0;\n                    }\n                }\n                else if (rx_index &lt;         "contents": "# UWB Test Orchestrator Configuration\n# Settings can be overridden via .env file (see scripts/load-env.js)\n\nserial:\n  # Serial port configuration for RS-485 communication\n  # On Windows: COM3, COM4, etc.\n  # On Linux: /dev/ttyUSB0, /dev/ttyUSB1, etc.\n  node_a_port: COM3\n  node_b_port: COM4\n  baudrate: 115200\n  timeout: 5 # seconds\n\ntest:\n  # Test execution settings\n  poll_interval_seconds: 2 # How often to poll node stats during test\n  default_test_duration_seconds: 30 # Default test duration if not specified\n\n  # Default UWB configuration (can be overridden per test)\n  channel: 5\n  data_rate: 6m8 # Options: 850k, 6m8\n  preamble_len: 128\n  payload_len: 64\n  tx_power_idx: 5\n  pkt_rate_hz: 100\n\nweb:\n  # Web server configuration\n  port: 5000\n  host: 0.0.0.0 # Listen on all interfaces\n\nswagger:\n  # Swagger/OpenAPI documentation\n  title: UWB Test Orchestrator API\n  version: 1.0.0\n  description: API for controlling UWB DWM3001C test rig",

        "contents": "void dwm3001c_spi_init(void)\n{\n    nrf_drv_spi_t *spi_inst;\n    nrf_drv_spi_config_t *spi_config;\n\n    spi_handle_t *pSPI_handler = SPI-&gt;pSpi;\n\n    pSPI_handler-&gt;frequency_slow = NRF_SPIM_FREQ_4M;\n    pSPI_handler-&gt;frequency_fast = NRF_SPIM_FREQ_32M;\n\n    pSPI_handler-&gt;lock = DW_HAL_NODE_UNLOCKED;\n\n    spi_inst = &amp;pSPI_handler-&gt;spi_inst;\n    spi_config = &amp;pSPI_handler-&gt;spi_config;\n\n    spi_inst-&gt;inst_idx = SPI3_INSTANCE_INDEX;\n    spi_inst-&gt;use_easy_dma = SPI3_USE_EASY_DMA;\n    spi_inst-&gt;u.spim.p_reg = NRF_SPIM3;\n    spi_inst-&gt;u.spim.drv_inst_idx = NRFX_SPIM3_INST_IDX;\n\n    spi_config-&gt;sck_pin = DW3000_CLK_Pin;\n    spi_config-&gt;mosi_pin = DW3000_MOSI_Pin;\n    spi_config-&gt;miso_pin = DW3000_MISO_Pin;\n    spi_config-&gt;ss_pin   = NRF_DRV_SPI_PIN_NOT_USED;  // pin driven manually, not by the driver\n    spi_config-&gt;irq_priority = (APP_IRQ_PRIORITY_MID - 2);\n    spi_config-&gt;orc = 0xFF;\n    spi_config-&gt;frequency = NRF_SPIM_FREQ_4M;\n    spi_config-&gt;mode = NRF_DRV_SPI_MODE_0;\n    spi_config-&gt;bit_order = NRF_DRV_SPI_BIT_ORDER_MSB_FIRST;\n\n    // Configure the chip select as an output pin that can be toggled\n    nrf_drv_gpiote_out_config_t out_config = NRFX_GPIOTE_CONFIG_OUT_TASK_TOGGLE(NRF_GPIOTE_INITIAL_VALUE_HIGH);\n    nrf_drv_gpiote_out_init(DW3000_CS_Pin, &amp;out_config);\n}\n\n/*! ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n * Function: openspi()\n *\n * Low level abstract function to open and initialise access to the SPI device.\n * returns 0 for success, or -1 for error\n */\nstatic int openspi(nrf_drv_spi_t *p_instance)\n{\n    NRF_SPIM_Type *p_spi = p_instance-&gt;u.spim.p_reg;\n    nrf_spim_enable(p_spi);\n    return 0;\n} // end openspi()\n\n/*! ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n * Function: closespi()\n *\n * Low level abstract function to close the the SPI device.\n * returns 0 for success, or -1 for error\n */",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "void dwm3001c_spi_init(void)",
            "lineNumber": 52

        "contents": "#!/usr/bin/env node\n/**\n * Baud Rate and Hex Data Diagnostic Tool\n * Tests different baud rates and analyzes hex data corruption\n */\n\nimport { SerialPort } from 'serialport';\nimport { ReadlineParser } from 'serialport';\nimport { setTimeout as sleep } from 'timers/promises';\n\nconst BAUD_RATES = [9600, 19200, 38400, 57600, 115200, 230400, 460800, 921600, 1000000];\nconst TEST_PORTS = process.argv.slice(2);\n\nif (TEST_PORTS.length === 0) {\n  console.error('Usage: node scripts/diagnose-baud-hex.js /dev/ttyUSB0 [/dev/ttyUSB1]');\n  process.exit(1);\n}\n\nfunction analyzeHexData(hexString) {\n  const analysis = {\n    isCorrupted: false,\n    isPrintable: false,\n    patterns: [],\n    suggestions: []\n  };\n\n  // Check if it's mostly printable ASCII\n  const bytes = hexString.match(/.{2}/g) || [];\n  const printableCount = bytes.filter(b =&gt; {\n    const val = parseInt(b, 16);\n    return (val &gt;= 0x20 &amp;&amp; val &lt;= 0x7E) || val === 0x0D || val === 0x0A;\n  }).length;\n  \n  analysis.isPrintable = printableCount / bytes.length &gt; parseInt(b, 16) &gt;= 0x80).length;\n  if (highBitCount / bytes.length &gt; 0.5) {\n    analysis.patterns.push('Many high-bit values (0x80-0xFF) - suggests baud rate mismatch');\n    analysis.isCorrupted = true;\n  }\n  \n  // Check for alternating patterns (common in wrong baud)\n  if (hexString.match(/f[0-9a-f]f[0-9a-f]f[0-9a-f]/i)) {\n    analysis.patterns.push('Alternating high/low pattern - strong indicator of baud mismatch');\n    analysis.isCorrupted = true;\n  }\n  \n  return analysis;\n}\n\nfunction hexToAscii(hexString) {\n  const bytes = hexString.match(/.{2}/g) || [];\n}",

        "contents": "export function getConfig() {\n\n\n  try {\n    const envContent = fs.readFileSync(envPath, \"utf8\");\n    const envVars = {};\n\n    // Parse .env file (simple key=value format)\n    envContent.split(\"\\n\").forEach((line) =&gt; {\n      line = line.trim();\n      // Skip empty lines and comments\n      if (!line || line.startsWith(\"#\")) {\n        return;\n      }\n\n      const [key, ...valueParts] = line.split(\"=\");\n      if (key &amp;&amp; valueParts.length &gt; 0) {\n        const value = valueParts.join(\"=\").trim();\n        // Remove quotes if present\n        envVars[key.trim()] = value.replace(/^[\"']|[\"']$/g, \"\");\n      }\n    });\n\n    // Build structured config object\n    const config = {};\n\n    // Serial configuration\n    if (envVars.SERIAL_NODE_A_PORT || envVars.NODE_A_PORT) {\n      // Parse timeout as float (supports values like 2.0)\n      const timeoutValue = envVars.SERIAL_TIMEOUT || envVars.TIMEOUT || \"5\";\n      const timeout = parseFloat(timeoutValue);\n\n      config.serial = {\n        node_a_port: envVars.SERIAL_NODE_A_PORT || envVars.NODE_A_PORT,\n        node_b_port: envVars.SERIAL_NODE_B_PORT || envVars.NODE_B_PORT,\n        baudrate: parseInt(\n          envVars.SERIAL_BAUDRATE || envVars.BAUDRATE || \"115200\",\n          10\n        ),\n        timeout: isNaN(timeout) ? 5 : timeout,\n      };\n    }\n\n    // Test configuration\n    if\n}",

        "contents": "export class RS485Comm extends EventEmitter {\n\n\n  /**\n   * Send SET_CONFIG command\n   * @param {Object} config - Configuration object\n   * @returns {Promise&lt;string&gt;}\n   */\n  async setConfig(config) {\n    // Format: SET_CONFIG ch=5 rate=6m8 pl=128 len=64 pwr=5 rate_hz=100\n    // Use short code \"CFG\" for better reliability with long commands\n    // Firmware supports both \"CFG\" (short) and \"SET_CONFIG\" (full)\n    const params = [];\n    if (config.channel !== undefined) params.push(&#96;ch=${config.channel}&#96;);\n    if (config.data_rate !== undefined) {\n      // Firmware expects \"6m8\" for 6.8Mbps or \"850k\" for 850kbps\n      // Handle both string and numeric data_rate values\n      let rateStr;\n      if (typeof config.data_rate === \"string\") {\n        // Already in correct format (e.g., \"6m8\" or \"850k\")\n        rateStr = config.data_rate;\n      } else if (typeof config.data_rate === \"number\") {\n        // Legacy numeric format: 1 = 6.8Mbps, 0 = 850kbps\n        rateStr = config.data_rate === 1 ? \"6m8\" : \"850k\";\n      } else {\n        // Default to 6.8Mbps if unknown format\n        rateStr = \"6m8\";\n      }\n      params.push(&#96;rate=${rateStr}&#96;);\n    }\n    if (config.preamble_len !== undefined)\n      params.push(&#96;pl=${config.preamble_len}&#96;);\n    if (config.payload_len !== undefined)\n      params.push(&#96;len=${config.payload_len}&#96;);\n    if (config.tx_power_idx !== undefined)\n      params.push(&#96;pwr=${config.tx_power_idx}&#96;);\n    if (config.pkt_rate_hz !== undefined)\n      params.push(&#96;rate_hz=${config.pkt_rate_hz}&#96;);\n\n    // Use short code \"CFG\" instead of \"SET_CONFIG\" for better reliability\n    const command = &#96;CFG ${params.join(\" \")}&#96;;\n\n    // #region agent log - SET_CONFIG entry\n  }\n}",

        "contents": "async function testBaudRate(portPath, baudRate) {\n  return new Promise((resolve) =&gt; {\n    const port = new SerialPort({\n      path: portPath,\n      baudRate,\n      dataBits: 8,\n      parity: 'none',\n      stopBits: 1,\n      autoOpen: false,\n    });\n\n    const parser = port.pipe(new ReadlineParser({ delimiter: '\\r\\n' }));\n    let receivedData = [];\n    let rawHexData = [];\n    let timeout;\n\n    // Capture raw data\n    port.on('data', (data) =&gt; {\n      const hex = data.toString('hex');\n      if (hex.length &gt; 0) {\n        rawHexData.push(hex);\n      }\n    });\n\n    parser.on('data', (data) =&gt; {\n      const trimmed = data.toString().trim();\n      if (trimmed.length &gt; 0) {\n        receivedData.push(trimmed);\n      }\n    });\n\n    port.on('open', async () =&gt; {\n      // Wait 2 seconds for initialization messages\n      await sleep(2000);\n      \n      // Send test command\n      port.write('PNG\\r\\n');\n      \n      // Wait for response\n      timeout = setTimeout(() =&gt; {\n        port.close();\n        resolve({ \n          receivedData, \n          rawHexData: rawHexData.join(''),\n          baudRate \n        });\n      }, 2000);\n    });\n\n    port.on('error', (err) =&gt; {\n      clearTimeout(timeout);\n      port.close();\n      resolve({ error: err.message, baudRate });\n    });\n\n    port.open();\n  });\n}\n\nasync function testPort(portPath) {\n  console.log(&#96;\\n${'='.repeat(60)}&#96;);\n}",

        "contents": "int bw_cal(void)\n{\n    /* Variable to store raw temp value */\n    uint8_t raw_temp = 0;\n    /* Variable to store real temp value */\n    float real_temp = 0;\n    /* String to contain temp value for debug purposes */\n    char str_temp[32] = { 0 };\n\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC, or could wait for SPIRDY event)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enabling LEDs here for debug so that for each TX the D1 LED will flash on DW3000 red eval-shield boards. */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. See NOTE 3 below. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* At this point, we are emulating a process that needs to occur at room temperature when devices are being configured in factory. */\n    /* See NOTE 3 for more information */\n    txconfig_options.PGcount = dwt_calcpgcount(txconfig_options.PGdly);\n\n    /* Write the TX message into the TX buffer */\n    /* This only needs to be done once if we are sending the same frame over and over again */\n    dwt_writetxdata(sizeof(tx_msg), tx_msg, 0); /* Zero offset in TX buffer. */\n    dwt_writetxfctrl(sizeof(tx_msg), 0, 0);     /* Zero offset in TX buffer, no ranging. */\n\n    /* Loop forever, adjusting bandwidth periodically. */",

## UART configuration summary

### Pin configuration — correct
- RX Pin: GPIO 15 (`UART_0_RX_PIN` = `RX_PIN_NUMBER` = 15) — matches DWM3001CDK spec (P0.15)
- TX Pin: GPIO 19 (`UART_0_TX_PIN` = `TX_PIN_NUMBER` = 19) — matches DWM3001CDK spec (P0.19)
- RTS/CTS: Set to `UART_PIN_DISCONNECTED` (0xFFFFFFFF) — correct (not connected on DWM3001CDK)

### SDK configuration — correct
- `APP_UART_ENABLED = 1`
- `APP_FIFO_ENABLED = 1`
- `UART_ENABLED = 1`
- `UART0_ENABLED = 1`
- `APP_UART_DRIVER_INSTANCE = 0`

### Baud rate — correct
- Using `30801920` (115200 baud) — matches nRF52833 SDK values

### Flow control — correct
- `APP_UART_FLOW_CONTROL_DISABLED` — correct (RTS/CTS not connected)

### Code implementation — correct
- Includes: `app_uart.h`, `nrf_uart.h`, `custom_board.h`
- Uses `APP_UART_FIFO_INIT()` correctly
- Event handler implemented
- Error checking present

### Potential considerations
1. Hardware: Ensure RS-485 transceiver is connected to pins 15 (RX) and 19 (TX)
2. USB CDC: By default, DWM3001CDK uses USB CDC; GPIO UART must be enabled in firmware (already done)
3. Pin conflicts: No conflicts detected (P0.27 IRQ not used for UART)

## Final verdict: Will it work?

Yes — the UART configuration should work.

All checks pass:
- Correct pins (15/19)
- SDK properly configured
- Correct baud rate
- Proper initialization code
- Flow control disabled (as required)
- No pin conflicts

The implementation matches Nordic SDK patterns and DWM3001CDK hardware specifications. If UART doesn't work, check:
1. RS-485 transceiver wiring
2. RS-485 termination resistors (120Ω at each end)
3. Power supply stability
4. Physical connections to pins 15 and 19

## Explanation of `.specstory/history`

The `.specstory/history` directory contains automatically generated markdown files that document Cursor AI conversations and development sessions.

### What is SpecStory?

SpecStory is a Cursor feature that saves conversation history as markdown files. Each file records:
- User questions and requests
- AI agent responses
- Tool calls (file reads, searches, code edits)
- Code changes and explanations
- Session metadata (timestamps, session IDs)

### Files in `.specstory/history`

1. `2025-12-17_09-32Z-uart-example-in-src-examples.md`
   - Documents the UART example search
   - Includes the search process and findings

        "contents": "int ds_twr_initiator(void)\n{\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. See NOTE 2 below. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure the TX spectrum parameters (power, PG delay and PG count) */\n    dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options);\n\n    /* Apply default antenna delay value. See NOTE 1 below. */\n    dwt_setrxantennadelay(RX_ANT_DLY);\n    dwt_settxantennadelay(TX_ANT_DLY);\n\n    /* Set expected response's delay and timeout. See NOTE 4, 5 and 7 below.\n     * As this example only handles one incoming frame with always the same delay and timeout, those values can be set here once for all. */\n    dwt_setrxaftertxdelay(POLL_TX_TO_RESP_RX_DLY_UUS);\n    dwt_setrxtimeout(RESP_RX_TIMEOUT_UUS);\n    dwt_setpreambledetecttimeout(PRE_TIMEOUT);\n\n    /* Next can enable TX/RX states output on GPIOs 5 and 6 to help debug, and also TX/RX LEDs\n     * Note, in real low power applications the LEDs should not be used. */\n    dwt_setlnapamode(DWT_LNA_ENABLE | DWT_PA_ENABLE);\n    // dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Loop forever initiating ranging exchanges. */",

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": ".\\Src\\examples\\ex_21_orchestrator\\orchestrator_tx.c",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {
            "line": 431,
            "column": 1
          },
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 495,
            "column": 6
          }
        },
        "contents": "/**\n * Application entry point\n */\nint orchestrator_tx(void)\n{\n    uint32_t dev_id;\n\n    /* Display application name */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Initialize UART for RS-485 */\n    uart_init();\n\n    /* Initialize app timer module */\n    uint32_t err_code = app_timer_init();\n    if (err_code != NRF_SUCCESS)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"TIMER INIT FAILED\");\n    }\n    else\n    {\n        /* Create timer instance */\n        err_code = app_timer_create(&amp;m_tx_timer_id, APP_TIMER_MODE_REPEATED, tx_timer_handler);\n        if (err_code == NRF_SUCCESS)\n        {\n            g_timer_initialized = 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC();\n    Sleep(2);\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n    dev_id = dwt_readdevid();\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED\");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enable LEDs */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure with default settings */\n    configure_uwb();\n\n    /* Main loop - process UART commands */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        // Command processing happens in UART interrupt handler\n        Sleep(100);\n    }\n}\n\n#endif",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "/**",
            "lineNumber": 434
          },
          {
            "text": " * Application entry point",
            "lineNumber": 435
          },
          {
            "text": " */",
            "lineNumber": 436
          },
          {
            "text": "int orchestrator_tx(void)",
            "lineNumber": 437
          },
          {

        "contents": "extern dwt_txconfig_t txconfig_options;\n\n/**\n * Application entry point.\n */\nint ack_data_rx(void)\n{\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_IDLE) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED\");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure DW IC.         "contents": "int ss_twr_initiator(void)\n{\n\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset and initialize DW chip. */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW3000 low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC, or could wait for SPIRDY event)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enabling LEDs here for debug so that for each TX the D1 LED will flash on DW3000 red eval-shield boards. */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. See NOTE 13 below. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure the TX spectrum parameters (power, PG delay and PG count) */\n    dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options);\n\n    /* Apply default antenna delay value. See NOTE 2 below. */\n    dwt_setrxantennadelay(RX_ANT_DLY);\n    dwt_settxantennadelay(TX_ANT_DLY);\n\n    /* Set expected response's delay and timeout. See NOTE 1 and 5 below.\n     * As this example only handles one incoming frame with always the same delay and timeout, those values can be set here once for all. */\n    dwt_setrxaftertxdelay(POLL_TX_TO_RESP_RX_DLY_UUS);\n    dwt_setrxtimeout(RESP_RX_TIMEOUT_UUS);\n\n    /* Next can enable TX/RX states output on GPIOs 5 and 6 to help debug, and also TX/RX LEDs\n     * Note, in real low power applications the LEDs should not be used. */",

        "contents": "    if (config_options.chan == 5)\n    {\n        dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options);\n    }\n    else\n    {\n        dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options_ch9);\n    }\n\n    /* Apply default antenna delay value. See NOTE 2 below. */\n    dwt_setrxantennadelay(RX_ANT_DLY);\n    dwt_settxantennadelay(TX_ANT_DLY);\n\n    /* Set expected response's timeout. See NOTE 1 and 5 below.\n     * As this example only handles one incoming frame with always the same delay, this value can be set here once for all. */\n    set_resp_rx_timeout(RESP_RX_TIMEOUT_UUS, &amp;config_options);\n\n    /* Next can enable TX/RX states output on GPIOs 5 and 6 to help diagnostics, and also TX/RX LEDs */\n    dwt_setlnapamode(DWT_LNA_ENABLE | DWT_PA_ENABLE);\n\n    /* Loop for user defined number of ranges. */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        /*\n         * Set STS encryption key and IV (nonce).\n         * See NOTE 16 below.\n         */\n        if (!firstLoopFlag)\n        {\n            /*\n             * On first loop, configure the STS key &amp; IV, then load them.\n             */\n            dwt_configurestskey(&amp;cp_key);\n            dwt_configurestsiv(&amp;cp_iv);\n            dwt_configurestsloadiv();\n            firstLoopFlag = 1;\n        }\n        else\n        {\n            /*\n             * On subsequent loops, we only need to reload the lower 32 bits of STS IV.\n             */\n            dwt_configurestsiv(&amp;cp_iv);\n            dwt_configurestsloadiv();\n        }\n        /*\n         * Send the poll message to the responder.\n         */\n        send_tx_poll_msg();\n\n        /*\n         * Set a reference time for the RX to start after TX timestamp.\n         * See NOTE 14 below.\n         */\n        set_delayed_rx_time(POLL_TX_TO_RESP_RX_DLY_UUS, &amp;config_options);\n\n        /* Activate reception a set time period after the TX timestamp for the POLL message. */\n        dwt_rxenable(DWT_START_RX_DLY_TS);\n\n        /* We assume that the transmission is achieved correctly, poll for reception of a frame or error/timeout.         "contents": "extern dwt_txconfig_t txconfig_options;\n\n/*! ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n * @fn ds_twr_sts_sdc_initiator()\n *\n * @brief Application entry point.\n *\n * @param  none\n *\n * @return none\n */\nint ds_twr_sts_sdc_initiator(void)\n{\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. See NOTE 15 below. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure the TX spectrum parameters (power, PG delay and PG count) */\n    dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options);\n\n    /* Apply default antenna delay value. See NOTE 1 below. */\n    dwt_setrxantennadelay(RX_ANT_DLY);\n    dwt_settxantennadelay(TX_ANT_DLY);\n\n    /* Set expected response's delay and timeout. See NOTE 4, 5 and 6 below.\n     * As this example only handles one incoming frame with always the same delay and timeout, those values can be set here once for all. */\n    dwt_setrxaftertxdelay(POLL_TX_TO_RESP_RX_DLY_UUS);\n    dwt_setrxtimeout(RESP_RX_TIMEOUT_UUS);\n    dwt_setpreambledetecttimeout(PRE_TIMEOUT);\n\n    /* Next can enable TX/RX states output on GPIOs 5 and 6 to help debug */",

        "contents": "/* Hold copy of status register state here for reference so that it can be examined at a debug breakpoint. */\nstatic uint32_t status_reg;\n\n/* Hold copy of frame length of frame received (if good) so that it can be examined at a debug breakpoint. */\nstatic uint16_t frame_len;\n\n/**\n * Application entry point.\n */\nint simple_rx_sts_sdc(void)\n{\n    int goodSts = 0;    /* Used for checking STS quality in received signal */\n    int16_t stsQual;    /* This will contain STS quality index */\n    uint16_t stsStatus; /* Used to check for good STS status (no errors). */\n\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enabling LEDs here for debug so that for each RX-enable the D2 LED will flash on DW3000 red eval-shield boards. */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Loop forever receiving frames. */\n    while (TRUE)\n    {\n        /* TESTING BREAKPOINT LOCATION #1 */",

        "contents": "int rx_diagnostics(void)\n{\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC, or could wait for SPIRDY event)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED\");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Activate event counters. */\n    dwt_configeventcounters(1);\n\n    /* Enable IC diagnostic calculation and logging */\n    dwt_configciadiag(1);\n\n    /* Loop forever receiving frames. */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        int i;\n\n        /* TESTING BREAKPOINT LOCATION #1 */",

        "contents": "int rx_sniff(void)\n{\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC, or could wait for SPIRDY event)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* This is put here for testing, so that we can see the receiver ON/OFF pattern using an oscilloscope. */\n    dwt_setlnapamode(DWT_LNA_ENABLE | DWT_PA_ENABLE);\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure SNIFF mode. */\n    dwt_setsniffmode(1, SNIFF_ON_TIME, SNIFF_OFF_TIME);\n\n    /* Loop forever receiving frames. */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        int i = 0;\n\n        /* TESTING BREAKPOINT LOCATION #1 */",

        "contents": "    if (config_options.chan == 5)\n    {\n        dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options);\n    }\n    else\n    {\n        dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options_ch9);\n    }\n\n    /* Apply default antenna delay value. See NOTE 2 below. */\n    dwt_setrxantennadelay(RX_ANT_DLY);\n    dwt_settxantennadelay(TX_ANT_DLY);\n\n    /* Next can enable TX/RX states output on GPIOs 5 and 6 to help diagnostics, and also TX/RX LEDs */\n    dwt_setlnapamode(DWT_LNA_ENABLE | DWT_PA_ENABLE);\n\n    /* Loop forever responding to ranging requests. */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        /*\n         * Set STS encryption key and IV (nonce).\n         * See NOTE 15 below.\n         */\n        if (!firstLoopFlag)\n        {\n            /*\n             * On first loop, configure the STS key &amp; IV, then load them.\n             */\n            dwt_configurestskey(&amp;cp_key);\n            dwt_configurestsiv(&amp;cp_iv);\n            dwt_configurestsloadiv();\n            firstLoopFlag = 1;\n        }\n        else\n        {\n            /*\n             * On subsequent loops, we only need to reload the lower 32 bits of STS IV.\n             */\n            dwt_configurestsiv(&amp;cp_iv);\n            dwt_configurestsloadiv();\n        }\n\n        /* Activate reception immediately. */\n        dwt_rxenable(DWT_START_RX_IMMEDIATE);\n\n        /* Poll for reception of a frame or error/timeout. See NOTE 6 below. */\n        waitforsysstatus(&amp;status_reg, NULL, (DWT_INT_RXFCG_BIT_MASK | SYS_STATUS_ALL_RX_TO | SYS_STATUS_ALL_RX_ERR), 0);\n\n        /*\n         * Need to check the STS has been received and is good.\n         */\n        goodSts = dwt_readstsquality(&amp;stsQual);\n\n        /*\n         * Check for a good frame with good STS count.\n         */\n        if ((status_reg &amp; DWT_INT_RXFCG_BIT_MASK) &amp;&amp; (goodSts &gt;= 0) &amp;&amp; (dwt_readstsstatus(&amp;stsStatus, 0) == DWT_SUCCESS))\n        {\n            uint16_t frame_len;",

        "contents": "int ack_data_tx(void)\n{\n    /* Hold copy of frame length of frame received (if good) so that it can be examined at a debug breakpoint. */\n    uint16_t frame_len = 0, tx_frame_len;\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    tx_frame_len = sizeof(tx_msg) + FCS_LEN;\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_IDLE) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED\");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. See NOTE 11 below. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure the TX spectrum parameters (power, PG delay and PG count) */\n    dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options);\n\n    /* Set delay to turn reception on immediately after transmission of the frame. See NOTE 6 below. */\n    dwt_setrxaftertxdelay(50);\n\n    /* Set RX frame timeout for the response. */\n    dwt_setrxtimeout(RX_RESP_TO_UUS);\n    /* can enable TX/RX states output on GPIOs 5 and 6 to help debug */\n    dwt_setlnapamode(DWT_LNA_ENABLE | DWT_PA_ENABLE);\n\n    /* Loop forever transmitting data. */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        /* Write frame data to DW IC and prepare transmission. See NOTE 7 below.*/",

        "contents": "extern dwt_txconfig_t txconfig_options;\n\n/*! ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n * @fn ds_twr_responder()\n *\n * @brief Application entry point.\n *\n * @param  none\n *\n * @return none\n */\nint ds_twr_responder(void)\n{\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. See NOTE 15 below. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure the TX spectrum parameters (power, PG delay and PG count) */\n    dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options);\n\n    /* Apply default antenna delay value. See NOTE 1 below. */\n    dwt_setrxantennadelay(RX_ANT_DLY);\n    dwt_settxantennadelay(TX_ANT_DLY);\n\n    /* Next can enable TX/RX states output on GPIOs 5 and 6 to help debug, and also TX/RX LEDs\n     * Note, in real low power applications the LEDs should not be used. */\n    dwt_setlnapamode(DWT_LNA_ENABLE | DWT_PA_ENABLE);\n\n    /* Loop forever responding to ranging requests. */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        dwt_setpreambledetecttimeout(0);",

        "contents": "int tx_wait_resp(void)\n{\n    /* Hold copy of status register state here for reference so that it can be examined at a debug breakpoint. */\n    uint32_t status_reg = 0;\n    /* Hold copy of frame length of frame received (if good) so that it can be examined at a debug breakpoint. */\n    uint16_t frame_len = 0;\n\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC, or could wait for SPIRDY event)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Optionally Configure GPIOs to show TX/RX activity. See NOTE 10 below. */\n    /* Optionally enabling LEDs here for debug so that for each TX the D1 LED will flash on DW3000 red eval-shield boards. See Note 10 below.*/\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. See NOTE 2 below. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure the TX spectrum parameters (power, PG delay and PG count) */\n    dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options);\n\n    /* Set delay to turn reception on after transmission of the frame. See NOTE 3 below. */\n    dwt_setrxaftertxdelay(TX_TO_RX_DELAY_UUS);\n\n    /* Set response frame timeout. */\n    dwt_setrxtimeout(RX_RESP_TO_UUS);\n\n    /* Loop forever sending and receiving frames periodically. */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        /* Write frame data to DW3000 and prepare transmission. See NOTE 7 below. */",

        "contents": "            if (rx_diag.ipatovPower &gt; 0)\n            {\n                // Simplified RSSI calculation (needs calibration for accurate values)\n                // Using power value as an indicator\n                rssi_dbm = (int32_t)(rx_diag.ipatovPower &gt;&gt; 16);  // Simplified extraction\n            }\n            \n            // Preamble quality is represented by accumulator count\n            // Higher accumulator count indicates better preamble quality\n            uint16_t pre_q = rx_diag.ipatovAccumCount;\n            \n            // For SNR, we'll use a simplified calculation based on preamble quality\n            // In practice, SNR calculation is more complex and may require diagnostics\n            int32_t snr_est = (int32_t)pre_q;  // Simplified: use preamble quality as SNR estimate\n            \n            g_stats.rssi_sum += rssi_dbm;\n            g_stats.snr_sum += snr_est;\n            g_stats.pre_q_sum += pre_q;\n            g_stats.metric_count++;\n        }\n        \n        // Re-enable RX if test is running\n        if (g_test_running)\n        {\n            dwt_rxenable(DWT_START_RX_IMMEDIATE);\n        }\n    }\n    else\n    {\n        // RX error\n        g_stats.crc_err++;\n        dwt_writesysstatuslo(SYS_STATUS_ALL_RX_ERR);\n        \n        // Re-enable RX if test is running\n        if (g_test_running)\n        {\n            dwt_rxenable(DWT_START_RX_IMMEDIATE);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/**\n * Application entry point\n */\nint orchestrator_rx(void)\n{\n    uint32_t dev_id;\n\n    /* Display application name */",

            "line": 143,
            "column": 48

        },
        "contents": "    while (1)\n    {\n        int i;\n\n        /* TESTING BREAKPOINT LOCATION #1 */\n\n        /* Clear local RX buffer, rx_diag structure and accumulator values to avoid having leftovers from previous receptions  This is not necessary\n         * but is included here to aid reading the data for each new frame.\n         * This is a good place to put a breakpoint. Here (after first time through the loop) the local status register will be set for last event\n         * and if a good receive has happened the data buffer will have the data in it, and frame_len will be set to the length of the RX frame. All\n         * diagnostics data will also be available. */\n        for (i = 0; i &lt; FRAME_LEN_MAX; i++)\n        {\n            rx_buffer[i] = 0;\n        }\n        for (i = 0; i &lt; ACCUM_DATA_LEN; i++)\n        {\n            accum_data[i] = 0;\n        }\n\n        memset(&amp;rx_diag, 0, sizeof(rx_diag));\n\n        /* Activate reception immediately. See NOTE 4 below. */\n        dwt_rxenable(DWT_START_RX_IMMEDIATE);\n\n        /* Poll until a frame is properly received or an error/timeout occurs. See NOTE 5 below.\n         * STATUS register is 5 bytes long but, as the event we are looking at is in the first byte of the register, we can use this simplest API\n         * function to access it. */\n        waitforsysstatus(&amp;status_reg, NULL, (DWT_INT_RXFCG_BIT_MASK | SYS_STATUS_ALL_RX_ERR), 0);\n\n        if (status_reg &amp; DWT_INT_RXFCG_BIT_MASK)",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [

Found critical bugs in the orchestrator code. Summary:

## Critical bugs found

### RX code (`orchestrator_rx.c`)

1. RX never enabled initially (line 512)
   - After `configure_uwb()`, RX should be enabled before entering the main loop
   - Currently RX is only enabled when `STRT` command is received (line 320)

2. Blocking wait prevents UART processing (line 389)
   - `waitforsysstatus()` blocks indefinitely waiting for a packet
   - While blocked, UART commands cannot be processed
   - This breaks the command interface

3. Redundant RX enable at start of `process_rx_packet()` (line 386)
   - Calls `dwt_rxenable()` at the beginning
   - Should only re-enable RX after processing a packet

4. RX re-enable logic issue (lines 459, 471)
   - Re-enables RX even if test is not running
   - Should check `g_test_running` before re-enabling

### TX code (`orchestrator_tx.c`)

5. Timer start without initialization check (line 325)
   - Starts timer without verifying `g_timer_initialized`
   - Could cause crashes if timer init failed

## Comparison with working examples

Working `simple_rx.c`:
- Enables RX once before the main loop
- Uses blocking `waitforsysstatus()` in a simple loop (no UART commands)

Your orchestrator RX:
- Needs non-blocking operation to handle UART commands
- Should use interrupt-based or polled status checks instead of blocking waits

## Fixes needed

1. Enable RX initially after configuration
2. Make RX non-blocking (check status without blocking wait)
3. Remove redundant RX enable at start of `process_rx_packet()`
4. Add timer initialization check before starting TX timer
5. Fix RX re-enable logic to respect `g_test_running` flag

Should I provide the corrected code with these fixes?
