        "contents": "    while (1)\n    {\n        /* Activate reception immediately. See NOTE 5 below. */\n        dwt_rxenable(DWT_START_RX_IMMEDIATE);\n\n        /* Poll until a frame is properly received or an RX error occurs. See NOTE 6 below.\n         * STATUS register is 5 bytes long but we are not interested in the high byte here, so we read a more manageable 32-bits with this API call. */\n        waitforsysstatus(&amp;status_reg, NULL, (DWT_INT_RXFCG_BIT_MASK | SYS_STATUS_ALL_RX_ERR), 0);\n\n        if (status_reg &amp; DWT_INT_RXFCG_BIT_MASK)\n        {\n            /* Clear good RX frame event in the DW IC status register. */\n            dwt_writesysstatuslo(DWT_INT_RXFCG_BIT_MASK);\n\n            /* A frame has been received, read it into the local buffer. */\n            frame_len = dwt_getframelength();\n            if (frame_len &lt;= FRAME_LEN_MAX)\n            {\n                dwt_readrxdata(rx_buffer, frame_len, 0);\n            }\n\n            /* Since the auto ACK feature is enabled, an ACK should be sent if the received frame requests it, so we await the ACK TX completion\n             * before taking next action. See NOTE 8 below. */\n            if (rx_buffer[0] &amp; FCTRL_ACK_REQ_MASK)\n            {\n                /* Poll DW IC until confirmation of transmission of the ACK frame. */\n                waitforsysstatus(&amp;status_reg, NULL, DWT_INT_TXFRS_BIT_MASK, 0);\n\n                /* Clear TXFRS event. */\n                dwt_writesysstatuslo(DWT_INT_TXFRS_BIT_MASK);\n            }\n        }\n        else\n        {\n            /* Clear RX error events in the DW IC status register. */\n            dwt_writesysstatuslo(SYS_STATUS_ALL_RX_ERR);\n        }\n    }\n}\n#endif\n/*****************************************************************************************************************************************************\n * NOTES:\n *\n * 1. PAN ID and short address are hard coded constants to keep the example simple but for a real product every device should have a unique ID.\n *    For development purposes it is possible to generate a DW IC unique ID by combining the Lot ID &amp; Part Number values programmed into the DW IC\n *    during its manufacture. However there is no guarantee this will not conflict with someone else’s implementation. We recommended that customers\n *    buy a block of addresses from the IEEE Registration Authority for their production items.\n * 2. In this example, maximum frame length is set to 127 bytes which is 802.15.4z UWB standard maximum frame length. DW IC supports an extended frame\n *    length (up to 1023 bytes long) mode which is not used in this example.\n * 3. In this example, the DW IC is put into IDLE state after calling dwt_initialise(). This means that a fast SPI rate of up to 20 MHz can be used\n *     thereafter.\n * 4. In a real application, for optimum performance within regulatory limits, it may be necessary to set TX pulse bandwidth and TX power, (using\n *    the dwt_configuretxrf API call) to per device calibrated values saved in the target system or the DW IC OTP memory.\n * 5. Manual reception activation is performed here but DW IC offers several features that can be used to handle more complex scenarios or to\n *    optimise system's overall performance (e.g. timeout after a given time, automatic re-enabling of reception in case of errors, etc.).\n * 6. We use polled mode of operation here to keep the example as simple as possible but all status events can be used to generate interrupts. Please\n *    refer to DW IC User Manual for more details on \"interrupts\".\n * 7. This is the purpose of the AAT bit in DW IC's STATUS register but because of an issue with the operation of AAT, it is simpler to directly\n *    check in the frame control if the ACK request bit is set. Please refer to DW IC User Manual for more details on Auto ACK feature and the AAT\n *    bit.\n * 8. The user is referred to DecaRanging ARM application (distributed with EVK1000 product) for additional practical example of usage, and to the\n *    DW IC API Guide for more details on the DW IC driver functions.\n * 9. Desired configuration by user may be different to the current programmed configuration. dwt_configure is called to set desired\n *    configuration.\n ****************************************************************************************************************************************************/",

### Pin configuration — correct

- `TX_PIN_NUMBER = 19` → `UART_0_TX_PIN = 19`
- `DW3000_RTS_PIN_NUM = UART_PIN_DISCONNECTED` (0xFFFFFFFF)
- `DW3000_CTS_PIN_NUM = UART_PIN_DISCONNECTED` (0xFFFFFFFF)

**Orchestrator code:**
- Uses `UART_0_RX_PIN`, `UART_0_TX_PIN`, `DW3000_RTS_PIN_NUM`, `DW3000_CTS_PIN_NUM`
- Matches `custom_board.h` definitions

### Status register constants — correct

- Uses `DWT_INT_RXFCG_BIT_MASK` (matches working examples)
- Uses `SYS_STATUS_ALL_RX_ERR` (matches working examples)
- Uses `DWT_INT_TXFRS_BIT_MASK` (matches working examples)

### Error clearing — correct

- Clears `DWT_INT_RXFCG_BIT_MASK` after good RX (line 403)
- Clears `SYS_STATUS_ALL_RX_ERR` after RX errors (line 471)
- Matches pattern from `simple_rx.c`

### Minor note

**Comment inconsistency in `custom_board.h` (lines 125-126):**
- Comment says "DWM1001 module pin 20, DEV board name RXD" for `UART_0_TX_PIN`
- Comment says "DWM1001 module pin 18, DEV board name TXD" for `UART_0_RX_PIN`
- Comments appear swapped, but pin numbers (15, 19) are correct

## Summary

- Pin definitions match
- Status constants match working examples
- Error handling matches working examples
- UART initialization uses correct pins
- Code structure follows SDK patterns

The code should work correctly. The only issue found was a comment inconsistency in `custom_board.h`, which doesn't affect functionality.

The fixes I made earlier (non-blocking RX, initial RX enable, timer check) are correct and align with the SDK patterns.

        "contents": "## LED Behavior\n\nThe firmware uses &#96;dwt_setleds()&#96; which controls the **DW3000 UWB chip's internal LEDs**, not the board LEDs.\n\n- **On startup**: LEDs will blink once during initialization\n- **During operation**: LEDs may flash during UWB activity (TX/RX events)\n- **Board LEDs**: The DWM3001CDK board LEDs (LED_1, LED_2, LED_3, LED_4) are not directly controlled by this firmware\n\n## RS-485 Connection\n\nConnect the RS-485 transceiver to:\n- **A+**: Connect to RS-485 A+ line\n- **B-**: Connect to RS-485 B- line  \n- **GND**: Connect to ground\n- **UART RX**: Connect to GPIO 15\n- **UART TX**: Connect to GPIO 19\n- **DE/RE**: Connect to control RS-485 direction (if needed)\n\nThe firmware communicates at **115200 baud** with the Orchestrator.\n\n## Testing\n\nAfter flashing:\n\n1. **Connect RS-485** from each board to the Orchestrator (RPi 5)\n2. **Power on** both boards\n3. **Run the Orchestrator**:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   cd Orchestrator\n   npm start\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe Orchestrator will:\n- Send &#96;PNG&#96; (PING) commands to verify connectivity\n- Configure both nodes with &#96;CFG&#96; commands\n- Start tests with &#96;STRT&#96; commands\n- Collect statistics with &#96;STAT&#96; commands\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n### UART Not Working\n- Verify pins 15 (RX) and 19 (TX) are connected correctly\n- Check RS-485 transceiver wiring (A+, B-, GND)\n- Verify baud rate is 115200\n- Check that RS-485 termination resistors are present (120Ω at each end)\n\n### Wrong Variant Flashed\n- Make sure you build and flash separately for each board\n- Check &#96;example_selection.h&#96; has the correct &#96;#define&#96; uncommented\n- Check &#96;main.c&#96; has the correct function call uncommented\n\n### LEDs Not Flashing\n- The firmware controls DW3000 internal LEDs, not board LEDs\n- Board LEDs may not flash unless you add code to control them\n- Check UWB activity with the Orchestrator's statistics",

        "contents": "static void uart_event_handler(app_uart_evt_t *p_event)\n{\n    static uint8_t rx_buffer[UART_BUFFER_SIZE];\n    static uint16_t rx_index = 0;\n\n    switch (p_event-&gt;evt_type)\n    {\n        case APP_UART_DATA_READY:\n        {\n            uint32_t err_code;\n            uint8_t byte;\n            err_code = app_uart_get(&amp;byte);\n            if (err_code == NRF_SUCCESS)\n            {\n                if (byte == '\\r' || byte == '\\n')\n                {\n                    if (rx_index &gt; 0)\n                    {\n                        rx_buffer[rx_index] = '\\0';\n                        parse_command((char *)rx_buffer);\n                        rx_index = 0;\n                    }\n                }\n                else if (rx_index &lt; (UART_BUFFER_SIZE - 1))\n                {\n                    rx_buffer[rx_index++] = byte;\n                }\n                else\n                {\n                    rx_index = 0; // Buffer overflow, reset\n                }\n            }\n            break;\n        }\n        case APP_UART_COMMUNICATION_ERROR:\n        case APP_UART_FIFO_ERROR:\n            break;\n        default:\n            break;\n    }\n}\n\n/**\n * Initialize UART for RS-485 communication\n */\nstatic void uart_init(void)\n{\n    uint32_t err_code;\n    uint32_t *p_err_code = &amp;err_code;\n    app_uart_comm_params_t comm_params =\n    {\n        .rx_pin_no = UART_0_RX_PIN,\n        .tx_pin_no = UART_0_TX_PIN,\n        .rts_pin_no = DW3000_RTS_PIN_NUM,\n        .cts_pin_no = DW3000_CTS_PIN_NUM,\n        .flow_control = APP_UART_FLOW_CONTROL_DISABLED,\n        .use_parity = false,\n        .baud_rate = 30801920  // 115200 baud\n    };\n\n    APP_UART_FIFO_INIT(&amp;comm_params,\n                       UART_RX_BUFFER_SIZE,\n                       UART_TX_BUFFER_SIZE,\n                       uart_event_handler,\n                       APP_IRQ_PRIORITY_LOW,\n                       p_err_code);\n    \n    if (err_code != NRF_SUCCESS)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"UART INIT FAILED\");\n    }\n}\n\n/**\n * Send response over UART\n */\nstatic void",

        "contents": "# Orchestrator Example - Build and Flash Guide\n\n## Overview\n\nThis example provides two firmware variants:\n- **TX Variant (Node A)**: Transmits UWB packets periodically\n- **RX Variant (Node B)**: Receives UWB packets and collects statistics\n\nBoth variants communicate with the Orchestrator via RS-485 using UART.\n\n## Pin Configuration\n\n### UART Pins (RS-485 Communication)\n- **RX Pin**: GPIO 15 (UART_0_RX_PIN)\n- **TX Pin**: GPIO 19 (UART_0_TX_PIN)\n- **Baud Rate**: 115200\n\n**Note**: Pins 8 and 10 are used for:\n- **Pin 8**: DW3000_IRQ_Pin (interrupt pin for UWB chip)\n- **Pin 10**: DW3000_CS_Pin (SPI chip select for UWB chip)\n\nThe UART for RS-485 communication uses **pins 15 (RX) and 19 (TX)**, not pins 8 and 10.\n\n## Building and Flashing\n\n### Step 1: Build TX Variant (Node A)\n\n1. Edit &#96;Src/example_selection.h&#96;:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;c\n   // Comment out other examples:\n   //#define TEST_READING_DEV_ID\n   \n   // Uncomment TX variant:\n   #define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_TX\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n2. Edit &#96;Src/main.c&#96;:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;c\n   // Comment out other examples:\n   // extern int read_dev_id(void); read_dev_id();\n   \n   // Uncomment TX variant:\n   extern int orchestrator_tx(void); orchestrator_tx();\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n3. Build:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   make build\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n4. Flash to Node A board:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   make flash\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 2: Build RX Variant (Node B)\n\n1. Edit &#96;Src/example_selection.h&#96;:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;c\n   // Comment out TX variant:\n   //#define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_TX\n   \n   // Uncomment RX variant:\n   #define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_RX\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n2. Edit &#96;Src/main.c&#96;:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;c\n   // Comment out TX variant:\n   // extern int orchestrator_tx(void); orchestrator_tx();\n   \n   // Uncomment RX variant:\n   extern int orchestrator_rx(void); orchestrator_rx();\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n3. Build:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   make build\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n4. Flash to Node B board:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   make flash\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Important**: You need to build and flash **separately** for each board. The firmware is compiled with either TX or RX code, not both.\n\n## LED Behavior\n\nThe firmware uses &#96;dwt_setleds()&#96; which controls the **DW3000 UWB chip's internal LEDs**, not the board LEDs.\n\n- **On startup**: LEDs will blink once during initialization",

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 57
          },
          {
            "text": "1. Edit &#96;Src/example_selection.h&#96;:",
            "lineNumber": 58
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;c",
            "lineNumber": 59
          },
          {
            "text": "   // Comment out TX variant:",
            "lineNumber": 60
          },
          {
            "text": "   //#define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_TX",
            "lineNumber": 61
          },
          {
            "text": "   ",
            "lineNumber": 62
          },
          {
            "text": "   // Uncomment RX variant:",
            "lineNumber": 63
          },
          {
            "text": "   #define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_RX",
            "lineNumber": 64
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 65
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 66
          },
          {
            "text": "2. Edit &#96;Src/main.c&#96;:",
            "lineNumber": 67
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;c",
            "lineNumber": 68
          },
          {
            "text": "   // Comment out TX variant:",
            "lineNumber": 69
          },
          {
            "text": "   // extern int orchestrator_tx(void); orchestrator_tx();",
            "lineNumber": 70
          },
          {
            "text": "   ",
            "lineNumber": 71
          },
          {
            "text": "   // Uncomment RX variant:",
            "lineNumber": 72
          },
          {
            "text": "   extern int orchestrator_rx(void); orchestrator_rx();",
            "lineNumber": 73
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 74
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 75
          },
          {
            "text": "3. Build:",
            "lineNumber": 76
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash",
            "lineNumber": 77
          },
          {
            "text": "   make build",
            "lineNumber": 78
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 79
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 80
          },
          {
            "text": "4. Flash to Node B board:",
            "lineNumber": 81
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash",
            "lineNumber": 82
          },
          {
            "text": "   make flash",
            "lineNumber": 83
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 84
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 85
          },
          {
            "text": "**Important**: You need to build and flash **separately** for each board. The firmware is compiled with either TX or RX code, not both.",
            "lineNumber": 86
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 87
          },
          {
            "text": "## LED Behavior",
            "lineNumber": 88
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 89
          },
          {
            "text": "The firmware uses &#96;dwt_setleds()&#96; which controls the **DW3000 UWB chip's internal LEDs**, not the board LEDs.",
            "lineNumber": 90
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 91
          },
          {
            "text": "- **On startup**: LEDs will blink once during initialization",
            "lineNumber": 92
          }
        ]
      },
      "score": 0.4578516483306885
    },

        "contents": "int orchestrator_rx(void)\n{\n    uint32_t dev_id;\n\n    /* Display application name */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Initialize UART for RS-485 */\n    uart_init();\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC();\n    Sleep(2);\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n    dev_id = dwt_readdevid();\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED\");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enable LEDs */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure with default settings */\n    configure_uwb();\n\n    /* Enable RX initially (will be controlled by START/STOP commands) */\n    dwt_rxenable(DWT_START_RX_IMMEDIATE);\n\n    /* Main loop - process UART commands and RX packets */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        if (g_test_running)\n        {\n            process_rx_packet();\n        }\n        else\n        {\n            Sleep(100);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#endif",

        "contents": "/**\n * Application entry point\n */\nint orchestrator_tx(void)\n{\n    uint32_t dev_id;\n\n    /* Display application name */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Initialize UART for RS-485 */\n    uart_init();\n\n    /* Initialize app timer module */\n    uint32_t err_code = app_timer_init();\n    if (err_code != NRF_SUCCESS)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"TIMER INIT FAILED\");\n    }\n    else\n    {\n        /* Create timer instance */\n        err_code = app_timer_create(&amp;m_tx_timer_id, APP_TIMER_MODE_REPEATED, tx_timer_handler);\n        if (err_code == NRF_SUCCESS)\n        {\n            g_timer_initialized = 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC();\n    Sleep(2);\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n    dev_id = dwt_readdevid();\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED\");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enable LEDs */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure with default settings */\n    configure_uwb();\n\n    /* Main loop - process UART commands */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        // Command processing happens in UART interrupt handler\n        Sleep(100);\n    }\n}\n\n#endif",

         // UWB channel: 5 or 9\n    uint8_t data_rate;        // 0 = 850kbps, 1 = 6.8Mbps\n    uint16_t preamble_len;    // e.g., 64, 128, 256\n    uint8_t preamble_code;    // TX/RX preamble code\n    uint8_t tx_power_idx;     // TX power index\n    uint32_t pkt_rate_hz;     // TX packets per second\n    uint16_t payload_len;     // Payload size in bytes\n    uint8_t configured;       // Configuration flag\n} uwb_config_t;\n\n/* Test packet structure */\ntypedef struct {\n    uint32_t seq;         "contents": "/**\n * Configure UWB radio\n */\nstatic void configure_uwb(void)\n{\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;dwt_config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED\");\n        return;\n    }\n}\n\n/**\n * Process received packet (non-blocking)\n */\nstatic void process_rx_packet(void)\n{\n    uint32_t status_reg;\n    uint16_t frame_len;\n    uwb_test_packet_t *rx_packet;\n\n    // Check status register non-blocking\n    status_reg = dwt_readsysstatuslo();\n    \n    // Check if we have a good RX frame or error\n    if (!(status_reg &amp; (DWT_INT_RXFCG_BIT_MASK | SYS_STATUS_ALL_RX_ERR)))\n    {\n        // No event yet, return without blocking\n        return;\n    }\n\n    if (status_reg &amp; DWT_INT_RXFCG_BIT_MASK)\n    {\n        // Good frame received\n        frame_len = dwt_getframelength();\n        if (frame_len &lt;= FRAME_LEN_MAX)\n        {\n            dwt_readrxdata(g_rx_buffer, frame_len - FCS_LEN, 0);\n            dwt_writesysstatuslo(DWT_INT_RXFCG_BIT_MASK);\n            \n            rx_packet = (uwb_test_packet_t *)g_rx_buffer;\n            \n            // Update statistics\n            g_stats.total_rx++;\n            \n            // Check sequence number\n            if (!g_stats.seq_init)\n            {\n                g_stats.last_seq = rx_packet-&gt;seq;\n                g_stats.seq_init = 1;\n            }\n            else\n            {\n                uint32_t expected_seq = g_stats.last_seq + 1;\n                if (rx_packet-&gt;seq != expected_seq)\n                {\n                    if (rx_packet-&gt;seq &gt; expected_seq)\n                    {\n                        g_stats.lost_pkts += (rx_packet-&gt;seq - expected_seq);\n                    }\n                }\n                g_stats.last_seq = rx_packet-&gt;seq;\n            }\n            \n            // Read RF metrics using diagnostics\n            dwt_rxdiag_t rx_diag;\n            dwt_readdiagnostics(&amp;rx_diag);\n            \n            // Extract RSSI from diagnostics\n            // RSSI can be calculated from the channel power (ipatovPower)\n            // For simplicity, we'll use a simplified RSSI calculation\n            // RSSI ≈ 10*log10(power) - A, where A is a calibration constant",

        "contents": "/**\n * Configure UWB radio\n */\nstatic void configure_uwb(void)\n{\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;dwt_config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED\");\n        return;\n    }\n\n    // Configure TX power (simplified - use default txconfig_options)\n    extern dwt_txconfig_t txconfig_options;\n    dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options);\n}\n\n/**\n * TX timer handler - called periodically to send packets\n */\nstatic void tx_timer_handler(void *p_context)\n{\n    if (g_test_running)\n    {\n        send_packet();\n    }\n}\n\n/**\n * Send a test packet\n */\nstatic void send_packet(void)\n{\n    uint32_t status_reg;\n\n    // Prepare packet\n    g_tx_packet.seq = g_seq_num++;\n    g_tx_packet.t_local = dwt_readsystimestamphi32();\n    \n    // Fill payload with pattern\n    for (int i = 0; i &lt; g_config.payload_len &amp;&amp; i &lt; sizeof(g_tx_packet.payload); i++)\n    {\n        g_tx_packet.payload[i] = 0xAA;\n    }\n\n    // Copy to TX buffer\n    // Calculate frame length: header (seq + t_local) + actual payload length\n    uint16_t frame_len = sizeof(uint32_t) + sizeof(uint32_t) + g_config.payload_len + FCS_LEN;\n    uint16_t data_len = sizeof(uint32_t) + sizeof(uint32_t) + g_config.payload_len;\n    memcpy(g_tx_buffer, &amp;g_tx_packet, data_len);\n\n    // Write TX data\n    dwt_writetxdata(data_len, g_tx_buffer, 0);\n    dwt_writetxfctrl(frame_len, 0, 0);\n\n    // Start transmission\n    dwt_starttx(DWT_START_TX_IMMEDIATE);\n\n    // Wait for TX complete\n    waitforsysstatus(&amp;status_reg, NULL, DWT_INT_TXFRS_BIT_MASK, 0);\n\n    if (status_reg &amp; DWT_INT_TXFRS_BIT_MASK)\n    {\n        dwt_writesysstatuslo(DWT_INT_TXFRS_BIT_MASK);\n        g_stats.total_sent++;\n        g_stats.last_error = 0;\n    }\n    else\n    {\n        g_stats.last_error = 1;\n    }\n}\n\n/**\n * Application entry point\n */\nint orchestrator_tx(void)\n{\n    uint32_t dev_id;\n\n    /* Display application name */",

        "contents": "/**\n * Parse command string\n */\nstatic void parse_command(char *cmd)\n{\n    // Convert to uppercase for comparison\n    char cmd_upper[64];\n    strncpy(cmd_upper, cmd, sizeof(cmd_upper) - 1);\n    cmd_upper[sizeof(cmd_upper) - 1] = '\\0';\n    \n    for (int i = 0; cmd_upper[i]; i++)\n    {\n        if (cmd_upper[i] &gt;= 'a' &amp;&amp; cmd_upper[i] &lt;= 'z')\n        {\n            cmd_upper[i] = cmd_upper[i] - 'a' + 'A';\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Handle commands (support both short and long forms)\n    if (strcmp(cmd_upper, \"PNG\") == 0 || strcmp(cmd_upper, \"PING\") == 0)\n    {\n        send_response(\"OK\");\n    }\n    else if (strncmp(cmd_upper, \"NODE_TYPE\", 9) == 0)\n    {\n        send_response(\"OK NODE_TYPE=TX\");\n    }\n    else if (strncmp(cmd_upper, \"CFG \", 4) == 0 || strncmp(cmd_upper, \"SET_CONFIG \", 11) == 0)\n    {\n        char *params = strchr(cmd, ' ');\n        if (params) params++; // Skip space\n        else params = \"\";\n        parse_set_config(params);\n    }\n    else if (strcmp(cmd_upper, \"STRT\") == 0 || strcmp(cmd_upper, \"START_TEST\") == 0)\n    {\n        if (!g_config.configured)\n        {",

        "contents": "            // For simplicity, we'll use a simplified RSSI calculation\n            // RSSI ≈ 10*log10(power) - A, where A is a calibration constant\n            // Using ipatovPower as a proxy for signal strength\n            // Note: This is a simplified calculation - actual RSSI requires calibration\n            int32_t rssi_dbm = 0;  // Default value\n            if (rx_diag.ipatovPower &gt; 0)\n            {\n                // Simplified RSSI calculation (needs calibration for accurate values)\n                // Using power value as an indicator\n                rssi_dbm = (int32_t)(rx_diag.ipatovPower &gt;&gt; 16);  // Simplified extraction\n            }\n            \n            // Preamble quality is represented by accumulator count\n            // Higher accumulator count indicates better preamble quality\n            uint16_t pre_q = rx_diag.ipatovAccumCount;\n            \n            // For SNR, we'll use a simplified calculation based on preamble quality\n            // In practice, SNR calculation is more complex and may require diagnostics\n            int32_t snr_est = (int32_t)pre_q;  // Simplified: use preamble quality as SNR estimate\n            \n            g_stats.rssi_sum += rssi_dbm;\n            g_stats.snr_sum += snr_est;\n            g_stats.pre_q_sum += pre_q;\n            g_stats.metric_count++;\n        }\n        \n        // Re-enable RX if test is running\n        if (g_test_running)\n        {\n            dwt_rxenable(DWT_START_RX_IMMEDIATE);\n        }\n    }\n    else\n    {\n        // RX error\n        g_stats.crc_err++;\n        dwt_writesysstatuslo(SYS_STATUS_ALL_RX_ERR);\n        \n        // Re-enable RX if test is running\n        if (g_test_running)\n        {\n            dwt_rxenable(DWT_START_RX_IMMEDIATE);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/**\n * Application entry point\n */\nint orchestrator_rx(void)\n{\n    uint32_t dev_id;\n\n    /* Display application name */",

## Explanation of `custom_board.h` Comments (Lines 125-126)

### Pin definitions

```c
#define RX_PIN_NUMBER  15   // GPIO 15
#define TX_PIN_NUMBER  19   // GPIO 19

#define UART_0_TX_PIN  TX_PIN_NUMBER  // GPIO 19 - "DWM1001 module pin 20, DEV board name RXD"
#define UART_0_RX_PIN  RX_PIN_NUMBER  // GPIO 15 - "DWM1001 module pin 18, DEV board name TXD"
```

### Why the comments seem reversed

The comments describe the connector labels from the external device’s perspective, not the DWM3001CDK’s.

- `UART_0_TX_PIN` (GPIO 19): DWM3001CDK transmits here → external device receives → connector labeled "RXD"
- `UART_0_RX_PIN` (GPIO 15): DWM3001CDK receives here → external device transmits → connector labeled "TXD"

### How the orchestrator uses them

**In `orchestrator_tx.c` and `orchestrator_rx.c` (lines 170-171):**
```c
.rx_pin_no = UART_0_RX_PIN,  // GPIO 15 - Receives commands FROM Orchestrator
.tx_pin_no = UART_0_TX_PIN,  // GPIO 19 - Sends responses TO Orchestrator
```

**Data flow:**
```
DWM3001CDK                    RS-485 Transceiver              Orchestrator (RPi)
─────────────────            ───────────────────            ────────────────
GPIO 19 (TX) ──────────────> RXD (receives) ──────────────> Receives responses
GPIO 15 (RX) <────────────── TXD (transmits) <────────────── Sends commands
```

### Summary

- The comments are correct: they reflect the connector labels from the external device’s perspective.
- The orchestrator code uses the pins correctly:
  - `UART_0_RX_PIN` (GPIO 15) receives commands
  - `UART_0_TX_PIN` (GPIO 19) sends responses
- The README (lines 14-15) correctly states GPIO 15 = RX, GPIO 19 = TX.

The comments clarify connector labeling, which helps with wiring. The code usage matches the pin definitions.

## What I can do

1. Add instrumentation/logging to capture runtime behavior
2. Analyze logs you collect from your hardware
3. Identify issues from runtime evidence
4. Fix bugs with confidence based on actual data

## What I cannot do

- Run firmware on physical hardware
- Test UWB communication directly
- Verify RS-485 connections
- See real-time behavior without logs

## How we can debug together

Since we're in Debug Mode, I can:

1. Add debug logging to critical functions (UART init, RX/TX processing, UWB operations)
2. You run the firmware on your hardware
3. Collect logs from the debug file
4. Analyze the logs to identify what's happening
5. Fix issues based on runtime evidence

## Next steps

If you want to debug systematically:

3. You run it and collect logs
4. I analyze the logs and fix the issues

- We debug based on your observations

Instrumentation updated. Created a test script. Summary:

## What I've done

1. Created `test-tx-rx.ps1` — builds, flashes both nodes, and runs the Orchestrator test
2. Updated Orchestrator instrumentation — all logs now use the correct endpoint
3. Existing logging — RS-485 communication is already logged

## Test script created

The script `test-tx-rx.ps1` will:
1. Build and flash TX node (Node A)
2. Build and flash RX node (Node B)
3. Wait for initialization
4. Start the Orchestrator test

## How to run the test

<reproduction_steps>
1. Ensure both DWM3001CDK boards are connected via RS-485 to your PC
2. Check serial ports in `Orchestrator/config/settings.yaml` (default: COM3 for Node A, COM4 for Node B)
3. Power on both boards
4. Run the test script: `.\test-tx-rx.ps1`
5. The script will build, flash both nodes, wait 5 seconds, then start the Orchestrator
6. Watch the console output for test results
7. After the test completes, check `.cursor\debug.log` for detailed debug logs
</reproduction_steps>

## What the logs will capture

- RS-485 communication (commands sent/received)
- Node state changes (IDLE → CONFIGURED → RUNNING)
- UWB packet statistics (TX count, RX count, errors)
- Connection status and errors

After you run the test, share the results and I'll analyze the logs to identify any issues.

Created automated build/flash/test scripts with iteration support.

## Created scripts

### 1. `auto-test-tx-rx.ps1` — Full automation
- Builds TX and RX firmware
- Flashes both boards (with prompts)
- Runs tests iteratively
- Captures debug logs
- Supports multiple iterations

### 2. `quick-test.ps1` — Quick test (skip build/flash)
- Assumes boards are already flashed
- Runs tests iteratively
- Faster for repeated testing

## Usage

### Full automation (first time):
```powershell
# Run 1 iteration (build, flash, test)
.\auto-test-tx-rx.ps1

# Run 3 iterations
.\auto-test-tx-rx.ps1 -Iterations 3

# Skip build (if firmware already built)
.\auto-test-tx-rx.ps1 -SkipBuild

# Skip flash (if boards already flashed)
.\auto-test-tx-rx.ps1 -SkipFlash

# Skip both (just run tests)
.\auto-test-tx-rx.ps1 -SkipBuild -SkipFlash
```

### Quick test (boards already flashed):
```powershell
# Run 1 quick test
.\quick-test.ps1

# Run 5 quick tests
.\quick-test.ps1 -Iterations 5
```

## What it does

1. Builds TX firmware → flashes TX board
2. Builds RX firmware → flashes RX board
3. Waits 5 seconds for initialization
4. Runs Orchestrator test (captures logs)
5. Repeats for specified iterations
6. Saves all logs to `.cursor\debug.log`

## Test workflow

<reproduction_steps>
1. Ensure both DWM3001CDK boards are powered off initially
2. Check serial ports in `Orchestrator/config/settings.yaml` (COM3 for Node A, COM4 for Node B)
3. Run: `.\auto-test-tx-rx.ps1 -Iterations 3`
4. When prompted, connect TX board (Node A) via USB and press any key
5. When prompted, connect RX board (Node B) via USB and press any key
6. Script will automatically build, flash, and run 3 test iterations
7. After completion, check `.cursor\debug.log` for detailed logs
8. For subsequent tests without rebuilding: `.\quick-test.ps1 -Iterations 5`
</reproduction_steps>

## Features

- Automated build/flash cycle
- Multiple iterations
- Debug log capture
- Error handling with clear messages
- Skip options for faster iteration
- Progress indicators

Run the script and share the results. I'll analyze the logs to identify any issues.

Updated the configuration to use COM20 and COM22.

## Updated configuration

**`Orchestrator/config/settings.yaml`:**
- Node A (TX): COM20
- Node B (RX): COM22

The test script now displays these ports at startup.

## Port assignment

- COM20 → Node A (TX) — transmits UWB packets
- COM22 → Node B (RX) — receives UWB packets

## Ready to test

You can now run:

```powershell
# Full automation (build, flash, test)
.\auto-test-tx-rx.ps1 -Iterations 3

# Quick test (if boards already flashed)
.\quick-test.ps1 -Iterations 5
```

The script will:
1. Use COM20 for Node A (TX)
2. Use COM22 for Node B (RX)
3. Display port configuration at startup
4. Capture debug logs to `.cursor\debug.log`

If you need to swap the ports (COM22 for TX, COM20 for RX), let me know and I'll update the configuration.

        "contents": "async start() {\n\n      try {\n        await this.nodeB.connect();\n        console.log(\"Node B connected\");\n\n        // Send PING first to verify basic communication\n        console.log(\"Pinging Node B...\");\n        try {\n          const pingResult = await this.nodeB.ping();\n          if (pingResult) {\n            console.log(\"✓ Node B PING successful\");\n          } else {\n            console.warn(\n              \"⚠️  Node B PING failed - firmware may not be responding\"\n            );\n          }\n        } catch (pingError) {\n          console.warn(&#96;⚠️  Node B PING error: ${pingError.message}&#96;);\n        }\n\n        // Verify Node B firmware type\n        const nodeBType = await this.nodeB.getFirmwareNodeType();\n        // #region agent log - server Node B type check\n        fetch(\n          \"http://127.0.0.1:7242/ingest/73b1b508-26e6-4c6a-a4a8-e78b93d01888\",\n          {\n            method: \"POST\",\n            headers: { \"Content-Type\": \"application/json\" },\n            body: JSON.stringify({\n              location: \"server.js:start\",\n              message: \"Node B firmware type check\",\n              data: { nodeBType, expected: \"B\", isNull: nodeBType === null },\n              timestamp: Date.now(),\n              sessionId: \"debug-session\",\n              runId: \"run1\",\n              hypothesisId: \"A\",\n            }),\n          }\n        ).catch(() =&gt; {});\n        // #endregion\n        if\n  }",

        "contents": "class WebServer {\n\n\n  /**\n   * Setup Socket.io\n   */\n  setupSocketIO() {\n    this.io.on(\"connection\", (socket) =&gt; {\n      console.log(\"Client connected:\", socket.id);\n\n      // Send initial status\n      socket.emit(\"status\", {\n        nodeA: {\n          state: this.nodeA.getState(),\n          connected: this.nodeA.isConnected(),\n        },\n        nodeB: {\n          state: this.nodeB.getState(),\n          connected: this.nodeB.isConnected(),\n        },\n        testRunning: this.testRunner.isRunning,\n      });\n\n      socket.on(\"disconnect\", () =&gt; {\n        console.log(\"Client disconnected:\", socket.id);\n      });\n    });\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Setup event listeners for real-time updates\n   */\n  setupEventListeners() {\n    // Node A events\n    this.nodeA.on\n\n  }",

        "contents": "class WebServer {\n\n\n  /**\n   * Setup event listeners for real-time updates\n   */\n  setupEventListeners() {\n    // Node A events\n    this.nodeA.on(\"stateChange\", (data) =&gt; {\n      this.io.emit(\"nodeStateChange\", { node: \"A\", ...data });\n    });\n\n    this.nodeA.on(\"statsUpdated\", (stats) =&gt; {\n      this.io.emit(\"stats\", { node: \"A\", stats });\n    });\n\n    // Node B events\n    this.nodeB.on(\"stateChange\", (data) =&gt; {\n      this.io.emit(\"nodeStateChange\", { node: \"B\", ...data });\n    });\n\n    this.nodeB.on(\"statsUpdated\", (stats) =&gt; {\n      this.io.emit(\"stats\", { node: \"B\", stats });\n    });\n\n    // Test runner events\n    this.testRunner.on(\"stats\", (data) =&gt; {\n      this.io.emit(\"stats\", data);\n    });\n\n    this.testRunner.on(\"testStarted\", (test) =&gt; {\n      this.io.emit(\"testStarted\", test);\n    });\n\n    this.testRunner.on(\"testStopped\", () =&gt; {\n      this.io.emit(\"testStopped\");\n    });\n\n    this.testRunner.on(\"error\", (error) =&gt; {\n      this.io.emit(\"error\", { message: error.message });\n    });\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Start server\n   */\n  async start() {\n    const webConfig = this.config.getWebConfig();\n  }",

        "contents": "import express from 'express';\n\n/**\n * API Routes\n * REST API endpoints for test orchestrator\n */\nexport function createApiRoutes(nodeA, nodeB, testRunner, csvLogger, config) {\n  const router = express.Router();\n\n  /**\n   * @swagger\n   * /api/status:\n   *   get:\n   *     summary: Get current test status\n   *     tags: [Status]\n   *     responses:\n   *       200:\n   *         description: Current test status\n   *         content:\n   *           application/json:\n   *             schema:\n   *               type: object\n   *               properties:\n   *                 nodeA:\n   *                   type: object\n   *                   properties:\n   *                     state: { type: string }\n   *                     connected: { type: boolean }\n   *                 nodeB:\n   *                   type: object\n   *                   properties:\n   *                     state: { type: string }\n   *                     connected: { type: boolean }\n   *                 testRunning: { type: boolean }\n   */\n  router.get('/status', (req, res) =&gt; {\n    res.json({\n      nodeA: {\n        state: nodeA.getState(),\n        connected: nodeA.isConnected(),\n        lastError: nodeA.getLastError(),\n      },\n      nodeB: {\n        state: nodeB.getState(),\n        connected: nodeB.isConnected(),\n        lastError: nodeB.getLastError(),\n      },\n      testRunning: testRunner.isRunning,\n    });\n  });\n\n  /**\n   * @swagger\n   * /api/stats:\n   *   get:\n   *     summary: Get latest stats from both nodes\n   *     tags: [Stats]\n   *     responses:\n   *       200:\n   *         description: Latest statistics\n   *         content:\n   *           application/json:\n   *             schema:\n   *               type: object\n   *               properties:\n   *                 nodeA: { type: object }\n   *                 nodeB: { type: object }\n   */\n  router.get('/stats', async (req, res) =&gt; {\n    try {\n      const statsA = nodeA.getStatsSync();\n      const statsB = nodeB.getStatsSync();\n\n      res.json({\n        nodeA: statsA || null,\n        nodeB: statsB || null,\n      });\n    } catch (error) {\n      res.status(500).json({ error: error.message });\n    }\n  });\n\n  /**\n   * @swagger\n   * /api/history:\n   *   get:\n   *     summary: Get historical CSV data\n   *     tags: [History]\n   *     parameters:\n   *       - in: query\n   *         name: page\n   *         schema: { type: integer, default: 1 }\n   *       - in: query\n   *         name: limit\n   *         schema: { type: integer, default: 100 }\n   *       - in: query\n   *         name: file\n   *         schema: { type: string }\n   *     responses:\n   *       200:\n   *         description: Historical data\n   */\n}",

        "contents": "// Start server if run directly\nconst isMainModule =\n  import.meta.url === &#96;file://${process.argv[1]}&#96; ||\n  import.meta.url.endsWith(process.argv[1].replace(/\\\\/g, \"/\"));\n\nif (isMainModule) {\n  const server = new WebServer();\n  server.start();\n\n  // Graceful shutdown\n  process.on(\"SIGTERM\", async () =&gt; {\n    console.log(\"SIGTERM received, shutting down gracefully...\");\n    await server.stop();\n    process.exit(0);\n  });\n\n  process.on(\"SIGINT\", async () =&gt; {\n    console.log(\"SIGINT received, shutting down gracefully...\");\n    await server.stop();\n    process.exit(0);\n  });\n}\n\nexport default WebServer;",

        "contents": "class WebServer {\n\n\n  /**\n   * Setup middleware\n   */\n  setupMiddleware() {\n    this.app.use(cors());\n    this.app.use(express.json());\n    this.app.use(express.urlencoded({ extended: true }));\n\n    // Serve static files from React build\n    const frontendBuild = path.join(__dirname, \"../../frontend/dist\");\n    this.app.use(express.static(frontendBuild));\n\n    // Serve CSV files\n    this.app.use(\n      \"/data/logs\",\n      express.static(path.join(__dirname, \"../../data/logs\"))\n    );\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Setup routes\n   */\n  setupRoutes() {\n    // Initialize nodes and test runner\n    const serialConfig = this.config.getSerialConfig();\n  }",

        "contents": "import swaggerUi from 'swagger-ui-express';\n\n/**\n * Swagger/OpenAPI Setup\n */\nexport function setupSwagger(app, config) {\n  const swaggerConfig = config.getSwaggerConfig();\n\n  if (!swaggerConfig.enabled) {\n    return;\n  }\n\n  const options = {\n    definition: {\n      openapi: '3.0.0',\n      info: {\n        title: 'UWB Test Orchestrator API',\n        version: '1.0.0',\n        description: 'REST API for UWB DWM3001C test rig orchestrator',\n      },\n      servers: [\n        {\n          url: &#96;http://localhost:${config.getWebConfig().port}&#96;,\n          description: 'Development server',\n        },\n      ],\n    },\n    apis: ['./src/web/routes/*.js', './src/web/server.js'],\n  };\n\n  const swaggerSpec = swaggerJsdoc(options);\n\n  app.use(swaggerConfig.path || '/api-docs', swaggerUi.serve);\n  app.get(swaggerConfig.path || '/api-docs', swaggerUi.setup(swaggerSpec, {\n    customCss: '.swagger-ui .topbar { display: none }',\n  }));\n\n  // JSON endpoint\n  app.get('/api-docs.json', (req, res) =&gt; {\n    res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json');\n    res.send(swaggerSpec);\n  });\n}",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [

            "text": "/**",

Synchronized the Orchestrator code with the starter-firmware. Summary of changes:

## Synchronization complete

### 1. Command/Response format — synchronized
- Firmware sends: `"OK"` for PNG, `"OK NODE_TYPE=TX"` or `"OK NODE_TYPE=RX"`
- Orchestrator expects: exactly the same format

### 2. Error messages updated
- Removed references to `west build` (wrong build system)
- Updated to use correct PowerShell scripts:
  - Node A (TX): `.\build-and-flash-tx.ps1`
  - Node B (RX): `.\build-and-flash-rx.ps1`
- Fixed expected values: "TX" and "RX" instead of "A" and "B"

### 3. Debug endpoint updated
- All instrumentation now uses the correct endpoint: `http://127.0.0.1:7246/ingest/53b9dbf8-c6bb-42df-aadd-00e84572bd7f`

### 4. COM ports configured
- Node A (TX): COM17
- Node B (RX): COM18

## Next steps

The code is synchronized. The PING failures suggest the boards aren't running the orchestrator firmware. Flash them:

```powershell
# Flash TX node (Node A)
.\build-and-flash-tx.ps1

# Flash RX node (Node B)  
.\build-and-flash-rx.ps1

# Or use the automated script
.\auto-test-tx-rx.ps1
```

After flashing, the Orchestrator should receive responses from both nodes. The commands and responses are now synchronized.

        "contents": "# run SEGGER Embedded Studio's build system and output the results to ./Output/Common/Exe\nbuild: development-environment\n\tdocker run -v \"$$(pwd)\":/project uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board /usr/local/segger_embedded_studio_V5.42a/bin/emBuild -config \"Common\" /project/dw3000_api.emProject\n\n# remove all build outputs from the project (you may want to run this if you run into issues with stale interfaces)\nclean: development-environment\n\tdocker run -v \"$$(pwd)\":/project uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board /usr/local/segger_embedded_studio_V5.42a/bin/emBuild -config \"Common\" -clean /project/dw3000_api.emProject\n\n# program the DWM3001CDK using nrfjprog, communicating via USB and the on-board SEGGER J-Link\n# TODO: this uses --privileged and exposes all development-environment\n\tdocker run --privileged  -v /dev/bus/usb/:/dev/bus/usb -v \"$$(pwd)/Output\":/project/Output:ro uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board nrfjprog --force -f nrf52 --program /project/Output/Common/Exe/dw3000_api.hex --sectorerase --verify\n\n# read the RTT debug output of the DWM3001CDK using SEGGER J-Link RTT Logger, communicating via USB and the on-board SEGGER         "contents": "# Flash script for DWM3001C firmware\n# Usage: .\\flash.ps1\n# Note: Requires Docker Desktop with WSL2 backend for USB device access\n\nWrite-Host \"Flashing DWM3001C firmware...\" -ForegroundColor Green\n\n# Get the project root directory\n$projectRoot = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path\n$projectPath = $projectRoot.Replace('\\', '/')\n\n# Check if hex file exists\n$hexFile = Join-Path $projectRoot \"Output\\Common\\Exe\\dw3000_api.hex\"\nif (-not (Test-Path $hexFile)) {\n    Write-Host \"Error: Firmware not found at $hexFile\" -ForegroundColor Red\n    Write-Host \"Please run .\\build.ps1 first to build the firmware.\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    exit 1\n}\n\n# Ensure Docker is running\n$dockerRunning = docker info 2&gt;&amp;1\nif ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n    Write-Host \"Error: Docker is not running. Please start Docker Desktop.\" -ForegroundColor Red\n    exit 1\n}\n\nWrite-Host \"Connecting to board via J-Link...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\nWrite-Host \"Make sure the board is connected via USB (J9 port) and powered on.\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n\n# Check if running in WSL2\n$isWSL = $env:WSL_DISTRO_NAME -ne $null\n\nif ($isWSL) {\n    # Running in WSL2 - can mount USB devices directly",

        "contents": "} else {\n    # Running in Windows PowerShell\n    # Docker Desktop on Windows doesn't support USB passthrough\n    Write-Host \"Windows PowerShell detected.\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n    Write-Host \"\"\n    \n    # Check if usbipd is available\n    $usbipdCheck = Get-Command usbipd -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue\n    if ($usbipdCheck) {\n        Write-Host \"usbipd-win detected. Checking USB devices...\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n        $usbDevices = usbipd wsl list 2&gt;&amp;1\n        Write-Host $usbDevices\n        \n        Write-Host \"\"\n        Write-Host \"To share J-Link device with WSL2:\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n        Write-Host \"  1. Find J-Link device: usbipd wsl list\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n        Write-Host \"  2. Share it: usbipd wsl attach --busid &lt;busid&gt;\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n        Write-Host \"  3. Then run this script again or use WSL2 directly\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n        Write-Host \"\"\n    } else {\n        Write-Host \"USB device sharing not configured.\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n        Write-Host \"\"\n        Write-Host \"SETUP REQUIRED: Install usbipd-win for USB passthrough:\" -ForegroundColor Green\n        Write-Host \"  winget install usbipd-win\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n        Write-Host \"\"\n        Write-Host \"Then share the J-Link device:\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n        Write-Host \"  1. usbipd wsl list  (find J-Link device)\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n        Write-Host \"  2. usbipd wsl attach --busid &lt;busid&gt;\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n        Write-Host \"\"\n    }\n    \n    Write-Host \"OPTION 1: Use WSL2 directly (Recommended after USB setup)\" -ForegroundColor Green\n    Write-Host \"  Open WSL2 terminal and run:\" -ForegroundColor White\n    Write-Host \"    cd /mnt/c$($projectPath.Replace('C:', ''))\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n    Write-Host \"    make flash\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n    Write-Host \"\"\n    Write-Host \"OPTION 2: Try WSL2 from PowerShell (requires USB sharing)\" -ForegroundColor Green\n    Write-Host \"  Attempting to run via WSL2...\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n    \n    # Convert Windows path to WSL2 path\n    $wslPath = $projectPath.Replace('C:', '/mnt/c').Replace('\\', '/')",

        "contents": "# build: docker build -t uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board .\n# run: docker run -it uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board\n\nFROM ubuntu:22.04\n\nARG DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive\nRUN apt-get -y update\nRUN apt-get install -y build-essential wget unzip\n\nWORKDIR /usr/local\n\n# install nRF5 SDK version 17.1.0 (the same version expected by the Qorvo project)\nRUN wget -q https://nsscprodmedia.blob.core.windows.net/prod/software-and-other-downloads/sdks/nrf5/binaries/nrf5_sdk_17.1.0_ddde560.zip &amp;&amp; unzip nrf5_sdk_17.1.0_ddde560.zip &amp;&amp; rm nrf5_sdk_17.1.0_ddde560.zip\n\n# install SEGGER Embedded Studio version 5.42a (the same version expected by the nRF5 SDK)\n# it has an installer that has to be run as root, and has a EULA that needs to be scrolled through\nRUN wget -q https://www.segger.com/downloads/embedded-studio/Setup_EmbeddedStudio_ARM_v542a_linux_x64.tar.gz &amp;&amp; tar xf Setup_EmbeddedStudio_ARM_v542a_linux_x64.tar.gz --strip-components=1 arm_segger_embedded_studio_542a_linux_x64/install_segger_embedded_studio &amp;&amp; rm Setup_EmbeddedStudio_ARM_v542a_linux_x64.tar.gz\nRUN apt-get install -y libxrender1 libxext6\nRUN yes yes | ./install_segger_embedded_studio --copy-files-to /usr/local/segger_embedded_studio_V5.42a\n\n# install nRF command line tools, including nrfjprog for programming using SEGGER J-Link programmers/debuggers\n# TODO: as of 2023-10-30, this requires the workaround of disabling udevadm, since the package is still broken for Docker builds: https://forum.segger.com/index.php/Thread/8953-SOLVED-J-Link-Linux-installer-fails-for-Docker-containers-Error-Failed-to-update/\nRUN apt-get install -y libusb-1.0-0 apt-utils udev\nRUN wget -q https://nsscprodmedia.blob.core.windows.net/prod/software-and-other-downloads/desktop-software/nrf-command-line-tools/sw/versions-10-x-x/10-23-2/nrf-command-line-tools_10.23.2_amd64.deb &amp;&amp; dpkg -i nrf-command-line-tools_10.23.2_amd64.deb\nRUN echo '#!/bin/bash\\necho not running udevadm \"$@\"' &gt; /usr/bin/udevadm &amp;&amp; chmod +x /usr/bin/udevadm &amp;&amp; apt-get install -y /opt/nrf-command-line-tools/share/JLink_Linux_V788j_x86_64.deb --fix-broken\n\n# install J-Link tools, including JLink RTT Logger for viewing debug output from the J-Link transferred via SEGGER RTT",

          {

            "text": "RUN wget -q https://nsscprodmedia.blob.core.windows.net/prod/software-and-other-downloads/sdks/nrf5/binaries/nrf5_sdk_17.1.0_ddde560.zip &amp;&amp; unzip nrf5_sdk_17.1.0_ddde560.zip &amp;&amp; rm nrf5_sdk_17.1.0_ddde560.zip",
            "lineNumber": 13
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 14
          },
          {
            "text": "# install SEGGER Embedded Studio version 5.42a (the same version expected by the nRF5 SDK)",
            "lineNumber": 15
          },
          {
            "text": "# it has an installer that has to be run as root, and has a EULA that needs to be scrolled through",
            "lineNumber": 16
          },
          {
            "text": "RUN wget -q https://www.segger.com/downloads/embedded-studio/Setup_EmbeddedStudio_ARM_v542a_linux_x64.tar.gz &amp;&amp; tar xf Setup_EmbeddedStudio_ARM_v542a_linux_x64.tar.gz --strip-components=1 arm_segger_embedded_studio_542a_linux_x64/install_segger_embedded_studio &amp;&amp; rm Setup_EmbeddedStudio_ARM_v542a_linux_x64.tar.gz",
            "lineNumber": 17
          },
          {
            "text": "RUN apt-get install -y libxrender1 libxext6",
            "lineNumber": 18
          },
          {
            "text": "RUN yes yes | ./install_segger_embedded_studio --copy-files-to /usr/local/segger_embedded_studio_V5.42a",
            "lineNumber": 19
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 20
          },
          {
            "text": "# install nRF command line tools, including nrfjprog for programming using SEGGER J-Link programmers/debuggers",
            "lineNumber": 21
          },
          {
            "text": "# TODO: as of 2023-10-30, this requires the workaround of disabling udevadm, since the package is still broken for Docker builds: https://forum.segger.com/index.php/Thread/8953-SOLVED-J-Link-Linux-installer-fails-for-Docker-containers-Error-Failed-to-update/",
            "lineNumber": 22
          },
          {
            "text": "RUN apt-get install -y libusb-1.0-0 apt-utils udev",
            "lineNumber": 23
          },
          {
            "text": "RUN wget -q https://nsscprodmedia.blob.core.windows.net/prod/software-and-other-downloads/desktop-software/nrf-command-line-tools/sw/versions-10-x-x/10-23-2/nrf-command-line-tools_10.23.2_amd64.deb &amp;&amp; dpkg -i nrf-command-line-tools_10.23.2_amd64.deb",
            "lineNumber": 24
          },
          {
            "text": "RUN echo '#!/bin/bash\\necho not running udevadm \"$@\"' &gt; /usr/bin/udevadm &amp;&amp; chmod +x /usr/bin/udevadm &amp;&amp; apt-get install -y /opt/nrf-command-line-tools/share/JLink_Linux_V788j_x86_64.deb --fix-broken",
            "lineNumber": 25
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 26
          },
          {
            "text": "# install J-Link tools, including JLink RTT Logger for viewing debug output from the J-Link transferred via SEGGER RTT",
            "lineNumber": 27
          }
        ]
      },

        "contents": "# PowerShell Scripts for DWM3001C Firmware\n\nThis directory contains PowerShell scripts for building and flashing the DWM3001C firmware on Windows.\n\n## Prerequisites\n\n1. **Docker Desktop** installed and running (with WSL2 backend recommended for USB access)\n2. **PowerShell** (comes with Windows 10/11)\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### Flash Node A (TX)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n.\\build-and-flash-tx.ps1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis will:\n1. Configure the firmware for TX variant\n2. Build the firmware\n3. Flash it to the connected board\n\n### Flash Node B (RX)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n.\\build-and-flash-rx.ps1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis will:\n1. Configure the firmware for RX variant\n2. Build the firmware\n3. Flash it to the connected board\n\n## Individual Scripts\n\n### Configuration Scripts\n\n- **&#96;set-node-tx.ps1&#96;** - Configure firmware for Node A (TX)\n- **&#96;set-node-rx.ps1&#96;** - Configure firmware for Node B (RX)\n\n### Build Scripts\n\n- **&#96;build.ps1&#96;** - Build the firmware\n- **&#96;clean.ps1&#96;** - Clean build outputs\n- **&#96;flash.ps1&#96;** - Flash firmware to connected board\n\n### Combined Scripts\n\n- **&#96;build-and-flash-tx.ps1&#96;** - Configure, build, and flash TX variant\n- **&#96;build-and-flash-rx.ps1&#96;** - Configure, build, and flash RX variant\n\n## Usage Examples\n\n### Step-by-step (Manual)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n# 1. Configure for TX\n.\\set-node-tx.ps1\n\n# 2. Build\n.\\build.ps1\n\n# 3. Flash\n.\\flash.ps1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### One-command (Automatic)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n# For Node A (TX)\n.\\build-and-flash-tx.ps1\n\n# For Node B (RX)\n.\\build-and-flash-rx.ps1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n### Docker Not Running\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nError: Docker is not running. Please start Docker Desktop.\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n**Solution:** Start Docker Desktop and wait for it to fully initialize.\n\n### USB Device Access Issues\nIf flashing fails with USB device errors:\n1. Ensure Docker Desktop is using WSL2 backend (Settings → General → Use WSL 2)\n2. Try unplugging and replugging the USB cable\n3. Ensure the board is connected to the J9 port (lower USB port)\n4. Check that the board is powered on\n\n### Build Fails\n- Run &#96;.\\clean.ps1&#96; to clean old build outputs\n- Check that Docker has enough resources allocated (Settings → Resources)",

      "codeBlock": {

          "endPosition": {

          }
        },
        "contents": "**See also:** if you're looking for a fully-featured firmware that you just need some minor customizations for, check out my [DWM3001CDK demo firmware repository](https://github.com/Uberi/DWM3001CDK-demo-firmware).\n\nQuickstart\n----------\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sh\n# MANUAL ACTION (OPTIONAL): run this command to use my prebuilt development environment, otherwise it'll be automatically built from scratch: docker pull uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board\n\nmake build\n\n# MANUAL ACTION: connect the lower USB port of the DWM3001CDK (labelled J9) to this computer using a USB cable (this is the J-Link's USB port)\n\nmake flash\n\nmake stream-debug-logs\n\n# MANUAL ACTION: run the following command in another terminal to see the debug logs: tail -f Output/debug-log.txt\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nYou should now see RTT output from the DWM3001CDK, try pressing the reset buttom (labelled SW1) to re-run the example program and output more logs over RTT.\n\nDeveloping\n----------\n\nYou'll need Docker, and many of the hardware-facing commands in the Makefile assume you're using Linux. The &#96;make serial-terminal&#96; command assumes you have &#96;minicom&#96;, &#96;grep&#96;, and &#96;udevadm&#96; installed.\n\nYou can develop your custom applications by modifying &#96;Src/main.c&#96; and other files within &#96;Src/&#96;.\n\nNote that you'll have to manually edit &#96;dw3000_api.emProject&#96; with any file additions/removals/renames. It sounds annoying, and it is, but I still consider it an improvement over directly interacting with the proprietary SEGGER Embedded Studio.\n\nLicense\n-------\n\nMost of the code in this repository comes from the official Qorvo SDKs and examples published on their website. Here's the copyright notice that comes with the SDKs:\n\n&gt; Read the header of each file to know more about the license concerning this file.\n&gt; Following licenses are used in the SDK:\n&gt; \n&gt; * Apache-2.0 license\n&gt; * Qorvo license\n&gt; * FreeRTOS license\n&gt; * Nordic Semiconductor ASA license\n&gt; * Garmin Canada license\n&gt; * ARM Limited license\n&gt; * Third-party licenses: All third-party code contained in SDK_BSP/external (respective licenses included in each of the imported projects)\n&gt; \n&gt; The provided HEX files were compiled using the projects located in the folders. For license and copyright information,",

          {

        "contents": "RUN echo '#!/bin/bash\\necho not running udevadm \"$@\"' &gt; /usr/bin/udevadm &amp;&amp; chmod +x /usr/bin/udevadm &amp;&amp; apt-get install -y /opt/nrf-command-line-tools/share/JLink_Linux_V788j_x86_64.deb --fix-broken\n\n# install J-Link tools, including JLink RTT Logger for viewing debug output from the J-Link transferred via SEGGER RTT\nRUN wget -q --post-data accept_license_agreement=accepted https://www.segger.com/downloads/jlink/JLink_Linux_V792n_x86_64.tgz &amp;&amp; tar xf JLink_Linux_V792n_x86_64.tgz &amp;&amp; rm JLink_Linux_V792n_x86_64.tgz\n\nWORKDIR /project",

        "contents": "# auto-detect the DWM3001CDK's UART and open a minicom terminal connected to that UART, communicating via USB and the on-board SEGGER J-Link\nserial-terminal:\n\tDEVICE_FILE=$$(ls /dev/ttyUSB* /dev/ttyACM* 2&gt;/dev/null | while read -r dev; do if udevadm info -a -n $$dev | grep -q 'ATTRS{idVendor}==\"1915\"' &amp;&amp; udevadm info -a -n $$dev | grep -q 'ATTRS{idProduct}==\"520f\"'; then echo \"$$dev\"; break; fi; done); \\\n\tif [ -z \"$$DEVICE_FILE\" ]; then echo \"Device not found\"; exit 1; fi; \\\n\tminicom --device $$DEVICE_FILE\n\n# open a bash shell in the development environment with all of the development tools available\ndevelopment-shell: development-environment\n\tdocker run -it -v \"$$(pwd)\":/project uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board\n\n# build the development environment, reusing the existing build in the docker cache if available\ndevelopment-environment:\n\tdocker build -t uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board - &lt; Dockerfile  # build without sending any build context\n\n# export the development environment to the tar archive \"./uberi_qorvo-nrf52833-board.tar\", for offline archival purposes\nsave-development-environment:\n\tdocker image save -o uberi_qorvo-nrf52833-board.tar uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board\n\n# load a previously exported development environment from the tar archive \"./uberi_qorvo-nrf52833-board.tar\"\nload-development-environment:\n\tdocker image load -i uberi_qorvo-nrf52833-board.tar",

        "contents": "}\n\n# Function to flash firmware\nfunction Flash-Firmware {\n    param([string]$NodeType)\n    \n    Write-Host \"[FLASH] Flashing $NodeType node...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    Write-Host \"       Please ensure $NodeType board is connected and powered on\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n    \n    &amp; \"$projectRoot\\flash.ps1\"\n    \n    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n        throw \"Flash failed for $NodeType\"\n    }\n    \n    Write-Host \"[FLASH] $NodeType flash successful\" -ForegroundColor Green\n}\n\n# Function to run test\nfunction Run-Test {\n    param([int]$IterationNumber)\n    \n    Write-Host \"\"\n    Write-Host \"========================================\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n    Write-Host \"  Test Iteration $IterationNumber of $Iterations\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n    Write-Host \"========================================\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n    Write-Host \"\"\n    \n    # Clear debug log before each test\n    Clear-DebugLog\n    \n    Write-Host \"[TEST] Starting Orchestrator test...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    Write-Host \"       Test duration: $TestDurationSeconds seconds\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n    Write-Host \"\"\n    \n    # Change to Orchestrator directory\n    Push-Location \"$projectRoot\\Orchestrator\"\n    \n    try {\n        # Run Orchestrator (it will run the test plan)\n        $process = Start-Process -FilePath \"node\" -ArgumentList \"src/orchestrator/main.js\" -NoNewWindow -PassThru -Wait\n        \n        if ($process.ExitCode -ne 0) {\n            Write-Host \"[TEST] Orchestrator exited with code $($process.ExitCode)\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n        }\n    } finally {\n        Pop-Location\n    }\n    \n    # Check if log file was created\n    if (Test-Path $logFile) {\n        $logSize = (Get-Item $logFile).Length\n        Write-Host \"[LOG] Debug log created: $logSize bytes\" -ForegroundColor Green\n    } else {\n        Write-Host \"[LOG] Warning: Debug log not found\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    }\n    \n    Write-Host \"[TEST] Iteration $IterationNumber complete\" -ForegroundColor Green\n    Write-Host \"\"\n}\n\n# Main execution\ntry {\n    # Step 1: Build and Flash TX Node (unless skipped)",

        "contents": "    Write-Host \"\"\n}\n\n# Main execution\ntry {\n    # Step 1: Build and Flash TX Node (unless skipped)\n    if (-not $SkipBuild) {\n        Write-Host \"[SETUP] Step 1/4: Building TX Node...\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n        Build-Firmware \"TX\"\n        Write-Host \"\"\n    }\n    \n    if (-not $SkipFlash) {\n        Write-Host \"[SETUP] Step 2/4: Flashing TX Node...\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n        Write-Host \"        Connect TX board (Node A) now and press any key to continue...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n        $null = $Host.UI.RawUI.ReadKey(\"NoEcho,IncludeKeyDown\")\n        Flash-Firmware \"TX\"\n        Write-Host \"\"\n    }\n    \n    # Step 2: Build and Flash RX Node (unless skipped)\n    if (-not $SkipBuild) {\n        Write-Host \"[SETUP] Step 3/4: Building RX Node...\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n        Build-Firmware \"RX\"\n        Write-Host \"\"\n    }\n    \n    if (-not $SkipFlash) {\n        Write-Host \"[SETUP] Step 4/4: Flashing RX Node...\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n        Write-Host \"        Connect RX board (Node B) now and press any key to continue...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n        $null = $Host.UI.RawUI.ReadKey(\"NoEcho,IncludeKeyDown\")\n        Flash-Firmware \"RX\"\n        Write-Host \"\"\n    }\n    \n    # Wait for boards to initialize\n    Write-Host \"[SETUP] Waiting for boards to initialize (5 seconds)...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    Start-Sleep -Seconds 5\n    Write-Host \"\"\n    \n    # Step 3: Run tests iteratively\n    for ($i = 1; $i -le $Iterations; $i++) {\n        Run-Test -IterationNumber $i\n        \n        # Wait between iterations (except last one)\n        if ($i -lt $Iterations) {\n            Write-Host \"Waiting 3 seconds before next iteration...\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n            Start-Sleep -Seconds 3\n        }\n    }\n    \n    Write-Host \"========================================\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n    Write-Host \"  All Tests Complete!\" -ForegroundColor Green\n    Write-Host \"========================================\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n    Write-Host \"\"\n    Write-Host \"Debug logs saved to: $logFile\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n    Write-Host \"\"\n    Write-Host \"To analyze logs, check:\" -ForegroundColor Yellow",

        "contents": "{\n  \"name\": \"uwb-test-orchestrator\",\n  \"version\": \"1.0.0\",\n  \"description\": \"RPi5 orchestrator for UWB DWM3001C test rig\",\n  \"main\": \"src/orchestrator/main.js\",\n  \"type\": \"module\",\n  \"scripts\": {\n    \"start\": \"node src/orchestrator/main.js\",\n    \"dev\": \"node --watch src/orchestrator/main.js\",\n    \"web\": \"node src/web/server.js\",\n    \"frontend:dev\": \"cd frontend &amp;&amp; npm run dev\",\n    \"frontend:build\": \"cd frontend &amp;&amp; npm run build\",\n    \"start:win\": \"node src/orchestrator/main.js\",\n    \"start:linux\": \"node src/orchestrator/main.js\",\n    \"start:windows\": \"cmd /c start-windows.bat\",\n    \"dev:windows\": \"cmd /c start-windows-dev.bat\",\n    \"web:windows\": \"cmd /c start-windows-web.bat\",\n    \"list-ports\": \"node scripts/list-ports.js\",\n    \"test-ping\": \"node scripts/test-ping.js\",\n    \"diagnose-uart\": \"node scripts/diagnose-uart.js\",\n    \"diagnose-complete\": \"node scripts/diagnose-complete.js\",\n    \"verify-flash\": \"node scripts/verify-flash.js\",\n    \"test-rs485-tx\": \"node scripts/test-rs485-tx.js\",\n    \"test-uwb-commands\": \"node scripts/test-uwb-commands.js\",\n    \"verify-communication\": \"node scripts/verify-communication.js\"\n  },\n  \"keywords\": [\n    \"uwb\",\n    \"dwm3001c\",\n    \"test-rig\",\n    \"raspberry-pi\"\n  ],\n  \"author\": \"\",\n  \"license\": \"ISC\",\n  \"dependencies\": {\n    \"express\": \"^4.18.2\",\n    \"socket.io\": \"^4.6.1\",\n    \"serialport\": \"^12.0.0\",\n    \"csv-writer\": \"^1.6.0\",\n    \"csv-parser\": \"^3.0.0\",\n    \"js-yaml\": \"^4.1.0\",\n    \"swagger-jsdoc\": \"^6.2.8\",\n    \"swagger-ui-express\": \"^5.0.0\",\n    \"cors\": \"^2.8.5\"\n  }\n}",

        "contents": "# Build and flash Node B (RX) in one command\n# Usage: .\\build-and-flash-rx.ps1\n\nWrite-Host \"=== Building and Flashing Node B (RX) ===\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n\n# Configure for RX\nWrite-Host \"&#96;n[1/3] Configuring for RX...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n&amp; \"$PSScriptRoot\\set-node-rx.ps1\"\n\nif ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n    Write-Host \"Failed to configure for RX\" -ForegroundColor Red\n    exit 1\n}\n\n# Build\nWrite-Host \"&#96;n[2/3] Building firmware...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n&amp; \"$PSScriptRoot\\build.ps1\"\n\nif ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n    Write-Host \"Build failed!\" -ForegroundColor Red\n    exit 1\n}\n\n# Flash\nWrite-Host \"&#96;n[3/3] Flashing to board...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n&amp; \"$PSScriptRoot\\flash.ps1\"\n\nif ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) {\n    Write-Host \"&#96;n=== Node B (RX) ready! ===\" -ForegroundColor Green\n} else {\n    Write-Host \"&#96;nFlash failed!\" -ForegroundColor Red\n    exit 1\n}",

        "contents": "# Automated Build, Flash, and Test Script with Iteration Support\n# Usage: .\\auto-test-tx-rx.ps1 [iterations]\n# Example: .\\auto-test-tx-rx.ps1 3  (runs 3 iterations)\n\nparam(\n    [int]$Iterations = 1,\n    [int]$TestDurationSeconds = 30,\n    [switch]$SkipBuild = $false,\n    [switch]$SkipFlash = $false\n)\n\n$ErrorActionPreference = \"Stop\"\n$projectRoot = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path\n$logFile = Join-Path $projectRoot \".cursor\\debug.log\"\n\nWrite-Host \"========================================\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\nWrite-Host \"  UWB TX/RX Automated Test Script\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\nWrite-Host \"  Iterations: $Iterations\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\nWrite-Host \"========================================\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\nWrite-Host \"\"\nWrite-Host \"Serial Ports Configuration:\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\nWrite-Host \"  Node A (TX): COM17\" -ForegroundColor White\nWrite-Host \"  Node B (RX): COM18\" -ForegroundColor White\nWrite-Host \"\"\nWrite-Host \"Make sure both boards are connected via RS-485 to these COM ports\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\nWrite-Host \"\"\n\n# Function to clear debug log\nfunction Clear-DebugLog {\n    if (Test-Path $logFile) {\n        Remove-Item $logFile -Force\n        Write-Host \"[LOG] Cleared debug log\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n    }\n}\n\n# Function to build firmware\nfunction Build-Firmware {\n    param([string]$NodeType)\n    \n    Write-Host \"[BUILD] Building $NodeType firmware...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    \n    if ($NodeType -eq \"TX\") {\n        &amp; \"$projectRoot\\set-node-tx.ps1\"\n    } else {\n        &amp; \"$projectRoot\\set-node-rx.ps1\"\n    }\n    \n    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n        throw \"Failed to configure for $NodeType\"\n    }\n    \n    &amp; \"$projectRoot\\build.ps1\"\n    \n    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n        throw \"Build failed for $NodeType\"\n    }\n    \n    Write-Host \"[BUILD] $NodeType build successful\" -ForegroundColor Green\n}\n\n# Function to flash firmware\nfunction Flash-Firmware {\n    param([string]$NodeType)\n    \n    Write-Host \"[FLASH] Flashing $NodeType node...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow",

        "contents": "# Build script for DWM3001C firmware\n# Usage: .\\build.ps1\n\nWrite-Host \"Building DWM3001C firmware...\" -ForegroundColor Green\n\n# Get the project root directory\n$projectRoot = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path\n$projectPath = $projectRoot.Replace('\\', '/')\n\n# Ensure Docker is running\n$dockerRunning = docker info 2&gt;&amp;1\nif ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n    Write-Host \"Error: Docker is not running. Please start Docker Desktop.\" -ForegroundColor Red\n    exit 1\n}\n\n# Build the development environment if needed\nWrite-Host \"Checking development environment...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\nGet-Content Dockerfile | docker build -t uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board -\n\nif ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n    Write-Host \"Error: Failed to build development environment.\" -ForegroundColor Red\n    exit 1\n}\n\n# Build the firmware\nWrite-Host \"Compiling firmware...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\ndocker run -v \"${projectPath}:/project\" uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board /usr/local/segger_embedded_studio_V5.42a/bin/emBuild -config \"Common\" /project/dw3000_api.emProject\n\nif ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) {\n    Write-Host \"Build completed successfully!\" -ForegroundColor Green\n    Write-Host \"Output file: Output/Common/Exe/dw3000_api.hex\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n} else {\n    Write-Host \"Build failed!\" -ForegroundColor Red\n    exit 1\n}",

        "contents": "// &lt;/h&gt; \n//==========================================================\n\n// &lt;/e&gt;\n\n// &lt;q&gt; APP_USBD_AUDIO_ENABLED  - app_usbd_audio - USB AUDIO class\n \n\n#ifndef APP_USBD_AUDIO_ENABLED\n#define APP_USBD_AUDIO_ENABLED 0\n#endif\n\n// &lt;e&gt; APP_USBD_ENABLED - app_usbd - USB Device library\n//==========================================================\n#ifndef APP_USBD_ENABLED\n#define APP_USBD_ENABLED 1\n#endif\n// &lt;o&gt; APP_USBD_VID - Vendor ID.  &lt;0x0000-0xFFFF&gt; \n\n\n// &lt;i&gt; Note: This value is not editable in Configuration Wizard.\n// &lt;i&gt; Vendor ID ordered from USB IF: http://www.usb.org/developers/vendor/\n\n#ifndef APP_USBD_VID\n#define APP_USBD_VID 0x1915\n#endif\n\n// &lt;o&gt; APP_USBD_PID - Product ID.  &lt;0x0000-0xFFFF&gt; \n\n\n// &lt;i&gt; Note: This value is not editable in Configuration Wizard.\n// &lt;i&gt; Selected Product ID\n\n#ifndef APP_USBD_PID\n#define APP_USBD_PID 0x520F\n#endif\n\n// &lt;o&gt; APP_USBD_DEVICE_VER_MAJOR - Major device version  &lt;0-99&gt; \n\n\n// &lt;i&gt; Major device version, will be converted automatically to BCD notation. Use just decimal values.\n\n#ifndef APP_USBD_DEVICE_VER_MAJOR\n#define APP_USBD_DEVICE_VER_MAJOR 1\n#endif\n\n// &lt;o&gt; APP_USBD_DEVICE_VER_MINOR - Minor device version  &lt;0-9&gt; \n\n\n// &lt;i&gt; Minor device version, will be converted automatically to BCD notation. Use just decimal values.\n\n#ifndef APP_USBD_DEVICE_VER_MINOR\n#define APP_USBD_DEVICE_VER_MINOR 0\n#endif\n\n// &lt;o&gt; APP_USBD_DEVICE_VER_SUB - Sub-minor device version  &lt;0-9&gt; \n\n\n// &lt;i&gt; Sub-minor device version, will be converted automatically to BCD notation. Use just decimal values.\n\n#ifndef APP_USBD_DEVICE_VER_SUB\n#define APP_USBD_DEVICE_VER_SUB 0\n#endif\n\n// &lt;q&gt; APP_USBD_CONFIG_SELF_POWERED  - Self-powered device, as opposed to bus-powered.\n \n\n#ifndef APP_USBD_CONFIG_SELF_POWERED\n#define APP_USBD_CONFIG_SELF_POWERED 1\n#endif\n\n// &lt;o&gt; APP_USBD_CONFIG_MAX_POWER - MaxPower field in configuration descriptor in milliamps.  &lt;0-500&gt; \n\n\n#ifndef APP_USBD_CONFIG_MAX_POWER\n#define APP_USBD_CONFIG_MAX_POWER 500",

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": ".\\Src\\examples\\ex_21_orchestrator\\README.md",
        "range": {

        },
        "contents": "# Orchestrator Example - Build and Flash Guide\n\n## Overview\n\nThis example provides two firmware variants:\n- **TX Variant (Node A)**: Transmits UWB packets periodically\n- **RX Variant (Node B)**: Receives UWB packets and collects statistics\n\nBoth variants communicate with the Orchestrator via RS-485 using UART.\n\n## Pin Configuration\n\n### UART Pins (RS-485 Communication)\n- **RX Pin**: GPIO 15 (UART_0_RX_PIN)\n- **TX Pin**: GPIO 19 (UART_0_TX_PIN)\n- **Baud Rate**: 115200\n\n**Note**: Pins 8 and 10 are used for:\n- **Pin 8**: DW3000_IRQ_Pin (interrupt pin for UWB chip)\n- **Pin 10**: DW3000_CS_Pin (SPI chip select for UWB chip)\n\nThe UART for RS-485 communication uses **pins 15 (RX) and 19 (TX)**, not pins 8 and 10.\n\n## Building and Flashing\n\n### Step 1: Build TX Variant (Node A)\n\n1. Edit &#96;Src/example_selection.h&#96;:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;c\n   // Comment out other examples:\n   //#define TEST_READING_DEV_ID\n   \n   // Uncomment TX variant:\n   #define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_TX\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n2. Edit &#96;Src/main.c&#96;:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;c\n   // Comment out other examples:\n   // extern int read_dev_id(void); read_dev_id();\n   \n   // Uncomment TX variant:\n   extern int orchestrator_tx(void); orchestrator_tx();\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n3. Build:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   make build\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n4. Flash to Node A board:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   make flash\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 2: Build RX Variant (Node B)\n\n1. Edit &#96;Src/example_selection.h&#96;:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;c\n   // Comment out TX variant:\n   //#define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_TX\n   \n   // Uncomment RX variant:\n   #define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_RX\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n2. Edit &#96;Src/main.c&#96;:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;c\n   // Comment out TX variant:\n   // extern int orchestrator_tx(void); orchestrator_tx();\n   \n   // Uncomment RX variant:\n   extern int orchestrator_rx(void); orchestrator_rx();\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n3. Build:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   make build\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n4. Flash to Node B board:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   make flash\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Important**: You need to build and flash **separately** for each board. The firmware is compiled with either TX or RX code, not both.\n\n## LED Behavior\n\nThe firmware uses &#96;dwt_setleds()&#96; which controls the **DW3000 UWB chip's internal LEDs**, not the board LEDs.\n\n- **On startup**: LEDs will blink once during initialization",

        "contents": "DWM3001C Starter Firmware\n=========================\n\nA firmware for the [Qorvo DWM3001C](https://www.qorvo.com/products/p/DWM3001C) with comprehensive examples for all of the module's UWB and ranging functionality, and developer tooling that makes working with the firmware much easier than the official tooling. Features:\n\n* **Reproducible**: built-in Docker development environment automates away most of the fragile and finicky parts of setting up the Qorvo SDK, SEGGER Embedded Studio, SEGGER J-Link, nRF52 SDK, and nRF command line tools.\n* **Minimal**: based on a heavily-modified version of the [official Qorvo DWM3001C API software](https://www.qorvo.com/products/p/DWM3001C#documents) (2022-08 version), but significantly simpler in terms of code size and organization. Many source files and folders have been consolidated to make the project much easier to navigate.\n* **Complete**: includes build system, flashing tools, and logging/debugging tools. This is the only repository you need to work with the firmware.\n* **Portable**: run &#96;make save-development-environment&#96; to generate a 5GB tar file containing the entire development environment. In 10 years from now, when half of these dependencies disappear off the internet, run &#96;make load-development-environment&#96; and you'll still be able to compile this project.\n* Runs directly on the DWM3001C's onboard nRF52833: the official examples target an external microcontroller that then interacts with the DWM3001C, but this firmware is designed to run directly on the DWM3001C.\n\nThe firmware and instructions in this repository somewhat assume that you're using the DWM3001CDK (the official DWM3001C devkit), but you can also run it on a standalone DWM3001C simply by not using the definitions for the devkit's onboard LEDs, button, and SEGGER J-Link (see &#96;Src/custom_board.h&#96;).\n\n**See also:** if you're looking for a fully-featured firmware that you just need some minor customizations for, check out my [DWM3001CDK demo firmware repository](https://github.com/Uberi/DWM3001CDK-demo-firmware).\n\nQuickstart\n----------\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sh\n# MANUAL ACTION (OPTIONAL): run this command to use my prebuilt development environment, otherwise it'll be automatically built from scratch: docker pull uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board",
