                {
                  "lineNumber": 7276,
                  "content": "| Web Search Results |  | The DWM3001CDK development kit utilizes specific GPIO pins for UART communication. According to the DWM3001CDK Quick Start Guide, the UART pins are configured as follows:&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;- **UART TX (Transmit):** P0.19&lt;br/&gt;- **UART RX (Receive):** P0.15&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;These pins are accessible via the Raspberry Pi compatible header on the development board. Specifically, the connections are:&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;- **TXD (Transmit Data):** Pin 32 (P0.15)&lt;br/&gt;- **RXD (Receive Data):** Pin 34 (P0.19)&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;It's important to note that the DWM3001CDK is configured by default to use USB CDC (USB Virtual COM port) for communication, with UART over GPIO pins disabled. To enable UART communication via the GPIO pins, firmware modifications are necessary. This involves adjusting the firmware to route UCI communication through the GPIO UART interface instead of the default USB CDC. Detailed steps for this process can be found in the Qorvo Tech Forum discussion. ([forum.qorvo.com](https://forum"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 7309,
                  "content": "1. **Default behavior:** The DWM3001CDK uses USB CDC (Virtual COM port) by default. To use GPIO UART, enable it in firmware."
                },

Created a solution to flash without admin privileges. Here's what I added:

## Solution: Flash without admin privileges

### One-time setup script

Created `setup-usb.ps1` that:
1. Installs `usbipd-win` (may require admin once)
2. Finds your J-Link device
3. Shares it with WSL2

After this setup, flashing works without admin.

### Updated flash script

The `flash.ps1` script now:
- Automatically checks if USB is shared
- Runs setup if needed
- Uses WSL2 to flash (no admin required)

### Updated auto-test script

The `auto-test-tx-rx.ps1` script now:
- Automatically handles USB setup
- Prompts only if setup is needed

## How to use

### Step 1: One-time setup (may need admin once)

```powershell
.\setup-usb.ps1
```

This will:
- Install usbipd-win if needed (may prompt for admin)
- Find and share your J-Link device with WSL2
- Set up everything for future flashing

### Step 2: Flash normally (no admin needed)

After setup, just run:

```powershell
# Flash TX node (no admin!)
.\build-and-flash-tx.ps1

# Flash RX node (no admin!)
.\build-and-flash-rx.ps1

# Or automated test (no admin!)
.\auto-test-tx-rx.ps1 -Iterations 3
```

## How it works

1. usbipd-win shares USB devices from Windows to WSL2
2. Once shared, WSL2 can access the device without admin
3. The flash script uses WSL2 + Docker to flash
4. No admin privileges needed after initial setup

## If you unplug/replug USB

Just run the setup script again:

```powershell
.\setup-usb.ps1
```

The flash script will also auto-detect and prompt you if USB isn't shared.

## Documentation

Created `README-FLASH-NO-ADMIN.md` with full instructions and troubleshooting.

You can now flash without running PowerShell as Administrator.

Updated the setup script to handle installation and PATH issues. Changes:

## Fixed issues

### 1. PATH refresh after installation
- Refreshes PATH after installing usbipd-win
- Checks common installation locations
- Provides clear instructions if PATH refresh fails

### 2. WSL2 availability check
- Verifies WSL2 is installed before proceeding
- Provides installation instructions if missing

### 3. Better error messages
- Clearer troubleshooting steps
- Explains when to restart PowerShell
- Verifies setup at the end

### 4. Verification step
- Confirms USB devices are accessible in WSL2
- Suggests fixes if verification fails

## How to use

### Option 1: Install usbipd-win manually (recommended)

```powershell
# Install usbipd-win (may need admin)
winget install usbipd-win

# Restart PowerShell, then run:
.\setup-usb.ps1
```

### Option 2: Let the script install it

```powershell
# Run setup script (will install usbipd-win if needed)
.\setup-usb.ps1
```

If installation succeeds but usbipd isn't found:
1. Restart PowerShell (to refresh PATH)
2. Run `.\setup-usb.ps1` again

## What the script does now

1. Checks WSL2 is available
2. Installs usbipd-win if missing (may need admin)
3. Refreshes PATH to find usbipd
4. Finds J-Link devices automatically
5. Shares them with WSL2
6. Verifies setup worked

## If it still fails

The script will tell you:
- If usbipd needs to be installed manually
- If you need to restart PowerShell
- If WSL2 needs to be installed
- Step-by-step troubleshooting

Try running `.\setup-usb.ps1` again. If it still fails, share the error message and I'll help debug further.

Script updated and working. Summary:

## Fixed: Updated to new usbipd syntax

### Changes made

1. Updated command syntax:
   - Old: `usbipd wsl list` → New: `usbipd list`
   - Old: `usbipd wsl attach --busid` → New: `usbipd attach --wsl --busid`

2. Improved device detection:
   - Detects "Attached" and "Shared" states
   - Skips devices already attached to WSL2
   - Uses full path to usbipd.exe for reliability

3. Better error handling:
   - Clearer error messages
   - Handles PATH issues
   - Verifies setup at the end

### Test results

The script now:
- Finds usbipd at `C:\Program Files\usbipd-win\usbipd.exe`
- Detects J-Link devices (4-1, 4-2)
- Recognizes they're already attached
- Verifies USB devices are accessible in WSL2

## Ready to use

You can now flash without admin privileges:

```powershell
# Flash TX node (no admin needed!)
.\build-and-flash-tx.ps1

# Flash RX node (no admin needed!)
.\build-and-flash-rx.ps1

# Or automated test
.\auto-test-tx-rx.ps1 -Iterations 3
```

The setup script detected your J-Link devices are already attached to WSL2, so you're ready to flash. The flash script will automatically use WSL2 without requiring admin privileges.

        "contents": "async function main() {\n\n    const pingA = await nodeA.ping();\n    if (pingA) {\n      console.log('✓ Node A PING successful');\n    } else {\n      console.error('✗ Node A PING failed - check connection');\n    }\n\n    const pingB = await nodeB.ping();\n    if (pingB) {\n      console.log('✓ Node B PING successful');\n    } else {\n      console.error('✗ Node B PING failed - check connection');\n    }\n\n    if (!pingA || !pingB) {\n      console.error('\\nError: One or both nodes are not responding to PING');\n      console.error('Please check:');\n      console.error('  1.         "contents": "# Automated Build, Flash, and Test Script with Iteration Support\n# Usage: .\\auto-test-tx-rx.ps1 [iterations]\n# Example: .\\auto-test-tx-rx.ps1 3  (runs 3 iterations)\n\nparam(\n    [int]$Iterations = 1,\n    [int]$TestDurationSeconds = 30,\n    [switch]$SkipBuild = $false,\n    [switch]$SkipFlash = $false\n)\n\n$ErrorActionPreference = \"Stop\"\n$projectRoot = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path\n$logFile = Join-Path $projectRoot \".cursor\\debug.log\"\n\nWrite-Host \"========================================\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\nWrite-Host \"  UWB TX/RX Automated Test Script\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\nWrite-Host \"  Iterations: $Iterations\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\nWrite-Host \"========================================\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\nWrite-Host \"\"\nWrite-Host \"Serial Ports Configuration:\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\nWrite-Host \"  Node A (TX): COM17\" -ForegroundColor White\nWrite-Host \"  Node B (RX): COM18\" -ForegroundColor White\nWrite-Host \"\"\nWrite-Host \"Make sure both boards are connected via RS-485 to these COM ports\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\nWrite-Host \"\"\n\n# Function to clear debug log\nfunction Clear-DebugLog {\n    if (Test-Path $logFile) {\n        Remove-Item $logFile -Force\n        Write-Host \"[LOG] Cleared debug log\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n    }\n}\n\n# Function to build firmware\nfunction Build-Firmware {\n    param([string]$NodeType)\n    \n    Write-Host \"[BUILD] Building $NodeType firmware...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    \n    if ($NodeType -eq \"TX\") {\n        &amp; \"$projectRoot\\set-node-tx.ps1\"\n    } else {\n        &amp; \"$projectRoot\\set-node-rx.ps1\"\n    }\n    \n    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n        throw \"Failed to configure for $NodeType\"\n    }\n    \n    &amp; \"$projectRoot\\build.ps1\"\n    \n    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n        throw \"Build failed for $NodeType\"\n    }\n    \n    Write-Host \"[BUILD] $NodeType build successful\" -ForegroundColor Green\n}\n\n# Function to flash firmware\nfunction Flash-Firmware {\n    param([string]$NodeType)\n    \n    Write-Host \"[FLASH] Flashing $NodeType node...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow",

        "range": {

        "contents": "# PowerShell Scripts for DWM3001C Firmware\n\nThis directory contains PowerShell scripts for building and flashing the DWM3001C firmware on Windows.\n\n## Prerequisites\n\n1. **Docker Desktop** installed and running (with WSL2 backend recommended for USB access)\n2. **PowerShell** (comes with Windows 10/11)\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### Flash Node A (TX)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n.\\build-and-flash-tx.ps1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis will:\n1. Configure the firmware for TX variant\n2. Build the firmware\n3. Flash it to the connected board\n\n### Flash Node B (RX)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n.\\build-and-flash-rx.ps1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis will:\n1. Configure the firmware for RX variant\n2. Build the firmware\n3. Flash it to the connected board\n\n## Individual Scripts\n\n### Configuration Scripts\n\n- **&#96;set-node-tx.ps1&#96;** - Configure firmware for Node A (TX)\n- **&#96;set-node-rx.ps1&#96;** - Configure firmware for Node B (RX)\n\n### Build Scripts\n\n- **&#96;build.ps1&#96;** - Build the firmware\n- **&#96;clean.ps1&#96;** - Clean build outputs\n- **&#96;flash.ps1&#96;** - Flash firmware to connected board\n\n### Combined Scripts\n\n- **&#96;build-and-flash-tx.ps1&#96;** - Configure, build, and flash TX variant\n- **&#96;build-and-flash-rx.ps1&#96;** - Configure, build, and flash RX variant\n\n## Usage Examples\n\n### Step-by-step (Manual)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n# 1. Configure for TX\n.\\set-node-tx.ps1\n\n# 2. Build\n.\\build.ps1\n\n# 3. Flash\n.\\flash.ps1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### One-command (Automatic)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n# For Node A (TX)\n.\\build-and-flash-tx.ps1\n\n# For Node B (RX)\n.\\build-and-flash-rx.ps1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n### Docker Not Running\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nError: Docker is not running. Please start Docker Desktop.\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n**Solution:** Start Docker Desktop and wait for it to fully initialize.\n\n### USB Device Access Issues\nIf flashing fails with USB device errors:\n1. Ensure Docker Desktop is using WSL2 backend (Settings → General → Use WSL 2)\n2. Try unplugging and replugging the USB cable\n3. Ensure the board is connected to the J9 port (lower USB port)\n4. Check that the board is powered on\n\n### Build Fails\n- Run &#96;.\\clean.ps1&#96; to clean old build outputs\n- Check that Docker has enough resources allocated (Settings → Resources)",

        "contents": "# Flash script for DWM3001C firmware\n# Usage: .\\flash.ps1\n# Note: Requires Docker Desktop with WSL2 backend for USB device access\n\nWrite-Host \"Flashing DWM3001C firmware...\" -ForegroundColor Green\n\n# Get the project root directory\n$projectRoot = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path\n$projectPath = $projectRoot.Replace('\\', '/')\n\n# Check if hex file exists\n$hexFile = Join-Path $projectRoot \"Output\\Common\\Exe\\dw3000_api.hex\"\nif (-not (Test-Path $hexFile)) {\n    Write-Host \"Error: Firmware not found at $hexFile\" -ForegroundColor Red\n    Write-Host \"Please run .\\build.ps1 first to build the firmware.\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    exit 1\n}\n\n# Ensure Docker is running\n$dockerRunning = docker info 2&gt;&amp;1\nif ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n    Write-Host \"Error: Docker is not running. Please start Docker Desktop.\" -ForegroundColor Red\n    exit 1\n}\n\nWrite-Host \"Connecting to board via J-Link...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\nWrite-Host \"Make sure the board is connected via USB (J9 port) and powered on.\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n\n# Check if running in WSL2\n$isWSL = $env:WSL_DISTRO_NAME -ne $null\n\nif ($isWSL) {\n    # Running in WSL2 - can mount USB devices directly",

        "contents": "$usbDevices = &amp; $usbipdExe list 2&gt;&amp;1\n\nif ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n    Write-Host \"\"\n    Write-Host \"Error running usbipd.\" -ForegroundColor Red\n    Write-Host \"Command: $usbipdExe list\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n    Write-Host \"Error output: $usbDevices\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n    Write-Host \"\"\n    Write-Host \"Troubleshooting:\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    Write-Host \"  1. Make sure usbipd-win is installed: winget install usbipd-win\" -ForegroundColor White\n    Write-Host \"  2. Restart PowerShell after installation\" -ForegroundColor White\n    Write-Host \"  3. Check if usbipd is in PATH: Get-Command usbipd\" -ForegroundColor White\n    Write-Host \"\"\n    Write-Host \"If usbipd is installed but not found, restart PowerShell and try again.\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    exit 1\n}\n\nWrite-Host $usbDevices\nWrite-Host \"\"\n\n# Find J-Link devices (SEGGER devices)\n$jlinkDevices = $usbDevices | Select-String -Pattern \"SEGGER|J-Link|1366\" -CaseSensitive:$false\n\nif ($jlinkDevices.Count -eq 0) {\n    Write-Host \"No J-Link devices found!\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    Write-Host \"\"\n    Write-Host \"Make sure:\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n    Write-Host \"  1. DWM3001CDK board is connected via USB (J9 port)\" -ForegroundColor White\n    Write-Host \"  2. Board is powered on\" -ForegroundColor White\n    Write-Host \"  3. USB cable is properly connected\" -ForegroundColor White\n    Write-Host \"\"\n    Write-Host \"Run this script again after connecting the board.\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    exit 1\n}\n\nWrite-Host \"Found J-Link device(s):\" -ForegroundColor Green\n$jlinkDevices | ForEach-Object { Write-Host \"  $_\" -ForegroundColor White }\nWrite-Host \"\"\n\n# Extract bus IDs and check if already attached/shared\n$busIds = @()\n$attachedBusIds = @()\nforeach ($line in $usbDevices) {\n    if ($line -match \"SEGGER|J-Link|1366\") {\n        # Extract bus ID (format: BUSID  VID:PID    DESCRIPTION  STATE)\n        # Skip GUID entries (Persisted section)\n        if ($line -match \"^\\s*([0-9-]+)\") {\n            $busId = $matches[1]\n            # Check if already attached or shared\n            if ($line -match \"Attached|Shared\") {\n                $attachedBusIds += $busId\n                $state = if ($line -match \"Attached\") { \"attached\" } else { \"shared\" }\n                Write-Host \"  Bus ID $busId is already $state ✓\" -ForegroundColor Green",

        "contents": "} else {\n    # Running in Windows PowerShell\n    # Docker Desktop on Windows doesn't support USB passthrough\n    Write-Host \"Windows PowerShell detected.\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n    Write-Host \"\"\n    \n    # Check if usbipd is available\n    $usbipdCheck = Get-Command usbipd -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue\n    if (-not $usbipdCheck) {\n        Write-Host \"usbipd-win not found.         "contents": "# Build script for DWM3001C firmware\n# Usage: .\\build.ps1\n\nWrite-Host \"Building DWM3001C firmware...\" -ForegroundColor Green\n\n# Get the project root directory\n$projectRoot = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path\n$projectPath = $projectRoot.Replace('\\', '/')\n\n# Ensure Docker is running\n$dockerRunning = docker info 2&gt;&amp;1\nif ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n    Write-Host \"Error: Docker is not running. Please start Docker Desktop.\" -ForegroundColor Red\n    exit 1\n}\n\n# Build the development environment if needed\nWrite-Host \"Checking development environment...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\nGet-Content Dockerfile | docker build -t uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board -\n\nif ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n    Write-Host \"Error: Failed to build development environment.\" -ForegroundColor Red\n    exit 1\n}\n\n# Build the firmware\nWrite-Host \"Compiling firmware...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\ndocker run -v \"${projectPath}:/project\" uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board /usr/local/segger_embedded_studio_V5.42a/bin/emBuild -config \"Common\" /project/dw3000_api.emProject\n\nif ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) {\n    Write-Host \"Build completed successfully!\" -ForegroundColor Green\n    Write-Host \"Output file: Output/Common/Exe/dw3000_api.hex\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n} else {\n    Write-Host \"Build failed!\" -ForegroundColor Red\n    exit 1\n}",

        "contents": "export class TestRunner extends EventEmitter {\n\n\n  /**\n   * Run test from test plan\n   * @param {Object} test - Test configuration from test plan\n   */\n  async runTest(test) {\n    if (this.isRunning) {\n      throw new Error(\"Test is already running\");\n    }\n\n    this.currentTest = test;\n    this.isRunning = true;\n    this.emit(\"testStarted\", test);\n\n    try {\n      // Step 1: Prompt operator to set jammer\n      await this.promptJammer(test.jammer_label);\n\n      // Step 2: Configure both nodes\n      await this.configureNodes(test.config);\n\n      // Step 3: Create CSV log file\n      this.csvLogger.createLogFile(test.run_name);\n\n      // Step 4: Start both nodes\n      await this.startNodes();\n\n      // Step 5: Start periodic polling\n      this.startPolling(test);\n\n      // Step 6: Wait for test duration (or manual stop)\n      const testDuration =\n        this.config.getTestConfig().default_test_duration_seconds * 1000;\n      await this.sleep(testDuration);\n\n      // Step 7: Stop test\n      await this.stopTest();\n    } catch (error) {\n      this.emit(\"error\", error);\n      await this.stopTest();\n      throw error;\n    }\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Prompt operator to set jammer\n   * @param {string} jammerLabel - Expected jammer label\n   * @returns {Promise&lt;void&gt;}\n   */\n}",

Please attach devices manually:\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    Write-Host \"  usbipd attach --wsl --busid &lt;busid&gt;\" -ForegroundColor White\n    exit 1\n}\n\n# If all devices are already attached/shared, we're done\nif ($busIds.Count -eq 0 -and $attachedBusIds.Count -gt 0) {\n    Write-Host \"\"\n    Write-Host \"All J-Link devices are already attached to WSL2 ✓\" -ForegroundColor Green\n} else {\n    # Share each J-Link device with WSL2 (new syntax: attach --wsl --busid)\n    Write-Host \"Sharing J-Link device(s) with WSL2...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    foreach ($busId in $busIds) {\n        Write-Host \"  Attaching bus ID: $busId to WSL2...\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n        \n        # New syntax: usbipd attach --wsl --busid &lt;BUSID&gt;\n        &amp; $usbipdExe attach --wsl --busid $busId 2&gt;&amp;1 | Out-Null\n        \n        if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) {\n            Write-Host \"  ✓ Successfully attached $busId to WSL2\" -ForegroundColor Green\n        } else {\n            Write-Host \"  ✗ Failed to attach $busId\" -ForegroundColor Red\n            Write-Host \"\"\n            Write-Host \"    Troubleshooting:\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n            Write-Host \"    1.         "contents": "    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or $sharedDevices -match \"No such file\") {\n        Write-Host \"USB devices not accessible in WSL2. Sharing device...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n        \n        # Try to find and attach J-Link device automatically (new syntax)\n        $usbipdExe = Get-Command usbipd -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue\n        if (-not $usbipdExe) {\n            # Try common location\n            $usbipdExe = \"$env:ProgramFiles\\usbipd-win\\usbipd.exe\"\n            if (-not (Test-Path $usbipdExe)) {\n                Write-Host \"usbipd not found. Please run: .\\setup-usb.ps1\" -ForegroundColor Red\n                exit 1\n            }\n        } else {\n            $usbipdExe = $usbipdExe.Source\n        }\n        \n        $usbDevices = &amp; $usbipdExe list 2&gt;&amp;1\n        $jlinkLine = $usbDevices | Select-String -Pattern \"SEGGER|J-Link|1366\" -CaseSensitive:$false | Select-Object -First 1\n        \n        if ($jlinkLine -and $jlinkLine.Line -match \"^\\s*([0-9-]+)\") {\n            $busId = $matches[1]\n            \n            # Check if already attached or shared\n            if ($jlinkLine.Line -match \"Attached|Shared\") {\n                Write-Host \"J-Link device at bus ID $busId is already attached to WSL2 ✓\" -ForegroundColor Green\n            } else {\n                Write-Host \"Found J-Link device at bus ID: $busId\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n                Write-Host \"Attaching to WSL2...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n                \n                # New syntax: usbipd attach --wsl --busid &lt;BUSID&gt;\n                &amp; $usbipdExe attach --wsl --busid $busId 2&gt;&amp;1 | Out-Null\n            \n            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n                Write-Host \"\"\n                Write-Host \"Failed to share device automatically.\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n                Write-Host \"Please run setup script (may need admin ONCE):\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n                Write-Host \"  .\\setup-usb.ps1\" -ForegroundColor White\n                Write-Host \"\"\n                Write-Host \"Or attach manually:\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n                Write-Host \"  usbipd attach --wsl --busid $busId\" -ForegroundColor White\n                exit 1\n            }\n            ",

        "contents": "    Write-Host \"\"\n}\n\n# Main execution\ntry {\n    # Step 1: Build and Flash TX Node (unless skipped)\n    if (-not $SkipBuild) {\n        Write-Host \"[SETUP] Step 1/4: Building TX Node...\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n        Build-Firmware \"TX\"\n        Write-Host \"\"\n    }\n    \n    if (-not $SkipFlash) {\n        Write-Host \"[SETUP] Step 2/4: Flashing TX Node...\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n        Write-Host \"        Connect TX board (Node A) now and press any key to continue...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n        $null = $Host.UI.RawUI.ReadKey(\"NoEcho,IncludeKeyDown\")\n        Flash-Firmware \"TX\"\n        Write-Host \"\"\n    }\n    \n    # Step 2: Build and Flash RX Node (unless skipped)\n    if (-not $SkipBuild) {\n        Write-Host \"[SETUP] Step 3/4: Building RX Node...\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n        Build-Firmware \"RX\"\n        Write-Host \"\"\n    }\n    \n    if (-not $SkipFlash) {\n        Write-Host \"[SETUP] Step 4/4: Flashing RX Node...\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n        Write-Host \"        Connect RX board (Node B) now and press any key to continue...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n        $null = $Host.UI.RawUI.ReadKey(\"NoEcho,IncludeKeyDown\")\n        Flash-Firmware \"RX\"\n        Write-Host \"\"\n    }\n    \n    # Wait for boards to initialize\n    Write-Host \"[SETUP] Waiting for boards to initialize (5 seconds)...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    Start-Sleep -Seconds 5\n    Write-Host \"\"\n    \n    # Step 3: Run tests iteratively\n    for ($i = 1;         "contents": "# Setup USB device sharing with WSL2 (one-time setup)\n# This script finds J-Link devices and shares them with WSL2\n# Usage: .\\setup-usb.ps1\n# Note: This may require admin privileges ONCE to install usbipd-win\n\nWrite-Host \"=== USB Device Setup for WSL2 ===\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\nWrite-Host \"\"\n\n# Check if WSL2 is available\n$wslCheck = wsl --status 2&gt;&amp;1\nif ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n    Write-Host \"WSL2 not found or not configured!\" -ForegroundColor Red\n    Write-Host \"\"\n    Write-Host \"Please install WSL2:\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    Write-Host \"  wsl --install\" -ForegroundColor White\n    Write-Host \"\"\n    Write-Host \"Or enable it via:\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    Write-Host \"  dism.exe /online /enable-feature /featurename:Microsoft-Windows-Subsystem-Linux /all /norestart\" -ForegroundColor White\n    Write-Host \"  dism.exe /online /enable-feature /featurename:VirtualMachinePlatform /all /norestart\" -ForegroundColor White\n    Write-Host \"\"\n    Write-Host \"Then restart your computer and try again.\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    exit 1\n}\n\nWrite-Host \"WSL2 is available ✓\" -ForegroundColor Green\nWrite-Host \"\"\n\n# Find usbipd executable\n$usbipdExe = $null\n\n# Try to find usbipd in common installation locations\n$usbipdPaths = @(\n    \"$env:ProgramFiles\\usbipd-win\\usbipd.exe\",\n    \"${env:ProgramFiles(x86)}\\usbipd-win\\usbipd.exe\",\n    \"$env:LOCALAPPDATA\\Microsoft\\WindowsApps\\usbipd.exe\"\n)\n\n# Check if usbipd is in PATH\n$usbipdCheck = Get-Command usbipd -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue\nif ($usbipdCheck) {\n    $usbipdExe = $usbipdCheck.Source\n    Write-Host \"Found usbipd at: $usbipdExe\" -ForegroundColor Green\n} else {\n    # Try to find in common locations\n    foreach ($path in $usbipdPaths) {\n        if (Test-Path $path) {\n            $usbipdExe = $path\n            Write-Host \"Found usbipd at: $usbipdExe\" -ForegroundColor Green\n            break\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n# If still not found, try to install\nif (-not $usbipdExe) {\n    Write-Host \"usbipd-win not found. Installing...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow",

        "contents": "}\n\n# Function to flash firmware\nfunction Flash-Firmware {\n    param([string]$NodeType)\n    \n    Write-Host \"[FLASH] Flashing $NodeType node...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    Write-Host \"       Please ensure $NodeType board is connected and powered on\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n    \n    # Check if USB setup is needed (one-time check)\n    $usbipdCheck = Get-Command usbipd -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue\n    if ($usbipdCheck) {\n        $sharedCheck = wsl bash -c \"ls -la /dev/bus/usb 2&gt;&amp;1\" 2&gt;&amp;1\n        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or $sharedCheck -match \"No such file\") {\n            Write-Host \"[SETUP] USB device not shared with WSL2. Running setup...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n            Write-Host \"        (This may require admin ONCE for installation)\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n            &amp; \"$projectRoot\\setup-usb.ps1\"\n            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n                Write-Host \"[SETUP] USB setup failed. Please run manually:\" -ForegroundColor Red\n                Write-Host \"        .\\setup-usb.ps1\" -ForegroundColor White\n                throw \"USB setup required\"\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    \n    &amp; \"$projectRoot\\flash.ps1\"\n    \n    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n        throw \"Flash failed for $NodeType\"\n    }\n    \n    Write-Host \"[FLASH] $NodeType flash successful\" -ForegroundColor Green\n}\n\n# Function to run test\nfunction Run-Test {\n    param([int]$IterationNumber)",

## Fixed: PowerShell exit code handling

### Problem
PowerShell scripts don't set `$LASTEXITCODE` unless they explicitly exit. The `set-node-tx.ps1` and `set-node-rx.ps1` scripts completed but didn't return an exit code, so `build-and-flash-tx.ps1` couldn't detect success.

### Solution
Added explicit exit codes and error handling to both scripts:

1. Added `$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"` to catch errors
2. Wrapped code in try-catch blocks
3. Added file existence checks before processing
4. Added explicit `exit 0` on success and `exit 1` on failure

### Test results
- Configuration step completes successfully
- Build step proceeds normally
- Exit codes are properly set

The build is now running. You can use:
- `.\build-and-flash-tx.ps1` - Build and flash TX node
- `.\build-and-flash-rx.ps1` - Build and flash RX node
- `.\auto-test-tx-rx.ps1` - Automated testing

All scripts now properly handle exit codes and error conditions.

## Fixed: Missing closing brace in flash.ps1

### Problem
The `else` block starting at line 107 was missing its closing brace, causing a PowerShell parser error: "Missing closing '}' in statement block or type definition."

### Solution
Added the missing closing brace after line 126 to properly close the `else` block before the next `} else {` at line 128.

### Structure (now correct):
```powershell
if ($jlinkLine.Line -match "Attached|Shared") {
    // already attached
} else {
    // attach device
    & $usbipdExe attach --wsl --busid $busId
    
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        // error handling
    }
    
    Write-Host "Device shared successfully!"
    Start-Sleep -Seconds 1
}  // ← This closing brace was missing!
```

The script now runs without syntax errors. You can use:
- `.\build-and-flash-tx.ps1` - Build and flash TX node
- `.\build-and-flash-rx.ps1` - Build and flash RX node

The flash step should now complete successfully.

        "range": {

        "contents": "# Orchestrator Example - Build and Flash Guide\n\n## Overview\n\nThis example provides two firmware variants:\n- **TX Variant (Node A)**: Transmits UWB packets periodically\n- **RX Variant (Node B)**: Receives UWB packets and collects statistics\n\nBoth variants communicate with the Orchestrator via RS-485 using UART.\n\n## Pin Configuration\n\n### UART Pins (RS-485 Communication)\n- **RX Pin**: GPIO 15 (UART_0_RX_PIN)\n- **TX Pin**: GPIO 19 (UART_0_TX_PIN)\n- **Baud Rate**: 115200\n\n**Note**: Pins 8 and 10 are used for:\n- **Pin 8**: DW3000_IRQ_Pin (interrupt pin for UWB chip)\n- **Pin 10**: DW3000_CS_Pin (SPI chip select for UWB chip)\n\nThe UART for RS-485 communication uses **pins 15 (RX) and 19 (TX)**, not pins 8 and 10.\n\n## Building and Flashing\n\n### Step 1: Build TX Variant (Node A)\n\n1. Edit &#96;Src/example_selection.h&#96;:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;c\n   // Comment out other examples:\n   //#define TEST_READING_DEV_ID\n   \n   // Uncomment TX variant:\n   #define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_TX\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n2. Edit &#96;Src/main.c&#96;:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;c\n   // Comment out other examples:\n   // extern int read_dev_id(void); read_dev_id();\n   \n   // Uncomment TX variant:\n   extern int orchestrator_tx(void); orchestrator_tx();\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n3. Build:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   make build\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n4. Flash to Node A board:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   make flash\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 2: Build RX Variant (Node B)\n\n1. Edit &#96;Src/example_selection.h&#96;:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;c\n   // Comment out TX variant:\n   //#define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_TX\n   \n   // Uncomment RX variant:\n   #define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_RX\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n2. Edit &#96;Src/main.c&#96;:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;c\n   // Comment out TX variant:\n   // extern int orchestrator_tx(void); orchestrator_tx();\n   \n   // Uncomment RX variant:\n   extern int orchestrator_rx(void); orchestrator_rx();\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n3. Build:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   make build\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n4. Flash to Node B board:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   make flash\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Important**: You need to build and flash **separately** for each board. The firmware is compiled with either TX or RX code, not both.\n\n## LED Behavior\n\nThe firmware uses &#96;dwt_setleds()&#96; which controls the **DW3000 UWB chip's internal LEDs**, not the board LEDs.\n\n- **On startup**: LEDs will blink once during initialization",

        "contents": "}\n\n# Function to flash firmware\nfunction Flash-Firmware {\n    param([string]$NodeType)\n    \n    Write-Host \"[FLASH] Flashing $NodeType node...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    Write-Host \"       Please ensure $NodeType board is connected and powered on\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n    \n    # Check if USB setup is needed (one-time check)\n    $usbipdCheck = Get-Command usbipd -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue\n    if ($usbipdCheck) {\n        $sharedCheck = wsl bash -c \"ls -la /dev/bus/usb 2&gt;&amp;1\" 2&gt;&amp;1\n        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or $sharedCheck -match \"No such file\") {\n            Write-Host \"[SETUP] USB device not shared with WSL2. Running setup...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n            Write-Host \"        (This may require admin ONCE for installation)\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n            &amp; \"$projectRoot\\setup-usb.ps1\"\n            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n                Write-Host \"[SETUP] USB setup failed.         "contents": "    Write-Host \"\"\n}\n\n# Main execution\ntry {\n    # Step 1: Build and Flash TX Node (unless skipped)\n    if (-not $SkipBuild) {\n        Write-Host \"[SETUP] Step 1/4: Building TX Node...\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n        Build-Firmware \"TX\"\n        Write-Host \"\"\n    }\n    \n    if (-not $SkipFlash) {\n        Write-Host \"[SETUP] Step 2/4: Flashing TX Node...\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n        Write-Host \"        Connect TX board (Node A) now and press any key to continue...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n        $null = $Host.UI.RawUI.ReadKey(\"NoEcho,IncludeKeyDown\")\n        Flash-Firmware \"TX\"\n        Write-Host \"\"\n    }\n    \n    # Step 2: Build and Flash RX Node (unless skipped)\n    if (-not $SkipBuild) {\n        Write-Host \"[SETUP] Step 3/4: Building RX Node...\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n        Build-Firmware \"RX\"\n        Write-Host \"\"\n    }\n    \n    if (-not $SkipFlash) {\n        Write-Host \"[SETUP] Step 4/4: Flashing RX Node...\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n        Write-Host \"        Connect RX board (Node B) now and press any key to continue...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n        $null = $Host.UI.RawUI.ReadKey(\"NoEcho,IncludeKeyDown\")\n        Flash-Firmware \"RX\"\n        Write-Host \"\"\n    }\n    \n    # Wait for boards to initialize\n    Write-Host \"[SETUP] Waiting for boards to initialize (5 seconds)...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    Start-Sleep -Seconds 5\n    Write-Host \"\"\n    \n    # Step 3: Run tests iteratively\n    for ($i = 1; $i -le $Iterations; $i++) {\n        Run-Test -IterationNumber $i\n        \n        # Wait between iterations (except last one)\n        if ($i -lt $Iterations) {\n            Write-Host \"Waiting 3 seconds before next iteration...\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n            Start-Sleep -Seconds 3\n        }\n    }\n    \n    Write-Host \"========================================\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n    Write-Host \"  All Tests Complete!\" -ForegroundColor Green\n    Write-Host \"========================================\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n    Write-Host \"\"\n    Write-Host \"Debug logs saved to: $logFile\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n    Write-Host \"\"\n    Write-Host \"To analyze logs, check:\" -ForegroundColor Yellow",

        "contents": "if ($isWSL) {\n    # Running in WSL2 - can mount USB devices directly\n    Write-Host \"Detected WSL2 environment - using USB device mounting...\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n    \n    # Check if USB devices are accessible\n    $usbCheck = wsl bash -c \"ls -la /dev/bus/usb 2&gt;&amp;1\"\n    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n        Write-Host \"WARNING: USB devices not accessible in WSL2.\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n        Write-Host \"You may need to install usbipd-win and share the USB device:\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n        Write-Host \"  1. Install: winget install usbipd-win\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n        Write-Host \"  2. List devices: usbipd list\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n        Write-Host \"  3. Attach device: usbipd attach --wsl --busid &lt;busid&gt;\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n    }\n    \n    docker run --privileged &#96;\n        -v /dev/bus/usb:/dev/bus/usb &#96;\n        -v \"${projectPath}/Output:/project/Output:ro\" &#96;\n        uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board &#96;\n        nrfjprog --force -f nrf52 --program /project/Output/Common/Exe/dw3000_api.hex --sectorerase --verify\n} else {\n    # Running in Windows PowerShell",

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": ".\\README-FLASH-NO-ADMIN.md",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {},
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 100
          }
        },
        "contents": "# Flashing Without Administrator Privileges\n\n## Quick Setup (One-Time)\n\nRun the setup script **once** (may require admin for installation only):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n.\\setup-usb.ps1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis will:\n\n1. Install &#96;usbipd-win&#96; if not already installed (may need admin)\n2. Find your J-Link device\n3. Share it with WSL2\n\n**After this one-time setup, you can flash without admin!**\n\n## How It Works\n\n1. **usbipd-win** shares USB devices from Windows to WSL2\n2. Once shared, WSL2 can access the device without admin privileges\n3. The flash script automatically uses WSL2 to flash via Docker\n\n## Usage\n\nAfter setup, just run:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n# Flash TX node\n.\\build-and-flash-tx.ps1\n\n# Flash RX node\n.\\build-and-flash-rx.ps1\n\n# Or use automated test\n.\\auto-test-tx-rx.ps1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**No admin privileges needed!**\n\n## If USB Device Changes\n\nIf you:\n\n- Unplug/replug the USB cable\n- Connect a different board\n- Restart your computer\n\nJust run the setup script again:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n.\\setup-usb.ps1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n### \"USB device not accessible\"\n\n- Run &#96;.\\setup-usb.ps1&#96; again\n- Check device is connected: &#96;usbipd list&#96;\n- Verify device is attached: Look for \"Shared\" status\n\n### \"usbipd-win not found\"\n\n- Install manually: &#96;winget install usbipd-win&#96;\n- Or run &#96;.\\setup-usb.ps1&#96; (it will install automatically)\n\n### \"Flash failed\"\n\n- Make sure board is powered on\n- Check USB cable connection\n- Verify Docker Desktop is running\n- Try unplugging and replugging USB\n\n## Manual Setup (Alternative)\n\nIf the automated script doesn't work:\n\n1. Install usbipd-win:\n\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n   winget install usbipd-win\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n2. List USB devices:\n\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n   usbipd list\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n3. Find J-Link device (look for SEGGER or bus ID)\n\n4. Attach to WSL2:\n\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n   usbipd attach --wsl --busid &lt;busid&gt;\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n5. Now flash normally - no admin needed!",

            "text": "- Run &#96;.\\setup-usb.ps1&#96; again",
            "lineNumber": 60
          },
          {
            "text": "- Check device is connected: &#96;usbipd list&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 61
          },
          {
            "text": "- Verify device is attached: Look for \"Shared\" status",
            "lineNumber": 62
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 63
          },
          {
            "text": "### \"usbipd-win not found\"",
            "lineNumber": 64
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 65
          },
          {
            "text": "- Install manually: &#96;winget install usbipd-win&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 66
          },
          {
            "text": "- Or run &#96;.\\setup-usb.ps1&#96; (it will install automatically)",
            "lineNumber": 67
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 68
          },
          {
            "text": "### \"Flash failed\"",
            "lineNumber": 69
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 70
          },
          {
            "text": "- Make sure board is powered on",
            "lineNumber": 71
          },
          {
            "text": "- Check USB cable connection",
            "lineNumber": 72
          },
          {
            "text": "- Verify Docker Desktop is running",
            "lineNumber": 73
          },
          {
            "text": "- Try unplugging and replugging USB",
            "lineNumber": 74
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 75
          },
          {
            "text": "## Manual Setup (Alternative)",
            "lineNumber": 76
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 77
          },
          {
            "text": "If the automated script doesn't work:",
            "lineNumber": 78
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 79
          },
          {
            "text": "1. Install usbipd-win:",
            "lineNumber": 80
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 81
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;powershell",
            "lineNumber": 82
          },
          {
            "text": "   winget install usbipd-win",
            "lineNumber": 83
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 84
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 85
          },
          {
            "text": "2. List USB devices:",
            "lineNumber": 86
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 87
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;powershell",
            "lineNumber": 88
          },
          {
            "text": "   usbipd list",
            "lineNumber": 89
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 90
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 91
          },
          {
            "text": "3. Find J-Link device (look for SEGGER or bus ID)",
            "lineNumber": 92
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 93
          },
          {
            "text": "4. Attach to WSL2:",
            "lineNumber": 94
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 95
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;powershell",
            "lineNumber": 96
          },
          {
            "text": "   usbipd attach --wsl --busid &lt;busid&gt;",
            "lineNumber": 97
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 98
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 99
          },
          {
            "text": "5. Now flash normally - no admin needed!",
            "lineNumber": 100
          }
        ]
      },
      "score": 0.3206113576889038

        "contents": "# Build and flash Node B (RX) in one command\n# Usage: .\\build-and-flash-rx.ps1\n\nWrite-Host \"=== Building and Flashing Node B (RX) ===\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n\n# Configure for RX\nWrite-Host \"&#96;n[1/3] Configuring for RX...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n&amp; \"$PSScriptRoot\\set-node-rx.ps1\"\n\nif ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n    Write-Host \"Failed to configure for RX\" -ForegroundColor Red\n    exit 1\n}\n\n# Build\nWrite-Host \"&#96;n[2/3] Building firmware...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n&amp; \"$PSScriptRoot\\build.ps1\"\n\nif ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n    Write-Host \"Build failed!\" -ForegroundColor Red\n    exit 1\n}\n\n# Flash\nWrite-Host \"&#96;n[3/3] Flashing to board...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n&amp; \"$PSScriptRoot\\flash.ps1\"\n\nif ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) {\n    Write-Host \"&#96;n=== Node B (RX) ready! ===\" -ForegroundColor Green\n} else {\n    Write-Host \"&#96;nFlash failed!\" -ForegroundColor Red\n    exit 1\n}",

        "contents": "# run SEGGER Embedded Studio's build system and output the results to ./Output/Common/Exe\nbuild: development-environment\n\tdocker run -v \"$$(pwd)\":/project uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board /usr/local/segger_embedded_studio_V5.42a/bin/emBuild -config \"Common\" /project/dw3000_api.emProject\n\n# remove all build outputs from the project (you may want to run this if you run into issues with stale interfaces)\nclean: development-environment\n\tdocker run -v \"$$(pwd)\":/project uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board /usr/local/segger_embedded_studio_V5.42a/bin/emBuild -config \"Common\" -clean /project/dw3000_api.emProject\n\n# program the DWM3001CDK using nrfjprog, communicating via USB and the on-board SEGGER J-Link\n# TODO: this uses --privileged and exposes all USB devices because SEGGER's libraries require it for some reason, it's not very good for security but it's the only way for now: https://wiki.segger.com/J-Link_Docker_Container\nflash: development-environment\n\tdocker run --privileged  -v /dev/bus/usb/:/dev/bus/usb -v \"$$(pwd)/Output\":/project/Output:ro uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board nrfjprog --force -f nrf52 --program /project/Output/Common/Exe/dw3000_api.hex --sectorerase --verify\n\n# read the RTT debug output of the DWM3001CDK using SEGGER J-Link RTT Logger, communicating via USB and the on-board SEGGER J-Link\n# TODO: this uses --privileged and exposes all USB devices because SEGGER's libraries require it for some reason, it's not very good for security but it's the only way for now: https://wiki.segger.com/J-Link_Docker_Container\nstream-debug-logs:\n\techo \"Run this command to view debug logs: tail -f Output/debug-log.txt\"\n\tdocker run --privileged -it -v /dev/bus/usb:/dev/bus/usb -v \"$$(pwd)/Output\":/project/Output uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board /usr/local/JLink_Linux_V792n_x86_64/JLinkRTTLogger -Device NRF52833_XXAA -if SWD -Speed 4000 -RTTChannel 0 /project/Output/debug-log.txt\n\n# auto-detect the DWM3001CDK's UART and open a minicom terminal connected to that UART, communicating via USB and the on-board SEGGER J-Link\nserial-terminal:\n\tDEVICE_FILE=$$(ls /dev/ttyUSB* /dev/ttyACM* 2&gt;/dev/null | while read -r dev; do if udevadm info -a -n $$dev | grep -q 'ATTRS{idVendor}==\"1915\"' &amp;&amp; udevadm info -a -n $$dev | grep -q 'ATTRS{idProduct}==\"520f\"'; then echo \"$$dev\"; break; fi; done); \\",

        "contents": "# PowerShell Scripts for DWM3001C Firmware\n\nThis directory contains PowerShell scripts for building and flashing the DWM3001C firmware on Windows.\n\n## Prerequisites\n\n1. **Docker Desktop** installed and running (with WSL2 backend recommended for USB access)\n2. **PowerShell** (comes with Windows 10/11)\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### Flash Node A (TX)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n.\\build-and-flash-tx.ps1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis will:\n1. Configure the firmware for TX variant\n2. Build the firmware\n3. Flash it to the connected board\n\n### Flash Node B (RX)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n.\\build-and-flash-rx.ps1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis will:\n1. Configure the firmware for RX variant\n2. Build the firmware\n3. Flash it to the connected board\n\n## Individual Scripts\n\n### Configuration Scripts\n\n- **&#96;set-node-tx.ps1&#96;** - Configure firmware for Node A (TX)\n- **&#96;set-node-rx.ps1&#96;** - Configure firmware for Node B (RX)\n\n### Build Scripts\n\n- **&#96;build.ps1&#96;** - Build the firmware\n- **&#96;clean.ps1&#96;** - Clean build outputs\n- **&#96;flash.ps1&#96;** - Flash firmware to connected board\n\n### Combined Scripts\n\n- **&#96;build-and-flash-tx.ps1&#96;** - Configure, build, and flash TX variant\n- **&#96;build-and-flash-rx.ps1&#96;** - Configure, build, and flash RX variant\n\n## Usage Examples\n\n### Step-by-step (Manual)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n# 1. Configure for TX\n.\\set-node-tx.ps1\n\n# 2. Build\n.\\build.ps1\n\n# 3. Flash\n.\\flash.ps1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### One-command (Automatic)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n# For Node A (TX)\n.\\build-and-flash-tx.ps1\n\n# For Node B (RX)\n.\\build-and-flash-rx.ps1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n### Docker Not Running\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nError: Docker is not running. Please start Docker Desktop.\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n**Solution:** Start Docker Desktop and wait for it to fully initialize.\n\n### USB Device Access Issues\nIf flashing fails with USB device errors:\n1. Ensure Docker Desktop is using WSL2 backend (Settings → General → Use WSL 2)\n2. Try unplugging and replugging the USB cable\n3. Ensure the board is connected to the J9 port (lower USB port)\n4. Check that the board is powered on\n\n### Build Fails\n- Run &#96;.\\clean.ps1&#96; to clean old build outputs\n- Check that Docker has enough resources allocated (Settings → Resources)",

          },
          {
            "text": "## Troubleshooting",
            "lineNumber": 77
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 78
          },
          {
            "text": "### Docker Not Running",
            "lineNumber": 79
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 80
          },
          {
            "text": "Error: Docker is not running. Please start Docker Desktop.",
            "lineNumber": 81
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 82
          },
          {
            "text": "**Solution:** Start Docker Desktop and wait for it to fully initialize.",
            "lineNumber": 83
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 84
          },
          {
            "text": "### USB Device Access Issues",
            "lineNumber": 85
          },
          {
            "text": "If flashing fails with USB device errors:",
            "lineNumber": 86
          },
          {
            "text": "1. Ensure Docker Desktop is using WSL2 backend (Settings → General → Use WSL 2)",
            "lineNumber": 87
          },
          {
            "text": "2. Try unplugging and replugging the USB cable",
            "lineNumber": 88
          },
          {
            "text": "3. Ensure the board is connected to the J9 port (lower USB port)",
            "lineNumber": 89
          },
          {
            "text": "4. Check that the board is powered on",
            "lineNumber": 90
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 91
          },
          {
            "text": "### Build Fails",
            "lineNumber": 92
          },
          {
            "text": "- Run &#96;.\\clean.ps1&#96; to clean old build outputs",
            "lineNumber": 93
          },
          {
            "text": "- Check that Docker has enough resources allocated (Settings → Resources)",
            "lineNumber": 94
          }
        ]

        "contents": "class WebServer {\n\n\n  /**\n   * Start server\n   */\n  async start() {\n    const webConfig = this.config.getWebConfig();\n    const port = webConfig.port || 5000;\n    const host = webConfig.host || \"0.0.0.0\";\n\n    // Connect to nodes\n    try {\n      console.log(\"Connecting to Node A...\");\n      try {\n        await this.nodeA.connect();\n        console.log(\"Node A connected\");\n\n        // Send PING first to verify basic communication\n        console.log(\"Pinging Node A...\");\n        try {\n          const pingResult = await this.nodeA.ping();\n          if (pingResult) {\n            console.log(\"✓ Node A PING successful\");\n          } else {\n            console.warn(\n              \"⚠️  Node A PING failed - firmware may not be responding\"\n            );\n          }\n        } catch (pingError) {\n          console.warn(&#96;⚠️  Node A PING error: ${pingError.message}&#96;);\n        }\n\n        // Verify Node A firmware type\n        const nodeAType = await this.nodeA.getFirmwareNodeType();\n        if (nodeAType) {\n          console.log(&#96;Node A firmware type: ${nodeAType} (expected: TX)&#96;);\n          if (nodeAType !== \"A\") {\n            console.warn(\n              &#96;⚠️  WARNING: Node A firmware is type '${nodeAType}' but expected 'TX'!&#96;\n            );\n            console.warn(\n              &#96;⚠️  Rebuild Node A (TX) with: .\\\\set-node-tx.ps1 &amp;&amp; .\\\\build.ps1 &amp;&amp; .\\\\flash.ps1&#96;\n            );\n          }\n        } else {\n          console.warn(\n            &#96;⚠️  WARNING: Could not determine Node A firmware type (NODE_TYPE command failed or returned null)&#96;\n          );\n          console.warn(\n            &#96;⚠️  This indicates Node A firmware may not be running the orchestrator example&#96;\n          );\n          console.warn(\n            &#96;⚠️  Rebuild and flash Node A (TX) with: .\\\\build-and-flash-tx.ps1&#96;\n          );\n          console.warn(\n            &#96;⚠️  Or use: .\\\\set-node-tx.ps1 &amp;&amp; .\\\\build.ps1 &amp;&amp; .\\\\flash.ps1&#96;\n          );\n        }\n      } catch (nodeAError) {\n        console.error(&#96;Failed to connect to Node A: ${nodeAError.message}&#96;);\n        console.log(\"Node A will not be available, but server will continue\");\n  }",

        "contents": "# Automated Build, Flash, and Test Script with Iteration Support\n# Usage: .\\auto-test-tx-rx.ps1 [iterations]\n# Example: .\\auto-test-tx-rx.ps1 3  (runs 3 iterations)\n\nparam(\n    [int]$Iterations = 1,\n    [int]$TestDurationSeconds = 30,\n    [switch]$SkipBuild = $false,\n    [switch]$SkipFlash = $false\n)\n\n$ErrorActionPreference = \"Stop\"\n$projectRoot = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path\n$logFile = Join-Path $projectRoot \".cursor\\debug.log\"\n\nWrite-Host \"========================================\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\nWrite-Host \"  UWB TX/RX Automated Test Script\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\nWrite-Host \"  Iterations: $Iterations\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\nWrite-Host \"========================================\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\nWrite-Host \"\"\nWrite-Host \"Serial Ports Configuration:\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\nWrite-Host \"  Node A (TX): COM17\" -ForegroundColor White\nWrite-Host \"  Node B (RX): COM18\" -ForegroundColor White\nWrite-Host \"\"\nWrite-Host \"Make sure both boards are connected via RS-485 to these COM ports\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\nWrite-Host \"\"\n\n# Function to clear debug log\nfunction Clear-DebugLog {\n    if (Test-Path $logFile) {\n        Remove-Item $logFile -Force\n        Write-Host \"[LOG] Cleared debug log\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n    }\n}\n\n# Function to build firmware\nfunction Build-Firmware {\n    param([string]$NodeType)\n    \n    Write-Host \"[BUILD] Building $NodeType firmware...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    \n    if ($NodeType -eq \"TX\") {\n        &amp; \"$projectRoot\\set-node-tx.ps1\"\n    } else {\n        &amp; \"$projectRoot\\set-node-rx.ps1\"\n    }\n    \n    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n        throw \"Failed to configure for $NodeType\"\n    }\n    \n    &amp; \"$projectRoot\\build.ps1\"\n    \n    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n        throw \"Build failed for $NodeType\"\n    }\n    \n    Write-Host \"[BUILD] $NodeType build successful\" -ForegroundColor Green\n}\n\n# Function to flash firmware\nfunction Flash-Firmware {\n    param([string]$NodeType)\n    \n    Write-Host \"[FLASH] Flashing $NodeType node...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow",

        "contents": "# Test TX/RX Communication Script (Legacy - use auto-test-tx-rx.ps1 instead)\n# This script builds, flashes both nodes, and runs the Orchestrator test\n\nWrite-Host \"=== UWB TX/RX Test Script ===\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\nWrite-Host \"NOTE: Consider using auto-test-tx-rx.ps1 for better automation\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\nWrite-Host \"\"\n\n# Step 1: Build and Flash TX Node\nWrite-Host \"[1/4] Building and Flashing TX Node (Node A)...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n&amp; \"$PSScriptRoot\\build-and-flash-tx.ps1\"\nif ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n    Write-Host \"Failed to flash TX node!\" -ForegroundColor Red\n    exit 1\n}\nWrite-Host \"TX Node flashed successfully\" -ForegroundColor Green\nWrite-Host \"\"\n\n# Step 2: Build and Flash RX Node  \nWrite-Host \"[2/4] Building and Flashing RX Node (Node B)...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n&amp; \"$PSScriptRoot\\build-and-flash-rx.ps1\"\nif ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n    Write-Host \"Failed to flash RX node!\" -ForegroundColor Red\n    exit 1\n}\nWrite-Host \"RX Node flashed successfully\" -ForegroundColor Green\nWrite-Host \"\"\n\n# Step 3: Wait for boards to initialize\nWrite-Host \"[3/4] Waiting for boards to initialize (5 seconds)...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\nStart-Sleep -Seconds 5\n\n# Step 4: Run Orchestrator test\nWrite-Host \"[4/4] Starting Orchestrator test...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\nWrite-Host \"\"\nWrite-Host \"Make sure:\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\nWrite-Host \"  - Both boards are powered on\" -ForegroundColor White\nWrite-Host \"  - RS-485 connections are correct\" -ForegroundColor White\nWrite-Host \"  - Serial ports are configured in Orchestrator/config/settings.yaml\" -ForegroundColor White\nWrite-Host \"\"\nWrite-Host \"Starting Orchestrator...\" -ForegroundColor Green\nWrite-Host \"\"\n\nSet-Location Orchestrator\nnpm start",

        "contents": "# Configure firmware for Node A (TX variant)\n# Usage: .\\set-node-tx.ps1\n\n$ErrorActionPreference = \"Stop\"\n\ntry {\n    Write-Host \"Configuring firmware for Node A (TX)...\" -ForegroundColor Green\n\n    $projectRoot = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path\n    $exampleSelectionFile = Join-Path $projectRoot \"Src\\example_selection.h\"\n    $mainFile = Join-Path $projectRoot \"Src\\main.c\"\n\n    # Verify files exist\n    if (-not (Test-Path $exampleSelectionFile)) {\n        Write-Host \"Error: $exampleSelectionFile not found!\" -ForegroundColor Red\n        exit 1\n    }\n    if (-not (Test-Path $mainFile)) {\n        Write-Host \"Error: $mainFile not found!\" -ForegroundColor Red\n        exit 1\n    }\n\n    # Read example_selection.h\n    $content = Get-Content $exampleSelectionFile -Raw\n\n    # Comment out TEST_READING_DEV_ID\n    $content = $content -replace '(?m)^#define TEST_READING_DEV_ID', '//#define TEST_READING_DEV_ID'\n\n    # Uncomment TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_TX\n    $content = $content -replace '(?m)^//#define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_TX', '#define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_TX'\n\n    # Comment out TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_RX\n    $content = $content -replace '(?m)^#define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_RX', '//#define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_RX'\n\n    # Write back\n    Set-Content -Path $exampleSelectionFile -Value $content -NoNewline\n\n    # Read main.c\n    $mainContent = Get-Content $mainFile -Raw\n\n    # Comment out read_dev_id\n    $mainContent = $mainContent -replace '(?m)^(\\s*)extern int read_dev_id\\(void\\); read_dev_id\\(\\);', '$1// extern int read_dev_id(void); read_dev_id();'\n\n    # Comment out orchestrator_rx\n    $mainContent = $mainContent -replace '(?m)^(\\s*)// extern int orchestrator_rx\\(void\\); orchestrator_rx\\(\\);', '$1// extern int orchestrator_rx(void); orchestrator_rx();'\n    $mainContent = $mainContent -replace '(?m)^(\\s*)extern int orchestrator_rx\\(void\\); orchestrator_rx\\(\\);', '$1// extern int orchestrator_rx(void); orchestrator_rx();'\n\n    # Uncomment orchestrator_tx\n    $mainContent = $mainContent -replace '(?m)^(\\s*)// extern int orchestrator_tx\\(void\\); orchestrator_tx\\(\\);', '$1extern int orchestrator_tx(void); orchestrator_tx();'\n\n    # Write back\n    Set-Content -Path $mainFile -Value $mainContent -NoNewline",

        "contents": "/*! ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n *  @file    read_dev_id.c\n *  @brief   This example just read DW IC's device ID. It can be used to verify\n *           the SPI comms are working correctly.\n *\n * @attention\n *\n * Copyright 2018 - 2021 (c) Decawave Ltd, Dublin, Ireland.\n *\n * All rights reserved.\n *\n * @author Decawave\n */\n\n#include \"deca_probe_interface.h\"\n#include &lt;deca_device_api.h&gt;\n#include &lt;example_selection.h&gt;\n#include &lt;port.h&gt;\n#include &lt;stdio.h&gt;\n\n#if defined(TEST_READING_DEV_ID)\n\nextern void test_run_info(unsigned char *data);\n\n/* Example application name and version to display on LCD screen/VCOM port. */\n#define APP_NAME \"READ DEV ID      \"\n\n/**\n * Application entry point.\n */\nint read_dev_id(void)\n{\n    int err;\n    uint32_t dev_id;\n\n    bsp_board_led_on(0);\n\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    bsp_board_led_on(1);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    bsp_board_led_on(2);\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    bsp_board_led_on(3);\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC, or could wait for SPIRDY event)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n\n    dev_id = dwt_readdevid();\n\n\n    /* Reads and validate device ID returns DWT_ERROR if it does not match expected else DWT_SUCCESS */\n    if ((err = dwt_check_dev_id()) == DWT_SUCCESS)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"DEV ID OK\");\n    }\n    else\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"DEV ID FAILED\");\n    }\n\n    return err;\n}\n\n#endif\n/*****************************************************************************************************************************************************\n * NOTES:\n ****************************************************************************************************************************************************/",

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": ".\\Src\\examples\\ex_21_orchestrator\\README.md",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {
            "line": 86
          },
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 143
          }
        },
        "contents": "## LED Behavior\n\nThe firmware uses &#96;dwt_setleds()&#96; which controls the **DW3000 UWB chip's internal LEDs**, not the board LEDs.\n\n- **On startup**: LEDs will blink once during initialization\n- **During operation**: LEDs may flash during UWB activity (TX/RX events)\n- **Board LEDs**: The DWM3001CDK board LEDs (LED_1, LED_2, LED_3, LED_4) are not directly controlled by this firmware\n\n## RS-485 Connection\n\nConnect the RS-485 transceiver to:\n- **A+**: Connect to RS-485 A+ line\n- **B-**: Connect to RS-485 B- line  \n- **GND**: Connect to ground\n- **UART RX**: Connect to GPIO 15\n- **UART TX**: Connect to GPIO 19\n- **DE/RE**: Connect to control RS-485 direction (if needed)\n\nThe firmware communicates at **115200 baud** with the Orchestrator.\n\n## Testing\n\nAfter flashing:\n\n1. **Connect RS-485** from each board to the Orchestrator (RPi 5)\n2. **Power on** both boards\n3. **Run the Orchestrator**:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   cd Orchestrator\n   npm start\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe Orchestrator will:\n- Send &#96;PNG&#96; (PING) commands to verify connectivity\n- Configure both nodes with &#96;CFG&#96; commands\n- Start tests with &#96;STRT&#96; commands\n- Collect statistics with &#96;STAT&#96; commands\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n### UART Not Working\n- Verify pins 15 (RX) and 19 (TX) are connected correctly\n- Check RS-485 transceiver wiring (A+, B-, GND)\n- Verify baud rate is 115200\n- Check that RS-485 termination resistors are present (120Ω at each end)\n\n### Wrong Variant Flashed\n- Make sure you build and flash separately for each board\n- Check &#96;example_selection.h&#96; has the correct &#96;#define&#96; uncommented\n- Check &#96;main.c&#96; has the correct function call uncommented\n\n### LEDs Not Flashing\n- The firmware controls DW3000 internal LEDs, not board LEDs\n- Board LEDs may not flash unless you add code to control them\n- Check UWB activity with the Orchestrator's statistics",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "## LED Behavior",

            "text": "- **A+**: Connect to RS-485 A+ line",

            "text": "- **UART TX**: Connect to GPIO 19",
            "lineNumber": 103

          {
            "text": "- **DE/RE**: Connect to control RS-485 direction (if needed)",
            "lineNumber": 104
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 105
          },
          {
            "text": "The firmware communicates at **115200 baud** with the Orchestrator.",
            "lineNumber": 106
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 107
          },
          {
            "text": "## Testing",
            "lineNumber": 108
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 109
          },
          {
            "text": "After flashing:",
            "lineNumber": 110

            "lineNumber": 111

          {
            "text": "1. **Connect RS-485** from each board to the Orchestrator (RPi 5)",

            "lineNumber": 113

          {
            "text": "3. **Run the Orchestrator**:",

          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash",
            "lineNumber": 115
          },
          {
            "text": "   cd Orchestrator",
            "lineNumber": 116

          {
            "text": "   npm start",
            "lineNumber": 117

            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 118

            "lineNumber": 119

          {
            "text": "The Orchestrator will:",
            "lineNumber": 120

            "text": "- Start tests with &#96;STRT&#96; commands",

            "text": "- Collect statistics with &#96;STAT&#96; commands",
            "lineNumber": 124
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 125
          },
          {
            "text": "## Troubleshooting",
            "lineNumber": 126

          {
            "lineNumber": 127
          },
          {
            "text": "### UART Not Working",
            "lineNumber": 128

          {
            "text": "- Verify pins 15 (RX) and 19 (TX) are connected correctly",
            "lineNumber": 129

        "contents": "# auto-detect the DWM3001CDK's UART and open a minicom terminal connected to that UART, communicating via USB and the on-board SEGGER J-Link\nserial-terminal:\n\tDEVICE_FILE=$$(ls /dev/ttyUSB* /dev/ttyACM* 2&gt;/dev/null | while read -r dev; do if udevadm info -a -n $$dev | grep -q 'ATTRS{idVendor}==\"1915\"' &amp;&amp; udevadm info -a -n $$dev | grep -q 'ATTRS{idProduct}==\"520f\"'; then echo \"$$dev\"; break; fi; done); \\\n\tif [ -z \"$$DEVICE_FILE\" ]; then echo \"Device not found\"; exit 1; fi; \\\n\tminicom --device $$DEVICE_FILE\n\n# open a bash shell in the development environment with all of the development tools available\ndevelopment-shell: development-environment\n\tdocker run -it -v \"$$(pwd)\":/project uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board\n\n# build the development environment, reusing the existing build in the docker cache if available\ndevelopment-environment:\n\tdocker build -t uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board - &lt; Dockerfile  # build without sending any build context\n\n# export the development environment to the tar archive \"./uberi_qorvo-nrf52833-board.tar\", for offline archival purposes\nsave-development-environment:\n\tdocker image save -o uberi_qorvo-nrf52833-board.tar uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board\n\n# load a previously exported development environment from the tar archive \"./uberi_qorvo-nrf52833-board.tar\"\nload-development-environment:\n\tdocker image load -i uberi_qorvo-nrf52833-board.tar",

## Fixed: Board selection for TX/RX flashing

### Problem
Both `build-and-flash-tx.ps1` and `build-and-flash-rx.ps1` were flashing the same board because `flash.ps1` always selected the first J-Link device (`Select-Object -First 1`).

### Solution
Added board selection logic to `flash.ps1`:

1. Parameters:
   - `-BusId <busid>` - Specify bus ID directly
   - `-ComPort <comport>` - Specify COM port
   - `-NodeType TX|RX` - Show menu for TX/RX selection

2. Device selection menu:
   - Lists all J-Link devices with bus ID, COM port, and attachment status
   - Prompts user to select which board to flash
   - Shows menu when `-NodeType` is used or multiple devices are found

3. Updated build scripts:
   - `build-and-flash-tx.ps1` now calls `flash.ps1 -NodeType TX`
   - `build-and-flash-rx.ps1` now calls `flash.ps1 -NodeType RX`

### Usage

When you run:
- `.\build-and-flash-tx.ps1` - Shows menu to select TX board
- `.\build-and-flash-rx.ps1` - Shows menu to select RX board

Or directly:
- `.\flash.ps1 -BusId 4-1` - Flash specific bus ID
- `.\flash.ps1 -ComPort COM11` - Flash specific COM port
- `.\flash.ps1 -NodeType TX` - Show menu for TX board

The script now prompts you to select which board to flash, preventing both scripts from flashing the same board.

                             read addresses from both the external memory
                             device and the nRF device.

     --halt                  Halts the CPU core.

     --run [--pc &lt;pc_addr&gt; --sp &lt;sp_addr&gt;]          Starts the CPU. If --pc and
                             --sp options are given, the pc_addr and sp_addr
--
     --readuicr &lt;file&gt;       Reads the device UICR and stores it in the given
                             file name. Can be combined with --readram,
                             --readcode and --readqspi. If combined, only one
                             instruction can provide a file name.
                             Supported output formats are .hex, .ihex, .elf,
                             .axf, and .bin. A valid format must be specified
--
     --readcode &lt;file&gt;       Reads the device flash and stores it in the given
                             file name. Can be combined with --readuicr,
                             --readram and --readqspi. If combined, only one
                             instruction can provide a file name.
                             Supported output formats are .hex, .ihex, .elf,
                             .axf, and .bin. A valid format must be specified
--
     --readram &lt;file&gt;        Reads the device ram and stores it in the given
                             file name. Can be combined with --readuicr,
                             --readcode and --readqspi. If combined, only one
                             instruction can provide a file name.
                             Supported output formats are .hex, .ihex, .elf,
                             .axf, and .bin. A valid format must be specified
--
    --readficr &lt;file&gt;        Reads the device FICR and stores it into the provided
                             file name. Can be combined with --readuicr, --readram and
                             --readcode. If combined, only one instruction can
                             provide a file name.
                             Supported output formats are .hex, .ihex, .elf,
                             .axf, and .bin. A valid format must be specified
--
     --coprocessor &lt;coprocessor&gt;                    Connects the device to the
                             selected coprocessor. Valid arguments are 
                             CP_APPLICATION and CP_NETWORK. 
                             If --coprocessor option is not used,
                             CP_APPLICATION will be the target of the other
                             operation. Must be combined with another command.

        "contents": "# Flash script for DWM3001C firmware\n# Usage: .\\flash.ps1 [-BusId &lt;busid&gt;] [-ComPort &lt;comport&gt;] [-NodeType TX|RX]\n# Examples:\n#   .\\flash.ps1 -BusId 4-1\n#   .\\flash.ps1 -ComPort COM11\n#   .\\flash.ps1 -NodeType TX\n# Note: Requires Docker Desktop with WSL2 backend for USB device access\n\nparam(\n    [string]$BusId = \"\",\n    [string]$ComPort = \"\",\n    [string]$NodeType = \"\"  # TX or RX\n)\n\nWrite-Host \"Flashing DWM3001C firmware...\" -ForegroundColor Green\n\n# Get the project root directory\n$projectRoot = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path\n$projectPath = $projectRoot.Replace('\\', '/')\n\n# Check if hex file exists\n$hexFile = Join-Path $projectRoot \"Output\\Common\\Exe\\dw3000_api.hex\"\nif (-not (Test-Path $hexFile)) {\n    Write-Host \"Error: Firmware not found at $hexFile\" -ForegroundColor Red\n    Write-Host \"Please run .\\build.ps1 first to build the firmware.\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    exit 1\n}\n\n# Ensure Docker is running\n$dockerRunning = docker info 2&gt;&amp;1\nif ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n    Write-Host \"Error: Docker is not running.         "contents": "# run SEGGER Embedded Studio's build system and output the results to ./Output/Common/Exe\nbuild: development-environment\n\tdocker run -v \"$$(pwd)\":/project uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board /usr/local/segger_embedded_studio_V5.42a/bin/emBuild -config \"Common\" /project/dw3000_api.emProject\n\n# remove all build outputs from the project (you may want to run this if you run into issues with stale interfaces)\nclean: development-environment\n\tdocker run -v \"$$(pwd)\":/project uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board /usr/local/segger_embedded_studio_V5.42a/bin/emBuild -config \"Common\" -clean /project/dw3000_api.emProject\n\n# program the DWM3001CDK using nrfjprog, communicating via USB and the on-board SEGGER J-Link\n# TODO: this uses --privileged and exposes all USB devices because SEGGER's libraries require it for some reason, it's not very good for security but it's the only way for now: https://wiki.segger.com/J-Link_Docker_Container\nflash: development-environment\n\tdocker run --privileged  -v /dev/bus/usb/:/dev/bus/usb -v \"$$(pwd)/Output\":/project/Output:ro uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board nrfjprog --force -f nrf52 --program /project/Output/Common/Exe/dw3000_api.hex --sectorerase --verify\n\n# read the RTT debug output of the DWM3001CDK using SEGGER J-Link RTT Logger, communicating via USB and the on-board SEGGER J-Link\n# TODO: this uses --privileged and exposes all USB devices because SEGGER's libraries require it for some reason, it's not very good for security but it's the only way for now: https://wiki.segger.com/J-Link_Docker_Container\nstream-debug-logs:\n\techo \"Run this command to view debug logs: tail -f Output/debug-log.txt\"\n\tdocker run --privileged -it -v /dev/bus/usb:/dev/bus/usb -v \"$$(pwd)/Output\":/project/Output uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board /usr/local/JLink_Linux_V792n_x86_64/JLinkRTTLogger -Device NRF52833_XXAA -if SWD -Speed 4000 -RTTChannel 0 /project/Output/debug-log.txt\n\n# auto-detect the DWM3001CDK's UART and open a minicom terminal connected to that UART, communicating via USB and the on-board SEGGER J-Link\nserial-terminal:\n\tDEVICE_FILE=$$(ls /dev/ttyUSB* /dev/ttyACM* 2&gt;/dev/null | while read -r dev; do if udevadm info -a -n $$dev | grep -q 'ATTRS{idVendor}==\"1915\"' &amp;&amp; udevadm info -a -n $$dev | grep -q 'ATTRS{idProduct}==\"520f\"'; then echo \"$$dev\"; break; fi; done); \\",
        "signatures": {},

        "contents": "}\n\n# Function to flash firmware\nfunction Flash-Firmware {\n    param([string]$NodeType)\n    \n    Write-Host \"[FLASH] Flashing $NodeType node...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    Write-Host \"       Please ensure $NodeType board is connected and powered on\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n    \n    # Check if USB setup is needed (one-time check)\n    $usbipdCheck = Get-Command usbipd -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue\n    if ($usbipdCheck) {\n        $sharedCheck = wsl bash -c \"ls -la /dev/bus/usb 2&gt;&amp;1\" 2&gt;&amp;1\n        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or $sharedCheck -match \"No such file\") {\n            Write-Host \"[SETUP] USB device not shared with WSL2. Running setup...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n            Write-Host \"        (This may require admin ONCE for installation)\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n            &amp; \"$projectRoot\\setup-usb.ps1\"\n            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n                Write-Host \"[SETUP] USB setup failed. Please run manually:\" -ForegroundColor Red\n                Write-Host \"        .\\setup-usb.ps1\" -ForegroundColor White\n                throw \"USB setup required\"\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    \n    &amp; \"$projectRoot\\flash.ps1\"\n    \n    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n        throw \"Flash failed for $NodeType\"\n    }\n    \n    Write-Host \"[FLASH] $NodeType flash successful\" -ForegroundColor Green\n}\n\n# Function to run test\nfunction Run-Test {\n    param([int]$IterationNumber)",

        "contents": "# Build and flash Node B (RX) in one command\n# Usage: .\\build-and-flash-rx.ps1\n\nWrite-Host \"=== Building and Flashing Node B (RX) ===\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n\n# Configure for RX\nWrite-Host \"&#96;n[1/3] Configuring for RX...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n&amp; \"$PSScriptRoot\\set-node-rx.ps1\"\n\nif ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n    Write-Host \"Failed to configure for RX\" -ForegroundColor Red\n    exit 1\n}\n\n# Build\nWrite-Host \"&#96;n[2/3] Building firmware...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n&amp; \"$PSScriptRoot\\build.ps1\"\n\nif ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n    Write-Host \"Build failed!\" -ForegroundColor Red\n    exit 1\n}\n\n# Flash\nWrite-Host \"&#96;n[3/3] Flashing to board...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\nWrite-Host \"Select the RX board (Node B) from the list below:\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n&amp; \"$PSScriptRoot\\flash.ps1\" -NodeType RX\n\nif ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) {\n    Write-Host \"&#96;n=== Node B (RX) ready! ===\" -ForegroundColor Green\n} else {\n    Write-Host \"&#96;nFlash failed!\" -ForegroundColor Red\n    exit 1\n}",

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": ".\\README-FLASH-NO-ADMIN.md",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {},
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 100
          }
        },
        "contents": "# Flashing Without Administrator Privileges\n\n## Quick Setup (One-Time)\n\nRun the setup script **once** (may require admin for installation only):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n.\\setup-usb.ps1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis will:\n\n1. Install &#96;usbipd-win&#96; if not already installed (may need admin)\n2. Find your J-Link device\n3. Share it with WSL2\n\n**After this one-time setup, you can flash without admin!**\n\n## How It Works\n\n1. **usbipd-win** shares USB devices from Windows to WSL2\n2. Once shared, WSL2 can access the device without admin privileges\n3. The flash script automatically uses WSL2 to flash via Docker\n\n## Usage\n\nAfter setup, just run:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n# Flash TX node\n.\\build-and-flash-tx.ps1\n\n# Flash RX node\n.\\build-and-flash-rx.ps1\n\n# Or use automated test\n.\\auto-test-tx-rx.ps1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**No admin privileges needed!**\n\n## If USB Device Changes\n\nIf you:\n\n- Unplug/replug the USB cable\n- Connect a different board\n- Restart your computer\n\nJust run the setup script again:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n.\\setup-usb.ps1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n### \"USB device not accessible\"\n\n- Run &#96;.\\setup-usb.ps1&#96; again\n- Check device is connected: &#96;usbipd list&#96;\n- Verify device is attached: Look for \"Shared\" status\n\n### \"usbipd-win not found\"\n\n- Install manually: &#96;winget install usbipd-win&#96;\n- Or run &#96;.\\setup-usb.ps1&#96; (it will install automatically)\n\n### \"Flash failed\"\n\n- Make sure board is powered on\n- Check USB cable connection\n- Verify Docker Desktop is running\n- Try unplugging and replugging USB\n\n## Manual Setup (Alternative)\n\nIf the automated script doesn't work:\n\n1. Install usbipd-win:\n\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n   winget install usbipd-win\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n2. List USB devices:\n\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n   usbipd list\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n3. Find J-Link device (look for SEGGER or bus ID)\n\n4. Attach to WSL2:\n\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n   usbipd attach --wsl --busid &lt;busid&gt;\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n5. Now flash normally - no admin needed!",
        "signatures": {},
