            "line": 190
          }
        },
        "contents": "    Write-Host \"\"\n}\n\n# Main execution\ntry {\n    # Step 1: Build and Flash TX Node (unless skipped)\n    if (-not $SkipBuild) {\n        Write-Host \"[SETUP] Step 1/4: Building TX Node...\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n        Build-Firmware \"TX\"\n        Write-Host \"\"\n    }\n    \n    if (-not $SkipFlash) {\n        Write-Host \"[SETUP] Step 2/4: Flashing TX Node...\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n        Write-Host \"        Connect TX board (Node A) now and press any key to continue...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n        $null = $Host.UI.RawUI.ReadKey(\"NoEcho,IncludeKeyDown\")\n        Flash-Firmware \"TX\"\n        Write-Host \"\"\n    }\n    \n    # Step 2: Build and Flash RX Node (unless skipped)\n    if (-not $SkipBuild) {\n        Write-Host \"[SETUP] Step 3/4: Building RX Node...\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n        Build-Firmware \"RX\"\n        Write-Host \"\"\n    }\n    \n    if (-not $SkipFlash) {\n        Write-Host \"[SETUP] Step 4/4: Flashing RX Node...\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n        Write-Host \"        Connect RX board (Node B) now and press any key to continue...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n        $null = $Host.UI.RawUI.ReadKey(\"NoEcho,IncludeKeyDown\")\n        Flash-Firmware \"RX\"\n        Write-Host \"\"\n    }\n    \n    # Wait for boards to initialize\n    Write-Host \"[SETUP] Waiting for boards to initialize (5 seconds)...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    Start-Sleep -Seconds 5\n    Write-Host \"\"\n    \n    # Step 3: Run tests iteratively\n    for ($i = 1; $i -le $Iterations; $i++) {\n        Run-Test -IterationNumber $i\n        \n        # Wait between iterations (except last one)\n        if ($i -lt $Iterations) {\n            Write-Host \"Waiting 3 seconds before next iteration...\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n            Start-Sleep -Seconds 3\n        }\n    }\n    \n    Write-Host \"========================================\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n    Write-Host \"  All Tests Complete!\" -ForegroundColor Green\n    Write-Host \"========================================\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n    Write-Host \"\"\n    Write-Host \"Debug logs saved to: $logFile\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n    Write-Host \"\"\n    Write-Host \"To analyze logs, check:\" -ForegroundColor Yellow",

        "contents": "# Automated Build, Flash, and Test Script with Iteration Support\n# Usage: .\\auto-test-tx-rx.ps1 [iterations]\n# Example: .\\auto-test-tx-rx.ps1 3  (runs 3 iterations)\n\nparam(\n    [int]$Iterations = 1,\n    [int]$TestDurationSeconds = 30,\n    [switch]$SkipBuild = $false,\n    [switch]$SkipFlash = $false\n)\n\n$ErrorActionPreference = \"Stop\"\n$projectRoot = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path\n$logFile = Join-Path $projectRoot \".cursor\\debug.log\"\n\nWrite-Host \"========================================\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\nWrite-Host \"  UWB TX/RX Automated Test Script\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\nWrite-Host \"  Iterations: $Iterations\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\nWrite-Host \"========================================\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\nWrite-Host \"\"\nWrite-Host \"Serial Ports Configuration:\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\nWrite-Host \"  Node A (TX): COM17\" -ForegroundColor White\nWrite-Host \"  Node B (RX): COM18\" -ForegroundColor White\nWrite-Host \"\"\nWrite-Host \"Make sure both boards are connected via RS-485 to these COM ports\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\nWrite-Host \"\"\n\n# Function to clear debug log\nfunction Clear-DebugLog {\n    if (Test-Path $logFile) {\n        Remove-Item $logFile -Force\n        Write-Host \"[LOG] Cleared debug log\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n    }\n}\n\n# Function to build firmware\nfunction Build-Firmware {\n    param([string]$NodeType)\n    \n    Write-Host \"[BUILD] Building $NodeType firmware...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    \n    if ($NodeType -eq \"TX\") {\n        &amp; \"$projectRoot\\set-node-tx.ps1\"\n    } else {\n        &amp; \"$projectRoot\\set-node-rx.ps1\"\n    }\n    \n    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n        throw \"Failed to configure for $NodeType\"\n    }\n    \n    &amp; \"$projectRoot\\build.ps1\"\n    \n    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n        throw \"Build failed for $NodeType\"\n    }\n    \n    Write-Host \"[BUILD] $NodeType build successful\" -ForegroundColor Green\n}\n\n# Function to flash firmware\nfunction Flash-Firmware {\n    param([string]$NodeType)\n    \n    Write-Host \"[FLASH] Flashing $NodeType node...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow",

        "contents": "class WebServer {\n\n\n  /**\n   * Start server\n   */\n  async start() {\n    const webConfig = this.config.getWebConfig();\n    const port = webConfig.port || 5000;\n    const host = webConfig.host || \"0.0.0.0\";\n\n    // Connect to nodes\n    try {\n      console.log(\"Connecting to Node A...\");\n      try {\n        await this.nodeA.connect();\n        console.log(\"Node A connected\");\n\n        // Send PING first to verify basic communication\n        console.log(\"Pinging Node A...\");\n        try {\n          const pingResult = await this.nodeA.ping();\n          if (pingResult) {\n            console.log(\"✓ Node A PING successful\");\n          } else {\n            console.warn(\n              \"⚠️  Node A PING failed - firmware may not be responding\"\n            );\n          }\n        } catch (pingError) {\n          console.warn(&#96;⚠️  Node A PING error: ${pingError.message}&#96;);\n        }\n\n        // Verify Node A firmware type\n        const nodeAType = await this.nodeA.getFirmwareNodeType();\n        if (nodeAType) {\n          console.log(&#96;Node A firmware type: ${nodeAType} (expected: TX)&#96;);\n          if (nodeAType !== \"A\") {\n            console.warn(\n              &#96;⚠️  WARNING: Node A firmware is type '${nodeAType}' but expected 'TX'!&#96;\n            );\n            console.warn(\n              &#96;⚠️  Rebuild Node A (TX) with: .\\\\set-node-tx.ps1 &amp;&amp; .\\\\build.ps1 &amp;&amp; .\\\\flash.ps1&#96;\n            );\n          }\n        } else {\n          console.warn(\n            &#96;⚠️  WARNING: Could not determine Node A firmware type (NODE_TYPE command failed or returned null)&#96;\n          );\n          console.warn(\n            &#96;⚠️  This indicates Node A firmware may not be running the orchestrator example&#96;\n          );\n          console.warn(\n            &#96;⚠️  Rebuild and flash Node A (TX) with: .\\\\build-and-flash-tx.ps1&#96;\n          );\n          console.warn(\n            &#96;⚠️  Or use: .\\\\set-node-tx.ps1 &amp;&amp; .\\\\build.ps1 &amp;&amp; .\\\\flash.ps1&#96;\n          );\n        }\n      } catch (nodeAError) {\n        console.error(&#96;Failed to connect to Node A: ${nodeAError.message}&#96;);\n        console.log(\"Node A will not be available, but server will continue\");\n  }",

        "contents": "import { getConfig } from './config.js';\nimport { RS485Comm } from './rs485Comm.js';\nimport { NodeController } from './nodeController.js';\nimport { CSVLogger } from './csvLogger.js';\nimport { TestRunner } from './testRunner.js';\n\n/**\n * Main Orchestrator Entry Point\n * Runs test plan from command line\n */\nasync function main() {\n  console.log('UWB Test Orchestrator Starting...\\n');\n\n  try {\n    // Load configuration\n    const config = getConfig();\n    config.loadSettings();\n    config.loadTestPlan();\n\n    const serialConfig = config.getSerialConfig();\n    const testPlan = config.getTestPlan();\n\n    if (testPlan.length === 0) {\n      console.error('No tests found in test plan');\n      process.exit(1);\n    }\n\n    // Initialize RS-485 connections\n    console.log('Initializing RS-485 connections...');\n    const rs485A = new RS485Comm(\n      serialConfig.node_a_port,\n      serialConfig.baudrate,\n      serialConfig.timeout * 1000\n    );\n    const rs485B = new RS485Comm(\n      serialConfig.node_b_port,\n      serialConfig.baudrate,\n      serialConfig.timeout * 1000\n    );\n\n    // Initialize node controllers\n    const nodeA = new NodeController('A', rs485A);\n    const nodeB = new NodeController('B', rs485B);\n\n    // Initialize CSV logger\n    const csvLogger = new CSVLogger();\n\n    // Initialize test runner\n    const testRunner = new TestRunner(nodeA, nodeB, csvLogger, config);\n\n    // Connect to nodes in parallel for faster startup\n    console.log('Connecting to nodes...');\n    const [connectedA, connectedB] = await Promise.all([\n      nodeA.connect().then(() =&gt; {\n        console.log('Node A connected');\n        return true;\n      }),\n      nodeB.connect().then(() =&gt; {\n        console.log('Node B connected');\n        return true;\n      })\n    ]);\n    console.log('');\n\n    // Test connectivity with PING\n    console.log('Testing connectivity...');\n    const pingA = await nodeA.ping();\n    if (pingA) {\n      console.log('✓ Node A PING successful');\n    }\n}",

        "contents": "# auto-detect the DWM3001CDK's UART and open a minicom terminal connected to that UART, communicating via USB and the on-board SEGGER J-Link\nserial-terminal:\n\tDEVICE_FILE=$$(ls /dev/ttyUSB* /dev/ttyACM* 2&gt;/dev/null | while read -r dev; do if udevadm info -a -n $$dev | grep -q 'ATTRS{idVendor}==\"1915\"' &amp;&amp; udevadm info -a -n $$dev | grep -q 'ATTRS{idProduct}==\"520f\"'; then echo \"$$dev\"; break; fi; done); \\\n\tif [ -z \"$$DEVICE_FILE\" ]; then echo \"Device not found\"; exit 1; fi; \\\n\tminicom --device $$DEVICE_FILE\n\n# open a bash shell in the development environment with all of the development tools available\ndevelopment-shell: development-environment\n\tdocker run -it -v \"$$(pwd)\":/project uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board\n\n# build the development environment, reusing the existing build in the docker cache if available\ndevelopment-environment:\n\tdocker build -t uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board - &lt; Dockerfile  # build without sending any build context\n\n# export the development environment to the tar archive \"./uberi_qorvo-nrf52833-board.tar\", for offline archival purposes\nsave-development-environment:\n\tdocker image save -o uberi_qorvo-nrf52833-board.tar uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board\n\n# load a previously exported development environment from the tar archive \"./uberi_qorvo-nrf52833-board.tar\"\nload-development-environment:\n\tdocker image load -i uberi_qorvo-nrf52833-board.tar",

        "contents": "# build: docker build -t uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board .\n# run: docker run -it uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board\n\nFROM ubuntu:22.04\n\nARG DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive\nRUN apt-get -y update\nRUN apt-get install -y build-essential wget unzip\n\nWORKDIR /usr/local\n\n# install nRF5 SDK version 17.1.0 (the same version expected by the Qorvo project)\nRUN wget -q https://nsscprodmedia.blob.core.windows.net/prod/software-and-other-downloads/sdks/nrf5/binaries/nrf5_sdk_17.1.0_ddde560.zip &amp;&amp; unzip nrf5_sdk_17.1.0_ddde560.zip &amp;&amp; rm nrf5_sdk_17.1.0_ddde560.zip\n\n# install SEGGER Embedded Studio version 5.42a (the same version expected by the nRF5 SDK)\n# it has an installer that has to be run as root, and has a EULA that needs to be scrolled through\nRUN wget -q https://www.segger.com/downloads/embedded-studio/Setup_EmbeddedStudio_ARM_v542a_linux_x64.tar.gz &amp;&amp; tar xf Setup_EmbeddedStudio_ARM_v542a_linux_x64.tar.gz --strip-components=1 arm_segger_embedded_studio_542a_linux_x64/install_segger_embedded_studio &amp;&amp; rm Setup_EmbeddedStudio_ARM_v542a_linux_x64.tar.gz\nRUN apt-get install -y libxrender1 libxext6\nRUN yes yes | ./install_segger_embedded_studio --copy-files-to /usr/local/segger_embedded_studio_V5.42a\n\n# install nRF command line tools, including nrfjprog for programming using SEGGER J-Link programmers/debuggers\n# TODO: as of 2023-10-30, this requires the workaround of disabling udevadm, since the package is still broken for Docker builds: https://forum.segger.com/index.php/Thread/8953-SOLVED-J-Link-Linux-installer-fails-for-Docker-containers-Error-Failed-to-update/\nRUN apt-get install -y libusb-1.0-0 apt-utils udev\nRUN wget -q https://nsscprodmedia.blob.core.windows.net/prod/software-and-other-downloads/desktop-software/nrf-command-line-tools/sw/versions-10-x-x/10-23-2/nrf-command-line-tools_10.23.2_amd64.deb &amp;&amp; dpkg -i nrf-command-line-tools_10.23.2_amd64.deb\nRUN echo '#!/bin/bash\\necho not running udevadm \"$@\"' &gt; /usr/bin/udevadm &amp;&amp; chmod +x /usr/bin/udevadm &amp;&amp; apt-get install -y /opt/nrf-command-line-tools/share/JLink_Linux_V788j_x86_64.deb --fix-broken\n\n# install J-Link tools, including JLink RTT Logger for viewing debug output from the J-Link transferred via SEGGER RTT",

        "contents": "# Orchestrator Example - Build and Flash Guide\n\n## Overview\n\nThis example provides two firmware variants:\n- **TX Variant (Node A)**: Transmits UWB packets periodically\n- **RX Variant (Node B)**: Receives UWB packets and collects statistics\n\nBoth variants communicate with the Orchestrator via RS-485 using UART.\n\n## Pin Configuration\n\n### UART Pins (RS-485 Communication)\n- **RX Pin**: GPIO 15 (UART_0_RX_PIN)\n- **TX Pin**: GPIO 19 (UART_0_TX_PIN)\n- **Baud Rate**: 115200\n\n**Note**: Pins 8 and 10 are used for:\n- **Pin 8**: DW3000_IRQ_Pin (interrupt pin for UWB chip)\n- **Pin 10**: DW3000_CS_Pin (SPI chip select for UWB chip)\n\nThe UART for RS-485 communication uses **pins 15 (RX) and 19 (TX)**, not pins 8 and 10.\n\n## Building and Flashing\n\n### Step 1: Build TX Variant (Node A)\n\n1. Edit &#96;Src/example_selection.h&#96;:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;c\n   // Comment out other examples:\n   //#define TEST_READING_DEV_ID\n   \n   // Uncomment TX variant:\n   #define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_TX\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n2. Edit &#96;Src/main.c&#96;:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;c\n   // Comment out other examples:\n   // extern int read_dev_id(void); read_dev_id();\n   \n   // Uncomment TX variant:\n   extern int orchestrator_tx(void); orchestrator_tx();\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n3. Build:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   make build\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n4. Flash to Node A board:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   make flash\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 2: Build RX Variant (Node B)\n\n1. Edit &#96;Src/example_selection.h&#96;:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;c\n   // Comment out TX variant:\n   //#define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_TX\n   \n   // Uncomment RX variant:\n   #define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_RX\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n2. Edit &#96;Src/main.c&#96;:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;c\n   // Comment out TX variant:\n   // extern int orchestrator_tx(void); orchestrator_tx();\n   \n   // Uncomment RX variant:\n   extern int orchestrator_rx(void); orchestrator_rx();\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n3. Build:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   make build\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n4. Flash to Node B board:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   make flash\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Important**: You need to build and flash **separately** for each board. The firmware is compiled with either TX or RX code, not both.\n\n## LED Behavior\n\nThe firmware uses &#96;dwt_setleds()&#96; which controls the **DW3000 UWB chip's internal LEDs**, not the board LEDs.\n\n- **On startup**: LEDs will blink once during initialization",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "# Orchestrator Example - Build and Flash Guide",
            "lineNumber": 1
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2
          },
          {
            "text": "## Overview",
            "lineNumber": 3
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 4
          },
          {
            "text": "This example provides two firmware variants:",
            "lineNumber": 5
          },
          {
            "text": "- **TX Variant (Node A)**: Transmits UWB packets periodically",
            "lineNumber": 6
          },
          {
            "text": "- **RX Variant (Node B)**: Receives UWB packets and collects statistics",
            "lineNumber": 7
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 8
          },
          {
            "text": "Both variants communicate with the Orchestrator via RS-485 using UART.",
            "lineNumber": 9
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 10
          },
          {
            "text": "## Pin Configuration",
            "lineNumber": 11
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 12
          },
          {
            "text": "### UART Pins (RS-485 Communication)",
            "lineNumber": 13
          },
          {
            "text": "- **RX Pin**: GPIO 15 (UART_0_RX_PIN)",
            "lineNumber": 14
          },
          {
            "text": "- **TX Pin**: GPIO 19 (UART_0_TX_PIN)",
            "lineNumber": 15
          },
          {
            "text": "- **Baud Rate**: 115200",
            "lineNumber": 16
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 17
          },
          {
            "text": "**Note**: Pins 8 and 10 are used for:",
            "lineNumber": 18
          },
          {
            "text": "- **Pin 8**: DW3000_IRQ_Pin (interrupt pin for UWB chip)",
            "lineNumber": 19
          },
          {
            "text": "- **Pin 10**: DW3000_CS_Pin (SPI chip select for UWB chip)",
            "lineNumber": 20
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 21
          },
          {
            "text": "The UART for RS-485 communication uses **pins 15 (RX) and 19 (TX)**, not pins 8 and 10.",
            "lineNumber": 22
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 23
          },
          {
            "text": "## Building and Flashing",
            "lineNumber": 24
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 25
          },
          {
            "text": "### Step 1: Build TX Variant (Node A)",
            "lineNumber": 26
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27
          },
          {
            "text": "1. Edit &#96;Src/example_selection.h&#96;:",
            "lineNumber": 28
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;c",
            "lineNumber": 29
          },
          {
            "text": "   // Comment out other examples:",
            "lineNumber": 30
          },
          {
            "text": "   //#define TEST_READING_DEV_ID",
            "lineNumber": 31
          },
          {
            "text": "   ",
            "lineNumber": 32
          },
          {
            "text": "   // Uncomment TX variant:",
            "lineNumber": 33
          },
          {
            "text": "   #define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_TX",
            "lineNumber": 34
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 35
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 36
          },
          {
            "text": "2. Edit &#96;Src/main.c&#96;:",
            "lineNumber": 37
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;c",
            "lineNumber": 38
          },
          {
            "text": "   // Comment out other examples:",
            "lineNumber": 39
          },
          {
            "text": "   // extern int read_dev_id(void); read_dev_id();",
            "lineNumber": 40
          },
          {
            "text": "   ",
            "lineNumber": 41
          },
          {
            "text": "   // Uncomment TX variant:",
            "lineNumber": 42
          },
          {
            "text": "   extern int orchestrator_tx(void); orchestrator_tx();",
            "lineNumber": 43
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 44
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 45
          },
          {
            "text": "3. Build:",
            "lineNumber": 46
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash",
            "lineNumber": 47
          },
          {
            "text": "   make build",
            "lineNumber": 48
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 49
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 50
          },
          {
            "text": "4. Flash to Node A board:",
            "lineNumber": 51
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash",
            "lineNumber": 52
          },
          {
            "text": "   make flash",
            "lineNumber": 53
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 54
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 55
          },
          {
            "text": "### Step 2: Build RX Variant (Node B)",
            "lineNumber": 56
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 57
          },
          {
            "text": "1. Edit &#96;Src/example_selection.h&#96;:",
            "lineNumber": 58
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;c",
            "lineNumber": 59
          },
          {
            "text": "   // Comment out TX variant:",
            "lineNumber": 60
          },
          {
            "text": "   //#define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_TX",
            "lineNumber": 61
          },
          {
            "text": "   ",
            "lineNumber": 62
          },
          {
            "text": "   // Uncomment RX variant:",
            "lineNumber": 63
          },
          {
            "text": "   #define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_RX",
            "lineNumber": 64
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 65
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 66
          },
          {
            "text": "2. Edit &#96;Src/main.c&#96;:",
            "lineNumber": 67
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;c",
            "lineNumber": 68
          },
          {
            "text": "   // Comment out TX variant:",
            "lineNumber": 69
          },
          {
            "text": "   // extern int orchestrator_tx(void); orchestrator_tx();",
            "lineNumber": 70
          },
          {
            "text": "   ",
            "lineNumber": 71
          },
          {
            "text": "   // Uncomment RX variant:",
            "lineNumber": 72
          },
          {
            "text": "   extern int orchestrator_rx(void); orchestrator_rx();",
            "lineNumber": 73
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 74
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 75
          },
          {
            "text": "3. Build:",
            "lineNumber": 76
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash",
            "lineNumber": 77
          },
          {
            "text": "   make build",
            "lineNumber": 78
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 79
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 80
          },
          {
            "text": "4. Flash to Node B board:",
            "lineNumber": 81
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash",
            "lineNumber": 82
          },
          {
            "text": "   make flash",
            "lineNumber": 83
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 84
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 85
          },
          {
            "text": "**Important**: You need to build and flash **separately** for each board. The firmware is compiled with either TX or RX code, not both.",
            "lineNumber": 86
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 87
          },
          {
            "text": "## LED Behavior",
            "lineNumber": 88
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 89
          },
          {
            "text": "The firmware uses &#96;dwt_setleds()&#96; which controls the **DW3000 UWB chip's internal LEDs**, not the board LEDs.",
            "lineNumber": 90
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 91
          },
          {
            "text": "- **On startup**: LEDs will blink once during initialization",
            "lineNumber": 92
          }
        ]
      },
      "score": 0.2648206055164337

        "contents": "# PowerShell Scripts for DWM3001C Firmware\n\nThis directory contains PowerShell scripts for building and flashing the DWM3001C firmware on Windows.\n\n## Prerequisites\n\n1. **Docker Desktop** installed and running (with WSL2 backend recommended for USB access)\n2. **PowerShell** (comes with Windows 10/11)\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### Flash Node A (TX)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n.\\build-and-flash-tx.ps1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis will:\n1. Configure the firmware for TX variant\n2. Build the firmware\n3. Flash it to the connected board\n\n### Flash Node B (RX)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n.\\build-and-flash-rx.ps1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis will:\n1. Configure the firmware for RX variant\n2. Build the firmware\n3. Flash it to the connected board\n\n## Individual Scripts\n\n### Configuration Scripts\n\n- **&#96;set-node-tx.ps1&#96;** - Configure firmware for Node A (TX)\n- **&#96;set-node-rx.ps1&#96;** - Configure firmware for Node B (RX)\n\n### Build Scripts\n\n- **&#96;build.ps1&#96;** - Build the firmware\n- **&#96;clean.ps1&#96;** - Clean build outputs\n- **&#96;flash.ps1&#96;** - Flash firmware to connected board\n\n### Combined Scripts\n\n- **&#96;build-and-flash-tx.ps1&#96;** - Configure, build, and flash TX variant\n- **&#96;build-and-flash-rx.ps1&#96;** - Configure, build, and flash RX variant\n\n## Usage Examples\n\n### Step-by-step (Manual)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n# 1. Configure for TX\n.\\set-node-tx.ps1\n\n# 2. Build\n.\\build.ps1\n\n# 3. Flash\n.\\flash.ps1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### One-command (Automatic)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n# For Node A (TX)\n.\\build-and-flash-tx.ps1\n\n# For Node B (RX)\n.\\build-and-flash-rx.ps1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n### Docker Not Running\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nError: Docker is not running. Please start Docker Desktop.\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n**Solution:** Start Docker Desktop and wait for it to fully initialize.\n\n### USB Device Access Issues\nIf flashing fails with USB device errors:\n1. Ensure Docker Desktop is using WSL2 backend (Settings → General → Use WSL 2)\n2. Try unplugging and replugging the USB cable\n3. Ensure the board is connected to the J9 port (lower USB port)\n4. Check that the board is powered on\n\n### Build Fails\n- Run &#96;.\\clean.ps1&#96; to clean old build outputs\n- Check that Docker has enough resources allocated (Settings → Resources)",

        "contents": "**See also:** if you're looking for a fully-featured firmware that you just need some minor customizations for, check out my [DWM3001CDK demo firmware repository](https://github.com/Uberi/DWM3001CDK-demo-firmware).\n\nQuickstart\n----------\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sh\n# MANUAL ACTION (OPTIONAL): run this command to use my prebuilt development environment, otherwise it'll be automatically built from scratch: docker pull uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board\n\nmake build\n\n# MANUAL ACTION: connect the lower USB port of the DWM3001CDK (labelled J9) to this computer using a USB cable (this is the J-Link's USB port)\n\nmake flash\n\nmake stream-debug-logs\n\n# MANUAL ACTION: run the following command in another terminal to see the debug logs: tail -f Output/debug-log.txt\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nYou should now see RTT output from the DWM3001CDK, try pressing the reset buttom (labelled SW1) to re-run the example program and output more logs over RTT.\n\nDeveloping\n----------\n\nYou'll need Docker, and many of the hardware-facing commands in the Makefile assume you're using Linux. The &#96;make serial-terminal&#96; command assumes you have &#96;minicom&#96;, &#96;grep&#96;, and &#96;udevadm&#96; installed.\n\nYou can develop your custom applications by modifying &#96;Src/main.c&#96; and other files within &#96;Src/&#96;.\n\nNote that you'll have to manually edit &#96;dw3000_api.emProject&#96; with any file additions/removals/renames. It sounds annoying, and it is, but I still consider it an improvement over directly interacting with the proprietary SEGGER Embedded Studio.\n\nLicense\n-------\n\nMost of the code in this repository comes from the official Qorvo SDKs and examples published on their website. Here's the copyright notice that comes with the SDKs:\n\n&gt; Read the header of each file to know more about the license concerning this file.\n&gt; Following licenses are used in the SDK:\n&gt; \n&gt; * Apache-2.0 license\n&gt; * Qorvo license\n&gt; * FreeRTOS license\n&gt; * Nordic Semiconductor ASA license\n&gt; * Garmin Canada license\n&gt; * ARM Limited license\n&gt; * Third-party licenses: All third-party code contained in SDK_BSP/external (respective licenses included in each of the imported projects)\n&gt; \n&gt; The provided HEX files were compiled using the projects located in the folders. For license and copyright information,",

## Fixed: Physical board selection for flashing

### Problem
Both TX and RX scripts were flashing the same physical board because:
1. Both J-Link devices were attached to WSL2 simultaneously
2. `nrfjprog` was selecting the first device it found
3. The menu selection didn't isolate the target device

### Solution
Updated `flash.ps1` to isolate the target device:

1. Detach other devices: Before flashing, detach all other J-Link devices from WSL2
2. Attach only target: Ensure only the selected device is attached to WSL2
3. Use serial number: Get the device serial number and use `--snr` to target it specifically
4. Verification: Check that only one device is visible before flashing

### How it works now:

When you run `.\build-and-flash-tx.ps1` or `.\build-and-flash-rx.ps1`:

1. Shows menu with available devices
2. You select which board (e.g., Bus ID 4-1 or 4-2)
3. Script automatically:
   - Detaches the other J-Link device from WSL2
   - Attaches only the selected device
   - Gets its serial number
   - Flashes using `--snr <serial>` to target that specific device

### Test it:

```powershell
# Flash TX board (select Bus ID 4-1 or 4-2)
.\build-and-flash-tx.ps1

# Flash RX board (select the OTHER Bus ID)
.\build-and-flash-rx.ps1
```

The script now ensures only the selected device is attached to WSL2, so `nrfjprog` will flash the correct board. Each script will flash a different physical board based on your selection.

## Fixed: Serial number parsing

### Problem
The script extracted "7" instead of the full serial number (e.g., "760201599") because:
1. The parsing logic was too simple
2. The regex might have matched individual characters
3. Line splitting didn't handle all cases

### Solution
Updated the serial number parsing in `flash.ps1`:

1. Robust line splitting: Uses `[\r\n]+` to handle Windows and Unix line endings
2. Explicit filtering: Removes empty lines before processing
3. Better regex: Matches serial numbers with at least 6 digits (`^\d{6,}$`) instead of any digits
4. Debug output: Shows what's being parsed to help troubleshoot

### Changes

**Before:**
```powershell
$serialNumbers = $serialNumbers.Trim() -split "`n" | Where-Object { $_ -match "^\d+$" }
```

**After:**
```powershell
$serialNumbers = @()
$lines = $nrfjprogOutput -split "[\r\n]+" | Where-Object { $_.Trim() -ne "" }
foreach ($line in $lines) {
    $trimmed = $line.Trim()
    if ($trimmed -match "^\d{6,}$") {
        $serialNumbers += $trimmed
    }
}
```

The script now correctly extracts the full serial number (e.g., "760201599") and uses it with `--snr` to flash the correct device.

Try running `.\build-and-flash-tx.ps1` again; it should correctly identify and flash the selected board.

        "contents": "    }\n    \n    Write-Host \"Flashing via WSL2 (no admin required)...\" -ForegroundColor Green\n    \n    # Convert Windows path to WSL2 path\n    $wslPath = $projectPath.Replace('C:', '/mnt/c').Replace('\\', '/')\n    \n    # CRITICAL: Detach ALL other J-Link devices to ensure only target device is accessible\n    Write-Host \"Detaching other J-Link devices to ensure correct target...\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n    $allJlinkDevices = $usbDevices | Select-String -Pattern \"SEGGER|J-Link|1366\" -CaseSensitive:$false\n    foreach ($device in $allJlinkDevices) {\n        if ($device.Line -match \"^\\s*([0-9-]+)\") {\n            $devBusId = $matches[1]\n            if ($devBusId -ne $targetBusId) {\n                # Detach any other J-Link device\n                if ($device.Line -match \"Attached|Shared\") {\n                    Write-Host \"  Detaching other device: Bus ID $devBusId\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n                    &amp; $usbipdExe detach --busid $devBusId 2&gt;&amp;1 | Out-Null\n                    Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 500\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    \n    # Ensure ONLY the target device is attached\n    Write-Host \"Ensuring target device (Bus ID $targetBusId) is attached...\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n    $currentDevices = &amp; $usbipdExe list 2&gt;&amp;1\n    $targetDeviceStatus = $currentDevices | Select-String -Pattern \"^\\s*$targetBusId\\s+\" | Select-Object -First 1\n    \n    if (-not $targetDeviceStatus -or $targetDeviceStatus.Line -notmatch \"Attached|Shared\") {\n        Write-Host \"Attaching target device...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n        &amp; $usbipdExe attach --wsl --busid $targetBusId 2&gt;&amp;1 | Out-Null\n        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n            Write-Host \"Failed to attach target device!\" -ForegroundColor Red\n            exit 1\n        }\n        Write-Host \"Waiting for device to be ready...\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n        Start-Sleep -Seconds 3  # Give WSL2 time to see the device\n    } else {\n        Write-Host \"Target device is already attached ✓\" -ForegroundColor Green\n    }\n    \n    # Verify only one device is visible to nrfjprog\n    Write-Host \"Verifying device availability...\" -ForegroundColor Cyan",

Make sure WSL2 is running: wsl --status\" -ForegroundColor White\n            Write-Host \"    2. Try binding first: usbipd bind --busid $busId\" -ForegroundColor White\n            Write-Host \"    3. Check device status: usbipd list\" -ForegroundColor White\n            Write-Host \"\"\n            Write-Host \"    If device shows 'Shared', it's already attached - you're good to go!\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nWrite-Host \"\"\nWrite-Host \"=== Verifying Setup ===\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n\n# Verify device is accessible in WSL2\n$wslUsbCheck = wsl bash -c \"ls -la /dev/bus/usb 2&gt;&amp;1\" 2&gt;&amp;1\nif ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0 -and $wslUsbCheck -notmatch \"No such file\") {\n    Write-Host \"✓ USB devices are accessible in WSL2\" -ForegroundColor Green\n} else {\n    Write-Host \"⚠ USB devices may not be accessible in WSL2 yet\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    Write-Host \"  Try restarting WSL2: wsl --shutdown\" -ForegroundColor White\n    Write-Host \"  Then run this script again\" -ForegroundColor White\n}\n\nWrite-Host \"\"\nWrite-Host \"=== Setup Complete ===\" -ForegroundColor Green\nWrite-Host \"\"\nWrite-Host \"USB devices are now shared with WSL2.\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\nWrite-Host \"You can now flash firmware without admin privileges!\" -ForegroundColor Green\nWrite-Host \"\"\nWrite-Host \"Next steps:\" -ForegroundColor Yellow",

Attaching device...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n        \n        # Check if already attached or shared\n        if ($jlinkLine.Line -match \"Attached|Shared\") {\n            Write-Host \"J-Link device at bus ID $targetBusId is already attached to WSL2 ✓\" -ForegroundColor Green\n        } else {\n            Write-Host \"Found J-Link device at bus ID: $targetBusId\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n            Write-Host \"Attaching to WSL2...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n            \n            # New syntax: usbipd attach --wsl --busid &lt;BUSID&gt;\n            &amp; $usbipdExe attach --wsl --busid $targetBusId 2&gt;&amp;1 | Out-Null\n            \n            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n                Write-Host \"\"\n                Write-Host \"Failed to attach device automatically.\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n                Write-Host \"Please run setup script (may need admin ONCE):\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n                Write-Host \"  .\\setup-usb.ps1\" -ForegroundColor White\n                Write-Host \"\"\n                Write-Host \"Or attach manually:\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n                Write-Host \"  usbipd attach --wsl --busid $targetBusId\" -ForegroundColor White\n                exit 1\n            }\n            \n            Write-Host \"Device attached successfully!\" -ForegroundColor Green\n            Start-Sleep -Seconds 1  # Give WSL2 time to see the device\n        }\n    } else {\n        Write-Host \"USB devices are accessible in WSL2 ✓\" -ForegroundColor Green\n    }\n    \n    Write-Host \"Flashing via WSL2 (no admin required)...\" -ForegroundColor Green\n    \n    # Convert Windows path to WSL2 path",

        "contents": "$busIds = @()\n$attachedBusIds = @()\nforeach ($line in $usbDevices) {\n    if ($line -match \"SEGGER|J-Link|1366\") {\n        # Extract bus ID (format: BUSID  VID:PID    DESCRIPTION  STATE)\n        # Skip GUID entries (Persisted section)\n        if ($line -match \"^\\s*([0-9-]+)\") {\n            $busId = $matches[1]\n            # Check if already attached or shared\n            if ($line -match \"Attached|Shared\") {\n                $attachedBusIds += $busId\n                $state = if ($line -match \"Attached\") { \"attached\" } else { \"shared\" }\n                Write-Host \"  Bus ID $busId is already $state ✓\" -ForegroundColor Green\n            } else {\n                $busIds += $busId\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nif ($busIds.Count -eq 0 -and $attachedBusIds.Count -eq 0) {\n    Write-Host \"Could not parse bus IDs. Please attach devices manually:\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    Write-Host \"  usbipd attach --wsl --busid &lt;busid&gt;\" -ForegroundColor White\n    exit 1\n}\n\n# If all devices are already attached/shared, we're done\nif ($busIds.Count -eq 0 -and $attachedBusIds.Count -gt 0) {\n    Write-Host \"\"\n    Write-Host \"All J-Link devices are already attached to WSL2 ✓\" -ForegroundColor Green\n} else {\n    # Share each J-Link device with WSL2 (new syntax: attach --wsl --busid)",

        "contents": "if ($isWSL) {\n    # Running in WSL2 - can mount USB devices directly\n    Write-Host \"Detected WSL2 environment - using USB device mounting...\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n    \n    # Check if USB devices are accessible\n    $usbCheck = wsl bash -c \"ls -la /dev/bus/usb 2&gt;&amp;1\"\n    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n        Write-Host \"WARNING: USB devices not accessible in WSL2.\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n        Write-Host \"You may need to install usbipd-win and share the USB device:\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n        Write-Host \"  1. Install: winget install usbipd-win\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n        Write-Host \"  2. List devices: usbipd list\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n        Write-Host \"  3. Attach device: usbipd attach --wsl --busid &lt;busid&gt;\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n    }\n    \n    docker run --privileged &#96;\n        -v /dev/bus/usb:/dev/bus/usb &#96;\n        -v \"${projectPath}/Output:/project/Output:ro\" &#96;\n        uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board &#96;\n        nrfjprog --force -f nrf52 --program /project/Output/Common/Exe/dw3000_api.hex --sectorerase --verify\n} else {\n    # Running in Windows PowerShell",

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": ".\\README-FLASH-NO-ADMIN.md",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {},
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 100
          }
        },
        "contents": "# Flashing Without Administrator Privileges\n\n## Quick Setup (One-Time)\n\nRun the setup script **once** (may require admin for installation only):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n.\\setup-usb.ps1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis will:\n\n1. Install &#96;usbipd-win&#96; if not already installed (may need admin)\n2. Find your J-Link device\n3. Share it with WSL2\n\n**After this one-time setup, you can flash without admin!**\n\n## How It Works\n\n1. **usbipd-win** shares USB devices from Windows to WSL2\n2. Once shared, WSL2 can access the device without admin privileges\n3. The flash script automatically uses WSL2 to flash via Docker\n\n## Usage\n\nAfter setup, just run:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n# Flash TX node\n.\\build-and-flash-tx.ps1\n\n# Flash RX node\n.\\build-and-flash-rx.ps1\n\n# Or use automated test\n.\\auto-test-tx-rx.ps1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**No admin privileges needed!**\n\n## If USB Device Changes\n\nIf you:\n\n- Unplug/replug the USB cable\n- Connect a different board\n- Restart your computer\n\nJust run the setup script again:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n.\\setup-usb.ps1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n### \"USB device not accessible\"\n\n- Run &#96;.\\setup-usb.ps1&#96; again\n- Check device is connected: &#96;usbipd list&#96;\n- Verify device is attached: Look for \"Shared\" status\n\n### \"usbipd-win not found\"\n\n- Install manually: &#96;winget install usbipd-win&#96;\n- Or run &#96;.\\setup-usb.ps1&#96; (it will install automatically)\n\n### \"Flash failed\"\n\n- Make sure board is powered on\n- Check USB cable connection\n- Verify Docker Desktop is running\n- Try unplugging and replugging USB\n\n## Manual Setup (Alternative)\n\nIf the automated script doesn't work:\n\n1. Install usbipd-win:\n\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n   winget install usbipd-win\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n2. List USB devices:\n\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n   usbipd list\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n3. Find J-Link device (look for SEGGER or bus ID)\n\n4. Attach to WSL2:\n\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n   usbipd attach --wsl --busid &lt;busid&gt;\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n5. Now flash normally - no admin needed!",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {

          },
          {
            "text": "1. Install &#96;usbipd-win&#96; if not already installed (may need admin)",
            "lineNumber": 13
          },
          {
            "text": "2. Find your J-Link device",
            "lineNumber": 14
          },
          {
            "text": "3. Share it with WSL2",
            "lineNumber": 15
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 16
          },
          {
            "text": "**After this one-time setup, you can flash without admin!**",
            "lineNumber": 17
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 18
          },
          {
            "text": "## How It Works",
            "lineNumber": 19
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 20
          },
          {
            "text": "1. **usbipd-win** shares USB devices from Windows to WSL2",
            "lineNumber": 21
          },
          {
            "text": "2. Once shared, WSL2 can access the device without admin privileges",
            "lineNumber": 22
          },
          {
            "text": "3. The flash script automatically uses WSL2 to flash via Docker",
            "lineNumber": 23
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 24
          },
          {
            "text": "## Usage",
            "lineNumber": 25
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 26
          },
          {
            "text": "After setup, just run:",
            "lineNumber": 27
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 28
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;powershell",
            "lineNumber": 29
          },
          {
            "text": "# Flash TX node",
            "lineNumber": 30
          },
          {
            "text": ".\\build-and-flash-tx.ps1",
            "lineNumber": 31
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 32
          },
          {
            "text": "# Flash RX node",
            "lineNumber": 33
          },
          {
            "text": ".\\build-and-flash-rx.ps1",
            "lineNumber": 34
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 35
          },
          {
            "text": "# Or use automated test",
            "lineNumber": 36
          },
          {
            "text": ".\\auto-test-tx-rx.ps1",
            "lineNumber": 37
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 38
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 39
          },
          {
            "text": "**No admin privileges needed!**",
            "lineNumber": 40
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 41
          },
          {
            "text": "## If USB Device Changes",
            "lineNumber": 42
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 43
          },
          {
            "text": "If you:",
            "lineNumber": 44
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 45
          },
          {
            "text": "- Unplug/replug the USB cable",
            "lineNumber": 46
          },
          {
            "text": "- Connect a different board",
            "lineNumber": 47
          },
          {
            "text": "- Restart your computer",
            "lineNumber": 48
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 49
          },
          {
            "text": "Just run the setup script again:",
            "lineNumber": 50
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 51
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;powershell",
            "lineNumber": 52
          },
          {
            "text": ".\\setup-usb.ps1",
            "lineNumber": 53
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 54
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 55
          },
          {
            "text": "## Troubleshooting",
            "lineNumber": 56
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 57
          },
          {
            "text": "### \"USB device not accessible\"",
            "lineNumber": 58
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 59
          },
          {
            "text": "- Run &#96;.\\setup-usb.ps1&#96; again",
            "lineNumber": 60
          },
          {
            "text": "- Check device is connected: &#96;usbipd list&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 61
          },
          {
            "text": "- Verify device is attached: Look for \"Shared\" status",
            "lineNumber": 62
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 63
          },
          {
            "text": "### \"usbipd-win not found\"",
            "lineNumber": 64
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 65
          },
          {
            "text": "- Install manually: &#96;winget install usbipd-win&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 66
          },
          {
            "text": "- Or run &#96;.\\setup-usb.ps1&#96; (it will install automatically)",
            "lineNumber": 67
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 68
          },
          {
            "text": "### \"Flash failed\"",
            "lineNumber": 69
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 70
          },
          {
            "text": "- Make sure board is powered on",
            "lineNumber": 71
          },
          {
            "text": "- Check USB cable connection",
            "lineNumber": 72
          },
          {
            "text": "- Verify Docker Desktop is running",
            "lineNumber": 73
          },
          {
            "text": "- Try unplugging and replugging USB",
            "lineNumber": 74
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 75
          },
          {
            "text": "## Manual Setup (Alternative)",
            "lineNumber": 76
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 77
          },
          {
            "text": "If the automated script doesn't work:",
            "lineNumber": 78
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 79
          },
          {
            "text": "1. Install usbipd-win:",
            "lineNumber": 80
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 81
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;powershell",
            "lineNumber": 82
          },
          {
            "text": "   winget install usbipd-win",
            "lineNumber": 83
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 84
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 85
          },
          {
            "text": "2. List USB devices:",
            "lineNumber": 86
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 87
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;powershell",
            "lineNumber": 88
          },
          {
            "text": "   usbipd list",
            "lineNumber": 89
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 90
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 91
          },
          {
            "text": "3. Find J-Link device (look for SEGGER or bus ID)",
            "lineNumber": 92
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 93
          },
          {
            "text": "4. Attach to WSL2:",
            "lineNumber": 94
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 95
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;powershell",
            "lineNumber": 96
          },
          {
            "text": "   usbipd attach --wsl --busid &lt;busid&gt;",
            "lineNumber": 97
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 98
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 99
          },
          {
            "text": "5. Now flash normally - no admin needed!",
            "lineNumber": 100
          }
        ]
      },

        "contents": "# Setup USB device sharing with WSL2 (one-time setup)\n# This script finds J-Link devices and shares them with WSL2\n# Usage: .\\setup-usb.ps1\n# Note: This may require admin privileges ONCE to install usbipd-win\n\nWrite-Host \"=== USB Device Setup for WSL2 ===\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\nWrite-Host \"\"\n\n# Check if WSL2 is available\n$wslCheck = wsl --status 2&gt;&amp;1\nif ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n    Write-Host \"WSL2 not found or not configured!\" -ForegroundColor Red\n    Write-Host \"\"\n    Write-Host \"Please install WSL2:\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    Write-Host \"  wsl --install\" -ForegroundColor White\n    Write-Host \"\"\n    Write-Host \"Or enable it via:\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    Write-Host \"  dism.exe /online /enable-feature /featurename:Microsoft-Windows-Subsystem-Linux /all /norestart\" -ForegroundColor White\n    Write-Host \"  dism.exe /online /enable-feature /featurename:VirtualMachinePlatform /all /norestart\" -ForegroundColor White\n    Write-Host \"\"\n    Write-Host \"Then restart your computer and try again.\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    exit 1\n}\n\nWrite-Host \"WSL2 is available ✓\" -ForegroundColor Green\nWrite-Host \"\"\n\n# Find usbipd executable\n$usbipdExe = $null\n\n# Try to find usbipd in common installation locations\n$usbipdPaths = @(\n    \"$env:ProgramFiles\\usbipd-win\\usbipd.exe\",\n    \"${env:ProgramFiles(x86)}\\usbipd-win\\usbipd.exe\",\n    \"$env:LOCALAPPDATA\\Microsoft\\WindowsApps\\usbipd.exe\"\n)\n\n# Check if usbipd is in PATH\n$usbipdCheck = Get-Command usbipd -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue\nif ($usbipdCheck) {\n    $usbipdExe = $usbipdCheck.Source\n    Write-Host \"Found usbipd at: $usbipdExe\" -ForegroundColor Green\n} else {\n    # Try to find in common locations\n    foreach ($path in $usbipdPaths) {\n        if (Test-Path $path) {\n            $usbipdExe = $path\n            Write-Host \"Found usbipd at: $usbipdExe\" -ForegroundColor Green\n            break\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n# If still not found, try to install\nif (-not $usbipdExe) {\n    Write-Host \"usbipd-win not found. Installing...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow",

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": ".\\flash.ps1",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {
            "line": 318
          },
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 356,
            "column": 4
          }

        "contents": "            Write-Host \"  nrfjprog output: $nrfjprogOutput\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n            exit 1\n        } elseif ($serialNumbers.Count -eq 1) {\n            $targetSerial = $serialNumbers[0]\n            Write-Host \"Found target device serial: $targetSerial\" -ForegroundColor Green\n            Write-Host \"Flashing to device serial $targetSerial (Bus ID $targetBusId)...\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n            \n            # Flash with specific serial number\n            wsl bash -c \"cd '$wslPath' &amp;&amp; docker run --privileged -v /dev/bus/usb:/dev/bus/usb -v '$wslPath/Output:/project/Output:ro' uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board nrfjprog --snr $targetSerial --force -f nrf52 --program /project/Output/Common/Exe/dw3000_api.hex --sectorerase --verify\"\n        } else {\n            Write-Host \"Warning: Multiple devices still visible ($($serialNumbers.Count))!\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n            Write-Host \"  Serial numbers found: $($serialNumbers -join ', ')\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n            Write-Host \"  This should not happen.         "contents": "    \n    if ($jlinkDevices.Count -eq 0) {\n        Write-Host \"\"\n        Write-Host \"No J-Link devices found!\" -ForegroundColor Red\n        Write-Host \"Make sure board is connected and run:\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n        Write-Host \"  .\\setup-usb.ps1\" -ForegroundColor White\n        exit 1\n    }\n    \n    # Find the target device\n    $targetBusId = $null\n    $jlinkLine = $null\n    \n    # Helper function to show device selection menu\n    function Show-DeviceMenu {\n        param([array]$Devices, [string]$Prompt)\n        \n        Write-Host \"\"\n        Write-Host $Prompt -ForegroundColor Yellow\n        Write-Host \"\"\n        $deviceList = @()\n        $index = 1\n        foreach ($device in $Devices) {\n            if ($device.Line -match \"^\\s*([0-9-]+).*?(COM\\d+)\") {\n                $devBusId = $matches[1]\n                $devComPort = $matches[2]\n                $state = if ($device.Line -match \"Attached|Shared\") { \"✓ Attached\" } else { \"Not attached\" }\n                Write-Host \"  [$index] Bus ID: $devBusId  COM Port: $devComPort  State: $state\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\n                $deviceList += @{ BusId = $devBusId; ComPort = $devComPort; Line = $device.Line }\n                $index++\n            }\n        }\n        Write-Host \"\"\n        return $deviceList\n    }\n    \n    if ($BusId) {\n        # User specified bus ID directly\n        $jlinkLine = $jlinkDevices | Where-Object { $_.Line -match \"^\\s*$BusId\\s+\" } | Select-Object -First 1\n        if ($jlinkLine) {\n            $targetBusId = $BusId\n        } else {\n            Write-Host \"Error: Bus ID $BusId not found!\" -ForegroundColor Red\n            exit 1\n        }\n    } elseif ($ComPort) {\n        # User specified COM port\n        $jlinkLine = $jlinkDevices | Where-Object { $_.Line -match $ComPort } | Select-Object -First 1",

        "contents": "}\n\n# Function to flash firmware\nfunction Flash-Firmware {\n    param([string]$NodeType)\n    \n    Write-Host \"[FLASH] Flashing $NodeType node...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    Write-Host \"       Please ensure $NodeType board is connected and powered on\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n    \n    # Check if USB setup is needed (one-time check)\n    $usbipdCheck = Get-Command usbipd -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue\n    if ($usbipdCheck) {\n        $sharedCheck = wsl bash -c \"ls -la /dev/bus/usb 2&gt;&amp;1\" 2&gt;&amp;1\n        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or $sharedCheck -match \"No such file\") {\n            Write-Host \"[SETUP] USB device not shared with WSL2. Running setup...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n            Write-Host \"        (This may require admin ONCE for installation)\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n            &amp; \"$projectRoot\\setup-usb.ps1\"\n            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n                Write-Host \"[SETUP] USB setup failed. Please run manually:\" -ForegroundColor Red\n                Write-Host \"        .\\setup-usb.ps1\" -ForegroundColor White\n                throw \"USB setup required\"\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    \n    &amp; \"$projectRoot\\flash.ps1\"\n    \n    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n        throw \"Flash failed for $NodeType\"\n    }\n    \n    Write-Host \"[FLASH] $NodeType flash successful\" -ForegroundColor Green\n}\n\n# Function to run test\nfunction Run-Test {\n    param([int]$IterationNumber)",

        "contents": "&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\ngraph TB\n    subgraph NodeA[\"Node A (UWB Endpoint #1)\"]\n        RS485A[\"RS-485 Transceiver\"]\n        MCUA[\"MCU / UWB Firmware\"]\n        DWM1[\"DWM3001C #1 + Antenna\"]\n        RS485A --&gt; MCUA\n        MCUA --&gt; DWM1\n    end\n    \n    subgraph Hub[\"Center Hub\"]\n        RPI[\"RPI 5 - Test Orchestrator\"]\n        USB1[\"USB-RS-485 Adapter #1\"]\n        USB2[\"USB-RS-485 Adapter #2\"]\n        RPI --&gt; USB1\n        RPI --&gt; USB2\n    end\n    \n    subgraph NodeB[\"Node B (UWB Endpoint #2)\"]\n        DWM2[\"DWM3001C #2 + Antenna\"]\n        MCUB[\"MCU / UWB Firmware\"]\n        RS485B[\"RS-485 Transceiver\"]\n        DWM2 --&gt; MCUB\n        MCUB --&gt; RS485B\n    end\n    \n    subgraph Radio[\"Radio Channel (d_link)\"]\n        Channel[\"UWB Communication\"]\n    end\n    \n    JAMMER[\"JAMMER\"]\n    \n    RS485A &lt;--&gt;|\"STP Cable (RS-485)\"| USB1\n    RS485B &lt;--&gt;|\"STP Cable (RS-485)\"| USB2\n    DWM1 -.-&gt;|\"UWB over air\"| Channel\n    Channel -.-&gt;|\"UWB over air\"| DWM2\n    JAMMER -.-&gt;|\"Noise over air\"| Channel\n    \n    style NodeA fill:#e1f5ff\n    style NodeB fill:#e1f5ff\n    style Hub fill:#fff4e1\n    style Radio fill:#f0f0f0\n    style JAMMER fill:#ffe1e1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## **3\\. Control &amp; Cabling (RPi ↔ Nodes)**\n\n### **3.1 Physical interface**\n\nFor each node:\n\n* Cable: **shielded twisted pair (STP)**, e.g. a pair from CAT5e/CAT6, length up to \\~25 m.  \n* Electrical interface: **RS-485 point-to-point**.\n\nAt **RPi side**:\n\n* Node A: &#96;/dev/ttyUSB_A&#96; via &#96;USB_RS485_A&#96;.  \n* Node B: &#96;/dev/ttyUSB_B&#96; via &#96;USB_RS485_B&#96;.\n\nAt **node side**:\n\n* RS-485 transceiver connected to MCU UART (TX, RX, DE/RE).\n\n**Termination &amp; biasing:**\n\n* 120 Ω between A/B at RPi end and 120 Ω at node end for each link.  \n* Fail-safe biasing (pull-up / pull-down) at RPi side so the line idles in a known state.\n\n## **4\\. Node Firmware Specification**\n\nBoth nodes implement the same **ASCII command protocol over RS-485** and participate in an over-the-air UWB link:\n\n* **Node A** – TX initiator (main packet source).  \n* **Node B** – RX logger (collects RF metrics &amp; PER).",

        "contents": "# run SEGGER Embedded Studio's build system and output the results to ./Output/Common/Exe\nbuild: development-environment\n\tdocker run -v \"$$(pwd)\":/project uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board /usr/local/segger_embedded_studio_V5.42a/bin/emBuild -config \"Common\" /project/dw3000_api.emProject\n\n# remove all build outputs from the project (you may want to run this if you run into issues with stale interfaces)\nclean: development-environment\n\tdocker run -v \"$$(pwd)\":/project uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board /usr/local/segger_embedded_studio_V5.42a/bin/emBuild -config \"Common\" -clean /project/dw3000_api.emProject\n\n# program the DWM3001CDK using nrfjprog, communicating via USB and the on-board SEGGER J-Link\n# TODO: this uses --privileged and exposes all USB devices because SEGGER's libraries require it for some reason, it's not very good for security but it's the only way for now: https://wiki.segger.com/J-Link_Docker_Container\nflash: development-environment\n\tdocker run --privileged  -v /dev/bus/usb/:/dev/bus/usb -v \"$$(pwd)/Output\":/project/Output:ro uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board nrfjprog --force -f nrf52 --program /project/Output/Common/Exe/dw3000_api.hex --sectorerase --verify\n\n# read the RTT debug output of the DWM3001CDK using SEGGER J-Link RTT Logger, communicating via USB and the on-board SEGGER J-Link\n# TODO: this uses --privileged and exposes all USB devices because SEGGER's libraries require it for some reason, it's not very good for security but it's the only way for now: https://wiki.segger.com/J-Link_Docker_Container\nstream-debug-logs:\n\techo \"Run this command to view debug logs: tail -f Output/debug-log.txt\"\n\tdocker run --privileged -it -v /dev/bus/usb:/dev/bus/usb -v \"$$(pwd)/Output\":/project/Output uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board /usr/local/JLink_Linux_V792n_x86_64/JLinkRTTLogger -Device NRF52833_XXAA -if SWD -Speed 4000 -RTTChannel 0 /project/Output/debug-log.txt\n\n# auto-detect the DWM3001CDK's UART and open a minicom terminal connected to that UART, communicating via USB and the on-board SEGGER J-Link\nserial-terminal:\n\tDEVICE_FILE=$$(ls /dev/ttyUSB* /dev/ttyACM* 2&gt;/dev/null | while read -r dev; do if udevadm info -a -n $$dev | grep -q 'ATTRS{idVendor}==\"1915\"' &amp;&amp; udevadm info -a -n $$dev | grep -q 'ATTRS{idProduct}==\"520f\"'; then echo \"$$dev\"; break; fi; done); \\",

        "contents": "# Flash script for DWM3001C firmware\n# Usage: .\\flash.ps1 [-BusId &lt;busid&gt;] [-ComPort &lt;comport&gt;] [-NodeType TX|RX]\n# Examples:\n#   .\\flash.ps1 -BusId 4-1\n#   .\\flash.ps1 -ComPort COM11\n#   .\\flash.ps1 -NodeType TX\n# Note: Requires Docker Desktop with WSL2 backend for USB device access\n\nparam(\n    [string]$BusId = \"\",\n    [string]$ComPort = \"\",\n    [string]$NodeType = \"\"  # TX or RX\n)\n\nWrite-Host \"Flashing DWM3001C firmware...\" -ForegroundColor Green\n\n# Get the project root directory\n$projectRoot = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path\n$projectPath = $projectRoot.Replace('\\', '/')\n\n# Check if hex file exists\n$hexFile = Join-Path $projectRoot \"Output\\Common\\Exe\\dw3000_api.hex\"\nif (-not (Test-Path $hexFile)) {\n    Write-Host \"Error: Firmware not found at $hexFile\" -ForegroundColor Red\n    Write-Host \"Please run .\\build.ps1 first to build the firmware.\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    exit 1\n}\n\n# Ensure Docker is running\n$dockerRunning = docker info 2&gt;&amp;1\nif ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n    Write-Host \"Error: Docker is not running. Please start Docker Desktop.\" -ForegroundColor Red\n    exit 1\n}\n\nWrite-Host \"Connecting to board via J-Link...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\nWrite-Host \"Make sure the board is connected via USB (J9 port) and powered on.\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n\n# Check if running in WSL2\n$isWSL = $env:WSL_DISTRO_NAME -ne $null\n\nif ($isWSL) {\n    # Running in WSL2 - can mount USB devices directly",

        "range": {

        "contents": "# PowerShell Scripts for DWM3001C Firmware\n\nThis directory contains PowerShell scripts for building and flashing the DWM3001C firmware on Windows.\n\n## Prerequisites\n\n1. **Docker Desktop** installed and running (with WSL2 backend recommended for USB access)\n2. **PowerShell** (comes with Windows 10/11)\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### Flash Node A (TX)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n.\\build-and-flash-tx.ps1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis will:\n1. Configure the firmware for TX variant\n2. Build the firmware\n3. Flash it to the connected board\n\n### Flash Node B (RX)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n.\\build-and-flash-rx.ps1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis will:\n1. Configure the firmware for RX variant\n2. Build the firmware\n3. Flash it to the connected board\n\n## Individual Scripts\n\n### Configuration Scripts\n\n- **&#96;set-node-tx.ps1&#96;** - Configure firmware for Node A (TX)\n- **&#96;set-node-rx.ps1&#96;** - Configure firmware for Node B (RX)\n\n### Build Scripts\n\n- **&#96;build.ps1&#96;** - Build the firmware\n- **&#96;clean.ps1&#96;** - Clean build outputs\n- **&#96;flash.ps1&#96;** - Flash firmware to connected board\n\n### Combined Scripts\n\n- **&#96;build-and-flash-tx.ps1&#96;** - Configure, build, and flash TX variant\n- **&#96;build-and-flash-rx.ps1&#96;** - Configure, build, and flash RX variant\n\n## Usage Examples\n\n### Step-by-step (Manual)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n# 1. Configure for TX\n.\\set-node-tx.ps1\n\n# 2. Build\n.\\build.ps1\n\n# 3. Flash\n.\\flash.ps1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### One-command (Automatic)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;powershell\n# For Node A (TX)\n.\\build-and-flash-tx.ps1\n\n# For Node B (RX)\n.\\build-and-flash-rx.ps1\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n### Docker Not Running\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nError: Docker is not running. Please start Docker Desktop.\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n**Solution:** Start Docker Desktop and wait for it to fully initialize.\n\n### USB Device Access Issues\nIf flashing fails with USB device errors:\n1. Ensure Docker Desktop is using WSL2 backend (Settings → General → Use WSL 2)\n2. Try unplugging and replugging the USB cable\n3. Ensure the board is connected to the J9 port (lower USB port)\n4. Check that the board is powered on\n\n### Build Fails\n- Run &#96;.\\clean.ps1&#96; to clean old build outputs\n- Check that Docker has enough resources allocated (Settings → Resources)",

        "contents": "/**\n * Node Controller\n * High-level control for UWB nodes (Node A = TX, Node B = RX)\n */\nexport class NodeController extends EventEmitter {\n  constructor(nodeId, rs485Comm) {\n    super();\n    this.nodeId = nodeId; // 'A' or 'B'\n    this.rs485Comm = rs485Comm;\n    this.state = NodeState.IDLE;\n    this.config = null;\n    this.stats = null;\n    this.lastError = null;\n\n    // Bind RS-485 events\n    this.rs485Comm.on(\"error\", (error) =&gt; {\n      this.setState(NodeState.ERROR);\n      this.lastError = error.message;\n      // Only emit error if there are listeners to prevent uncaught exceptions\n      if (this.listenerCount(\"error\") &gt; 0) {\n        this.emit(\"error\", error);\n      } else {\n        // Log error if no listeners (prevents uncaught exception)\n        console.error(\n          &#96;[NodeController ${this.nodeId}] Unhandled error:&#96;,\n          error.message\n        );\n      }\n    });\n\n    this.rs485Comm.on(\"open\", () =&gt; {\n      this.emit(\"connected\");\n    });\n\n    this.rs485Comm.on(\"close\", () =&gt; {\n      this.setState(NodeState.IDLE);\n      this.emit(\"disconnected\");\n    });\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Set node state\n   * @param {string} newState\n   */\n  setState(newState) {\n    if\n  }\n}",

        "contents": "# auto-detect the DWM3001CDK's UART and open a minicom terminal connected to that UART, communicating via USB and the on-board SEGGER J-Link\nserial-terminal:\n\tDEVICE_FILE=$$(ls /dev/ttyUSB* /dev/ttyACM* 2&gt;/dev/null | while read -r dev; do if udevadm info -a -n $$dev | grep -q 'ATTRS{idVendor}==\"1915\"' &amp;&amp; udevadm info -a -n $$dev | grep -q 'ATTRS{idProduct}==\"520f\"'; then echo \"$$dev\"; break; fi; done); \\\n\tif [ -z \"$$DEVICE_FILE\" ]; then echo \"Device not found\"; exit 1; fi; \\\n\tminicom --device $$DEVICE_FILE\n\n# open a bash shell in the development environment with all of the development tools available\ndevelopment-shell: development-environment\n\tdocker run -it -v \"$$(pwd)\":/project uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board\n\n# build the development environment, reusing the existing build in the docker cache if available\ndevelopment-environment:\n\tdocker build -t uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board - &lt; Dockerfile  # build without sending any build context\n\n# export the development environment to the tar archive \"./uberi_qorvo-nrf52833-board.tar\", for offline archival purposes\nsave-development-environment:\n\tdocker image save -o uberi_qorvo-nrf52833-board.tar uberi/qorvo-nrf52833-board\n\n# load a previously exported development environment from the tar archive \"./uberi_qorvo-nrf52833-board.tar\"\nload-development-environment:\n\tdocker image load -i uberi_qorvo-nrf52833-board.tar",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {

        "contents": "import { io } from 'socket.io-client';\n\nconst SOCKET_URL = import.meta.env.VITE_SOCKET_URL || 'http://localhost:5000';\n\n/**\n * Socket.io Client\n * Handles real-time WebSocket communication\n */\nclass SocketService {\n  constructor() {\n    this.socket = null;\n    this.listeners = new Map();\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Connect to server\n   */\n  connect() {\n    if (this.socket?.connected) {\n      return;\n    }\n\n    this.socket = io(SOCKET_URL, {\n      transports: ['websocket', 'polling'],\n      reconnection: true,\n      reconnectionDelay: 1000,\n      reconnectionAttempts: 5,\n    });\n\n    this.socket.on('connect', () =&gt; {\n      console.log('Socket connected');\n      this.emit('connected');\n    });\n\n    this.socket.on('disconnect', () =&gt; {\n      console.log('Socket disconnected');\n      this.emit('disconnected');\n    });\n\n    this.socket.on('error', (error) =&gt; {\n      console.error('Socket error:', error);\n      this.emit('error', error);\n    });\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Disconnect from server\n   */\n  disconnect() {\n    if (this.socket) {\n      this.socket.disconnect();\n      this.socket = null;\n    }\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Subscribe to event\n   */\n  on(event, callback) {\n    if (!this.socket) {\n      this.connect();\n    }\n\n    this.socket.on(event, callback);\n\n    if (!this.listeners.has(event)) {\n      this.listeners.set(event, []);\n    }\n    this.listeners.get(event).push(callback);\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Unsubscribe from event\n   */\n  off(event, callback) {\n    if (this.socket) {\n      this.socket.off(event, callback);\n    }\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Emit event to internal listeners (for connection status)\n   */\n  emit(event, data) {\n    const listeners = this.listeners.get(event) || [];\n    listeners.forEach((listener) =&gt; listener(data));\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Send event to server\n   */\n  send(event, data) {\n    if (this.socket) {\n      this.socket.emit(event, data);\n    }\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Check if connected\n   */\n  isConnected() {\n    return this.socket?.connected || false;\n  }\n}\n\n// Singleton instance\nconst socketService = new SocketService();",

        "contents": "export class RS485Comm extends EventEmitter {\nasync sendCommand(command, timeout = this.timeout) {\n(resolve, reject) =&gt; {\n(writeError) =&gt; {\n\n          return;\n        }\n\n        // Ensure data is flushed to hardware (critical for RS-485)\n        // This must complete before the Promise can resolve, preventing race conditions\n        this.serialPort.drain((drainError) =&gt; {\n          // #region agent log - sendCommand drain callback\n          fetch(\n            \"http://127.0.0.1:7246/ingest/53b9dbf8-c6bb-42df-aadd-00e84572bd7f\",\n            {\n              method: \"POST\",\n              headers: { \"Content-Type\": \"application/json\" },\n              body: JSON.stringify({\n                location: \"rs485Comm.js:sendCommand\",\n                message: \"sendCommand drain callback\",\n                data: { commandId, drainError: drainError?.message },\n                timestamp: Date.now(),\n                sessionId: \"debug-session\",\n                runId: \"run1\",\n                hypothesisId: \"C\",\n              }),\n            }\n          ).catch(() =&gt; {});\n          // #endregion\n          if (drainError) {\n            clearTimeout(timer);\n            this.pendingCommands.delete(commandId);\n            reject(drainError);\n            return;\n          }\n\n          if (process.env.DEBUG_RS485) {\n            console.log(\n              &#96;[RS485 TX] ${this.port}: Data drained (sent to hardware)&#96;\n            );\n          }\n\n          // Drain complete - data is now guaranteed to be flushed\n          // The outer Promise will resolve when response is received via handleResponse()\n        });\n      });\n    });\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Handle incoming response\n   * @param {string} data - Response data\n   */\n}",

## Fixed: Device isolation after detaching

### Problem
After detaching the other device, `nrfjprog` couldn't see the target device because:
1. The target device wasn't reattached after detaching others
2. Detaching one device can affect others
3. Insufficient wait time for WSL2 to recognize the device

### Solution
Updated the device isolation logic in `flash.ps1`:

1. Detach all devices first: Detach all J-Link devices (including the target) to start clean
2. Wait for completion: Add a 2-second wait after detachments
3. Reattach only target: Reattach only the selected target device
4. Longer wait time: Increase wait to 4 seconds for WSL2 to recognize the device
5. Verification: Check that the target device is properly attached before proceeding

### New flow:

```
1. Detach ALL J-Link devices (clean slate)
2. Wait 2 seconds
3. Attach ONLY target device (Bus ID 4-2)
4. Wait 4 seconds for WSL2 recognition
5. Verify device is attached
6. Run nrfjprog (should see only one device)
```

This ensures:
- Only the target device is attached to WSL2
- `nrfjprog` sees exactly one device
- The correct board gets flashed

Try running `.\build-and-flash-rx.ps1` again; it should correctly isolate and flash the selected board.

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": ".\\Src\\examples\\ex_21_orchestrator\\README.md",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {
            "line": 86
          },
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 143
          }
        },
        "contents": "## LED Behavior\n\nThe firmware uses &#96;dwt_setleds()&#96; which controls the **DW3000 UWB chip's internal LEDs**, not the board LEDs.\n\n- **On startup**: LEDs will blink once during initialization\n- **During operation**: LEDs may flash during UWB activity (TX/RX events)\n- **Board LEDs**: The DWM3001CDK board LEDs (LED_1, LED_2, LED_3, LED_4) are not directly controlled by this firmware\n\n## RS-485 Connection\n\nConnect the RS-485 transceiver to:\n- **A+**: Connect to RS-485 A+ line\n- **B-**: Connect to RS-485 B- line  \n- **GND**: Connect to ground\n- **UART RX**: Connect to GPIO 15\n- **UART TX**: Connect to GPIO 19\n- **DE/RE**: Connect to control RS-485 direction (if needed)\n\nThe firmware communicates at **115200 baud** with the Orchestrator.\n\n## Testing\n\nAfter flashing:\n\n1. **Connect RS-485** from each board to the Orchestrator (RPi 5)\n2. **Power on** both boards\n3. **Run the Orchestrator**:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   cd Orchestrator\n   npm start\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe Orchestrator will:\n- Send &#96;PNG&#96; (PING) commands to verify connectivity\n- Configure both nodes with &#96;CFG&#96; commands\n- Start tests with &#96;STRT&#96; commands\n- Collect statistics with &#96;STAT&#96; commands\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n### UART Not Working\n- Verify pins 15 (RX) and 19 (TX) are connected correctly\n- Check RS-485 transceiver wiring (A+, B-, GND)\n- Verify baud rate is 115200\n- Check that RS-485 termination resistors are present (120Ω at each end)\n\n### Wrong Variant Flashed\n- Make sure you build and flash separately for each board\n- Check &#96;example_selection.h&#96; has the correct &#96;#define&#96; uncommented\n- Check &#96;main.c&#96; has the correct function call uncommented\n\n### LEDs Not Flashing\n- The firmware controls DW3000 internal LEDs, not board LEDs\n- Board LEDs may not flash unless you add code to control them\n- Check UWB activity with the Orchestrator's statistics",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "## LED Behavior",

        "contents": "int orchestrator_rx(void)\n{\n    uint32_t dev_id;\n\n    /* Display application name */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Initialize UART for RS-485 */\n    uart_init();\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC();\n    Sleep(2);\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n    dev_id = dwt_readdevid();\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED\");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enable LEDs */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure with default settings */\n    configure_uwb();\n\n    /* Enable RX initially (will be controlled by START/STOP commands) */\n    dwt_rxenable(DWT_START_RX_IMMEDIATE);\n\n    /* Main loop - process UART commands and RX packets */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        if (g_test_running)\n        {\n            process_rx_packet();\n        }\n        else\n        {\n            Sleep(100);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#endif",

(DWT_INT_RXFCG_BIT_MASK | SYS_STATUS_ALL_RX_ERR)))\n    {\n        // No event yet, return without blocking\n        return;\n    }\n\n    if (status_reg &amp; DWT_INT_RXFCG_BIT_MASK)\n    {\n        // Good frame received\n        frame_len = dwt_getframelength();\n        if (frame_len &lt;= FRAME_LEN_MAX)\n        {\n            dwt_readrxdata(g_rx_buffer, frame_len - FCS_LEN, 0);\n            dwt_writesysstatuslo(DWT_INT_RXFCG_BIT_MASK);\n            \n            rx_packet = (uwb_test_packet_t *)g_rx_buffer;\n            \n            // Update statistics\n            g_stats.total_rx++;\n            \n            // Check sequence number\n            if (!g_stats.seq_init)\n            {\n                g_stats.last_seq = rx_packet-&gt;seq;\n                g_stats.seq_init = 1;\n            }\n            else\n            {\n                uint32_t expected_seq = g_stats.last_seq + 1;\n                if (rx_packet-&gt;seq != expected_seq)\n                {\n                    if (rx_packet-&gt;seq &gt; expected_seq)\n                    {\n                        g_stats.lost_pkts += (rx_packet-&gt;seq - expected_seq);\n                    }\n                }\n                g_stats.last_seq = rx_packet-&gt;seq;\n            }\n            \n            // Read RF metrics using diagnostics\n            dwt_rxdiag_t rx_diag;\n            dwt_readdiagnostics(&amp;rx_diag);\n            \n            // Extract RSSI from diagnostics\n            // RSSI can be calculated from the channel power (ipatovPower)\n            // For simplicity, we'll use a simplified RSSI calculation\n            // RSSI ≈ 10*log10(power) - A, where A is a calibration constant",

        "contents": "/**\n * Application entry point\n */\nint orchestrator_tx(void)\n{\n    uint32_t dev_id;\n\n    /* Display application name */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Initialize UART for RS-485 */\n    uart_init();\n\n    /* Initialize app timer module */\n    uint32_t err_code = app_timer_init();\n    if (err_code != NRF_SUCCESS)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"TIMER INIT FAILED\");\n    }\n    else\n    {\n        /* Create timer instance */\n        err_code = app_timer_create(&amp;m_tx_timer_id, APP_TIMER_MODE_REPEATED, tx_timer_handler);\n        if (err_code == NRF_SUCCESS)\n        {\n            g_timer_initialized = 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC();\n    Sleep(2);\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n    dev_id = dwt_readdevid();\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED\");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enable LEDs */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure with default settings */\n    configure_uwb();\n\n    /* Main loop - process UART commands */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        // Command processing happens in UART interrupt handler\n        Sleep(100);\n    }\n}\n\n#endif",
