        },
        "contents": "/*! ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n *  @file    read_dev_id.c\n *  @brief   This example just read DW IC's device ID. It can be used to verify\n *           the SPI comms are working correctly.\n *\n * @attention\n *\n * Copyright 2018 - 2021 (c) Decawave Ltd, Dublin, Ireland.\n *\n * All rights reserved.\n *\n * @author Decawave\n */\n\n#include \"deca_probe_interface.h\"\n#include &lt;deca_device_api.h&gt;\n#include &lt;example_selection.h&gt;\n#include &lt;port.h&gt;\n#include &lt;stdio.h&gt;\n\n#if defined(TEST_READING_DEV_ID)\n\nextern void test_run_info(unsigned char *data);\n\n/* Example application name and version to display on LCD screen/VCOM port. */\n#define APP_NAME \"READ DEV ID      \"\n\n/**\n * Application entry point.\n */\nint read_dev_id(void)\n{\n    int err;\n    uint32_t dev_id;\n\n    bsp_board_led_on(0);\n\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    bsp_board_led_on(1);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    bsp_board_led_on(2);\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    bsp_board_led_on(3);\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC, or could wait for SPIRDY event)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n\n    dev_id = dwt_readdevid();\n\n\n    /* Reads and validate device ID returns DWT_ERROR if it does not match expected else DWT_SUCCESS */\n    if ((err = dwt_check_dev_id()) == DWT_SUCCESS)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"DEV ID OK\");\n    }\n    else\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"DEV ID FAILED\");\n    }\n\n    return err;\n}\n\n#endif\n/*****************************************************************************************************************************************************\n * NOTES:\n ****************************************************************************************************************************************************/",
        "signatures": {},

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": ".\\Src\\examples\\ex_21_orchestrator\\README.md",
        "range": {

          },
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 143
          }
        },
        "contents": "## LED Behavior\n\nThe firmware uses &#96;dwt_setleds()&#96; which controls the **DW3000 UWB chip's internal LEDs**, not the board LEDs.\n\n- **On startup**: LEDs will blink once during initialization\n- **During operation**: LEDs may flash during UWB activity (TX/RX events)\n- **Board LEDs**: The DWM3001CDK board LEDs (LED_1, LED_2, LED_3, LED_4) are not directly controlled by this firmware\n\n## RS-485 Connection\n\nConnect the RS-485 transceiver to:\n- **A+**: Connect to RS-485 A+ line\n- **B-**: Connect to RS-485 B- line  \n- **GND**: Connect to ground\n- **UART RX**: Connect to GPIO 15\n- **UART TX**: Connect to GPIO 19\n- **DE/RE**: Connect to control RS-485 direction (if needed)\n\nThe firmware communicates at **115200 baud** with the Orchestrator.\n\n## Testing\n\nAfter flashing:\n\n1. **Connect RS-485** from each board to the Orchestrator (RPi 5)\n2. **Power on** both boards\n3. **Run the Orchestrator**:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   cd Orchestrator\n   npm start\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe Orchestrator will:\n- Send &#96;PNG&#96; (PING) commands to verify connectivity\n- Configure both nodes with &#96;CFG&#96; commands\n- Start tests with &#96;STRT&#96; commands\n- Collect statistics with &#96;STAT&#96; commands\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n### UART Not Working\n- Verify pins 15 (RX) and 19 (TX) are connected correctly\n- Check RS-485 transceiver wiring (A+, B-, GND)\n- Verify baud rate is 115200\n- Check that RS-485 termination resistors are present (120Ω at each end)\n\n### Wrong Variant Flashed\n- Make sure you build and flash separately for each board\n- Check &#96;example_selection.h&#96; has the correct &#96;#define&#96; uncommented\n- Check &#96;main.c&#96; has the correct function call uncommented\n\n### LEDs Not Flashing\n- The firmware controls DW3000 internal LEDs, not board LEDs\n- Board LEDs may not flash unless you add code to control them\n- Check UWB activity with the Orchestrator's statistics",

        "contents": "int orchestrator_rx(void)\n{\n    uint32_t dev_id;\n\n    /* Display application name */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Initialize UART for RS-485 */\n    uart_init();\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC();\n    Sleep(2);\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n    dev_id = dwt_readdevid();\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED\");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enable LEDs */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure with default settings */\n    configure_uwb();\n\n    /* Enable RX initially (will be controlled by START/STOP commands) */\n    dwt_rxenable(DWT_START_RX_IMMEDIATE);\n\n    /* Main loop - process UART commands and RX packets */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        if (g_test_running)\n        {\n            process_rx_packet();\n        }\n        else\n        {\n            Sleep(100);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#endif",

        "contents": "export class TestRunner extends EventEmitter {\n\n\n  /**\n   * Run test from test plan\n   * @param {Object} test - Test configuration from test plan\n   */\n  async runTest(test) {\n    if (this.isRunning) {\n      throw new Error(\"Test is already running\");\n    }\n\n    this.currentTest = test;\n    this.isRunning = true;\n    this.emit(\"testStarted\", test);\n\n    try {\n      // Step 1: Prompt operator to set jammer\n      await this.promptJammer(test.jammer_label);\n\n      // Step 2: Configure both nodes\n      await this.configureNodes(test.config);\n\n      // Step 3: Create CSV log file\n      this.csvLogger.createLogFile(test.run_name);\n\n      // Step 4: Start both nodes\n      await this.startNodes();\n\n      // Step 5: Start periodic polling\n      this.startPolling(test);\n\n      // Step 6: Wait for test duration (or manual stop)\n      const testDuration =\n        this.config.getTestConfig().default_test_duration_seconds * 1000;\n      await this.sleep(testDuration);\n\n      // Step 7: Stop test\n      await this.stopTest();\n    } catch (error) {\n      this.emit(\"error\", error);\n      await this.stopTest();\n      throw error;\n    }\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Prompt operator to set jammer\n   * @param {string} jammerLabel - Expected jammer label\n   * @returns {Promise&lt;void&gt;}\n   */\n}",

        "contents": "static void uart_event_handler(app_uart_evt_t *p_event)\n{\n    static uint8_t rx_buffer[UART_BUFFER_SIZE];\n    static uint16_t rx_index = 0;\n\n    switch (p_event-&gt;evt_type)\n    {\n        case APP_UART_DATA_READY:\n        {\n            uint32_t err_code;\n            uint8_t byte;\n            err_code = app_uart_get(&amp;byte);\n            if (err_code == NRF_SUCCESS)\n            {\n                if (byte == '\\r' || byte == '\\n')\n                {\n                    if (rx_index &gt; 0)\n                    {\n                        rx_buffer[rx_index] = '\\0';\n                        parse_command((char *)rx_buffer);\n                        rx_index = 0;\n                    }\n                }\n                else if (rx_index &lt; (UART_BUFFER_SIZE - 1))\n                {\n                    rx_buffer[rx_index++] = byte;\n                }\n                else\n                {\n                    rx_index = 0; // Buffer overflow, reset\n                }\n            }\n            break;\n        }\n        case APP_UART_COMMUNICATION_ERROR:\n        case APP_UART_FIFO_ERROR:\n            break;\n        default:\n            break;\n    }\n}\n\n/**\n * Initialize UART for RS-485 communication\n */\nstatic void uart_init(void)\n{\n    uint32_t err_code;\n    uint32_t *p_err_code = &amp;err_code;\n    app_uart_comm_params_t comm_params =\n    {\n        .rx_pin_no = UART_0_RX_PIN,\n        .tx_pin_no = UART_0_TX_PIN,\n        .rts_pin_no = DW3000_RTS_PIN_NUM,\n        .cts_pin_no = DW3000_CTS_PIN_NUM,\n        .flow_control = APP_UART_FLOW_CONTROL_DISABLED,\n        .use_parity = false,\n        .baud_rate = 30801920  // 115200 baud\n    };\n\n    APP_UART_FIFO_INIT(&amp;comm_params,\n                       UART_RX_BUFFER_SIZE,\n                       UART_TX_BUFFER_SIZE,\n                       uart_event_handler,\n                       APP_IRQ_PRIORITY_LOW,\n                       p_err_code);\n    \n    if (err_code != NRF_SUCCESS)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"UART INIT FAILED\");\n    }\n}\n\n/**\n * Send response over UART\n */\nstatic void",

        "contents": "/**\n * Application entry point\n */\nint orchestrator_tx(void)\n{\n    uint32_t dev_id;\n\n    /* Display application name */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Initialize UART for RS-485 */\n    uart_init();\n\n    /* Initialize app timer module */\n    uint32_t err_code = app_timer_init();\n    if (err_code != NRF_SUCCESS)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"TIMER INIT FAILED\");\n    }\n    else\n    {\n        /* Create timer instance */\n        err_code = app_timer_create(&amp;m_tx_timer_id, APP_TIMER_MODE_REPEATED, tx_timer_handler);\n        if (err_code == NRF_SUCCESS)\n        {\n            g_timer_initialized = 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC();\n    Sleep(2);\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n    dev_id = dwt_readdevid();\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED\");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enable LEDs */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure with default settings */\n    configure_uwb();\n\n    /* Main loop - process UART commands */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        // Command processing happens in UART interrupt handler\n        Sleep(100);\n    }\n}\n\n#endif",

        "contents": "int simple_rx(void)\n{\n    /* Hold copy of status register state here for reference so that it can be examined at a debug breakpoint. */\n    uint32_t status_reg;\n    /* Hold copy of frame length of frame received (if good) so that it can be examined at a debug breakpoint. */\n    uint16_t frame_len;\n\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW IC supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC, or could wait for SPIRDY event)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED\");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enabling LEDs here for debug so that for each RX-enable the D2 LED will flash on DW3000 red eval-shield boards. */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Loop forever receiving frames. */\n    while (TRUE)\n    {\n        /* TESTING BREAKPOINT LOCATION #1 */",

        "contents": "/**\n * UART event handler\n */\nstatic void uart_event_handler(app_uart_evt_t *p_event)\n{\n    static uint8_t rx_buffer[UART_BUFFER_SIZE];\n    static uint16_t rx_index = 0;\n\n    switch (p_event-&gt;evt_type)\n    {\n        case APP_UART_DATA_READY:\n        {\n            uint32_t err_code;\n            uint8_t byte;\n            err_code = app_uart_get(&amp;byte);\n            if (err_code == NRF_SUCCESS)\n            {\n                if (byte == '\\r' || byte == '\\n')\n                {\n                    if (rx_index &gt; 0)\n                    {\n                        rx_buffer[rx_index] = '\\0';\n                        parse_command((char *)rx_buffer);\n                        rx_index = 0;\n                    }\n                }\n                else if (rx_index &lt; (UART_BUFFER_SIZE - 1))\n                {\n                    rx_buffer[rx_index++] = byte;\n                }\n                else\n                {\n                    rx_index = 0; // Buffer overflow, reset\n                }\n            }\n            break;\n        }\n        case APP_UART_COMMUNICATION_ERROR:\n        case APP_UART_FIFO_ERROR:\n            break;\n        default:\n            break;\n    }\n}\n\n/**\n * Initialize UART for RS-485 communication\n */\nstatic void uart_init(void)\n{\n    uint32_t err_code;\n    uint32_t *p_err_code = &amp;err_code;\n    app_uart_comm_params_t comm_params =\n    {\n        .rx_pin_no = UART_0_RX_PIN,\n        .tx_pin_no = UART_0_TX_PIN,\n        .rts_pin_no = DW3000_RTS_PIN_NUM,\n        .cts_pin_no = DW3000_CTS_PIN_NUM,\n        .flow_control = APP_UART_FLOW_CONTROL_DISABLED,\n        .use_parity = false,\n        .baud_rate = 30801920  // 115200 baud\n    };\n\n    APP_UART_FIFO_INIT(&amp;comm_params,\n                       UART_RX_BUFFER_SIZE,\n                       UART_TX_BUFFER_SIZE,\n                       uart_event_handler,\n                       APP_IRQ_PRIORITY_LOW,\n                       p_err_code);\n    \n    if (err_code != NRF_SUCCESS)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"UART INIT FAILED\");\n    }\n}\n\n/**\n * Send response over UART\n */\nstatic void",

        "contents": "/**\n * Application entry point.\n */\nint simple_rx_pdoa(void)\n{\n    uint32_t dev_id;\n    int16_t last_pdoa_val = 0;\n\n    /* Sends application name to test_run_info function. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    dev_id = dwt_readdevid();\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_IDLE) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED\");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure DW3000. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Register RX call-back. */\n    dwt_setcallbacks(NULL, rx_ok_cb, rx_err_cb, rx_err_cb, NULL, NULL, NULL);\n\n    /* Enable wanted interrupts (RX good frames and RX errors). */\n    dwt_setinterrupt(DWT_INT_RXFCG_BIT_MASK | SYS_STATUS_ALL_RX_ERR, 0, DWT_ENABLE_INT);\n\n    /*Clearing the SPI ready interrupt*/\n    dwt_writesysstatuslo(DWT_INT_RCINIT_BIT_MASK | DWT_INT_SPIRDY_BIT_MASK);\n\n    /* Install DW IC IRQ handler. */\n    port_set_dwic_isr(dwt_isr);\n\n    /* Activate reception immediately. See NOTE 1 below. */\n    dwt_rxenable(DWT_START_RX_IMMEDIATE);\n\n    /*loop forever receiving frames*/\n    while (1)\n    {\n        if (last_pdoa_val != pdoa_val)",

        "contents": "# Automated Build, Flash, and Test Script with Iteration Support\n# Usage: .\\auto-test-tx-rx.ps1 [iterations]\n# Example: .\\auto-test-tx-rx.ps1 3  (runs 3 iterations)\n\nparam(\n    [int]$Iterations = 1,\n    [int]$TestDurationSeconds = 30,\n    [switch]$SkipBuild = $false,\n    [switch]$SkipFlash = $false\n)\n\n$ErrorActionPreference = \"Stop\"\n$projectRoot = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path\n$logFile = Join-Path $projectRoot \".cursor\\debug.log\"\n\nWrite-Host \"========================================\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\nWrite-Host \"  UWB TX/RX Automated Test Script\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\nWrite-Host \"  Iterations: $Iterations\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\nWrite-Host \"========================================\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\nWrite-Host \"\"\nWrite-Host \"Serial Ports Configuration:\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\nWrite-Host \"  Node A (TX): COM17\" -ForegroundColor White\nWrite-Host \"  Node B (RX): COM18\" -ForegroundColor White\nWrite-Host \"\"\nWrite-Host \"Make sure both boards are connected via RS-485 to these COM ports\" -ForegroundColor Cyan\nWrite-Host \"\"\n\n# Function to clear debug log\nfunction Clear-DebugLog {\n    if (Test-Path $logFile) {\n        Remove-Item $logFile -Force\n        Write-Host \"[LOG] Cleared debug log\" -ForegroundColor Gray\n    }\n}\n\n# Function to build firmware\nfunction Build-Firmware {\n    param([string]$NodeType)\n    \n    Write-Host \"[BUILD] Building $NodeType firmware...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    \n    if ($NodeType -eq \"TX\") {\n        &amp; \"$projectRoot\\set-node-tx.ps1\"\n    } else {\n        &amp; \"$projectRoot\\set-node-rx.ps1\"\n    }\n    \n    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n        throw \"Failed to configure for $NodeType\"\n    }\n    \n    &amp; \"$projectRoot\\build.ps1\"\n    \n    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n        throw \"Build failed for $NodeType\"\n    }\n    \n    Write-Host \"[BUILD] $NodeType build successful\" -ForegroundColor Green\n}\n\n# Function to flash firmware\nfunction Flash-Firmware {\n    param([string]$NodeType)\n    \n    Write-Host \"[FLASH] Flashing $NodeType node...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow",

        "contents": "int rx_diagnostics(void)\n{\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC, or could wait for SPIRDY event)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED\");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Activate event counters. */\n    dwt_configeventcounters(1);\n\n    /* Enable IC diagnostic calculation and logging */\n    dwt_configciadiag(1);\n\n    /* Loop forever receiving frames. */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        int i;\n\n        /* TESTING BREAKPOINT LOCATION #1 */",

        "contents": "int rx_send_resp(void)\n{\n    /* Hold copy of status register state here for reference so that it can be examined at a debug breakpoint. */\n    uint32_t status_reg = 0;\n    /* Hold copy of frame length of frame received (if good) so that it can be examined at a debug breakpoint. */\n    uint16_t frame_len = 0;\n\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC, or could wait for SPIRDY event)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enabling LEDs here for debug so that for each TX the D1 LED will flash on DW3000 red eval-shield boards. */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. See NOTE 8 below. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure the TX spectrum parameters (power, PG delay and PG count) */\n    dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options);\n\n    /* Loop forever sending and receiving frames periodically. */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        /* Activate reception immediately. See NOTE 4 below. */",

        "contents": "# Flash script for DWM3001C firmware\n# Usage: .\\flash.ps1 [-BusId &lt;busid&gt;] [-ComPort &lt;comport&gt;] [-NodeType TX|RX]\n# Examples:\n#   .\\flash.ps1 -BusId 4-1\n#   .\\flash.ps1 -ComPort COM11\n#   .\\flash.ps1 -NodeType TX\n# Note: Requires Docker Desktop with WSL2 backend for USB device access\n\nparam(\n    [string]$BusId = \"\",\n    [string]$ComPort = \"\",\n    [string]$NodeType = \"\"  # TX or RX\n)\n\nWrite-Host \"Flashing DWM3001C firmware...\" -ForegroundColor Green\n\n# Get the project root directory\n$projectRoot = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path\n$projectPath = $projectRoot.Replace('\\', '/')\n\n# Check if hex file exists\n$hexFile = Join-Path $projectRoot \"Output\\Common\\Exe\\dw3000_api.hex\"\nif (-not (Test-Path $hexFile)) {\n    Write-Host \"Error: Firmware not found at $hexFile\" -ForegroundColor Red\n    Write-Host \"Please run .\\build.ps1 first to build the firmware.\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n    exit 1\n}\n\n# Ensure Docker is running\n$dockerRunning = docker info 2&gt;&amp;1\nif ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {\n    Write-Host \"Error: Docker is not running. Please start Docker Desktop.\" -ForegroundColor Red\n    exit 1\n}\n\nWrite-Host \"Connecting to board via J-Link...\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\nWrite-Host \"Make sure the board is connected via USB (J9 port) and powered on.\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\n\n# Check if running in WSL2\n$isWSL = $env:WSL_DISTRO_NAME -ne $null\n\nif ($isWSL) {\n    # Running in WSL2 - can mount USB devices directly",

      "codeBlock": {

        "contents": "        parse_set_config(params);\n    }\n    else if (strcmp(cmd_upper, \"STRT\") == 0 || strcmp(cmd_upper, \"START_TEST\") == 0)\n    {\n        if (!g_config.configured)\n        {\n            send_response(\"ERR NOT_CONFIGURED\");\n            return;\n        }\n        \n        if (!g_timer_initialized)\n        {\n            send_response(\"ERR TIMER_NOT_INIT\");\n            return;\n        }\n        \n        g_test_running = 1;\n        g_seq_num = 0;\n        g_stats.total_sent = 0;\n        g_stats.last_error = 0;\n\n        // Start timer for periodic TX\n        uint32_t period_ms = 1000 / g_config.pkt_rate_hz;\n        if (period_ms &lt;         "contents": "int tx_wait_resp(void)\n{\n    /* Hold copy of status register state here for reference so that it can be examined at a debug breakpoint. */\n    uint32_t status_reg = 0;\n    /* Hold copy of frame length of frame received (if good) so that it can be examined at a debug breakpoint. */\n    uint16_t frame_len = 0;\n\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC, or could wait for SPIRDY event)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Optionally Configure GPIOs to show TX/RX activity. See NOTE 10 below. */\n    /* Optionally enabling LEDs here for debug so that for each TX the D1 LED will flash on DW3000 red eval-shield boards. See Note 10 below.*/\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. See NOTE 2 below. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure the TX spectrum parameters (power, PG delay and PG count) */\n    dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options);\n\n    /* Set delay to turn reception on after transmission of the frame. See NOTE 3 below. */\n    dwt_setrxaftertxdelay(TX_TO_RX_DELAY_UUS);\n\n    /* Set response frame timeout. */\n    dwt_setrxtimeout(RX_RESP_TO_UUS);\n\n    /* Loop forever sending and receiving frames periodically. */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        /* Write frame data to DW3000 and prepare transmission. See NOTE 7 below. */",

Fixed blocking issues in the firmware. Changes:

1. Added startup message: sends "OK STARTUP" immediately after UART init to verify UART works
2. Added timeout: `dwt_checkidlerc()` now times out after 1 second instead of hanging forever
3. Removed infinite loop: on DW3000 init failure, firmware continues so UART commands still work
4. Added status messages: reports DW3000 initialization status

## Fixed: Firmware blocking issues

### Problem
The firmware was likely hanging at:
- `while (!dwt_checkidlerc())` - infinite wait for DW3000 to be ready
- `while (1) { }` - infinite loop if DW3000 initialization failed

This prevented UART from processing commands even though it was initialized.

### Solution
1. Startup verification: sends "OK STARTUP" right after UART init
2. Timeout protection: `dwt_checkidlerc()` waits max 1 second
3. Graceful degradation: continues even if DW3000 fails, so UART commands still work
4. Status reporting: sends messages about initialization progress

### Next steps

<reproduction_steps>
1. Rebuild both firmware variants:
   ```powershell
   .\build-and-flash-tx.ps1
   .\build-and-flash-rx.ps1
   ```

2. After flashing, wait 5 seconds for boards to initialize

3. Test UART communication:
   ```powershell
   .\test-uart-direct.ps1
   ```
   You should now see "OK STARTUP" responses if UART is working

4. If you see "OK STARTUP" but still no PING responses, check RS-485 wiring

5. If you see "ERR DW3000_TIMEOUT" or "ERR DW3000_INIT_FAILED", the DW3000 IC may have issues, but UART should still work for commands
</reproduction_steps>

The firmware will now:
- Send "OK STARTUP" immediately after UART init (proves UART works)
- Continue even if DW3000 has issues (UART commands still work)
- Report initialization status via UART

Rebuild and test to see if you get responses.

   - Verify COM ports match your RS-485 adapter

   - Verify RS-485 adapters are connected to COM17/COM18
</reproduction_steps>

4. Initialization delay: added 100ms delay after UART init

Added instrumentation to diagnose the issue. The firmware will send diagnostic messages at each stage.

## Hypotheses

1. UART initialization fails silently
2. Firmware crashes before reaching main loop
3. UART pins misconfigured
4. RS-485 transceiver not working
5. Firmware stuck in blocking operation
6. Baud rate mismatch

## Instrumentation added

The firmware now sends diagnostic messages:
- `OK UART_INIT` - UART initialized successfully
- `OK STARTUP` - Reached startup code
- `OK FIRMWARE_RUNNING` - Firmware is running
- `OK MAIN_LOOP` - Reached main loop
- `ERR DW3000_TIMEOUT` - DW3000 not responding
- `ERR DW3000_INIT_FAILED` - DW3000 initialization failed
- `OK DW3000_READY` - DW3000 ready

<reproduction_steps>
1. Rebuild TX firmware with instrumentation:
   ```powershell
   .\build-and-flash-tx.ps1
   ```
   Select TX board when prompted

2. Rebuild RX firmware with instrumentation:
   ```powershell
   .\build-and-flash-rx.ps1
   ```
   Select RX board when prompted

3. Wait 5 seconds after flashing for initialization

4. Test UART communication:
   ```powershell
   .\test-uart-direct.ps1
   ```
   Look for diagnostic messages:
   - If you see "OK UART_INIT" → UART is working
   - If you see "OK STARTUP" → Firmware reached startup
   - If you see "OK MAIN_LOOP" → Firmware is running
   - If you see nothing → UART init failed or firmware crashed early

5. Share the output from test-uart-direct.ps1 so we can analyze which stage is failing
</reproduction_steps>

These messages will show where the firmware stops. Rebuild and test, then share the output.

        "contents": "unsigned SEGGER_RTT_PutChar(unsigned BufferIndex, char c) {\n  SEGGER_RTT_BUFFER_UP* pRing;\n  unsigned              WrOff;\n  unsigned              Status;\n  //\n  // Prepare\n  //\n  INIT();\n  SEGGER_RTT_LOCK();\n  //\n  // Get \"to-host\" ring buffer.\n  //\n  pRing = &amp;_SEGGER_RTT.aUp[BufferIndex];\n  //\n  // Get write position and handle wrap-around if necessary\n  //\n  WrOff = pRing-&gt;WrOff + 1;\n  if (WrOff == pRing-&gt;SizeOfBuffer) {\n    WrOff = 0;\n  }\n  //\n  // Wait for free space if mode is set to blocking\n  //\n  if (pRing-&gt;Flags == SEGGER_RTT_MODE_BLOCK_IF_FIFO_FULL) {\n    while (WrOff == pRing-&gt;RdOff) {\n      ;\n    }\n  }\n  //\n  // Output byte if free space is available\n  //\n  if (WrOff != pRing-&gt;RdOff) {\n    pRing-&gt;pBuffer[pRing-&gt;WrOff] = c;\n    pRing-&gt;WrOff = WrOff;\n    Status = 1;\n  } else {\n    Status = 0;\n  }\n  //\n  // Finish up.\n  //\n  SEGGER_RTT_UNLOCK();\n  //\n  return Status;\n}\n\n/*********************************************************************\n*\n*       SEGGER_RTT_GetKey\n*\n*  Function description\n*    Reads one character from the SEGGER RTT buffer.\n*    Host has previously stored data there.\n*\n*  Return value\n*    &lt;  0 -   No character available (buffer empty).\n*    &gt;= 0 -   Character which has been read.         "contents": "unsigned SEGGER_RTT_WriteNoLock(unsigned BufferIndex, const void* pBuffer, unsigned NumBytes) {\n  unsigned              Status;\n  unsigned              Avail;\n  const char*           pData;\n  SEGGER_RTT_BUFFER_UP* pRing;\n\n  pData = (const char *)pBuffer;\n  //\n  // Get \"to-host\" ring buffer.\n  //\n  pRing = &amp;_SEGGER_RTT.aUp[BufferIndex];\n  //\n  // How we output depends upon the mode...\n  //\n  switch (pRing-&gt;Flags) {\n  case SEGGER_RTT_MODE_NO_BLOCK_SKIP:\n    //\n    // If we are in skip mode and there is no space for the whole\n    // of this output, don't bother.\n    //\n    Avail = _GetAvailWriteSpace(pRing);\n    if (Avail &lt; NumBytes) {\n      Status = 0u;\n    } else {\n      Status = NumBytes;\n      _WriteNoCheck(pRing, pData, NumBytes);\n    }\n    break;\n  case SEGGER_RTT_MODE_NO_BLOCK_TRIM:\n    //\n    // If we are in trim mode, trim to what we can output without blocking.\n    //\n    Avail = _GetAvailWriteSpace(pRing);\n    Status = Avail &lt; NumBytes ? Avail : NumBytes;\n    _WriteNoCheck(pRing, pData, Status);\n    break;\n  case SEGGER_RTT_MODE_BLOCK_IF_FIFO_FULL:\n    //\n    // If we are in blocking mode, output everything.\n    //\n    Status = _WriteBlocking(pRing, pData, NumBytes);\n    break;\n  default:\n    Status = 0u;\n    break;\n  }\n  //\n  // Finish up.\n  //\n  return Status;\n}\n\n/*********************************************************************\n*\n*       SEGGER_RTT_Write\n*\n*  Function description\n*    Stores a specified number of characters in SEGGER RTT\n*    control block which is then read by the host.\n*\n*  Parameters\n*    BufferIndex  Index of \"Up\"-buffer to be used (e.g. 0 for \"Terminal\").\n*    pBuffer      Pointer to character array. Does not need to point to a \\0 terminated string.\n*    NumBytes     Number of bytes to be stored in the SEGGER RTT control block.\n*\n*  Return value\n*    Number of bytes which have been stored in the \"Up\"-buffer.\n*\n*  Notes\n*    (1) Data is stored according to buffer flags.\n*/",

        "contents": "static unsigned _WriteBlocking(SEGGER_RTT_BUFFER_UP* pRing, const char* pBuffer, unsigned NumBytes) {\n  unsigned NumBytesToWrite;\n  unsigned NumBytesWritten;\n  unsigned RdOff;\n  unsigned WrOff;\n#if SEGGER_RTT_MEMCPY_USE_BYTELOOP\n  char*    pDst;\n#endif\n  //\n  // Write data to buffer and handle wrap-around if necessary\n  //\n  NumBytesWritten = 0u;\n  WrOff = pRing-&gt;WrOff;\n  do {\n    RdOff = pRing-&gt;RdOff;                         // May be changed by host (debug probe) in the meantime\n    if (RdOff &gt; WrOff) {\n      NumBytesToWrite = RdOff - WrOff - 1u;\n    } else {\n      NumBytesToWrite = pRing-&gt;SizeOfBuffer - (WrOff - RdOff + 1u);\n    }\n    NumBytesToWrite = MIN(NumBytesToWrite, (pRing-&gt;SizeOfBuffer - WrOff));      // Number of bytes that can be written until buffer wrap-around\n    NumBytesToWrite = MIN(NumBytesToWrite, NumBytes);\n#if SEGGER_RTT_MEMCPY_USE_BYTELOOP\n    pDst = pRing-&gt;pBuffer + WrOff;\n    NumBytesWritten += NumBytesToWrite;\n    NumBytes        -= NumBytesToWrite;\n    WrOff           += NumBytesToWrite;\n    while (NumBytesToWrite--) {\n      *pDst++ = *pBuffer++;\n    };\n#else\n    SEGGER_RTT_MEMCPY(pRing-&gt;pBuffer + WrOff, pBuffer, NumBytesToWrite);\n    NumBytesWritten += NumBytesToWrite;\n    pBuffer         += NumBytesToWrite;\n    NumBytes        -= NumBytesToWrite;\n    WrOff           += NumBytesToWrite;\n#endif\n    if (WrOff == pRing-&gt;SizeOfBuffer) {\n      WrOff = 0u;\n    }\n    pRing-&gt;WrOff = WrOff;\n  } while (NumBytes);\n  //\n  return NumBytesWritten;\n}\n\n/*********************************************************************\n*\n*       _WriteNoCheck()\n*\n*  Function description\n*    Stores a specified number of characters in SEGGER RTT ring buffer\n*    and updates the associated write pointer which is periodically\n*    read by the host.\n*    It is callers responsibility to make sure data actually fits in buffer.\n*\n*  Parameters\n*    pRing        Ring buffer to post to.\n*    pBuffer      Pointer to character array. Does not need to point to a \\0 terminated string.\n*    NumBytes     Number of bytes to be stored in the SEGGER RTT control block.\n*\n*  Notes\n*    (1) If there might not be enough space in the \"Up\"-buffer, call _WriteBlocking\n*/",

        "contents": "/*********************************************************************\n*\n*       SEGGER_RTT_PutCharSkipNoLock\n*\n*  Function description\n*    Stores a single character/byte in SEGGER RTT buffer.\n*    SEGGER_RTT_PutCharSkipNoLock does not lock the application and\n*    skips the byte, if it does not fit into the buffer.\n*\n*  Parameters\n*    BufferIndex  Index of \"Up\"-buffer to be used (e.g. 0 for \"Terminal\").\n*    c            Byte to be stored.\n*\n*  Return value\n*    Number of bytes which have been stored in the \"Up\"-buffer.\n*\n*  Notes\n*    (1) If there is not enough space in the \"Up\"-buffer, the character is dropped.\n*    (2) For performance reasons this function does not call Init()\n*        and may only be called after RTT has been initialized.\n*        Either by calling SEGGER_RTT_Init() or calling another RTT API function first.\n*/\n\nunsigned SEGGER_RTT_PutCharSkipNoLock(unsigned BufferIndex, char c) {\n  SEGGER_RTT_BUFFER_UP* pRing;\n  unsigned              WrOff;\n  unsigned              Status;\n  //\n  // Get \"to-host\" ring buffer.\n  //\n  pRing = &amp;_SEGGER_RTT.aUp[BufferIndex];\n  //\n  // Get write position and handle wrap-around if necessary\n  //\n  WrOff = pRing-&gt;WrOff + 1;\n  if (WrOff == pRing-&gt;SizeOfBuffer) {\n    WrOff = 0;\n  }\n  //\n  // Output byte if free space is available\n  //\n  if (WrOff != pRing-&gt;RdOff) {\n    pRing-&gt;pBuffer[pRing-&gt;WrOff] = c;\n    pRing-&gt;WrOff = WrOff;\n    Status = 1;\n  } else {\n    Status = 0;\n  }\n  //\n  return Status;\n}\n\n/*********************************************************************\n*\n*       SEGGER_RTT_PutCharSkip\n*\n*  Function description\n*    Stores a single character/byte in SEGGER RTT buffer.\n*\n*  Parameters\n*    BufferIndex  Index of \"Up\"-buffer to be used (e.g. 0 for \"Terminal\").\n*    c            Byte to be stored.\n*\n*  Return value\n*    Number of bytes which have been stored in the \"Up\"-buffer.\n*\n*  Notes\n*    (1) If there is not enough space in the \"Up\"-buffer, the character is dropped.\n*/",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {

        "contents": "  return Status;\n}\n\n/*********************************************************************\n*\n*       SEGGER_RTT_PutCharSkip\n*\n*  Function description\n*    Stores a single character/byte in SEGGER RTT buffer.\n*\n*  Parameters\n*    BufferIndex  Index of \"Up\"-buffer to be used (e.g. 0 for \"Terminal\").\n*    c            Byte to be stored.\n*\n*  Return value\n*    Number of bytes which have been stored in the \"Up\"-buffer.\n*\n*  Notes\n*    (1) If there is not enough space in the \"Up\"-buffer, the character is dropped.\n*/\n\nunsigned SEGGER_RTT_PutCharSkip(unsigned BufferIndex, char c) {\n  SEGGER_RTT_BUFFER_UP* pRing;\n  unsigned              WrOff;\n  unsigned              Status;\n  //\n  // Prepare\n  //\n  INIT();\n  SEGGER_RTT_LOCK();\n  //\n  // Get \"to-host\" ring buffer.\n  //\n  pRing = &amp;_SEGGER_RTT.aUp[BufferIndex];\n  //\n  // Get write position and handle wrap-around if necessary\n  //\n  WrOff = pRing-&gt;WrOff + 1;\n  if (WrOff == pRing-&gt;SizeOfBuffer) {\n    WrOff = 0;\n  }\n  //\n  // Output byte if free space is available\n  //\n  if (WrOff != pRing-&gt;RdOff) {\n    pRing-&gt;pBuffer[pRing-&gt;WrOff] = c;\n    pRing-&gt;WrOff = WrOff;\n    Status = 1;\n  } else {\n    Status = 0;\n  }\n  //\n  // Finish up.\n  //\n  SEGGER_RTT_UNLOCK();\n  //\n  return Status;\n}\n\n /*********************************************************************\n*\n*       SEGGER_RTT_PutChar\n*\n*  Function description\n*    Stores a single character/byte in SEGGER RTT buffer.\n*\n*  Parameters\n*    BufferIndex  Index of \"Up\"-buffer to be used (e.g. 0 for \"Terminal\").\n*    c            Byte to be stored.\n*\n*  Return value\n*    Number of bytes which have been stored in the \"Up\"-buffer.\n*\n*  Notes\n*    (1) Data is stored according to buffer flags.\n*/\n\nunsigned SEGGER_RTT_PutChar(unsigned BufferIndex, char c)",

        "relativeWorkspacePath": ".\\Src\\examples\\ex_21_orchestrator\\orchestrator_tx.c",

        },
        "contents": "/**\n * Application entry point\n */\nint orchestrator_tx(void)\n{\n    uint32_t dev_id;\n\n    /* Display application name */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Initialize UART for RS-485 */\n    uart_init();\n    \n    /* Small delay to ensure UART is ready */\n    Sleep(200);\n    \n    /* Send startup message to verify UART is working */\n    send_response(\"OK STARTUP\");\n    \n    /* Send additional diagnostic info */\n    Sleep(100);\n    send_response(\"OK FIRMWARE_RUNNING\");\n\n    /* Initialize app timer module */\n    uint32_t err_code = app_timer_init();\n    if (err_code != NRF_SUCCESS)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"TIMER INIT FAILED\");\n    }\n    else\n    {\n        /* Create timer instance */\n        err_code = app_timer_create(&amp;m_tx_timer_id, APP_TIMER_MODE_REPEATED, tx_timer_handler);\n        if (err_code == NRF_SUCCESS)\n        {\n            g_timer_initialized = 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC();\n    Sleep(2);\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n    dev_id = dwt_readdevid();\n\n    /* Wait for DW3000 to be ready with timeout */\n    uint32_t timeout_count = 0;\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc() &amp;&amp; timeout_count &lt; 1000)\n    {\n        timeout_count++;\n        Sleep(1);\n    }\n    \n    if (timeout_count &gt;= 1000)\n    {\n        send_response(\"ERR DW3000_TIMEOUT\");\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"DW3000 TIMEOUT\");\n    }\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        send_response(\"ERR DW3000_INIT_FAILED\");\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED\");\n        // Don't hang - continue so UART commands still work\n    }\n    else\n    {\n        send_response(\"OK DW3000_READY\");\n    }\n\n    /* Enable LEDs */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure with default settings */\n    configure_uwb();\n\n    /* Send message that we reached main loop */\n    Sleep(100);\n    send_response(\"OK MAIN_LOOP\");\n    \n    /* Main loop - process UART commands */",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [

        "contents": "/**\n * Configure UWB radio\n */\nstatic void configure_uwb(void)\n{\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;dwt_config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED\");\n        return;\n    }\n\n    // Configure TX power (simplified - use default txconfig_options)\n    extern dwt_txconfig_t txconfig_options;\n    dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options);\n}\n\n/**\n * TX timer handler - called periodically to send packets\n */\nstatic void tx_timer_handler(void *p_context)\n{\n    if (g_test_running)\n    {\n        send_packet();\n    }\n}\n\n/**\n * Send a test packet\n */\nstatic void send_packet(void)\n{\n    uint32_t status_reg;\n\n    // Prepare packet\n    g_tx_packet.seq = g_seq_num++;\n    g_tx_packet.t_local = dwt_readsystimestamphi32();\n    \n    // Fill payload with pattern\n    for (int i = 0; i &lt; g_config.payload_len &amp;&amp; i &lt; sizeof(g_tx_packet.payload); i++)\n    {\n        g_tx_packet.payload[i] = 0xAA;\n    }\n\n    // Copy to TX buffer\n    // Calculate frame length: header (seq + t_local) + actual payload length\n    uint16_t frame_len = sizeof(uint32_t) + sizeof(uint32_t) + g_config.payload_len + FCS_LEN;\n    uint16_t data_len = sizeof(uint32_t) + sizeof(uint32_t) + g_config.payload_len;\n    memcpy(g_tx_buffer, &amp;g_tx_packet, data_len);\n\n    // Write TX data\n    dwt_writetxdata(data_len, g_tx_buffer, 0);\n    dwt_writetxfctrl(frame_len, 0, 0);\n\n    // Start transmission\n    dwt_starttx(DWT_START_TX_IMMEDIATE);\n\n    // Wait for TX complete\n    waitforsysstatus(&amp;status_reg, NULL, DWT_INT_TXFRS_BIT_MASK, 0);\n\n    if (status_reg &amp; DWT_INT_TXFRS_BIT_MASK)\n    {\n        dwt_writesysstatuslo(DWT_INT_TXFRS_BIT_MASK);\n        g_stats.total_sent++;\n        g_stats.last_error = 0;\n    }\n    else\n    {\n        g_stats.last_error = 1;\n    }\n}\n\n/**\n * Application entry point\n */\nint orchestrator_tx(void)\n{\n    uint32_t dev_id;\n\n    /* Display application name */",

If no room\n      // for terminal switch, skip that totally.\n      //\n      if (Avail &lt; 4u) {\n        Status = -1;\n      } else {\n        _PostTerminalSwitch(pRing, TerminalId);\n        Status = (int)_WriteBlocking(pRing, s, (FragLen &lt; (Avail - 4u)) ? FragLen : (Avail - 4u));\n        _PostTerminalSwitch(pRing, _ActiveTerminal);\n      }\n      break;\n    case SEGGER_RTT_MODE_BLOCK_IF_FIFO_FULL:\n      //",

        "contents": "export class RS485Comm extends EventEmitter {\nasync sendCommand(command, timeout = this.timeout) {\n(resolve, reject) =&gt; {\n(writeError) =&gt; {\n\n          return;\n        }\n\n        // Ensure data is flushed to hardware (critical for RS-485)\n        // This must complete before the Promise can resolve, preventing race conditions\n        this.serialPort.drain((drainError) =&gt; {\n          // #region agent log - sendCommand drain callback\n          fetch(\n            \"http://127.0.0.1:7246/ingest/53b9dbf8-c6bb-42df-aadd-00e84572bd7f\",\n            {\n              method: \"POST\",\n              headers: { \"Content-Type\": \"application/json\" },\n              body: JSON.stringify({\n                location: \"rs485Comm.js:sendCommand\",\n                message: \"sendCommand drain callback\",\n                data: { commandId, drainError: drainError?.message },\n                timestamp: Date.now(),\n                sessionId: \"debug-session\",\n                runId: \"run1\",\n                hypothesisId: \"C\",\n              }),\n            }\n          ).catch(() =&gt; {});\n          // #endregion\n          if (drainError) {\n            clearTimeout(timer);\n            this.pendingCommands.delete(commandId);\n            reject(drainError);\n            return;\n          }\n\n          if (process.env.DEBUG_RS485) {\n            console.log(\n              &#96;[RS485 TX] ${this.port}: Data drained (sent to hardware)&#96;\n            );\n          }\n\n          // Drain complete - data is now guaranteed to be flushed\n          // The outer Promise will resolve when response is received via handleResponse()\n        });\n      });\n    });\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Handle incoming response\n   * @param {string} data - Response data\n   */\n}",

        "contents": "    while (1)\n    {\n        /* Write frame data to DW3000 and prepare transmission. See NOTE 5 below.*/\n        dwt_writetxdata(FRAME_LENGTH - FCS_LEN, tx_msg, 0); /* Zero offset in TX buffer. */\n        dwt_writetxfctrl(FRAME_LENGTH, 0, 0);               /* Zero offset in TX buffer, no ranging. */\n\n        /* Start transmission with CCA. The transmission will only start once there is no preamble detected within 3 PACs as defined above\n         * e.g. once we get the preamble timeout or TX will be canceled if a preamble is detected. */\n        dwt_starttx(DWT_START_TX_CCA);\n\n        /* Poll DW3000 until either TX complete or CCA_FAIL. See NOTE 6 below. */\n        waitforsysstatus(&amp;status_reg, &amp;status_regh, DWT_INT_TXFRS_BIT_MASK, DWT_INT_HI_CCA_FAIL_BIT_MASK);\n\n        if (status_reg &amp; DWT_INT_TXFRS_BIT_MASK)\n        {\n            tx_sleep_period = TX_DELAY_MS;                  /* sent a frame - set interframe period */\n            next_backoff_interval = INITIAL_BACKOFF_PERIOD; /* set initial backoff period */\n            /* Increment the blink frame sequence number (modulo 256). */\n            tx_msg[BLINK_FRAME_SN_IDX]++;\n        }\n        else\n        {\n            /* if DW IC detected the preamble, device will be in IDLE */\n\n            tx_sleep_period = next_backoff_interval; /* set the TX sleep period */\n            /* If failed to transmit, increase backoff and try again.\n             * In a real implementation the back-off is typically a randomised period\n             * whose range is an exponentially related to the number of successive failures.\n             * See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exponential_backoff */\n            next_backoff_interval++;\n        }\n\n        /* Clear TX frame sent event. */\n        dwt_writesysstatuslo(DWT_INT_TXFRS_BIT_MASK);\n\n        /* Execute a delay between transmissions. */\n        Sleep(tx_sleep_period);\n    }\n}\n#endif\n/*****************************************************************************************************************************************************\n * NOTES:\n *\n * 1. For Wireless Sensor Networks application, most of the MAC protocols rely on Clear Channel Assessment (CCA) to avoid collisions with other frames\n *    in the air. This consists in sampling the air for a short period to see if the medium is idle before transmitting. For most radios this involves\n *    looking for the RF carrier, but for UWB where this is not possible, one approach is to just look for preamble to avoid conflicting transmissions,\n *    since any sending of preamble during data will typically not disturb those receivers who are demodulating in data mode.\n *    The idea then is to sample the air for a small amount of time to see if a preamble can be detected, then if preamble is not seen the transmission\n *    is initiated, otherwise we defer the transmission typically for a random back-off period after which transmission is again attempted with CCA.\n *    Note: we return to idle for the back-off period and do not receive the frame whose preamble was detected, since the MAC (and upper layer) wants\n *    to transmit and not receive at this time.\n *    This example has been designed to operate with example 4b - Continuous Frame. The 4b device will fill the air with frames which will be detected\n *    by the CCA and thus the CCA will cancel the transmission and will use back off to try sending again at later stage. This example will actually\n *    get to send when the CCA preamble detection overlaps with the data portion of the continuous TX or inter frame period, Note the Continuous Frame\n *    example actually stops after 30s interval (thus the user should toggle the reset button on the unit running example 4b to restart it if they wish\n *    to continue observing this pseudo CCA experiencing an environment of high air-utilisation).\n * 2. The device ID is a hard coded constant in the blink to keep the example simple but for a real product every device should have a unique ID.\n *    For development purposes it is possible to generate a DW3000 unique ID by combining the Lot ID &amp; Part Number values programmed into the\n *    DW3000 during its manufacture. However there is no guarantee this will not conflict with someone else’s implementation. We recommended that\n *    customers buy a block of addresses from the IEEE Registration Authority for their production items. See \"EUI\" in the DW3000 User Manual.\n * 3. In a real application, for optimum performance within regulatory limits, it may be necessary to set TX pulse bandwidth and TX power, (using\n *    the dwt_configuretxrf API call) to per device calibrated values saved in the target system or the DW3000 OTP memory.\n * 4. The preamble timeout of 3 PACs is recommended as sufficient for this CCA example for all modes and data rates. The PAC size should be different\n *    when is different for different preamble configurations, as per User Manual guidelines.\n * 5. dwt_writetxdata() takes the tx_msg buffer and copies it into devices TX buffer memory, the two byte check-sum at the end of the frame is\n *    automatically appended by the DW3000, thus the dwt_writetxfctrl() should be given the total length.\n * 6. We use polled mode of operation here to keep the example as simple as possible, but the TXFRS and CCA_FAIL status events can be used to generate\n *    an interrupt. Please refer to DW3000 User Manual for more details on \"interrupts\".\n * 7. Desired configuration by user may be different to the current programmed configuration. dwt_configure is called to set desired\n *    configuration.\n ****************************************************************************************************************************************************/",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [

            "lineNumber": 147
          },
          {
            "text": "         * e.g. once we get the preamble timeout or TX will be canceled if a preamble is detected. */",
            "lineNumber": 148
          },
          {
            "text": "        dwt_starttx(DWT_START_TX_CCA);",
            "lineNumber": 149
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 150
          },
          {
            "text": "        /* Poll DW3000 until either TX complete or CCA_FAIL. See NOTE 6 below. */",
            "lineNumber": 151
          },
          {
            "text": "        waitforsysstatus(&amp;status_reg, &amp;status_regh, DWT_INT_TXFRS_BIT_MASK, DWT_INT_HI_CCA_FAIL_BIT_MASK);",
            "lineNumber": 152
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 153
          },
          {
            "text": "        if (status_reg &amp; DWT_INT_TXFRS_BIT_MASK)",
            "lineNumber": 154
          },
          {
            "text": "        {",
            "lineNumber": 155
          },
          {
            "text": "            tx_sleep_period = TX_DELAY_MS;                  /* sent a frame - set interframe period */",
            "lineNumber": 156
          },
          {
            "text": "            next_backoff_interval = INITIAL_BACKOFF_PERIOD; /* set initial backoff period */",
            "lineNumber": 157
          },
          {
            "text": "            /* Increment the blink frame sequence number (modulo 256). */",
            "lineNumber": 158
          },
          {
            "text": "            tx_msg[BLINK_FRAME_SN_IDX]++;",
            "lineNumber": 159
          },
          {
            "text": "        }",
            "lineNumber": 160
          },
          {
            "text": "        else",
            "lineNumber": 161
          },
          {
            "text": "        {",
            "lineNumber": 162
          },
          {
            "text": "            /* if DW IC detected the preamble, device will be in IDLE */",
            "lineNumber": 163
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 164
          },
          {
            "text": "            tx_sleep_period = next_backoff_interval; /* set the TX sleep period */",
            "lineNumber": 165
          },
          {
            "text": "            /* If failed to transmit, increase backoff and try again.",
            "lineNumber": 166
          },
          {
            "text": "             * In a real implementation the back-off is typically a randomised period",
            "lineNumber": 167
          },
          {
            "text": "             * whose range is an exponentially related to the number of successive failures.",
            "lineNumber": 168
          },
          {
            "text": "             * See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exponential_backoff */",
            "lineNumber": 169
          },
          {
            "text": "            next_backoff_interval++;",
            "lineNumber": 170
          },
          {
            "text": "        }",
            "lineNumber": 171
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 172
          },
          {
            "text": "        /* Clear TX frame sent event. */",
            "lineNumber": 173
          },
          {
            "text": "        dwt_writesysstatuslo(DWT_INT_TXFRS_BIT_MASK);",
            "lineNumber": 174
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 175
          },
          {
            "text": "        /* Execute a delay between transmissions. */",
            "lineNumber": 176
          },
          {
            "text": "        Sleep(tx_sleep_period);",
            "lineNumber": 177
          },
          {
            "text": "    }",
            "lineNumber": 178
          },
          {
            "text": "}",
            "lineNumber": 179
          },
          {
            "text": "#endif",
            "lineNumber": 180
          },
          {
            "text": "/*****************************************************************************************************************************************************",
            "lineNumber": 181
          },
          {
            "text": " * NOTES:",
            "lineNumber": 182
          },
          {
            "text": " *",
            "lineNumber": 183
          },
          {
            "text": " * 1. For Wireless Sensor Networks application, most of the MAC protocols rely on Clear Channel Assessment (CCA) to avoid collisions with other frames",
            "lineNumber": 184
          },
          {
            "text": " *    in the air. This consists in sampling the air for a short period to see if the medium is idle before transmitting. For most radios this involves",
            "lineNumber": 185
          },
          {
            "text": " *    looking for the RF carrier, but for UWB where this is not possible, one approach is to just look for preamble to avoid conflicting transmissions,",
            "lineNumber": 186
          },
          {
            "text": " *    since any sending of preamble during data will typically not disturb those receivers who are demodulating in data mode.",
            "lineNumber": 187
          },
          {
            "text": " *    The idea then is to sample the air for a small amount of time to see if a preamble can be detected, then if preamble is not seen the transmission",
            "lineNumber": 188
          },
          {
            "text": " *    is initiated, otherwise we defer the transmission typically for a random back-off period after which transmission is again attempted with CCA.",
            "lineNumber": 189
          },
          {
            "text": " *    Note: we return to idle for the back-off period and do not receive the frame whose preamble was detected, since the MAC (and upper layer) wants",
            "lineNumber": 190
          },
          {
            "text": " *    to transmit and not receive at this time.",
            "lineNumber": 191
          },
          {
            "text": " *    This example has been designed to operate with example 4b - Continuous Frame. The 4b device will fill the air with frames which will be detected",
            "lineNumber": 192
          },
          {
            "text": " *    by the CCA and thus the CCA will cancel the transmission and will use back off to try sending again at later stage. This example will actually",
            "lineNumber": 193
          },
          {
            "text": " *    get to send when the CCA preamble detection overlaps with the data portion of the continuous TX or inter frame period, Note the Continuous Frame",
            "lineNumber": 194
          },
          {
            "text": " *    example actually stops after 30s interval (thus the user should toggle the reset button on the unit running example 4b to restart it if they wish",
            "lineNumber": 195
          },
          {
            "text": " *    to continue observing this pseudo CCA experiencing an environment of high air-utilisation).",
            "lineNumber": 196
          },
          {
            "text": " * 2. The device ID is a hard coded constant in the blink to keep the example simple but for a real product every device should have a unique ID.",
            "lineNumber": 197
          },
          {
            "text": " *    For development purposes it is possible to generate a DW3000 unique ID by combining the Lot ID &amp; Part Number values programmed into the",
            "lineNumber": 198
          },
          {
            "text": " *    DW3000 during its manufacture. However there is no guarantee this will not conflict with someone else’s implementation. We recommended that",
            "lineNumber": 199
          },
          {
            "text": " *    customers buy a block of addresses from the IEEE Registration Authority for their production items. See \"EUI\" in the DW3000 User Manual.",
            "lineNumber": 200
          },
          {
            "text": " * 3. In a real application, for optimum performance within regulatory limits, it may be necessary to set TX pulse bandwidth and TX power, (using",
            "lineNumber": 201
          },
          {
            "text": " *    the dwt_configuretxrf API call) to per device calibrated values saved in the target system or the DW3000 OTP memory.",
            "lineNumber": 202
          },
          {
            "text": " * 4. The preamble timeout of 3 PACs is recommended as sufficient for this CCA example for all modes and data rates. The PAC size should be different",
            "lineNumber": 203
          },
          {
            "text": " *    when is different for different preamble configurations, as per User Manual guidelines.",
            "lineNumber": 204
          },
          {
            "text": " * 5. dwt_writetxdata() takes the tx_msg buffer and copies it into devices TX buffer memory, the two byte check-sum at the end of the frame is",
            "lineNumber": 205
          },
          {
            "text": " *    automatically appended by the DW3000, thus the dwt_writetxfctrl() should be given the total length.",
            "lineNumber": 206
          },
          {
            "text": " * 6. We use polled mode of operation here to keep the example as simple as possible, but the TXFRS and CCA_FAIL status events can be used to generate",
            "lineNumber": 207
          },
          {
            "text": " *    an interrupt. Please refer to DW3000 User Manual for more details on \"interrupts\".",
            "lineNumber": 208
          },
          {
            "text": " * 7. Desired configuration by user may be different to the current programmed configuration. dwt_configure is called to set desired",
            "lineNumber": 209
          },
          {
            "text": " *    configuration.",
            "lineNumber": 210
          },
          {
            "text": " ****************************************************************************************************************************************************/",
            "lineNumber": 211
          }
        ]
      },
      "score": 0.30896660685539246
    },

        "contents": "  return Status;\n}\n\n/*********************************************************************\n*\n*       SEGGER_RTT_Write\n*\n*  Function description\n*    Stores a specified number of characters in SEGGER RTT\n*    control block which is then read by the host.\n*\n*  Parameters\n*    BufferIndex  Index of \"Up\"-buffer to be used (e.g. 0 for \"Terminal\").\n*    pBuffer      Pointer to character array. Does not need to point to a \\0 terminated string.\n*    NumBytes     Number of bytes to be stored in the SEGGER RTT control block.\n*\n*  Return value\n*    Number of bytes which have been stored in the \"Up\"-buffer.\n*\n*  Notes\n*    (1) Data is stored according to buffer flags.\n*/\nunsigned SEGGER_RTT_Write(unsigned BufferIndex, const void* pBuffer, unsigned NumBytes) {\n  unsigned Status;\n  //\n  INIT();\n  SEGGER_RTT_LOCK();\n  //\n  // Call the non-locking write function\n  //\n  Status = SEGGER_RTT_WriteNoLock(BufferIndex, pBuffer, NumBytes);\n  //\n  // Finish up.\n  //\n  SEGGER_RTT_UNLOCK();\n  //\n  return Status;\n}\n\n/*********************************************************************\n*\n*       SEGGER_RTT_WriteString\n*\n*  Function description\n*    Stores string in SEGGER RTT control block.\n*    This data is read by the host.\n*\n*  Parameters\n*    BufferIndex  Index of \"Up\"-buffer to be used (e.g. 0 for \"Terminal\").\n*    s            Pointer to string.\n*\n*  Return value\n*    Number of bytes which have been stored in the \"Up\"-buffer.\n*\n*  Notes\n*    (1) Data is stored according to buffer flags.\n*    (2) String passed to this function has to be \\0 terminated\n*    (3) \\0 termination character is *not* stored in RTT buffer\n*/\nunsigned SEGGER_RTT_WriteString(unsigned BufferIndex, const char* s) {\n  unsigned Len;\n\n  Len = STRLEN(s);\n  return SEGGER_RTT_Write(BufferIndex, s, Len);\n}\n\n/*********************************************************************\n*\n*       SEGGER_RTT_PutCharSkipNoLock\n*\n*  Function description\n*    Stores a single character/byte in SEGGER RTT buffer.\n*    SEGGER_RTT_PutCharSkipNoLock does not lock the application and\n*    skips the byte, if it does not fit into the buffer.\n*\n*  Parameters\n*    BufferIndex  Index of \"Up\"-buffer to be used (e.g. 0 for \"Terminal\").\n*    c            Byte to be stored.\n*\n*  Return value\n*    Number of bytes which have been stored in the \"Up\"-buffer.\n*\n*  Notes\n*    (1) If there is not enough space in the \"Up\"-buffer, the character is dropped.\n*    (2) For performance reasons this function does not call Init()\n*        and may only be called after RTT has been initialized.\n*        Either by calling SEGGER_RTT_Init() or calling another RTT API function first.\n*/",

        "contents": "int orchestrator_rx(void)\n{\n    uint32_t dev_id;\n\n    /* Display application name */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Initialize UART for RS-485 */\n    uart_init();\n    \n    /* Small delay to ensure UART is ready */\n    Sleep(200);\n    \n    /* Send startup message to verify UART is working */\n    send_response(\"OK STARTUP\");\n    \n    /* Send additional diagnostic info */\n    Sleep(100);\n    send_response(\"OK FIRMWARE_RUNNING\");\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC();\n    Sleep(2);\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n    dev_id = dwt_readdevid();\n\n    /* Wait for DW3000 to be ready with timeout */\n    uint32_t timeout_count = 0;\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc() &amp;&amp; timeout_count &lt; 1000)\n    {\n        timeout_count++;\n        Sleep(1);\n    }\n    \n    if (timeout_count &gt;= 1000)\n    {\n        send_response(\"ERR DW3000_TIMEOUT\");\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"DW3000 TIMEOUT\");\n    }\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        send_response(\"ERR DW3000_INIT_FAILED\");\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED\");\n        // Don't hang - continue so UART commands still work\n    }\n    else\n    {\n        send_response(\"OK DW3000_READY\");\n    }\n\n    /* Enable LEDs */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure with default settings */\n    configure_uwb();\n\n    /* Enable RX initially (will be controlled by START/STOP commands) */\n    dwt_rxenable(DWT_START_RX_IMMEDIATE);\n\n    /* Send message that we reached main loop */\n    Sleep(100);\n    send_response(\"OK MAIN_LOOP\");\n    \n    /* Main loop - process UART commands and RX packets */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        if (g_test_running)\n        {\n            process_rx_packet();\n        }\n        else\n        {\n            Sleep(100);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#endif",

        "contents": "    /*! ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n     * @brief This API function writes the supplied TX data into the DW3000's\n     * TX buffer.  The input parameters are the data length in bytes and a pointer\n     * to those data bytes.\n     *\n     * input parameters\n     * @param txDataLength   - This is the total length of data (in bytes) to write to the tx buffer.\n     *                         Note: the size of tx buffer is 1024 bytes.\n     *                         The standard PHR mode allows to transmit frames of up to 127 bytes (including 2 byte CRC)\n     *                         The extended PHR mode allows to transmit frames of up to 1023 bytes (including 2 byte CRC)\n     *                         if &gt; 127 is programmed, DWT_PHRMODE_EXT needs to be set in the phrMode configuration\n     *                         see dwt_configure function\n     * @param txDataBytes    - Pointer to the user's buffer containing the data to send.\n     * @param txBufferOffset - This specifies an offset in the DW IC's TX Buffer at which to start writing data.\n     *\n     * output parameters\n     *\n     * returns DWT_SUCCESS for success, or DWT_ERROR for error\n     */\n    int dwt_writetxdata(uint16_t txDataLength, uint8_t *txDataBytes, uint16_t txBufferOffset);\n\n    /*! ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n     * @brief This API function configures the TX frame control register before the transmission of a frame\n     *\n     * input parameters:\n     * @param txFrameLength - this is the length of TX message (including the 2 byte CRC) - max is 1023\n     *                              NOTE: standard PHR mode allows up to 127 bytes\n     *                              if &gt; 127 is programmed, DWT_PHRMODE_EXT needs to be set in the phrMode configuration\n     *                              see dwt_configure function\n     * @param txBufferOffset - the offset in the tx buffer to start writing the data\n     * @param ranging - 1 if this is a ranging frame, else 0\n     *\n     * output parameters\n     *\n     * no return value\n     */",

Does not need to point to a \\0 terminated string.\n*    NumBytes     Number of bytes to be stored in the SEGGER RTT control block.\n*\n*  Notes\n*    (1) If there might not be enough space in the \"Up\"-buffer, call _WriteBlocking\n*/\nstatic void _WriteNoCheck(SEGGER_RTT_BUFFER_UP* pRing, const char* pData, unsigned NumBytes) {\n  unsigned NumBytesAtOnce;\n  unsigned WrOff;\n  unsigned Rem;",

        "contents": "int writetospiwithcrc(uint16_t headerLength, const uint8_t *headerBuffer, uint16_t bodyLength, const uint8_t *bodyBuffer, uint8_t crc8)\n{\n#ifdef DWT_ENABLE_CRC\n    uint8_t *p1;\n    uint32_t idatalength = headerLength + bodyLength + sizeof(crc8); // It cannot be more than 255 in total length (header + body)\n\n    if (idatalength &gt; DATALEN1)\n    {\n        return NRF_ERROR_NO_MEM;\n    }\n\n    while(pgSpiHandler-&gt;lock);\n\n    __HAL_LOCK(pgSpiHandler);\n\n    openspi(&amp;pgSpiHandler-&gt;spi_inst);\n\n    p1 = idatabuf;\n    memcpy(p1, headerBuffer, headerLength);\n    p1 += headerLength;\n    memcpy(p1, bodyBuffer, bodyLength);\n    p1 += bodyLength;\n    memcpy(p1, &amp;crc8, 1);\n\n    nrfx_gpiote_out_toggle(current_cs_pin);\n\n    spi_xfer_done = false;\n    nrf_drv_spi_transfer(&amp;pgSpiHandler-&gt;spi_inst, idatabuf, idatalength, itempbuf, idatalength);\n\n    closespi(&amp;pgSpiHandler-&gt;spi_inst);\n    nrfx_gpiote_out_toggle(current_cs_pin);\n\n    __HAL_UNLOCK(pgSpiHandler);\n#endif //DWT_ENABLE_CRC\n    return 0;\n} // end writetospiwithcrc()\n\n/*! ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n * Function: writetospi()\n *\n * Low level abstract function to write to the SPI\n * Takes two separate byte buffers for write header and write data\n * returns 0 for success, or -1 for error\n */\nint writetospi(uint16_t headerLength, const uint8_t *headerBuffer, uint16_t bodyLength, const uint8_t *bodyBuffer)\n{\n    uint8_t *p1;\n    uint32_t idatalength = headerLength + bodyLength;",

        "contents": "    dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options);\n\n    /* Loop forever sending frames periodically. */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        /* Write frame data to DW IC and prepare transmission. See NOTE 3 below.*/\n        dwt_writetxdata(FRAME_LENGTH - FCS_LEN, tx_msg, 0); /* Zero offset in TX buffer. */\n\n        /* In this example since the length of the transmitted frame does not change,\n         * nor the other parameters of the dwt_writetxfctrl function, the\n         * dwt_writetxfctrl call could be outside the main while(1) loop.\n         */\n        dwt_writetxfctrl(FRAME_LENGTH, 0, 0); /* Zero offset in TX buffer, no ranging. */\n\n        /* Start transmission. */\n        dwt_starttx(DWT_START_TX_IMMEDIATE);\n        /* Poll DW IC until TX frame sent event set. See NOTE 4 below.\n         * STATUS register is 4 bytes long but, as the event we are looking\n         * at is in the first byte of the register, we can use this simplest\n         * API function to access it.*/\n        waitforsysstatus(NULL, NULL, DWT_INT_TXFRS_BIT_MASK, 0);\n\n        /* Clear TX frame sent event. */\n        dwt_writesysstatuslo(DWT_INT_TXFRS_BIT_MASK);\n\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"TX Frame Sent\");\n\n        /* Execute a delay between transmissions. */\n        Sleep(TX_DELAY_MS);\n\n        /* Increment the blink frame sequence number (modulo 256). */\n        tx_msg[BLINK_FRAME_SN_IDX]++;\n    }\n}\n\n#endif\n/*****************************************************************************************************************************************************\n * NOTES:\n *\n * 1. The device ID is a hard coded constant in the blink to keep the example simple but for a real product every device should have a unique ID.\n *    For development purposes it is possible to generate a DW IC unique ID by combining the Lot ID &amp; Part Number values programmed into the\n *    DW IC during its manufacture. However there is no guarantee this will not conflict with someone else�s implementation. We recommended that\n *    customers buy a block of addresses from the IEEE Registration Authority for their production items. See \"EUI\" in the DW IC User Manual.\n * 2. In a real application, for optimum performance within regulatory limits, it may be necessary to set TX pulse bandwidth and TX power, (using\n *    the dwt_configuretxrf API call) to per device calibrated values saved in the target system or the DW IC OTP memory.\n * 3. dwt_writetxdata() takes the full size of tx_msg as a parameter but only copies (size - 2) bytes as the check-sum at the end of the frame is\n *    automatically appended by the DW IC. This means that our tx_msg could be two bytes shorter without losing any data (but the sizeof would not\n *    work anymore then as we would still have to indicate the full length of the frame to dwt_writetxdata()).\n * 4. We use polled mode of operation here to keep the example as simple as possible, but the TXFRS status event can be used to generate an interrupt.\n *    Please refer to DW IC User Manual for more details on \"interrupts\".\n * 5. Desired configuration by user may be different to the current programmed configuration. dwt_configure is called to set desired\n *    configuration.\n ****************************************************************************************************************************************************/",

Added timeout protection and test characters. The firmware will:

1. Send test characters `!UART` individually after UART init
2. Use timeouts to prevent infinite blocking
3. Send diagnostic messages at each stage

## Enhanced instrumentation

**Test characters:** `!UART` sent one character at a time (verifies UART TX works)  
**Timeout protection:** Prevents infinite blocking if UART isn't ready  
**Diagnostic messages:** Shows exactly where firmware execution reaches

<reproduction_steps>
1. Rebuild TX firmware with enhanced diagnostics:
   ```powershell
   .\build-and-flash-tx.ps1
   ```
   Select TX board when prompted

2. Rebuild RX firmware with enhanced diagnostics:
   ```powershell
   .\build-and-flash-rx.ps1
   ```
   Select RX board when prompted

3. Wait 5 seconds after flashing for initialization

4. Test UART communication:
   ```powershell
   .\test-uart-direct.ps1
   ```
   The enhanced script will:
   - Wait 2 seconds for startup messages
   - Show any data received (including test characters)
   - Display ASCII and hex for each chunk

5. Look for these indicators:
   - `!UART` characters → UART TX is working
   - `OK UART_INIT` → UART initialized successfully
   - `OK STARTUP` → Firmware reached startup code
   - `OK MAIN_LOOP` → Firmware is running
   - No data at all → UART not working or firmware crashed early

6. Share the complete output from test-uart-direct.ps1 so we can analyze which stage is failing
</reproduction_steps>

The test characters (`!UART`) will help verify if UART TX works at all, even if full messages don't get through. Rebuild and test, then share the output.

        "contents": "static void uart_init(void)\n{\n    uint32_t err_code;\n    uint32_t *p_err_code = &amp;err_code;\n    app_uart_comm_params_t comm_params =\n    {\n        .rx_pin_no = UART_0_RX_PIN,\n        .tx_pin_no = UART_0_TX_PIN,\n        .rts_pin_no = DW3000_RTS_PIN_NUM,\n        .cts_pin_no = DW3000_CTS_PIN_NUM,\n        .flow_control = APP_UART_FLOW_CONTROL_DISABLED,\n        .use_parity = false,\n        .baud_rate = 30801920  // 115200 baud\n    };\n\n    APP_UART_FIFO_INIT(&amp;comm_params,\n                       UART_RX_BUFFER_SIZE,\n                       UART_TX_BUFFER_SIZE,\n                       uart_event_handler,\n                       APP_IRQ_PRIORITY_LOW,\n                       p_err_code);\n    \n    if (err_code != NRF_SUCCESS)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"UART INIT FAILED\");\n        // Try to send error via UART anyway (might work if partially initialized)\n        // Note: This might block if UART isn't ready, but we're debugging\n        for (int i = 0; i &lt; 10; i++) {\n            if (app_uart_put('E') == NRF_SUCCESS) break;\n            Sleep(10);\n        }\n    }\n    else\n    {\n        // UART init succeeded - send confirmation\n        Sleep(100);  // Brief delay for UART to stabilize\n        \n        // Send test characters first to verify TX works\n        send_test_char('!');\n        Sleep(10);\n        send_test_char('U');\n        Sleep(10);\n        send_test_char('A');\n        Sleep(10);\n        send_test_char('R');\n        Sleep(10);\n        send_test_char('T');\n        Sleep(10);\n        \n        // Now send full message\n        send_response(\"OK UART_INIT\");\n    }\n}\n\n/**\n * Send response over UART (with timeout protection)\n */\nstatic void send_response(const char *response)\n{\n    uint32_t len = strlen(response);\n    uint32_t timeout;",
