        "contents": "/**\n * Configure UWB radio\n */\nstatic void configure_uwb(void)\n{\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;dwt_config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED\");\n        return;\n    }\n}\n\n/**\n * Process received packet (non-blocking)\n */\nstatic void process_rx_packet(void)\n{\n    uint32_t status_reg;\n    uint16_t frame_len;\n    uwb_test_packet_t *rx_packet;\n\n    // Check status register non-blocking\n    status_reg = dwt_readsysstatuslo();\n    \n    // Check if we have a good RX frame or error\n    if (!(status_reg &amp; (DWT_INT_RXFCG_BIT_MASK | SYS_STATUS_ALL_RX_ERR)))\n    {\n        // No event yet, return without blocking\n        return;\n    }\n\n    if (status_reg &amp; DWT_INT_RXFCG_BIT_MASK)\n    {\n        // Good frame received\n        frame_len = dwt_getframelength();\n        if (frame_len &lt;= FRAME_LEN_MAX)\n        {\n            dwt_readrxdata(g_rx_buffer, frame_len - FCS_LEN, 0);\n            dwt_writesysstatuslo(DWT_INT_RXFCG_BIT_MASK);\n            \n            rx_packet = (uwb_test_packet_t *)g_rx_buffer;\n            \n            // Update statistics\n            g_stats.total_rx++;\n            \n            // Check sequence number\n            if (!g_stats.seq_init)\n            {\n                g_stats.last_seq = rx_packet-&gt;seq;\n                g_stats.seq_init = 1;\n            }\n            else\n            {\n                uint32_t expected_seq = g_stats.last_seq + 1;\n                if (rx_packet-&gt;seq != expected_seq)\n                {\n                    if (rx_packet-&gt;seq &gt; expected_seq)\n                    {\n                        g_stats.lost_pkts += (rx_packet-&gt;seq - expected_seq);\n                    }\n                }\n                g_stats.last_seq = rx_packet-&gt;seq;\n            }\n            \n            // Read RF metrics using diagnostics\n            dwt_rxdiag_t rx_diag;\n            dwt_readdiagnostics(&amp;rx_diag);\n            \n            // Extract RSSI from diagnostics\n            // RSSI can be calculated from the channel power (ipatovPower)\n            // For simplicity, we'll use a simplified RSSI calculation\n            // RSSI ≈ 10*log10(power) - A, where A is a calibration constant",

        "contents": "/* Statistics structure */\ntypedef struct {\n    uint32_t total_rx;        // Total packets received\n    uint32_t lost_pkts;       // Lost packets (sequence gaps)\n    uint32_t crc_err;         // CRC errors\n    uint32_t last_seq;        // Last received sequence number\n    uint8_t seq_init;         // Sequence initialized flag\n    \n    int64_t rssi_sum;         // Sum of RSSI values\n    int64_t snr_sum;          // Sum of SNR values\n    int64_t pre_q_sum;        // Sum of preamble quality values\n    uint32_t metric_count;    // Number of metrics collected\n} rx_stats_t;\n\n/* Global state */\nstatic uwb_config_t g_config = {\n    .channel = 5,\n    .data_rate = 1,           // 6.8Mbps\n    .preamble_len = 128,\n    .preamble_code = 9,\n    .tx_power_idx = 5,\n    .pkt_rate_hz = 100,\n    .payload_len = 64,\n    .configured = 0\n};\n\nstatic dwt_config_t dwt_config = {\n    5,                /* Channel number. */\n    DWT_PLEN_128,     /* Preamble length. */\n    DWT_PAC8,         /* Preamble acquisition chunk size. */\n    9,                /* TX preamble code. */\n    9,                /* RX preamble code. */\n    1,                /* SFD type */\n    DWT_BR_6M8,       /* Data rate. */\n    DWT_PHRMODE_STD,  /* PHY header mode. */\n    DWT_PHRRATE_STD,  /* PHY header rate. */\n    (129 + 8 - 8),    /* SFD timeout. */\n    DWT_STS_MODE_OFF, /* STS mode off. */\n    DWT_STS_LEN_64,   /* STS length. */\n    DWT_PDOA_M0       /* PDOA mode off. */\n};\n\nstatic rx_stats_t g_stats = {0};\nstatic volatile uint8_t g_test_running = 0;\nstatic uint8_t g_rx_buffer[FRAME_LEN_MAX];\n\n\n/* Forward declarations */\nstatic void uart_event_handler(app_uart_evt_t *p_event);\nstatic void parse_command(char *cmd);\nstatic void send_response(const char *response);\nstatic void send_test_char(char c);\nstatic void configure_uwb(void);\nstatic void process_rx_packet(void);\n\n/**\n * UART event handler\n */\nstatic void uart_event_handler(app_uart_evt_t *p_event)\n{\n    static uint8_t rx_buffer[UART_BUFFER_SIZE];\n    static uint16_t rx_index = 0;",

        "contents": "    dev_id = dwt_readdevid();\n\n    /* Wait for DW3000 to be ready with timeout */\n    uint32_t timeout_count = 0;\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc() &amp;&amp; timeout_count &lt; 1000)\n    {\n        timeout_count++;\n        Sleep(1);\n    }\n    \n    if (timeout_count &gt;= 1000)\n    {\n        send_response(\"ERR DW3000_TIMEOUT\");\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"DW3000 TIMEOUT\");\n    }\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        send_response(\"ERR DW3000_INIT_FAILED\");\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED\");\n        // Don't hang - continue so UART commands still work\n    }\n    else\n    {\n        send_response(\"OK DW3000_READY\");\n    }\n\n    /* Enable LEDs */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure with default settings */\n    configure_uwb();\n\n    /* Send message that we reached main loop */\n    Sleep(100);\n    send_response(\"OK MAIN_LOOP\");\n    \n    /* Main loop - process UART commands */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        // Command processing happens in UART interrupt handler\n        Sleep(100);\n    }\n}\n\n#endif",

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": ".\\Src\\examples\\ex_21_orchestrator\\README.md",
        "range": {

        "contents": "# Orchestrator Example - Build and Flash Guide\n\n## Overview\n\nThis example provides two firmware variants:\n- **TX Variant (Node A)**: Transmits UWB packets periodically\n- **RX Variant (Node B)**: Receives UWB packets and collects statistics\n\nBoth variants communicate with the Orchestrator via RS-485 using UART.\n\n## Pin Configuration\n\n### UART Pins (RS-485 Communication)\n- **RX Pin**: GPIO 15 (UART_0_RX_PIN)\n- **TX Pin**: GPIO 19 (UART_0_TX_PIN)\n- **Baud Rate**: 115200\n\n**Note**: Pins 8 and 10 are used for:\n- **Pin 8**: DW3000_IRQ_Pin (interrupt pin for UWB chip)\n- **Pin 10**: DW3000_CS_Pin (SPI chip select for UWB chip)\n\nThe UART for RS-485 communication uses **pins 15 (RX) and 19 (TX)**, not pins 8 and 10.\n\n## Building and Flashing\n\n### Step 1: Build TX Variant (Node A)\n\n1. Edit &#96;Src/example_selection.h&#96;:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;c\n   // Comment out other examples:\n   //#define TEST_READING_DEV_ID\n   \n   // Uncomment TX variant:\n   #define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_TX\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n2. Edit &#96;Src/main.c&#96;:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;c\n   // Comment out other examples:\n   // extern int read_dev_id(void); read_dev_id();\n   \n   // Uncomment TX variant:\n   extern int orchestrator_tx(void); orchestrator_tx();\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n3. Build:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   make build\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n4. Flash to Node A board:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   make flash\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 2: Build RX Variant (Node B)\n\n1. Edit &#96;Src/example_selection.h&#96;:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;c\n   // Comment out TX variant:\n   //#define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_TX\n   \n   // Uncomment RX variant:\n   #define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_RX\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n2. Edit &#96;Src/main.c&#96;:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;c\n   // Comment out TX variant:\n   // extern int orchestrator_tx(void); orchestrator_tx();\n   \n   // Uncomment RX variant:\n   extern int orchestrator_rx(void); orchestrator_rx();\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n3. Build:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   make build\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n4. Flash to Node B board:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   make flash\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Important**: You need to build and flash **separately** for each board. The firmware is compiled with either TX or RX code, not both.\n\n## LED Behavior\n\nThe firmware uses &#96;dwt_setleds()&#96; which controls the **DW3000 UWB chip's internal LEDs**, not the board LEDs.\n\n- **On startup**: LEDs will blink once during initialization",

          },

          },
          {
            "text": "**Important**: You need to build and flash **separately** for each board. The firmware is compiled with either TX or RX code, not both.",
            "lineNumber": 86
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 87
          },
          {
            "text": "## LED Behavior",
            "lineNumber": 88
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 89
          },
          {
            "text": "The firmware uses &#96;dwt_setleds()&#96; which controls the **DW3000 UWB chip's internal LEDs**, not the board LEDs.",
            "lineNumber": 90
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 91
          },
          {
            "text": "- **On startup**: LEDs will blink once during initialization",
            "lineNumber": 92
          }
        ]

        "contents": "/**\n * Configure UWB radio\n */\nstatic void configure_uwb(void)\n{\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;dwt_config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED\");\n        return;\n    }\n\n    // Configure TX power (simplified - use default txconfig_options)\n    extern dwt_txconfig_t txconfig_options;\n    dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options);\n}\n\n/**\n * TX timer handler - called periodically to send packets\n */\nstatic void tx_timer_handler(void *p_context)\n{\n    if (g_test_running)\n    {\n        send_packet();\n    }\n}\n\n/**\n * Send a test packet\n */\nstatic void send_packet(void)\n{\n    uint32_t status_reg;\n\n    // Prepare packet\n    g_tx_packet.seq = g_seq_num++;\n    g_tx_packet.t_local = dwt_readsystimestamphi32();\n    \n    // Fill payload with pattern\n    for (int i = 0; i &lt; g_config.payload_len &amp;&amp; i &lt; sizeof(g_tx_packet.payload); i++)\n    {\n        g_tx_packet.payload[i] = 0xAA;\n    }\n\n    // Copy to TX buffer\n    // Calculate frame length: header (seq + t_local) + actual payload length\n    uint16_t frame_len = sizeof(uint32_t) + sizeof(uint32_t) + g_config.payload_len + FCS_LEN;\n    uint16_t data_len = sizeof(uint32_t) + sizeof(uint32_t) + g_config.payload_len;\n    memcpy(g_tx_buffer, &amp;g_tx_packet, data_len);\n\n    // Write TX data\n    dwt_writetxdata(data_len, g_tx_buffer, 0);\n    dwt_writetxfctrl(frame_len, 0, 0);\n\n    // Start transmission\n    dwt_starttx(DWT_START_TX_IMMEDIATE);\n\n    // Wait for TX complete\n    waitforsysstatus(&amp;status_reg, NULL, DWT_INT_TXFRS_BIT_MASK, 0);\n\n    if (status_reg &amp; DWT_INT_TXFRS_BIT_MASK)\n    {\n        dwt_writesysstatuslo(DWT_INT_TXFRS_BIT_MASK);\n        g_stats.total_sent++;\n        g_stats.last_error = 0;\n    }\n    else\n    {\n        g_stats.last_error = 1;\n    }\n}\n\n/**\n * Application entry point\n */\nint orchestrator_tx(void)\n{\n    uint32_t dev_id;\n    uint32_t err_code;\n\n    /* Display application name */",

Added diagnostics to verify UART RX. The firmware will:

1. Echo each received byte as `RX:<char>` — confirms UART RX is working
2. Send `OK CMD_RECEIVED` when a complete command is received — confirms command parsing
3. Blink LED when PNG command is processed — confirms command handling

## Changes Made

**Enhanced UART RX diagnostics:**
- Each received byte is echoed back as `RX:<char>` (e.g., `RX:P`, `RX:N`, `RX:G` for "PNG")
- `OK CMD_RECEIVED` is sent before parsing each command
- LED blinks when PNG command is processed

This helps determine:
- If UART RX receives data (you'll see `RX:` messages)
- If commands are parsed (you'll see `OK CMD_RECEIVED`)
- If PNG responses are sent (you'll see `OK` response)

<reproduction_steps>
1. Rebuild both firmware variants:
   ```powershell
   .\clean.ps1
   .\build-and-flash-rx.ps1
   # Wait for RX flash to complete, then:
   .\build-and-flash-tx.ps1
   ```

2. Wait 3-5 seconds after flashing for firmware to initialize

3. Test UART communication directly:
   ```powershell
   .\test-uart-direct.ps1
   ```
   Look for:
   - Startup messages: `ABCDEFGHIJ` pattern, `OK STARTUP`, `OK FIRMWARE_RUNNING`
   - When you send PNG: `RX:P`, `RX:N`, `RX:G` (echo of received bytes)
   - `OK CMD_RECEIVED` (command received confirmation)
   - `OK` (PNG response)

4. Run the Orchestrator test:
   ```powershell
   cd Orchestrator
   npm run test
   ```

5. Check LED behavior:
   - Double blink when firmware starts
   - Single blink after UART init
   - Brief blink when PNG command is processed

6. Share the output from both `test-uart-direct.ps1` and the Orchestrator test
</reproduction_steps>

The diagnostics will show where communication is failing. If you see `RX:` messages, UART RX is working. If you don't see any data, the firmware may not be running or UART TX may not be working.

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": ".\\Src\\examples\\ex_21_orchestrator\\README.md",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {
            "line": 86
          },
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 143
          }
        },
        "contents": "## LED Behavior\n\nThe firmware uses &#96;dwt_setleds()&#96; which controls the **DW3000 UWB chip's internal LEDs**, not the board LEDs.\n\n- **On startup**: LEDs will blink once during initialization\n- **During operation**: LEDs may flash during UWB activity (TX/RX events)\n- **Board LEDs**: The DWM3001CDK board LEDs (LED_1, LED_2, LED_3, LED_4) are not directly controlled by this firmware\n\n## RS-485 Connection\n\nConnect the RS-485 transceiver to:\n- **A+**: Connect to RS-485 A+ line\n- **B-**: Connect to RS-485 B- line  \n- **GND**: Connect to ground\n- **UART RX**: Connect to GPIO 15\n- **UART TX**: Connect to GPIO 19\n- **DE/RE**: Connect to control RS-485 direction (if needed)\n\nThe firmware communicates at **115200 baud** with the Orchestrator.\n\n## Testing\n\nAfter flashing:\n\n1. **Connect RS-485** from each board to the Orchestrator (RPi 5)\n2. **Power on** both boards\n3. **Run the Orchestrator**:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   cd Orchestrator\n   npm start\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe Orchestrator will:\n- Send &#96;PNG&#96; (PING) commands to verify connectivity\n- Configure both nodes with &#96;CFG&#96; commands\n- Start tests with &#96;STRT&#96; commands\n- Collect statistics with &#96;STAT&#96; commands\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n### UART Not Working\n- Verify pins 15 (RX) and 19 (TX) are connected correctly\n- Check RS-485 transceiver wiring (A+, B-, GND)\n- Verify baud rate is 115200\n- Check that RS-485 termination resistors are present (120Ω at each end)\n\n### Wrong Variant Flashed\n- Make sure you build and flash separately for each board\n- Check &#96;example_selection.h&#96; has the correct &#96;#define&#96; uncommented\n- Check &#96;main.c&#96; has the correct function call uncommented\n\n### LEDs Not Flashing\n- The firmware controls DW3000 internal LEDs, not board LEDs\n- Board LEDs may not flash unless you add code to control them\n- Check UWB activity with the Orchestrator's statistics",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [

        "contents": "    /*! ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n     * @brief This is used to program 32-bit value into the DW3700 OTP memory, it will not validate the word was written correctly\n     *\n     * input parameters\n     * @param value - this is the 32-bit value to be programmed into OTP\n     * @param address - this is the 16-bit OTP address into which the 32-bit value is programmed\n     *\n     * output parameters\n     *\n     * returns DWT_SUCCESS\n     */\n    int dwt_otpwrite(uint32_t value, uint16_t address);\n\n    /*! ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n     * @brief This is used to set up Tx/Rx GPIOs which could be used to control LEDs\n     * Note: not completely IC dependent, also needs board with LEDS fitted on right I/O lines\n     *       this function enables GPIOs 2 and 3 which are connected to LED3 and LED4 on EVB1000\n     *\n     * input parameters\n     * @param mode - this is a bit field interpreted as follows:\n     *          - bit 0: 1 to enable LEDs, 0 to disable them\n     *          - bit 1: 1 to make LEDs blink once on init. Only valid if bit 0 is set (enable LEDs)\n     *          - bit 2 to 7: reserved\n     *\n     * output parameters none\n     *\n     * no return value\n     */\n    void dwt_setleds(uint8_t mode);\n\n    /*! ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n     * @brief This is used to adjust the crystal frequency\n     *\n     * input parameters:\n     * @param   value - crystal trim value (in range 0x0 to 0x3F) 64 steps (~1.65ppm per step)\n     *\n     * output parameters\n     *\n     * no return value\n     */\n    void dwt_setxtaltrim(uint8_t value);\n\n    /*! ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\n     * @brief This function returns the value of XTAL trim that has been applied during initialisation (dwt_init). This can\n     *        be either the value read in OTP memory or a default value.\n     *\n     * NOTE: The value returned by this function is the initial value only! It is not updated on dwt_setxtaltrim calls.\n     *\n     * input parameters\n     *\n     * output parameters\n     *\n     * returns the XTAL trim value set upon initialisation\n     */",

        "contents": "    while (1)\n    {\n        read_ios_val = dwt_readgpiovalue();\n        /* Checks if GPIO0 input is high */\n        if (read_ios_val &amp; GPIO0_BIT_MASK)\n        {\n            blink_delay = FAST_BLINK;\n        }\n        else\n        {\n            blink_delay = SLOW_BLINK;\n        }\n\n        /* Set GPIO2 and GPIO3 high */\n        /* This will turn D1 (Green LED) and D2 (Red LED) on */\n        dwt_setgpiovalue(GPIO3_BIT_MASK | GPIO2_BIT_MASK, 1);\n        Sleep(blink_delay);\n        /* set GPIO2 &amp; GPIO3 low (LEDs will be turned off) */\n        /* Clear bits 2,3 */\n        dwt_setgpiovalue(GPIO3_BIT_MASK | GPIO2_BIT_MASK, 0);\n        Sleep(blink_delay);\n    }\n}\n\n#endif\n/*****************************************************************************************************************************************************\n * NOTES:\n *\n * 1. When enabling the GPIO mode/value, the GPIO clock needs to be enabled.\n *\n * 2. By default, all the available GPIO pins on the DW3000 B0 red evaluation boards (GPIO0, GPIO1, GPIO2, GPIO3 &amp; GPIO4) are set to work as GPIO.\n *    Other modes available are LED, AOA_SW, DBG_MUX, etc. Please see MFIO_MODE register details in datasheet for more information on this. You can\n *    see examples of how to set this register in functions like dwt_setleds().\n *\n * 3. The code above focuses mostly on how to test the GPIO outputs of the DW3000 chip. However, there is some code commented out that illustrates\n *    how to also test the input functionality of the GPIOs. On the DW3000 HW (Decawave shield / red board), there are a number of test points\n *    that are linked to the GPIO pins. In total, there are 9 GPIO pins available on the DW3000. However, only 5 of them are wired to test points on\n *    the Decawave shield / red board. The details of these GPIO pins are as follows:\n *    - GPIO0 - Test Point 3 (TP3)\n *    - GPIO1 - Test Point 4 (TP4)\n *    - GPIO2 - Test Point 6 (TP6) - Also controls RX LED (Green)\n *    - GPIO3 - Test Point 7 (TP7) - Also controls TX LED (Red)\n *    - GPIO4 - Test Point 8 (TP8)\n *    To use these GPIO pins, you can solder connections to your circuit to the test points on the Decawave Shield / red board. The simple GPIO input\n *    code example that is commented out above can be used if there are wires soldered to TP3 and TP4. These wires can be used as 'switches' to pull\n *    them high and act as an input on those GPIO input pins. This then controls the flashing frequency of the LEDs.\n *\n ****************************************************************************************************************************************************/",

        "contents": "# Orchestrator Example - Build and Flash Guide\n\n## Overview\n\nThis example provides two firmware variants:\n- **TX Variant (Node A)**: Transmits UWB packets periodically\n- **RX Variant (Node B)**: Receives UWB packets and collects statistics\n\nBoth variants communicate with the Orchestrator via RS-485 using UART.\n\n## Pin Configuration\n\n### UART Pins (RS-485 Communication)\n- **RX Pin**: GPIO 15 (UART_0_RX_PIN)\n- **TX Pin**: GPIO 19 (UART_0_TX_PIN)\n- **Baud Rate**: 115200\n\n**Note**: Pins 8 and 10 are used for:\n- **Pin 8**: DW3000_IRQ_Pin (interrupt pin for UWB chip)\n- **Pin 10**: DW3000_CS_Pin (SPI chip select for UWB chip)\n\nThe UART for RS-485 communication uses **pins 15 (RX) and 19 (TX)**, not pins 8 and 10.\n\n## Building and Flashing\n\n### Step 1: Build TX Variant (Node A)\n\n1. Edit &#96;Src/example_selection.h&#96;:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;c\n   // Comment out other examples:\n   //#define TEST_READING_DEV_ID\n   \n   // Uncomment TX variant:\n   #define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_TX\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n2. Edit &#96;Src/main.c&#96;:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;c\n   // Comment out other examples:\n   // extern int read_dev_id(void); read_dev_id();\n   \n   // Uncomment TX variant:\n   extern int orchestrator_tx(void); orchestrator_tx();\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n3. Build:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   make build\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n4. Flash to Node A board:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   make flash\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 2: Build RX Variant (Node B)\n\n1. Edit &#96;Src/example_selection.h&#96;:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;c\n   // Comment out TX variant:\n   //#define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_TX\n   \n   // Uncomment RX variant:\n   #define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_RX\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n2. Edit &#96;Src/main.c&#96;:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;c\n   // Comment out TX variant:\n   // extern int orchestrator_tx(void); orchestrator_tx();\n   \n   // Uncomment RX variant:\n   extern int orchestrator_rx(void); orchestrator_rx();\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n3. Build:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   make build\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n4. Flash to Node B board:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   make flash\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Important**: You need to build and flash **separately** for each board. The firmware is compiled with either TX or RX code, not both.\n\n## LED Behavior\n\nThe firmware uses &#96;dwt_setleds()&#96; which controls the **DW3000 UWB chip's internal LEDs**, not the board LEDs.\n\n- **On startup**: LEDs will blink once during initialization",
        "signatures": {},

          {

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 45
          },
          {
            "text": "3. Build:",

          },

          },

          },

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 50
          },
          {
            "text": "4. Flash to Node A board:",

          },
          {

          },
          {

          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 54
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 55
          },
          {
            "text": "### Step 2: Build RX Variant (Node B)",
            "lineNumber": 56
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 57
          },
          {
            "text": "1. Edit &#96;Src/example_selection.h&#96;:",
            "lineNumber": 58
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;c",
            "lineNumber": 59
          },
          {

            "text": "   ",
            "lineNumber": 62
          },
          {
            "text": "   // Uncomment RX variant:",
            "lineNumber": 63
          },
          {
            "text": "   #define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_RX",
            "lineNumber": 64
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 65
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 66
          },
          {
            "text": "2. Edit &#96;Src/main.c&#96;:",
            "lineNumber": 67
          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;c",
            "lineNumber": 68
          },
          {
            "text": "   // Comment out TX variant:",

          },

          },

            "lineNumber": 75
          },
          {
            "text": "3. Build:",

          },
          {
            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 79
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 80
          },
          {
            "text": "4. Flash to Node B board:",

          },
          {

          },
          {

          },

            "text": "   &#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 84
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 85
          },
          {
            "text": "**Important**: You need to build and flash **separately** for each board. The firmware is compiled with either TX or RX code, not both.",
            "lineNumber": 86
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 87
          },
          {
            "text": "## LED Behavior",
            "lineNumber": 88
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 89
          },
          {
            "text": "The firmware uses &#96;dwt_setleds()&#96; which controls the **DW3000 UWB chip's internal LEDs**, not the board LEDs.",
            "lineNumber": 90
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 91
          },
          {
            "text": "- **On startup**: LEDs will blink once during initialization",
            "lineNumber": 92
          }
        ]

        "contents": "int gpio_example(void)\n{\n    uint16_t blink_delay, read_ios_val;\n    int32_t dev_id;\n\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n    reset_DWIC();\n\n    /* Time needed for DW3000 to start up\n     * (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC) */\n    Sleep(2);\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_IDLE) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* See NOTE 1. */\n    /* 1st enable GPIO clocks */\n    dwt_enablegpioclocks();\n\n    dev_id = dwt_readdevid();\n\n    /* See NOTE 2.\n     * At this point we need to adjust the MFIO_MODE register to change the\n     * mode of the GPIO pins (GPIO, LED, etc.). Note that GPIO_4, GPIO_5, and\n     * GPIO_6 are already set to GPIO by default. */\n    /*Set mode to GPIOs */\n    if ((dev_id == DWT_DW3000_DEV_ID) || (dev_id == DWT_DW3000_PDOA_DEV_ID))\n    {\n        dwt_setgpiomode(GPIO_ALL, ENABLE_ALL_GPIOS_MASK_C0);\n    }\n    else\n    {\n        dwt_setgpiomode(GPIO_ALL, ENABLE_ALL_GPIOS_MASK_D0_E0);\n    }\n    /* Set output level for output pin to low. */\n    dwt_setgpiovalue(GPIO_ALL, 0x0);\n\n    /* Set GPIOs 2 &amp; 3 as outputs and all other GPIOs as input */\n    dwt_setgpiodir(SET_OUTPUT_GPIO2_GPIO3);\n\n    /* This function will loop around forever turning the GPIOs controlling\n     * the LEDs on and off */\n    /* The blink rate will be set according to the GPIO0 read level */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        read_ios_val = dwt_readgpiovalue();",

        "contents": "/*! ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n *  @file    gpio_example.c\n *  @brief   This example demonstrates how to enable DW IC GPIOs as inputs and\n *           outputs. It also demonstrates how to drive the output to turn\n *           on/off LEDs on DW3000 HW.\n *\n * @attention\n *\n * Copyright 2017 - 2021 (c) Decawave Ltd, Dublin, Ireland.\n *\n * All rights reserved.\n *\n * @author Decawave\n */\n#include \"deca_probe_interface.h\"\n#include &lt;deca_device_api.h&gt;\n#include &lt;deca_spi.h&gt;\n#include &lt;example_selection.h&gt;\n#include &lt;port.h&gt;\n\n#if defined(TEST_GPIO)\n\nextern void test_run_info(unsigned char *data);\n\n/* Example application name and version to display on LCD screen. */\n#define APP_NAME   \"GPIO        v1.0\"\n#define SLOW_BLINK 500 // 500ms between blinks.         "contents": "Write-Host \"\"\nWrite-Host \"1. Verify boards are POWERED ON:\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\nWrite-Host \"   - Check power LED on boards\" -ForegroundColor White\nWrite-Host \"   - LEDs should blink once on startup\" -ForegroundColor White\nWrite-Host \"\"\nWrite-Host \"2. Rebuild firmware with fixes:\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\nWrite-Host \"   .\\build-and-flash-tx.ps1\" -ForegroundColor White\nWrite-Host \"   .\\build-and-flash-rx.ps1\" -ForegroundColor White\nWrite-Host \"\"\nWrite-Host \"3. After flashing, wait 5 seconds for initialization\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\nWrite-Host \"\"\nWrite-Host \"4. Test again:\" -ForegroundColor Yellow\nWrite-Host \"   .\\test-uart-direct.ps1\" -ForegroundColor White\nWrite-Host \"\"\nWrite-Host \"5.         "contents": "/* Values for the PG_DELAY and TX_POWER registers reflect the bandwidth and power of the spectrum at the current\n * temperature. These values can be calibrated prior to taking reference measurements. See NOTE 2 below. */\nextern dwt_txconfig_t txconfig_options;\n\n/**\n * Application entry point.\n */\nint simple_tx_sts_sdc(void)\n{\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enabling LEDs here for debug so that for each TX the D1 LED will flash on DW3000 red eval-shield boards. */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. See NOTE 9 below. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure the TX spectrum parameters (power, PG delay and PG count) */\n    dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options);\n\n    /* can enable TX/RX states output on GPIOs 5 and 6 to help debug */\n    dwt_setlnapamode(DWT_LNA_ENABLE | DWT_PA_ENABLE);\n\n    /* Loop forever sending frames periodically. */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        /* Write frame data to DW IC and prepare transmission. See NOTE 3 below.*/",

        "contents": "/* Index to access to sequence number of the blink frame in the tx_msg array. */\n#define BLINK_FRAME_SN_IDX 1\n\n#define FRAME_LENGTH (sizeof(tx_msg) + FCS_LEN) // The real length that is going to be transmitted\n\n/* Inter-frame delay period, in milliseconds. */\n#define TX_DELAY_MS 500\n\n/* Values for the PG_DELAY and TX_POWER registers reflect the bandwidth and power of the spectrum at the current\n * temperature. These values can be calibrated prior to taking reference measurements. See NOTE 2 below. */\nextern dwt_txconfig_t txconfig_options;\n\n/**\n * Application entry point.\n */\nint simple_tx(void)\n{\n    uint32_t dev_id;\n\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC, or could wait for SPIRDY event)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    dev_id = dwt_readdevid();\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enabling LEDs here for debug so that for each TX the D1 LED will flash on DW3000 red eval-shield boards. */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. See NOTE 5 below. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure the TX spectrum parameters (power PG delay and PG Count) */\n    dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options);\n\n    /* Loop forever sending frames periodically. */",

        "contents": "int orchestrator_rx(void)\n{\n    uint32_t dev_id;\n    uint32_t err_code;\n\n    /* Display application name */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n    \n    /* LED diagnostic: Blink LED to show we reached this function */\n    nrf_gpio_cfg_output(BSP_LED_0);\n    nrf_gpio_pin_set(BSP_LED_0);\n    nrf_delay_ms(100);\n    nrf_gpio_pin_clear(BSP_LED_0);\n    nrf_delay_ms(100);\n    nrf_gpio_pin_set(BSP_LED_0);\n    nrf_delay_ms(100);\n    nrf_gpio_pin_clear(BSP_LED_0);\n    \n    /* CRITICAL: Initialize UART FIRST, before anything else */\n    /* This ensures UART works even if other init fails */\n    uart_init();\n    \n    /* LED diagnostic: Blink LED after UART init */\n    nrf_gpio_pin_set(BSP_LED_0);\n    nrf_delay_ms(50);\n    nrf_gpio_pin_clear(BSP_LED_0);\n    \n    /* Wait for UART to be ready */\n    Sleep(300);\n    \n    /* Send immediate test pattern - simple characters */\n    /* This verifies UART TX works before any other code */\n    for (int i = 0; i &lt; 10; i++) {\n        send_test_char('A' + (i % 26));  // Send A-Z pattern\n        Sleep(20);\n    }\n    send_test_char('\\r');\n    send_test_char('\\n');\n    Sleep(50);\n    \n    /* Send startup message */\n    send_response(\"OK STARTUP\");\n    Sleep(100);\n    \n    /* Send additional diagnostic info */\n    send_response(\"OK FIRMWARE_RUNNING\");\n    Sleep(100);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC();\n    Sleep(2);\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n    dev_id = dwt_readdevid();\n\n    /* Wait for DW3000 to be ready with timeout */\n    uint32_t timeout_count = 0;\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc() &amp;&amp; timeout_count &lt; 1000)\n    {\n        timeout_count++;\n        Sleep(1);\n    }\n    \n    if (timeout_count &gt;= 1000)\n    {\n        send_response(\"ERR DW3000_TIMEOUT\");\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"DW3000 TIMEOUT\");\n    }\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)",

        "contents": "int bw_cal(void)\n{\n    /* Variable to store raw temp value */\n    uint8_t raw_temp = 0;\n    /* Variable to store real temp value */\n    float real_temp = 0;\n    /* String to contain temp value for debug purposes */\n    char str_temp[32] = { 0 };\n\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC, or could wait for SPIRDY event)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enabling LEDs here for debug so that for each TX the D1 LED will flash on DW3000 red eval-shield boards. */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. See NOTE 3 below. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* At this point, we are emulating a process that needs to occur at room temperature when devices are being configured in factory. */\n    /* See NOTE 3 for more information */\n    txconfig_options.PGcount = dwt_calcpgcount(txconfig_options.PGdly);\n\n    /* Write the TX message into the TX buffer */\n    /* This only needs to be done once if we are sending the same frame over and over again */\n    dwt_writetxdata(sizeof(tx_msg), tx_msg, 0); /* Zero offset in TX buffer. */\n    dwt_writetxfctrl(sizeof(tx_msg), 0, 0);     /* Zero offset in TX buffer, no ranging. */\n\n    /* Loop forever, adjusting bandwidth periodically. */",

        "contents": "* **Node A** – TX initiator (main packet source).  \n* **Node B** – RX logger (collects RF metrics &amp; PER).\n\n### **4.1 Common configuration structure**\n\n&#96;typedef struct {&#96;  \n    &#96;uint8_t  channel;        // UWB channel: 5 or 9&#96;  \n    &#96;uint8_t  data_rate;      // 0 = 850kbps, 1 = 6.8Mbps&#96;  \n    &#96;uint8_t  prf;            // 16/64 MHz if applicable&#96;  \n    &#96;uint16_t preamble_len;   // e.g. 64 / 128 / 256&#96;  \n    &#96;uint8_t  preamble_code;&#96;  \n    &#96;uint8_t  sts_mode;       // 0 = off, &gt;0 for 802.15.4z profiles&#96;  \n    &#96;uint8_t  tx_power_idx;   // DW3000 TX power index&#96;  \n    &#96;uint32_t pkt_rate_hz;    // TX packets/s (Node A)&#96;  \n    &#96;uint16_t payload_len;    // payload size in bytes&#96;  \n&#96;} uwb_link_config_t;&#96;\n\n### **4.2 Test packet format**\n\n&#96;typedef struct {&#96;  \n    &#96;uint32_t seq;            // sequence number&#96;  \n    &#96;uint32_t t_local;        // local timestamp (ticks/UWB)&#96;  \n    &#96;uint8_t  payload[PAYLOAD_LEN];   // fixed pattern (e.g., 0xAA/0x55)&#96;  \n&#96;} __attribute__((packed)) uwb_test_packet_t;&#96;\n\n* &#96;seq&#96; increments by 1 for each TX packet.\n\n* &#96;payload&#96; constant pattern for debugging (not critical for Stage 1 logic).\n\n### **4.3 ASCII command protocol (RPi → nodes)**\n\nCommands (same for Node A &amp; B):\n\n* &#96;PING&#96;  \n* &#96;SET_CONFIG ch=5 rate=6m8 pl=128 len=64 pwr=5 rate_hz=100&#96;  \n* &#96;START_TEST&#96;  \n* &#96;STOP_TEST&#96;  \n* &#96;GET_STATS&#96;  \n* &#96;RESET_STATS&#96;  \n* &#96;SET_LOG_MODE level=0|1|2&#96; (optional; level 2 for per-packet logs)\n\nResponses:\n\n* Always start with &#96;OK&#96; or &#96;ERR&#96;.\n\n### **4.4 Node A – TX Initiator Logic**\n\n**Responsibilities:**\n\n* Apply UWB configuration on &#96;SET_CONFIG&#96;.\n\n* On &#96;START_TEST&#96;:  \n  * Start periodic TX at &#96;pkt_rate_hz&#96;.\n\n* On &#96;STOP_TEST&#96;:  \n  * Stop TX.\n\n* Keep TX stats:  \n  * &#96;total_sent&#96;, &#96;last_error&#96;.\n\nImplementation details:\n\n* Use a hardware timer / RTOS task to achieve &#96;pkt_rate_hz&#96;.  \n* Build &#96;uwb_test_packet_t&#96; for each TX, increment &#96;seq&#96;, update &#96;total_sent&#96;.  \n* Optionally expose &#96;GET_STATS&#96; to report &#96;total_sent&#96; and &#96;last_error&#96; (for debug).\n\n### **4.5 Node B – RX Logger Logic**\n\n**Responsibilities:**",

Added LED diagnostics. Summary:

## LED diagnostics added

**LED assignments:**
- **LED_1 (BSP_LED_0)**: Startup diagnostics (double blink on entry, single blink after UART init)
- **LED_2 (BSP_LED_1)**: Orange — blinks when a command is received (UART RX)
- **LED_3 (BSP_LED_2)**: Green — turns on while sending a response, then turns off (UART TX)

**Behavior:**
1. On startup: LED_1 double blink → UART init → LED_1 single blink
2. When command received: LED_2 (orange) blinks for 50ms
3. When response sent: LED_3 (green) turns on during transmission, then turns off

This helps verify:
- Firmware is running (startup blinks)
- Commands are received (orange LED blinks)
- Responses are sent (green LED turns on)

<reproduction_steps>
1. Rebuild both firmware variants:
   ```powershell
   .\clean.ps1
   .\build-and-flash-rx.ps1
   # Wait for RX flash to complete, then:
   .\build-and-flash-tx.ps1
   ```

2. After flashing, watch the LEDs:
   - LED_1 should double blink (firmware started)
   - LED_1 should single blink (UART initialized)
   - If no blinks, firmware may not be running

3. Test UART communication:
   ```powershell
   .\test-uart-direct.ps1
   ```
   Watch for:
   - Orange LED (LED_2) blinks when PNG command is received
   - Green LED (LED_3) turns on when response is sent

4. Run the Orchestrator test:
   ```powershell
   cd Orchestrator
   node src/orchestrator/main.js
   ```
   Watch LEDs during PING:
   - Orange LED should blink (command received)
   - Green LED should turn on (response sent)

5. Share observations:
   - Which LEDs blink/turn on?
   - Do you see any UART data in test-uart-direct.ps1?
   - Do orange/green LEDs activate when sending PNG?
</reproduction_steps>

The LED diagnostics will show:
- If firmware is running (startup blinks)
- If commands reach the board (orange LED)
- If responses are sent (green LED)

If the orange LED blinks but no UART data is received, it's likely a UART TX or RS-485 wiring issue. If the orange LED doesn't blink, commands aren't reaching the board.

---

_**User**_

Blue LED = UART works
Orange = RX
Green = TX
any left LED = Stand By state
Red = Default 

---

_**Agent (model composer-1, mode Custom)**_


Updating LED mapping: Blue = UART works, Orange = RX, Green = TX, remaining LED = Stand By, Red = Default/Error.

Updated LED mapping per your requirements:

## Updated LED mapping

**LED assignments:**
- **Red LED (BSP_LED_0)**: Default/Error states
  - Double blink on firmware startup
  - Stays on if UART init fails
  - Stays on if DW3000 init fails

- **Orange LED (BSP_LED_1)**: RX — Command received
  - Blinks for 50ms when a UART command is received

- **Green LED (BSP_LED_2)**: TX — Response sent
  - Turns on while sending a response, then turns off

- **Blue LED (BSP_LED_3)**: UART works + Stand By state
  - Turns on after successful UART initialization
  - Stays on continuously to indicate Stand By (firmware running, ready for commands)

**LED behavior flow:**
1. Startup: Red LED double blink → UART init → Blue LED turns on (UART works)
2. Stand By: Blue LED stays on (ready for commands)
3. Command received: Orange LED blinks
4. Response sent: Green LED turns on briefly
5. Errors: Red LED turns on and stays on

This helps verify:
- Firmware is running (red startup blink)
- UART is working (blue LED on)
- Commands are received (orange blink)
- Responses are sent (green LED)
- Stand By state (blue LED on continuously)

<reproduction_steps>
1. Rebuild both firmware variants:
   ```powershell
   .\clean.ps1
   .\build-and-flash-rx.ps1
   # Wait for RX flash to complete, then:
   .\build-and-flash-tx.ps1
   ```

2. After flashing, watch the LEDs:
   - Red LED should double blink (firmware started)
   - Blue LED should turn on and stay on (UART works, Stand By state)
   - If red LED stays on, there's an error
   - If blue LED doesn't turn on, UART init failed

3. Test UART communication:
   ```powershell
   .\test-uart-direct.ps1
   ```
   Watch for:
   - Blue LED should be on (Stand By state)
   - Orange LED should blink when PNG command is received
   - Green LED should turn on when response is sent

4. Run the Orchestrator test:
   ```powershell
   cd Orchestrator
   node src/orchestrator/main.js
   ```
   Watch LEDs during PING:
   - Blue LED should be on (Stand By)
   - Orange LED should blink (command received)
   - Green LED should turn on (response sent)

5. Share observations:
   - Is blue LED on? (UART works, Stand By)
   - Does orange LED blink when sending PNG? (RX working)
   - Does green LED turn on? (TX working)
   - Any red LED errors?
</reproduction_steps>

The blue LED staying on confirms UART is working and the firmware is in Stand By. If it doesn't turn on, UART initialization failed.

        "contents": "int orchestrator_rx(void)\n{\n    uint32_t dev_id;\n    uint32_t err_code;\n\n    /* Display application name */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n    \n    /* Configure all LED pins for diagnostics */\n    nrf_gpio_cfg_output(BSP_LED_0);  // Red LED - Default/Error states\n    nrf_gpio_cfg_output(BSP_LED_1);  // Orange LED - RX (command received)\n    nrf_gpio_cfg_output(BSP_LED_2);  // Green LED - TX (response sent)\n    nrf_gpio_cfg_output(BSP_LED_3);  // Blue LED - UART works + Stand By state\n    \n    /* Initialize all LEDs to off */\n    nrf_gpio_pin_clear(BSP_LED_0);\n    nrf_gpio_pin_clear(BSP_LED_1);\n    nrf_gpio_pin_clear(BSP_LED_2);\n    nrf_gpio_pin_clear(BSP_LED_3);\n    \n    /* Red LED: Default state - blink to show firmware started */\n    nrf_gpio_pin_set(BSP_LED_0);\n    nrf_delay_ms(100);\n    nrf_gpio_pin_clear(BSP_LED_0);\n    nrf_delay_ms(100);\n    nrf_gpio_pin_set(BSP_LED_0);\n    nrf_delay_ms(100);\n    nrf_gpio_pin_clear(BSP_LED_0);\n    \n    /* CRITICAL: Initialize UART FIRST, before anything else */\n    /* This ensures UART works even if other init fails */\n    uart_init();\n    \n    /* Blue LED: UART works - turn on to indicate UART initialized successfully */\n    nrf_gpio_pin_set(BSP_LED_3);\n    \n    /* Wait for UART to be ready */\n    Sleep(300);\n    \n    /* Send immediate test pattern - simple characters */\n    /* This verifies UART TX works before any other code */\n    for (int i = 0; i &lt; 10; i++) {\n        send_test_char('A' + (i % 26));  // Send A-Z pattern\n        Sleep(20);\n    }\n    send_test_char('\\r');\n    send_test_char('\\n');\n    Sleep(50);\n    \n    /* Send startup message */\n    send_response(\"OK STARTUP\");\n    Sleep(100);\n    \n    /* Send additional diagnostic info */\n    send_response(\"OK FIRMWARE_RUNNING\");\n    Sleep(100);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC();\n    Sleep(2);\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n    dev_id = dwt_readdevid();\n\n    /* Wait for DW3000 to be ready with timeout */",

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": ".\\Src\\examples\\ex_21_orchestrator\\README.md",
        "range": {

          },

          }
        },
        "contents": "## LED Behavior\n\nThe firmware uses &#96;dwt_setleds()&#96; which controls the **DW3000 UWB chip's internal LEDs**, not the board LEDs.\n\n- **On startup**: LEDs will blink once during initialization\n- **During operation**: LEDs may flash during UWB activity (TX/RX events)\n- **Board LEDs**: The DWM3001CDK board LEDs (LED_1, LED_2, LED_3, LED_4) are not directly controlled by this firmware\n\n## RS-485 Connection\n\nConnect the RS-485 transceiver to:\n- **A+**: Connect to RS-485 A+ line\n- **B-**: Connect to RS-485 B- line  \n- **GND**: Connect to ground\n- **UART RX**: Connect to GPIO 15\n- **UART TX**: Connect to GPIO 19\n- **DE/RE**: Connect to control RS-485 direction (if needed)\n\nThe firmware communicates at **115200 baud** with the Orchestrator.\n\n## Testing\n\nAfter flashing:\n\n1. **Connect RS-485** from each board to the Orchestrator (RPi 5)\n2. **Power on** both boards\n3. **Run the Orchestrator**:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   cd Orchestrator\n   npm start\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe Orchestrator will:\n- Send &#96;PNG&#96; (PING) commands to verify connectivity\n- Configure both nodes with &#96;CFG&#96; commands\n- Start tests with &#96;STRT&#96; commands\n- Collect statistics with &#96;STAT&#96; commands\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n### UART Not Working\n- Verify pins 15 (RX) and 19 (TX) are connected correctly\n- Check RS-485 transceiver wiring (A+, B-, GND)\n- Verify baud rate is 115200\n- Check that RS-485 termination resistors are present (120Ω at each end)\n\n### Wrong Variant Flashed\n- Make sure you build and flash separately for each board\n- Check &#96;example_selection.h&#96; has the correct &#96;#define&#96; uncommented\n- Check &#96;main.c&#96; has the correct function call uncommented\n\n### LEDs Not Flashing\n- The firmware controls DW3000 internal LEDs, not board LEDs\n- Board LEDs may not flash unless you add code to control them\n- Check UWB activity with the Orchestrator's statistics",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [

        "contents": "int gpio_example(void)\n{\n    uint16_t blink_delay, read_ios_val;\n    int32_t dev_id;\n\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n    reset_DWIC();\n\n    /* Time needed for DW3000 to start up\n     * (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC) */\n    Sleep(2);\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_IDLE) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* See NOTE 1. */\n    /* 1st enable GPIO clocks */\n    dwt_enablegpioclocks();\n\n    dev_id = dwt_readdevid();\n\n    /* See NOTE 2.\n     * At this point we need to adjust the MFIO_MODE register to change the\n     * mode of the GPIO pins (GPIO, LED, etc.). Note that GPIO_4, GPIO_5, and\n     * GPIO_6 are already set to GPIO by default. */\n    /*Set mode to GPIOs */\n    if ((dev_id == DWT_DW3000_DEV_ID) || (dev_id == DWT_DW3000_PDOA_DEV_ID))\n    {\n        dwt_setgpiomode(GPIO_ALL, ENABLE_ALL_GPIOS_MASK_C0);\n    }\n    else\n    {\n        dwt_setgpiomode(GPIO_ALL, ENABLE_ALL_GPIOS_MASK_D0_E0);\n    }\n    /* Set output level for output pin to low. */\n    dwt_setgpiovalue(GPIO_ALL, 0x0);\n\n    /* Set GPIOs 2 &amp; 3 as outputs and all other GPIOs as input */\n    dwt_setgpiodir(SET_OUTPUT_GPIO2_GPIO3);\n\n    /* This function will loop around forever turning the GPIOs controlling\n     * the LEDs on and off */\n    /* The blink rate will be set according to the GPIO0 read level */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        read_ios_val = dwt_readgpiovalue();",

        "contents": "    while (1)\n    {\n        read_ios_val = dwt_readgpiovalue();\n        /* Checks if GPIO0 input is high */\n        if (read_ios_val &amp; GPIO0_BIT_MASK)\n        {\n            blink_delay = FAST_BLINK;\n        }\n        else\n        {\n            blink_delay = SLOW_BLINK;\n        }\n\n        /* Set GPIO2 and GPIO3 high */\n        /* This will turn D1 (Green LED) and D2 (Red LED) on */\n        dwt_setgpiovalue(GPIO3_BIT_MASK | GPIO2_BIT_MASK, 1);\n        Sleep(blink_delay);\n        /* set GPIO2 &amp; GPIO3 low (LEDs will be turned off) */\n        /* Clear bits 2,3 */\n        dwt_setgpiovalue(GPIO3_BIT_MASK | GPIO2_BIT_MASK, 0);\n        Sleep(blink_delay);\n    }\n}\n\n#endif\n/*****************************************************************************************************************************************************\n * NOTES:\n *\n * 1. When enabling the GPIO mode/value, the GPIO clock needs to be enabled.\n *\n * 2. By default, all the available GPIO pins on the DW3000 B0 red evaluation boards (GPIO0, GPIO1, GPIO2, GPIO3 &amp; GPIO4) are set to work as GPIO.\n *    Other modes available are LED, AOA_SW, DBG_MUX, etc. Please see MFIO_MODE register details in datasheet for more information on this. You can\n *    see examples of how to set this register in functions like dwt_setleds().\n *\n * 3. The code above focuses mostly on how to test the GPIO outputs of the DW3000 chip. However, there is some code commented out that illustrates\n *    how to also test the input functionality of the GPIOs. On the DW3000 HW (Decawave shield / red board), there are a number of test points\n *    that are linked to the GPIO pins. In total, there are 9 GPIO pins available on the DW3000. However, only 5 of them are wired to test points on\n *    the Decawave shield / red board. The details of these GPIO pins are as follows:\n *    - GPIO0 - Test Point 3 (TP3)\n *    - GPIO1 - Test Point 4 (TP4)\n *    - GPIO2 - Test Point 6 (TP6) - Also controls RX LED (Green)\n *    - GPIO3 - Test Point 7 (TP7) - Also controls TX LED (Red)\n *    - GPIO4 - Test Point 8 (TP8)\n *    To use these GPIO pins, you can solder connections to your circuit to the test points on the Decawave Shield / red board. The simple GPIO input\n *    code example that is commented out above can be used if there are wires soldered to TP3 and TP4. These wires can be used as 'switches' to pull\n *    them high and act as an input on those GPIO input pins. This then controls the flashing frequency of the LEDs.\n *\n ****************************************************************************************************************************************************/",

        "contents": "int simple_rx(void)\n{\n    /* Hold copy of status register state here for reference so that it can be examined at a debug breakpoint. */\n    uint32_t status_reg;\n    /* Hold copy of frame length of frame received (if good) so that it can be examined at a debug breakpoint. */\n    uint16_t frame_len;\n\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW IC supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC, or could wait for SPIRDY event)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED\");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enabling LEDs here for debug so that for each RX-enable the D2 LED will flash on DW3000 red eval-shield boards. */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Loop forever receiving frames. */\n    while (TRUE)\n    {\n        /* TESTING BREAKPOINT LOCATION #1 */",

        },
        "contents": "/* Index to access to sequence number of the blink frame in the tx_msg array. */\n#define BLINK_FRAME_SN_IDX 1\n\n#define FRAME_LENGTH (sizeof(tx_msg) + FCS_LEN) // The real length that is going to be transmitted\n\n/* Inter-frame delay period, in milliseconds. */\n#define TX_DELAY_MS 500\n\n/* Values for the PG_DELAY and TX_POWER registers reflect the bandwidth and power of the spectrum at the current\n * temperature. These values can be calibrated prior to taking reference measurements. See NOTE 2 below. */\nextern dwt_txconfig_t txconfig_options;\n\n/**\n * Application entry point.\n */\nint simple_tx(void)\n{\n    uint32_t dev_id;\n\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC, or could wait for SPIRDY event)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    dev_id = dwt_readdevid();\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enabling LEDs here for debug so that for each TX the D1 LED will flash on DW3000 red eval-shield boards. */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. See NOTE 5 below. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure the TX spectrum parameters (power PG delay and PG Count) */\n    dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options);\n\n    /* Loop forever sending frames periodically. */",

        "contents": "int rx_send_resp(void)\n{\n    /* Hold copy of status register state here for reference so that it can be examined at a debug breakpoint. */\n    uint32_t status_reg = 0;\n    /* Hold copy of frame length of frame received (if good) so that it can be examined at a debug breakpoint. */\n    uint16_t frame_len = 0;\n\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC, or could wait for SPIRDY event)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enabling LEDs here for debug so that for each TX the D1 LED will flash on DW3000 red eval-shield boards. */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. See NOTE 8 below. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure the TX spectrum parameters (power, PG delay and PG count) */\n    dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options);\n\n    /* Loop forever sending and receiving frames periodically. */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        /* Activate reception immediately. See NOTE 4 below. */",

        "contents": "int bw_cal(void)\n{\n    /* Variable to store raw temp value */\n    uint8_t raw_temp = 0;\n    /* Variable to store real temp value */\n    float real_temp = 0;\n    /* String to contain temp value for debug purposes */\n    char str_temp[32] = { 0 };\n\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC, or could wait for SPIRDY event)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enabling LEDs here for debug so that for each TX the D1 LED will flash on DW3000 red eval-shield boards. */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. See NOTE 3 below. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* At this point, we are emulating a process that needs to occur at room temperature when devices are being configured in factory. */\n    /* See NOTE 3 for more information */\n    txconfig_options.PGcount = dwt_calcpgcount(txconfig_options.PGdly);\n\n    /* Write the TX message into the TX buffer */\n    /* This only needs to be done once if we are sending the same frame over and over again */\n    dwt_writetxdata(sizeof(tx_msg), tx_msg, 0); /* Zero offset in TX buffer. */\n    dwt_writetxfctrl(sizeof(tx_msg), 0, 0);     /* Zero offset in TX buffer, no ranging. */\n\n    /* Loop forever, adjusting bandwidth periodically. */",

        "contents": "/* Values for the PG_DELAY and TX_POWER registers reflect the bandwidth and power of the spectrum at the current\n * temperature. These values can be calibrated prior to taking reference measurements.         "contents": "    if (err_code != NRF_SUCCESS)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"TIMER INIT FAILED\");\n    }\n    else\n    {\n        /* Create timer instance */\n        err_code = app_timer_create(&amp;m_tx_timer_id, APP_TIMER_MODE_REPEATED, tx_timer_handler);\n        if (err_code == NRF_SUCCESS)\n        {\n            g_timer_initialized = 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC();\n    Sleep(2);\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n    dev_id = dwt_readdevid();\n\n    /* Wait for DW3000 to be ready with timeout */\n    uint32_t timeout_count = 0;\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc() &amp;&amp; timeout_count &lt; 1000)\n    {\n        timeout_count++;\n        Sleep(1);\n    }\n    \n    if (timeout_count &gt;= 1000)\n    {\n        send_response(\"ERR DW3000_TIMEOUT\");\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"DW3000 TIMEOUT\");\n    }\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        send_response(\"ERR DW3000_INIT_FAILED\");\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED\");\n        // RED LED: Error state - turn on red LED to indicate error\n        nrf_gpio_pin_set(BSP_LED_0);\n        // Don't hang - continue so UART commands still work\n    }\n    else\n    {\n        send_response(\"OK DW3000_READY\");\n    }\n\n    /* Enable LEDs */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure with default settings */\n    configure_uwb();\n\n    /* Send message that we reached main loop */\n    Sleep(100);\n    send_response(\"OK MAIN_LOOP\");\n    \n    /* Blue LED: Stand By state - firmware running, ready for commands */\n    /* Blue LED stays on (already on from UART init) to indicate stand by */\n    \n    /* Main loop - process UART commands */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        // Command processing happens in UART interrupt handler\n        Sleep(100);\n    }\n}\n\n#endif",

        "contents": "int ds_twr_initiator_sts(void)\n{\n    int goodSts = 0;           /* Used for checking STS quality in received signal */\n    int16_t stsQual;           /* This will contain STS quality index */\n    uint16_t stsStatus;        /* Used to check for good STS status (no errors). */\n    uint8_t firstLoopFlag = 0; /* Used for checking if the program has gone through the main loop for the first time */\n\n    /* Display application name on UART. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n#ifdef CONFIG_SPI_FAST_RATE\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n#endif /* CONFIG_SPI_FAST_RATE */\n#ifdef CONFIG_SPI_SLOW_RATE\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_slowrate();\n#endif /* CONFIG_SPI_SLOW_RATE */\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_IDLE) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enabling LEDs here for debug so that for each TX the D1 LED will flash on DW3000 red eval-shield boards.\n     * Note, in real low power applications the LEDs should not be used. */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. See NOTE 15 below. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config_options))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure the TX spectrum parameters (power, PG delay and PG count) */\n    if (config_options.chan == 5)\n    {\n        dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options);",

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": ".\\Src\\examples\\ex_21_orchestrator\\README.md",
        "range": {

        "contents": "# Orchestrator Example - Build and Flash Guide\n\n## Overview\n\nThis example provides two firmware variants:\n- **TX Variant (Node A)**: Transmits UWB packets periodically\n- **RX Variant (Node B)**: Receives UWB packets and collects statistics\n\nBoth variants communicate with the Orchestrator via RS-485 using UART.\n\n## Pin Configuration\n\n### UART Pins (RS-485 Communication)\n- **RX Pin**: GPIO 15 (UART_0_RX_PIN)\n- **TX Pin**: GPIO 19 (UART_0_TX_PIN)\n- **Baud Rate**: 115200\n\n**Note**: Pins 8 and 10 are used for:\n- **Pin 8**: DW3000_IRQ_Pin (interrupt pin for UWB chip)\n- **Pin 10**: DW3000_CS_Pin (SPI chip select for UWB chip)\n\nThe UART for RS-485 communication uses **pins 15 (RX) and 19 (TX)**, not pins 8 and 10.\n\n## Building and Flashing\n\n### Step 1: Build TX Variant (Node A)\n\n1. Edit &#96;Src/example_selection.h&#96;:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;c\n   // Comment out other examples:\n   //#define TEST_READING_DEV_ID\n   \n   // Uncomment TX variant:\n   #define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_TX\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n2. Edit &#96;Src/main.c&#96;:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;c\n   // Comment out other examples:\n   // extern int read_dev_id(void); read_dev_id();\n   \n   // Uncomment TX variant:\n   extern int orchestrator_tx(void); orchestrator_tx();\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n3. Build:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   make build\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n4. Flash to Node A board:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   make flash\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 2: Build RX Variant (Node B)\n\n1. Edit &#96;Src/example_selection.h&#96;:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;c\n   // Comment out TX variant:\n   //#define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_TX\n   \n   // Uncomment RX variant:\n   #define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_RX\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n2. Edit &#96;Src/main.c&#96;:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;c\n   // Comment out TX variant:\n   // extern int orchestrator_tx(void); orchestrator_tx();\n   \n   // Uncomment RX variant:\n   extern int orchestrator_rx(void); orchestrator_rx();\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n3. Build:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   make build\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n4. Flash to Node B board:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   make flash\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Important**: You need to build and flash **separately** for each board. The firmware is compiled with either TX or RX code, not both.\n\n## LED Behavior\n\nThe firmware uses &#96;dwt_setleds()&#96; which controls the **DW3000 UWB chip's internal LEDs**, not the board LEDs.\n\n- **On startup**: LEDs will blink once during initialization",

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": ".\\Src\\examples\\ex_21_orchestrator\\orchestrator_rx.c",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {
            "line": 622,

          "endPosition": {
            "line": 683,
            "column": 6
          }
        },
        "contents": "    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n    dev_id = dwt_readdevid();\n\n    /* Wait for DW3000 to be ready with timeout */\n    uint32_t timeout_count = 0;\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc() &amp;&amp; timeout_count &lt; 1000)\n    {\n        timeout_count++;\n        Sleep(1);\n    }\n    \n    if (timeout_count &gt;= 1000)\n    {\n        send_response(\"ERR DW3000_TIMEOUT\");\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"DW3000 TIMEOUT\");\n    }\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        send_response(\"ERR DW3000_INIT_FAILED\");\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED\");\n        // RED LED: Error state - turn on red LED to indicate error\n        nrf_gpio_pin_set(BSP_LED_0);\n        // Don't hang - continue so UART commands still work\n    }\n    else\n    {\n        send_response(\"OK DW3000_READY\");\n    }\n\n    /* Enable LEDs */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure with default settings */\n    configure_uwb();\n\n    /* Enable RX initially (will be controlled by START/STOP commands) */\n    dwt_rxenable(DWT_START_RX_IMMEDIATE);\n\n    /* Send message that we reached main loop */\n    Sleep(100);\n    send_response(\"OK MAIN_LOOP\");\n    \n    /* Blue LED: Stand By state - firmware running, ready for commands */\n    /* Blue LED stays on (already on from UART init) to indicate stand by */\n    \n    /* Main loop - process UART commands and RX packets */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        if (g_test_running)\n        {\n            process_rx_packet();\n        }\n        else\n        {\n            Sleep(100);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#endif",

        "contents": "int ds_twr_initiator(void)\n{\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. See NOTE 2 below. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure the TX spectrum parameters (power, PG delay and PG count) */\n    dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options);\n\n    /* Apply default antenna delay value. See NOTE 1 below. */\n    dwt_setrxantennadelay(RX_ANT_DLY);\n    dwt_settxantennadelay(TX_ANT_DLY);\n\n    /* Set expected response's delay and timeout. See NOTE 4, 5 and 7 below.\n     * As this example only handles one incoming frame with always the same delay and timeout, those values can be set here once for all. */\n    dwt_setrxaftertxdelay(POLL_TX_TO_RESP_RX_DLY_UUS);\n    dwt_setrxtimeout(RESP_RX_TIMEOUT_UUS);\n    dwt_setpreambledetecttimeout(PRE_TIMEOUT);\n\n    /* Next can enable TX/RX states output on GPIOs 5 and 6 to help debug, and also TX/RX LEDs\n     * Note, in real low power applications the LEDs should not be used. */\n    dwt_setlnapamode(DWT_LNA_ENABLE | DWT_PA_ENABLE);\n    // dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Loop forever initiating ranging exchanges. */",

        "contents": "int ss_twr_responder(void)\n{\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset and initialize DW chip. */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW3000 low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC, or could wait for SPIRDY event)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enabling LEDs here for debug so that for each TX the D1 LED will flash on DW3000 red eval-shield boards. */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. See NOTE 13 below. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure the TX spectrum parameters (power, PG delay and PG count) */\n    dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options);\n\n    /* Apply default antenna delay value. See NOTE 2 below. */\n    dwt_setrxantennadelay(RX_ANT_DLY);\n    dwt_settxantennadelay(TX_ANT_DLY);\n\n    /* Next can enable TX/RX states output on GPIOs 5 and 6 to help debug, and also TX/RX LEDs\n     * Note, in real low power applications the LEDs should not be used. */\n    dwt_setlnapamode(DWT_LNA_ENABLE | DWT_PA_ENABLE);\n\n    /* Loop forever responding to ranging requests. */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        /* Activate reception immediately. */",

        "contents": "/* Application entry point.\n */\nint le_pend_tx(void)\n{\n    /* Hold copy of status register state here for reference so that it can be examined at a debug breakpoint. */\n    uint32_t status_reg;\n\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC, or could wait for SPIRDY event)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enabling LEDs here for debug so that for each TX the D1 LED will flash on DW3000 red eval-shield boards. */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. See NOTE 4 below. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* loop forever */\n    while (1)\n    {",

        "contents": "int ss_aes_twr_initiator(void)\n{\n    static uint32_t frame_cnt = 0; /* See Note 13 */\n    static uint8_t seq_cnt = 0x0A; /* Frame sequence number, incremented after each transmission. */\n    uint32_t status_reg;\n    uint8_t nonce[13]; /* 13-byte nonce used in this example as per IEEE802.15.4 */\n    dwt_aes_job_t aes_job_tx, aes_job_rx;\n    int8_t status;\n\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset and initialize DW chip. */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW3000 low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC, or could wait for SPIRDY event)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enabling LEDs here for debug so that for each TX the D1 LED will flash on DW3000 red eval-shield boards.\n     * Note, in real low power applications the LEDs should not be used. */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure DW IC.
