        "contents": "/**\n * Application entry point\n */\nint orchestrator_tx(void)\n{\n    uint32_t dev_id;\n    uint32_t err_code;\n\n    /* Display application name */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n    \n    /* Configure all LED pins for diagnostics */\n    nrf_gpio_cfg_output(BSP_LED_0);  // Red LED - Default/Error states\n    nrf_gpio_cfg_output(BSP_LED_1);  // Orange LED - RX (command received)\n    nrf_gpio_cfg_output(BSP_LED_2);  // Green LED - TX (response sent)\n    nrf_gpio_cfg_output(BSP_LED_3);  // Blue LED - UART works + Stand By state\n    \n    /* Initialize all LEDs to off */\n    nrf_gpio_pin_clear(BSP_LED_0);\n    nrf_gpio_pin_clear(BSP_LED_1);\n    nrf_gpio_pin_clear(BSP_LED_2);\n    nrf_gpio_pin_clear(BSP_LED_3);\n    \n    /* Red LED: Default state - blink to show firmware started */\n    nrf_gpio_pin_set(BSP_LED_0);\n    nrf_delay_ms(100);\n    nrf_gpio_pin_clear(BSP_LED_0);\n    nrf_delay_ms(100);\n    nrf_gpio_pin_set(BSP_LED_0);\n    nrf_delay_ms(100);\n    nrf_gpio_pin_clear(BSP_LED_0);\n    \n    /* CRITICAL: Initialize UART FIRST, before anything else */\n    /* This ensures UART works even if other init fails */\n    uart_init();\n    \n    /* Blue LED: UART works - turn on to indicate UART initialized successfully */\n    nrf_gpio_pin_set(BSP_LED_3);\n    \n    /* Wait for UART to be ready */\n    Sleep(300);\n    \n    /* Send immediate test pattern - simple characters */\n    /* This verifies UART TX works before any other code */\n    for (int i = 0; i &lt; 10; i++) {\n        send_test_char('A' + (i % 26));  // Send A-Z pattern\n        Sleep(20);\n    }\n    send_test_char('\\r');\n    send_test_char('\\n');\n    Sleep(50);\n    \n    /* Send startup message */\n    send_response(\"OK STARTUP\");\n    Sleep(100);\n    \n    /* Send additional diagnostic info */\n    send_response(\"OK FIRMWARE_RUNNING\");\n    Sleep(100);\n\n    /* Initialize app timer module */\n    err_code = app_timer_init();\n    if (err_code != NRF_SUCCESS)\n    {\n        test_run_info",

          {

        "contents": "    if (err_code != NRF_SUCCESS)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"TIMER INIT FAILED\");\n    }\n    else\n    {\n        /* Create timer instance */\n        err_code = app_timer_create(&amp;m_tx_timer_id, APP_TIMER_MODE_REPEATED, tx_timer_handler);\n        if (err_code == NRF_SUCCESS)\n        {\n            g_timer_initialized = 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC();\n    Sleep(2);\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n    dev_id = dwt_readdevid();\n\n    /* Wait for DW3000 to be ready with timeout */\n    uint32_t timeout_count = 0;\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc() &amp;&amp; timeout_count &lt; 1000)\n    {\n        timeout_count++;\n        Sleep(1);\n    }\n    \n    if (timeout_count &gt;= 1000)\n    {\n        send_response(\"ERR DW3000_TIMEOUT\");\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"DW3000 TIMEOUT\");\n    }\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        send_response(\"ERR DW3000_INIT_FAILED\");\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED\");\n        // RED LED: Error state - turn on red LED to indicate error\n        nrf_gpio_pin_set(BSP_LED_0);\n        // Don't hang - continue so UART commands still work\n    }\n    else\n    {\n        send_response(\"OK DW3000_READY\");\n    }\n\n    /* Enable LEDs */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure with default settings */\n    configure_uwb();\n\n    /* Send message that we reached main loop */\n    Sleep(100);\n    send_response(\"OK MAIN_LOOP\");\n    \n    /* Blue LED: Stand By state - firmware running, ready for commands */\n    /* Blue LED stays on (already on from UART init) to indicate stand by */\n    \n    /* Main loop - process UART commands */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        // Command processing happens in UART interrupt handler\n        Sleep(100);\n    }\n}\n\n#endif",

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": ".\\Src\\examples\\ex_00a_reading_dev_id\\read_dev_id.c",

          }
        },
        "contents": "/*! ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n *  @file    read_dev_id.c\n *  @brief   This example just read DW IC's device ID. It can be used to verify\n *           the SPI comms are working correctly.\n *\n * @attention\n *\n * Copyright 2018 - 2021 (c) Decawave Ltd, Dublin, Ireland.\n *\n * All rights reserved.\n *\n * @author Decawave\n */\n\n#include \"deca_probe_interface.h\"\n#include &lt;deca_device_api.h&gt;\n#include &lt;example_selection.h&gt;\n#include &lt;port.h&gt;\n#include &lt;stdio.h&gt;\n\n#if defined(TEST_READING_DEV_ID)\n\nextern void test_run_info(unsigned char *data);\n\n/* Example application name and version to display on LCD screen/VCOM port. */\n#define APP_NAME \"READ DEV ID      \"\n\n/**\n * Application entry point.\n */\nint read_dev_id(void)\n{\n    int err;\n    uint32_t dev_id;\n\n    bsp_board_led_on(0);\n\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    bsp_board_led_on(1);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    bsp_board_led_on(2);\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    bsp_board_led_on(3);\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC, or could wait for SPIRDY event)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n\n    dev_id = dwt_readdevid();\n\n\n    /* Reads and validate device ID returns DWT_ERROR if it does not match expected else DWT_SUCCESS */\n    if ((err = dwt_check_dev_id()) == DWT_SUCCESS)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"DEV ID OK\");\n    }\n    else\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"DEV ID FAILED\");\n    }\n\n    return err;\n}\n\n#endif\n/*****************************************************************************************************************************************************\n * NOTES:\n ****************************************************************************************************************************************************/",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "/*! ----------------------------------------------------------------------------",

            "text": " *  @file    read_dev_id.c",

      "codeBlock": {

        },
        "contents": "/* Index to access to sequence number of the blink frame in the tx_msg array. */\n#define BLINK_FRAME_SN_IDX 1\n\n#define FRAME_LENGTH (sizeof(tx_msg) + FCS_LEN) // The real length that is going to be transmitted\n\n/* Inter-frame delay period, in milliseconds. */\n#define TX_DELAY_MS 500\n\n/* Values for the PG_DELAY and TX_POWER registers reflect the bandwidth and power of the spectrum at the current\n * temperature. These values can be calibrated prior to taking reference measurements. See NOTE 2 below. */\nextern dwt_txconfig_t txconfig_options;\n\n/**\n * Application entry point.\n */\nint simple_tx(void)\n{\n    uint32_t dev_id;\n\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC, or could wait for SPIRDY event)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    dev_id = dwt_readdevid();\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enabling LEDs here for debug so that for each TX the D1 LED will flash on DW3000 red eval-shield boards. */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. See NOTE 5 below. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure the TX spectrum parameters (power PG delay and PG Count) */\n    dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options);\n\n    /* Loop forever sending frames periodically. */",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "/* Index to access to sequence number of the blink frame in the tx_msg array. */",
            "lineNumber": 52

          {
            "lineNumber": 54

            "text": "/* Inter-frame delay period, in milliseconds. */",

            "text": "/* Values for the PG_DELAY and TX_POWER registers reflect the bandwidth and power of the spectrum at the current",

        "contents": "int rx_send_resp(void)\n{\n    /* Hold copy of status register state here for reference so that it can be examined at a debug breakpoint. */\n    uint32_t status_reg = 0;\n    /* Hold copy of frame length of frame received (if good) so that it can be examined at a debug breakpoint. */\n    uint16_t frame_len = 0;\n\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC, or could wait for SPIRDY event)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enabling LEDs here for debug so that for each TX the D1 LED will flash on DW3000 red eval-shield boards. */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. See NOTE 8 below. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure the TX spectrum parameters (power, PG delay and PG count) */\n    dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options);\n\n    /* Loop forever sending and receiving frames periodically. */\n    while (1)\n    {\n        /* Activate reception immediately. See NOTE 4 below. */",

        "contents": "int ds_twr_initiator_sts(void)\n{\n    int goodSts = 0;           /* Used for checking STS quality in received signal */\n    int16_t stsQual;           /* This will contain STS quality index */\n    uint16_t stsStatus;        /* Used to check for good STS status (no errors). */\n    uint8_t firstLoopFlag = 0; /* Used for checking if the program has gone through the main loop for the first time */\n\n    /* Display application name on UART. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n#ifdef CONFIG_SPI_FAST_RATE\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n#endif /* CONFIG_SPI_FAST_RATE */\n#ifdef CONFIG_SPI_SLOW_RATE\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_slowrate();\n#endif /* CONFIG_SPI_SLOW_RATE */\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_IDLE) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enabling LEDs here for debug so that for each TX the D1 LED will flash on DW3000 red eval-shield boards.\n     * Note, in real low power applications the LEDs should not be used. */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. See NOTE 15 below. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config_options))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure the TX spectrum parameters (power, PG delay and PG count) */\n    if (config_options.chan == 5)\n    {\n        dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options);",

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": ".\\Src\\examples\\ex_21_orchestrator\\README.md",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {
            "line": 86
          },
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 143
          }
        },
        "contents": "## LED Behavior\n\nThe firmware uses &#96;dwt_setleds()&#96; which controls the **DW3000 UWB chip's internal LEDs**, not the board LEDs.\n\n- **On startup**: LEDs will blink once during initialization\n- **During operation**: LEDs may flash during UWB activity (TX/RX events)\n- **Board LEDs**: The DWM3001CDK board LEDs (LED_1, LED_2, LED_3, LED_4) are not directly controlled by this firmware\n\n## RS-485 Connection\n\nConnect the RS-485 transceiver to:\n- **A+**: Connect to RS-485 A+ line\n- **B-**: Connect to RS-485 B- line  \n- **GND**: Connect to ground\n- **UART RX**: Connect to GPIO 15\n- **UART TX**: Connect to GPIO 19\n- **DE/RE**: Connect to control RS-485 direction (if needed)\n\nThe firmware communicates at **115200 baud** with the Orchestrator.\n\n## Testing\n\nAfter flashing:\n\n1. **Connect RS-485** from each board to the Orchestrator (RPi 5)\n2. **Power on** both boards\n3. **Run the Orchestrator**:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n   cd Orchestrator\n   npm start\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe Orchestrator will:\n- Send &#96;PNG&#96; (PING) commands to verify connectivity\n- Configure both nodes with &#96;CFG&#96; commands\n- Start tests with &#96;STRT&#96; commands\n- Collect statistics with &#96;STAT&#96; commands\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n### UART Not Working\n- Verify pins 15 (RX) and 19 (TX) are connected correctly\n- Check RS-485 transceiver wiring (A+, B-, GND)\n- Verify baud rate is 115200\n- Check that RS-485 termination resistors are present (120Ω at each end)\n\n### Wrong Variant Flashed\n- Make sure you build and flash separately for each board\n- Check &#96;example_selection.h&#96; has the correct &#96;#define&#96; uncommented\n- Check &#96;main.c&#96; has the correct function call uncommented\n\n### LEDs Not Flashing\n- The firmware controls DW3000 internal LEDs, not board LEDs\n- Board LEDs may not flash unless you add code to control them\n- Check UWB activity with the Orchestrator's statistics",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {

          },
          {
            "text": "- Configure both nodes with &#96;CFG&#96; commands",
            "lineNumber": 122
          },
          {
            "text": "- Start tests with &#96;STRT&#96; commands",
            "lineNumber": 123
          },
          {
            "text": "- Collect statistics with &#96;STAT&#96; commands",
            "lineNumber": 124
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 125
          },
          {
            "text": "## Troubleshooting",
            "lineNumber": 126
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 127
          },
          {
            "text": "### UART Not Working",
            "lineNumber": 128
          },
          {
            "text": "- Verify pins 15 (RX) and 19 (TX) are connected correctly",
            "lineNumber": 129
          },
          {
            "text": "- Check RS-485 transceiver wiring (A+, B-, GND)",
            "lineNumber": 130
          },
          {
            "text": "- Verify baud rate is 115200",
            "lineNumber": 131
          },
          {
            "text": "- Check that RS-485 termination resistors are present (120Ω at each end)",
            "lineNumber": 132
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 133
          },
          {
            "text": "### Wrong Variant Flashed",
            "lineNumber": 134
          },
          {
            "text": "- Make sure you build and flash separately for each board",
            "lineNumber": 135
          },
          {
            "text": "- Check &#96;example_selection.h&#96; has the correct &#96;#define&#96; uncommented",
            "lineNumber": 136
          },
          {
            "text": "- Check &#96;main.c&#96; has the correct function call uncommented",
            "lineNumber": 137
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 138
          },
          {
            "text": "### LEDs Not Flashing",
            "lineNumber": 139
          },
          {
            "text": "- The firmware controls DW3000 internal LEDs, not board LEDs",
            "lineNumber": 140
          },
          {
            "text": "- Board LEDs may not flash unless you add code to control them",
            "lineNumber": 141
          },
          {
            "text": "- Check UWB activity with the Orchestrator's statistics",
            "lineNumber": 142
          }
        ]
      },
      "score": 0.2833242416381836

        "contents": "int simple_rx(void)\n{\n    /* Hold copy of status register state here for reference so that it can be examined at a debug breakpoint. */\n    uint32_t status_reg;\n    /* Hold copy of frame length of frame received (if good) so that it can be examined at a debug breakpoint. */\n    uint16_t frame_len;\n\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW IC supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC, or could wait for SPIRDY event)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED\");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enabling LEDs here for debug so that for each RX-enable the D2 LED will flash on DW3000 red eval-shield boards. */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Loop forever receiving frames. */\n    while (TRUE)\n    {\n        /* TESTING BREAKPOINT LOCATION #1 */",

        "contents": "int bw_cal(void)\n{\n    /* Variable to store raw temp value */\n    uint8_t raw_temp = 0;\n    /* Variable to store real temp value */\n    float real_temp = 0;\n    /* String to contain temp value for debug purposes */\n    char str_temp[32] = { 0 };\n\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC, or could wait for SPIRDY event)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enabling LEDs here for debug so that for each TX the D1 LED will flash on DW3000 red eval-shield boards. */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. See NOTE 3 below. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* At this point, we are emulating a process that needs to occur at room temperature when devices are being configured in factory. */\n    /* See NOTE 3 for more information */\n    txconfig_options.PGcount = dwt_calcpgcount(txconfig_options.PGdly);\n\n    /* Write the TX message into the TX buffer */\n    /* This only needs to be done once if we are sending the same frame over and over again */\n    dwt_writetxdata(sizeof(tx_msg), tx_msg, 0); /* Zero offset in TX buffer. */\n    dwt_writetxfctrl(sizeof(tx_msg), 0, 0);     /* Zero offset in TX buffer, no ranging. */\n\n    /* Loop forever, adjusting bandwidth periodically. */",

        "contents": "int ds_twr_initiator(void)\n{\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. See NOTE 2 below. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure the TX spectrum parameters (power, PG delay and PG count) */\n    dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options);\n\n    /* Apply default antenna delay value. See NOTE 1 below. */\n    dwt_setrxantennadelay(RX_ANT_DLY);\n    dwt_settxantennadelay(TX_ANT_DLY);\n\n    /* Set expected response's delay and timeout. See NOTE 4, 5 and 7 below.\n     * As this example only handles one incoming frame with always the same delay and timeout, those values can be set here once for all. */\n    dwt_setrxaftertxdelay(POLL_TX_TO_RESP_RX_DLY_UUS);\n    dwt_setrxtimeout(RESP_RX_TIMEOUT_UUS);\n    dwt_setpreambledetecttimeout(PRE_TIMEOUT);\n\n    /* Next can enable TX/RX states output on GPIOs 5 and 6 to help debug, and also TX/RX LEDs\n     * Note, in real low power applications the LEDs should not be used. */\n    dwt_setlnapamode(DWT_LNA_ENABLE | DWT_PA_ENABLE);\n    // dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Loop forever initiating ranging exchanges. */",

        "contents": "int ss_twr_responder_sts(void)\n{\n    int goodSts = 0;           /* Used for checking STS quality in received signal */\n    int16_t stsQual;           /* This will contain STS quality index */\n    uint16_t stsStatus;        /* Used to check for good STS status (no errors). */\n    uint8_t firstLoopFlag = 0; /* Used to track if the program has gone through the first loop or not. */\n    /* Display application name on UART. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n#ifdef CONFIG_SPI_FAST_RATE\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n#endif /* CONFIG_SPI_FAST_RATE */\n#ifdef CONFIG_SPI_SLOW_RATE\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_slowrate();\n#endif /* CONFIG_SPI_SLOW_RATE */\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_IDLE) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enabling LEDs here for debug so that for each TX the D1 LED will flash on DW3000 red eval-shield boards.\n     * Note, in real low power applications the LEDs should not be used. */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure DW IC.         "contents": "import { getConfig } from './config.js';\nimport { RS485Comm } from './rs485Comm.js';\nimport { NodeController } from './nodeController.js';\nimport { CSVLogger } from './csvLogger.js';\nimport { TestRunner } from './testRunner.js';\n\n/**\n * Main Orchestrator Entry Point\n * Runs test plan from command line\n */\nasync function main() {\n  console.log('UWB Test Orchestrator Starting...\\n');\n\n  try {\n    // Load configuration\n    const config = getConfig();\n    config.loadSettings();\n    config.loadTestPlan();\n\n    const serialConfig = config.getSerialConfig();\n    const testPlan = config.getTestPlan();\n\n    if (testPlan.length === 0) {\n      console.error('No tests found in test plan');\n      process.exit(1);\n    }\n\n    // Initialize RS-485 connections\n    console.log('Initializing RS-485 connections...');\n    const rs485A = new RS485Comm(\n      serialConfig.node_a_port,\n      serialConfig.baudrate,\n      serialConfig.timeout * 1000\n    );\n    const rs485B = new RS485Comm(\n      serialConfig.node_b_port,\n      serialConfig.baudrate,\n      serialConfig.timeout * 1000\n    );\n\n    // Initialize node controllers\n    const nodeA = new NodeController('A', rs485A);\n    const nodeB = new NodeController('B', rs485B);\n\n    // Initialize CSV logger\n    const csvLogger = new CSVLogger();\n\n    // Initialize test runner\n    const testRunner = new TestRunner(nodeA, nodeB, csvLogger, config);\n\n    // Connect to nodes in parallel for faster startup\n    console.log('Connecting to nodes...');\n    const [connectedA, connectedB] = await Promise.all([\n      nodeA.connect().then(() =&gt; {\n        console.log('Node A connected');\n        return true;\n      }),\n      nodeB.connect().then(() =&gt; {\n        console.log('Node B connected');\n        return true;\n      })\n    ]);\n    console.log('');\n\n    // Test connectivity with PING\n    console.log('Testing connectivity...');\n    const pingA = await nodeA.ping();\n    if (pingA) {\n      console.log('✓ Node A PING successful');\n    }\n}",

        "contents": "int ss_twr_initiator(void)\n{\n\n    /* Display application name on LCD. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n\n    /* Reset and initialize DW chip. */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW3000 low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC, or could wait for SPIRDY event)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_INIT) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enabling LEDs here for debug so that for each TX the D1 LED will flash on DW3000 red eval-shield boards. */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. See NOTE 13 below. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure the TX spectrum parameters (power, PG delay and PG count) */\n    dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options);\n\n    /* Apply default antenna delay value. See NOTE 2 below. */\n    dwt_setrxantennadelay(RX_ANT_DLY);\n    dwt_settxantennadelay(TX_ANT_DLY);\n\n    /* Set expected response's delay and timeout. See NOTE 1 and 5 below.\n     * As this example only handles one incoming frame with always the same delay and timeout, those values can be set here once for all. */\n    dwt_setrxaftertxdelay(POLL_TX_TO_RESP_RX_DLY_UUS);\n    dwt_setrxtimeout(RESP_RX_TIMEOUT_UUS);\n\n    /* Next can enable TX/RX states output on GPIOs 5 and 6 to help debug, and also TX/RX LEDs\n     * Note, in real low power applications the LEDs should not be used. */",

        "contents": "int ss_twr_initiator_sts(void)\n{\n    int goodSts = 0;           /* Used for checking STS quality in received signal */\n    int16_t stsQual;           /* This will contain STS quality index */\n    uint16_t stsStatus;        /* Used to check for good STS status (no errors). */\n    uint8_t firstLoopFlag = 0; /* Used to track if the program has gone through the first loop or not. */\n\n    /* Display application name on UART. */\n    test_run_info((unsigned char *)APP_NAME);\n\n    /* Configure SPI rate, DW3000 supports up to 36 MHz */\n#ifdef CONFIG_SPI_FAST_RATE\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_fastrate();\n#endif /* CONFIG_SPI_FAST_RATE */\n#ifdef CONFIG_SPI_SLOW_RATE\n    port_set_dw_ic_spi_slowrate();\n#endif /* CONFIG_SPI_SLOW_RATE */\n\n    /* Reset DW IC */\n    reset_DWIC(); /* Target specific drive of RSTn line into DW IC low for a period. */\n\n    Sleep(2); // Time needed for DW3000 to start up (transition from INIT_RC to IDLE_RC)\n\n    /* Probe for the correct device driver. */\n    dwt_probe((struct dwt_probe_s *)&amp;dw3000_probe_interf);\n\n    while (!dwt_checkidlerc()) /* Need to make sure DW IC is in IDLE_RC before proceeding */ { };\n\n    if (dwt_initialise(DWT_DW_IDLE) == DWT_ERROR)\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"INIT FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Enabling LEDs here for debug so that for each TX the D1 LED will flash on DW3000 red eval-shield boards.\n     * Note, in real low power applications the LEDs should not be used. */\n    dwt_setleds(DWT_LEDS_ENABLE | DWT_LEDS_INIT_BLINK);\n\n    /* Configure DW IC. See NOTE 15 below. */\n    /* if the dwt_configure returns DWT_ERROR either the PLL or RX calibration has failed the host should reset the device */\n    if (dwt_configure(&amp;config_options))\n    {\n        test_run_info((unsigned char *)\"CONFIG FAILED     \");\n        while (1) { };\n    }\n\n    /* Configure the TX spectrum parameters (power, PG delay and PG count) */\n    if (config_options.chan == 5)\n    {\n        dwt_configuretxrf(&amp;txconfig_options);",

Updated the code to use `bsp_board_led_on()` and `bsp_board_led_off()` instead of direct GPIO control, matching other examples. Since `bsp_board_init(BSP_INIT_LEDS | BSP_INIT_BUTTONS)` is already called in `main.c`, the LEDs are initialized and we can use the BSP board LED functions directly.

## Changes Made

**Updated LED control to use BSP board functions:**
- Removed `nrf_gpio_cfg_output()` calls (LEDs already initialized by `bsp_board_init()`)
- Replaced `nrf_gpio_pin_set()` with `bsp_board_led_on()`
- Replaced `nrf_gpio_pin_clear()` with `bsp_board_led_off()`

**LED mapping (using BSP board functions):**
- **LED 0 (Red)**: Default/Error states — blinks on startup, stays on for errors
- **LED 1 (Orange)**: RX — blinks when command received
- **LED 2 (Green)**: TX — turns on when response sent
- **LED 3 (Blue)**: UART works + Stand By — turns on after UART init, stays on

This matches the pattern used in `ex_00a_reading_dev_id` and is consistent with the Nordic SDK BSP.

<reproduction_steps>
1. Rebuild both firmware variants:
   ```powershell
   .\clean.ps1
   .\build-and-flash-rx.ps1
   # Wait for RX flash to complete, then:
   .\build-and-flash-tx.ps1
   ```

2. After flashing, watch the LEDs:
   - Red LED (LED 0) should double blink (firmware started)
   - Blue LED (LED 3) should turn on and stay on (UART works, Stand By state)
   - If red LED stays on, there's an error
   - If blue LED doesn't turn on, UART init failed

3. Test UART communication:
   ```powershell
   .\test-uart-direct.ps1
   ```
   Watch for:
   - Blue LED should be on (Stand By state)
   - Orange LED should blink when PNG command is received
   - Green LED should turn on when response is sent

4. Run the Orchestrator test:
   ```powershell
   cd Orchestrator
   node src/orchestrator/main.js
   ```
   Watch LEDs during PING:
   - Blue LED should be on (Stand By)
   - Orange LED should blink (command received)
   - Green LED should turn on (response sent)

5. Share observations:
   - Is blue LED on? (UART works, Stand By)
   - Does orange LED blink when sending PNG? (RX working)
   - Does green LED turn on? (TX working)
   - Any red LED errors?
</reproduction_steps>

The code now uses the BSP board LED functions, consistent with other examples. The blue LED staying on confirms UART is working and the firmware is in Stand By state.

Updated all error cases to blink the red LED rapidly (20 blinks, 50ms on/off) before keeping it on. This makes errors clearly visible.

## Updated Error Handling

**Red LED intensive blinking (20 blinks @ 50ms intervals = 2 seconds):**
- UART initialization failed
- DW3000 timeout (checkidlerc timeout)
- DW3000 initialization failed
- Timer initialization failed (TX only)

**Error behavior:**
1. Rapid blinking: 20 blinks (50ms on, 50ms off) = 2 seconds
2. Then stays on: Red LED remains on to indicate persistent error

**LED status summary:**
- Red LED (LED 0):
  - Double blink on startup (normal)
  - Intensive rapid blinking on errors (20 blinks)
  - Stays on if error persists
- Orange LED (LED 1): Blinks when command received
- Green LED (LED 2): Turns on when response sent
- Blue LED (LED 3): Stays on when UART works (Stand By state)

<reproduction_steps>
1. Rebuild both firmware variants:
   ```powershell
   .\clean.ps1
   .\build-and-flash-rx.ps1
   # Wait for RX flash to complete, then:
   .\build-and-flash-tx.ps1
   ```

2. After flashing, watch the LEDs:
   - Red LED should double blink (firmware started - normal)
   - Blue LED should turn on and stay on (UART works, Stand By state)
   - If red LED blinks rapidly (20 times), there's an error
   - After rapid blinking, red LED stays on if error persists

3. Test UART communication:
   ```powershell
   .\test-uart-direct.ps1
   ```
   Watch for:
   - Blue LED should be on (Stand By state)
   - Orange LED should blink when PNG command is received
   - Green LED should turn on when response is sent
   - Red LED should NOT blink rapidly (no errors)

4. Run the Orchestrator test:
   ```powershell
   cd Orchestrator
   node src/orchestrator/main.js
   ```
   Watch LEDs during PING:
   - Blue LED should be on (Stand By)
   - Orange LED should blink (command received)
   - Green LED should turn on (response sent)
   - Red LED should NOT blink rapidly (no errors)

5. Share observations:
   - Is blue LED on? (UART works, Stand By)
   - Does orange LED blink when sending PNG? (RX working)
   - Does green LED turn on? (TX working)
   - Does red LED blink rapidly? (indicates which error occurred)
</reproduction_steps>

Rapid red blinking makes errors easy to spot. The 20-blink pattern (2 seconds) is distinct from the normal startup double blink.

The scripts update both files. The current state shows TX was active in both `example_selection.h` and `main.c`, so it was building TX.

The scripts work correctly:
- `set-node-tx.ps1` sets both files to TX
- `set-node-rx.ps1` sets both files to RX

After running `set-node-rx.ps1`, both files are now configured for RX:
- `example_selection.h`: `#define TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_RX`
- `main.c`: `extern int orchestrator_rx(void); orchestrator_rx();`

## The Problem

Both files must match:
- `example_selection.h` controls which code is compiled (`#if defined(TEST_ORCHESTRATOR_TX)`)
- `main.c` controls which function is called (`orchestrator_tx()` vs `orchestrator_rx()`)

If they don't match, the build may fail or run the wrong variant.

## Solution

Always run the set-node scripts before building:
```powershell
# For RX board:
.\set-node-rx.ps1
.\build.ps1

# For TX board:
.\set-node-tx.ps1
.\build.ps1
```

Or use the build-and-flash scripts which handle this automatically:
```powershell
.\build-and-flash-rx.ps1  # Runs set-node-rx.ps1, then build, then flash
.\build-and-flash-tx.ps1  # Runs set-node-tx.ps1, then build, then flash
```

The scripts are working correctly. Both files are now set to RX. Rebuild to get the RX firmware.
